title: Auric Artisan Docs
text: Auric Artisan is a colour and accessibility studio. It lives in three places: the website at https://auricartisan.com, with its tools, libraries and kits; a set of extensions for Visual Studio Code; and a browser extension that brings the colour tools to any web page. A few services — a font CDN, an icon CDN and a public API — let you use the same data from your own sites and code. This documentation is written for the people who use those products: designers, developers, accessibility specialists, students and anyone curious about colour. It explains what every screen, control, command and setting does, how to complete real tasks step by step, what each tool measures and how precisely, and what to do when something does not behave as you expect.

title: Create an account (optional)
heading: Sign up in short
text: 1. Go to https://auricartisan.com/auth/ (or select Create account in the header). 2. Select the Create Account tab. 3. Fill in Display Name , Username , Email , Password and Confirm Password . Passwords need 12–128 characters with upper and lower case letters, a number and a symbol. 4. Tick I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy . 5. Select Create Account and complete the short Auric human check (repeat a sequence of three marks). 6. Open the verification email and confirm your address within 24 hours. Or select Google or GitHub under or sign up with to use an existing account with one of those providers. The full walkthrough, including every rule and error message, is in [Sign up](../website/account-and-billing/docs/sign-up.md). Note: Until you verify your email address, the account works as a limited workspace. The sign-in page says billing, promotions, API keys and device approval stay locked until the address is verified.

title: Your first hour
text: This tour takes about an hour and needs no account. Each stop names the controls as they appear on screen, says roughly how long it takes, and ends with what you should see. Links point to the full documentation for each tool.

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 1 — Find your way around (5 minutes)
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/. On your very first visit a short welcome animation plays; press Esc , Enter or Space , or click, to skip it. 2. When the cookie bar appears at the bottom, choose Accept All , Reject All or Customise . Every tool works whichever you pick. See [Privacy basics](privacy-basics.md). 3. Look at the header. From left to right it gives you the home link, Search , and the Company , Tools and Learn menus, followed by icon buttons for the app, the browser extension, VS Code, search, the guide, the library, language and theme, and finally Sign in and Create account . 4. Press Ctrl + K and type "contrast". Open the Contrast Checker from the results, then come back. 5. Press ? (while not typing in a field) to open the Guide . It offers quick paths such as Run a quick audit , Build color assets , Check accessibility and Find a feature fast . Close it with Esc . Result: you can reach any tool from search, the menus or the guide.

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 2 — A first contrast check (5 minutes)
text: 1. On the home page, scroll to Pick two colours, watch the verdict move . 2. Choose a Text swatch and a Background swatch. 3. Read the contrast ratio and the Normal text and Large text verdicts (AA, AAA or fail). 4. Select Open the full checker to continue in the Contrast Checker with your own colours. Result: you know whether a colour pair is readable, and why. WCAG (the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) sets 4.5:1 as the AA minimum for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Full guide: [Contrast Checker](../website/tools/accessibility-and-vision/contrast-checker/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 3 — One brand colour to a token file (10 minutes)
text: 1. On the home page, find One brand color to a shippable system . 2. Enter your brand colour in Brand colour (or type a hex value in the field beside it). 3. Watch the three steps update: Accessible ramp (nine steps measured against the page surface), Vision check (the ramp through colour-vision models) and Export tokens . 4. Under Export tokens , choose CSS , Tailwind or JSON , then select Copy tokens . 5. Paste the tokens into your project. Result: a readable colour scale in a format your build reads. For a complete system (type, spacing, radius, shadow and motion as well as colour), continue in the [Design System Generator](../website/tools/colour-workspace/design-engine/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 4 — Audit a web page (15 minutes)
text: 1. Open Analyze URLs from Tools › Core tools (https://auricartisan.com/tool/analyzer/). 2. Paste the address of a page you own or are allowed to test. The Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy only permit analysis of sites you own or are authorised to test. 3. Run the audit and stay in Simple mode for your first run. 4. Work through Overview , then the fixes, then the report, as the Guide's "Run a quick audit" path suggests. 5. Export a report if you want to keep one. Result: a list of accessibility and colour issues on the page, with suggested fixes. Runs that need Auric Artisan's servers, such as whole-site crawls, show their token cost before you start and need an account. Full guide: [Analyzer](../website/tools/accessibility-and-vision/analyzer/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 5 — See it through other eyes (10 minutes)
text: 1. Open Vision Simulation (https://auricartisan.com/tool/vision-simulation/). 2. Load an image or screenshot of your design. 3. Switch between protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia and check that colour-coded information is still distinguishable. Result: you can spot colour pairs that collapse for people with colour-vision deficiency. The simulations are models for design and learning, not a medical test. Full guide: [Vision Simulation](../website/tools/accessibility-and-vision/vision-simulation/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 6 — Save and find your work (5 minutes)
text: 1. In any tool you used, use its save or export control to keep a palette, gradient or report. 2. Open Library from the header (the button described as "Saved palettes and exports"). 3. Find what you saved. Result: your work is kept in My Library in this browser. It stays on this device and is not uploaded unless you publish it. See [Library](../website/library/README.md) and [Library Kit](../website/kits/library-kit/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 7 — Make the site yours (5 minutes)
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , to open Settings . 2. Under Appearance , choose a Theme ( Light , Dark or System ), an accent colour, a Language and a Text size . 3. Under Comfort , try Reduce motion , Boost contrast or Reading mode ( Alt + R ). 4. Close with Esc . Result: the whole site follows your preferences on this device. See [Light and dark theme](light-and-dark-theme.md), [Language](language.md) and [Settings panel](../website/site-features/settings-panel/README.md).

title: Your first hour
heading: Stop 8 — Optional: create an account (5 minutes)
text: If you want to publish a portfolio, run server-backed crawls, or keep a paid plan across devices, create a free account: [Create an account (optional)](create-an-account.md). Then open the dashboard at https://auricartisan.com/auth/dashboard/ and follow Finish setting up in the side column.

title: The free-tools model
text: Every Auric Artisan tool is free, on every plan, for everyone. The pricing page (https://auricartisan.com/company/pricing/) opens with "Every tool is free, forever" and lists tools that used to sit behind a paywall — LUT Lab, the ICC Profile Parser, the Color Science Lab, the clinical vision simulations and the industrial suite — as free on every tier. Paid plans do not unlock tools. They sell conveniences and scale.

title: The free-tools model
heading: What stays free
text: - Every tool, with no login required to start. - Local saves in your browser. - The libraries, the Learning Hub and the documentation. - The browser extension and the VS Code extensions. - Two-step verification and account activity logging (the pricing page lists "2FA free for everyone"). - Everything that runs in your browser is free and unmetered — for example, the pricing page notes that vision simulations run in your browser and are not metered at all.

title: The free-tools model
heading: What the paid plans add
text: The paid plans on the pricing page add, depending on the tier: - ad-free browsing and ad controls; - watermark-free Pro exports and more export formats; - a monthly allowance of tokens for server-backed work, such as whole-site accessibility crawls of up to 24 pages a run; - higher limits (saved projects, URL analyses); - the REST API, with a monthly allowance of API credits (Specialist and above); - branded WCAG accessibility reports (Specialist and above); - email or priority support. Some listed perks — cloud sync across devices, version history, batch processing, team seats, white-label embedding and SSO — are marked coming soon or planned on the pricing page and are not live yet. The full plan-by-plan table is in [Plans and pricing](../website/account-and-billing/docs/plans-and-pricing.md).

title: The free-tools model
heading: How paid plans are sold
text: - One payment, fixed term. A paid plan is a one-time purchase of a pass for one month or twelve months. It does not auto-renew, no card is stored for a future charge, and there is no subscription to cancel. - When the term ends , the account returns to the free Apprentice plan on its own. Every tool keeps working and nothing you made is deleted. - Money-back window. Plan purchases carry a 7-day money-back window. - Account first. You must be signed in before you pay, so the pass belongs to your account rather than to one browser. - On sale today. The pricing page shows Artisan as available now; Specialist and Industrial Pro are marked Coming soon .

title: The free-tools model
heading: Tokens, in one paragraph
text: Tokens meter work that runs on Auric Artisan's servers. The free Apprentice plan includes 100 starter tokens once, which do not renew; paid plans include an allowance that refreshes each billing month (250 on Artisan). Unused included tokens expire at the end of the billing period. See [Tokens](../website/account-and-billing/docs/tokens.md).

title: How the pieces fit
text: Auric Artisan is several products built on one colour engine and one design system. This page explains how they relate, so you know what you need to install, what needs an account, and what needs a network connection.

title: How the pieces fit
heading: One engine, several places
text: The same colour-science code powers the website tools, the Learn library's interactive figures, the REST API, the browser extension and the colour-related VS Code extensions. The author page describes it this way: where an article states a formula or threshold, it is the formula the code uses. In practice this means a contrast ratio or a colour conversion should agree whether you get it from a website tool, the extension or the API. The products do not depend on each other. You can use the browser extension without ever visiting the website, or the VS Code extensions without an account.

title: How the pieces fit
heading: What runs where
text: Product Where it runs Needs an account? Needs a network? --- --- --- --- Website tools (most) In your browser tab No Only to load the page, unless you prepared it for offline use Website Analyzer, basic analysis In your browser No Yes, to fetch the page you analyse Website Analyzer, server-backed runs (rendered analyses, whole-site crawls) On Auric Artisan's servers Yes, and uses tokens Yes Libraries and Learn In your browser No Only to load, unless cached for offline use Portfolio Builder, drafting In your browser No for drafting Publishing needs an account and a connection Dashboard, plans, API keys On Auric Artisan's servers Yes Yes Browser extension Entirely in your browser No No (it makes no network calls) VS Code extensions On your computer, inside VS Code No Only for extensions that fetch fonts or icons REST API On Auric Artisan's servers Yes (an API key) and a plan with API access Yes

title: How the pieces fit
heading: What the account connects
text: An account is optional for the tools. When you have one, it connects: - Your identity — a display name, a username (your public handle), a profile photo and a verified email address. - Your plan — the Apprentice (free) plan by default, or a paid plan pass you have bought. A pass belongs to the account, not to one browser, so it follows you to other devices. - Tokens — the balance that pays for server-backed tool work such as whole-site accessibility crawls. See [Tokens](../website/account-and-billing/docs/tokens.md). - API keys and API credits — for the REST API, on plans that include it. See [API keys](../website/account-and-billing/docs/api-keys.md). - Your public portfolio — publishing a portfolio page at your own address. - Security — two-step verification, signed-in devices and a data export. Most of your saved work (palettes, gradients, collections, drafts and preferences) is stored in your browser, not in the account. The pricing page says so directly: "today the platform syncs account settings and saves your work locally." Cloud sync across devices is listed as coming soon. See [Privacy basics](privacy-basics.md).

title: How the pieces fit
heading: Two separate meters: tokens and API credits
text: The site uses two units that are easy to confuse: - Tokens pay for work you start in a website tool that runs on Auric Artisan's servers — for example a rendered page analysis or a whole-site crawl. Everything that runs in your browser is free and unmetered. - API credits pay for requests your own code makes to the REST API. They are separate balances with separate allowances. Neither pays for the other and nothing converts between them. If you only use the website tools you can ignore API credits; if you only use the API you can ignore tokens. Details: [Tokens](../website/account-and-billing/docs/tokens.md) and [API credits and spend controls](../website/account-and-billing/docs/api-credits-and-spend.md).

title: How the pieces fit
heading: Site-wide features
text: Every website page shares the same header, search, settings and floating kits: - Search — Ctrl + K , or the Search button in the header. - Guide — tours and quick paths; press ? when you are not typing. - Settings — theme, language, text size, motion and comfort options; Ctrl + , . - Kits — floating panels such as the Library Kit that open over any page. See [Site features](../website/site-features/README.md) and [Kits](../website/kits/README.md).

title: Language: English and Hindi
text: The Auric Artisan website is available in English and Hindi (हिन्दी). The interface, the tool pages and the articles are translated. English is the default.

title: Language: English and Hindi
heading: Switch language
text: Use any of these; they all change the same setting. - Header button — select the language button in the header (its label is "Switch language between English and Hindi"). Each press switches between the two. - Mobile menu — open the navigation menu and, under Preferences › Language , select English or हिन्दी . - Settings — press Ctrl + , (or use the floating settings button), open Appearance , and under Language select English or हिन्दी . - Switching to Hindi translates the page in place, without a reload. - Switching back to English reloads the page, because the original English text has to be loaded again. - Dates and numbers follow the chosen language.

title: Language: English and Hindi
heading: Things to know about Hindi
text: - The site transliterates its own brand and product names into Devanagari. Third-party names that people type or search for, such as Google, GitHub, VS Code, Figma and Razorpay, stay in Latin script. - Technical terms with no common Hindi equivalent — colour-space names like CIELAB, model names, font names and header names — stay in Latin script. - Search queries are matched against English text, so search in English if a Hindi query finds nothing. - Where a page asks you to type a confirmation sentence (for example, unlocking the danger zone in the dashboard), type the sentence exactly as it is displayed in your language. - The sign-in and other account pages are translated too.

title: Offline use
text: The Auric Artisan website can be installed as a web app (a PWA — a website your browser can install and keep in its own cache) and prepared to work without a connection. You do this once while you are online. The page for it is The app under Get Auric in the header, at https://auricartisan.com/download/.

title: Offline use
heading: Prepare the website for offline use
text: 1. While you are online, open https://auricartisan.com/download/. 2. Optional: if your browser offers it, select Install app to add Auric Artisan to your apps or home screen. Whether the button appears is your browser's decision. 3. Under How much to keep , leave Auto selected unless the device is short of storage. The profiles are: Profile Keeps Suits --- --- --- Auto Chooses for you from the device's memory, storage headroom and connection Almost everyone Lite The app shell and the core tools, and little else Phones, tight storage, metered connections Balanced Shell, core tools and the libraries you actually open A laptop you also use for other things Full The widest cache the profile allows A desktop that will be offline for a while 4. Select Prepare offline version , or Download full offline for the widest cache. The cache fills in the background and you can keep working. 5. Under Is this browser ready , select Check readiness . Six checks report on the shell, the full cache, persistent storage, local capabilities, install and update state. 6. Grant persistent storage if your browser asks. Without it, the browser may clear the cache when the device runs short of space. The result: cached libraries and tools open straight from the browser when you are offline, and palettes and exports you make stay on the device.

title: Privacy basics
text: This page is a short orientation. The detailed version is [Privacy overview](../help/privacy.md), and the official, authoritative text is the Privacy Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/ and the Cookie Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/.

title: Privacy basics
heading: The short version
text: - Most tools run in your browser. Colour calculations, palettes, vision simulations and theme generation are done locally where possible. - Your saved work and your preferences are stored in your browser on your device. - An account stores the details you give it (email, names, profile fields) and the security records needed to keep it safe. - Analytics is first-party, sets no cookies, and runs only if you consent to the Analytics category. - Payments go to Razorpay. Auric Artisan never sees or stores your card, UPI or bank details. - The Privacy Policy states that Auric Artisan does not sell personal data or use it for behavioural advertising.

title: Privacy basics
heading: What stays in your browser
text: Kept in your browser Examples --- --- Saved work Palettes, gradients, collections and exports in My Library Drafts Tool state and your Portfolio Builder draft Preferences Theme, language, accent colour, text size, eye-rest and other settings Your cookie choice The consent record from the cookie banner The Privacy Policy says many preferences stay on your device and are not sent to Auric Artisan's servers unless a tool needs them. Because this data lives in the browser, clearing your browser's site data removes it, and it does not follow you to another device. See [Clear data and start fresh](../help/troubleshooting.md clear-site-data-and-start-fresh).

title: Privacy basics
heading: What goes to a server
text: Sent to Auric Artisan's servers When --- --- Account details When you sign up, sign in, or edit your profile Security records Sessions, sign-in attempts and security events Web analysis inputs When a tool fetches or analyses a URL for you Server-backed tool work When you start a run that uses tokens Messages When you use the contact form Order records When you buy something (the item, amount and payment reference — not card details) Analytics events Only with your consent: an event name, the page path (never query strings), the referrer's origin and a few coarse properties such as device class

title: Privacy basics
heading: Cookies and consent
text: On your first visit a bar at the bottom of the page, We value your privacy , offers three choices: - Accept All — turns on every optional category. - Reject All — keeps only what is strictly necessary. - Customise — opens the preferences section of the Cookie Policy page, where you choose each category. Essential cookies (for example the signed-in session and its security companion) are always on because the site cannot work securely without them. You can change your choice at any time on https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/ or from Settings . The full walkthrough is in [Cookie consent and privacy](../website/site-features/cookie-consent-and-privacy/README.md). Analytics also stays off when your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, as the Privacy Policy states.

title: Privacy basics

text: The Privacy Policy names three: Cloudflare (hosting and storage), Razorpay (payments) and Google Fonts (font files on some pages, which means Google receives the technical request, such as your IP address). The Security page adds Resend for email delivery.

title: What Auric Artisan is
text: Auric Artisan is a colour-science and accessibility platform built by one independent developer in India. It brings together practical colour tools, accessibility checks, colour-vision simulations, learning material and developer services, and it publishes the same colour engine in several places: the website at https://auricartisan.com, a set of Visual Studio Code extensions, and a browser extension. The platform's own motto is "Tools That Respect Intelligence": the tools show their working, name the models they use and state their limits, so you can check a number rather than take it on trust.

title: What Auric Artisan is
heading: The website
text: The website is the largest part of Auric Artisan. It has four kinds of content. Interactive tools that run in your browser. The header's Tools menu groups them as follows (names as shown on the site): Group Tools --- --- Core tools Portfolio Builder, Portfolio Index, Analyze URLs, Vision Simulation, Design System Generator, Color Science Lab, Basic Tools, Personalization Generator Creative utilities Image Picker, Font Library, Icon Library, Generate ASCII Art, Generate Ishihara Plates Colour science Illuminants, Chromatic Adaptation, Gamut Mapping Gamut and rendering Gamut Explorer, HDR Gamut Plot, Tonal Steps Tints and Shades, Tone Mapping Perception Perception and Vision, Neuroscience, Psychophysics Engine Spectral Material Lighting, Industrial Dye Chemistry Utilities LUT Lab, ICC Parser, Collage Maker, M-Gradient Palette, SVG Recolor All Tools (https://auricartisan.com/collections/) lists every tool in one place. Every tool is free to use; see [The free-tools model](free-tools-model.md). The tools are documented one by one under [Website tools](../website/tools/README.md). Browsable, checkable collections of colour data, each under Learn › Libraries in the header: - Color Library — named colours and colour systems. - Palette Library — curated palettes. - Gradient Library — perceptual gradients. - Harmony Library — colour relationships with the maths shown. - Shade Library — tonal scales built in OKLCH (a colour space designed so that equal steps look equally different). - Accessibility Library — tested accessible colour pairs. My Library (under Workspace ) holds the palettes, gradients, reports and exports you save from the tools. See [Library](../website/library/README.md). - Learning Hub — lessons on colour science and accessible design, many with live interactive figures. - Accessibility Compliance — WCAG checks and guidance. - Blog , Documentation and Changelog — articles, technical guides and release notes. - Portfolio Builder lets you build and publish a public page of your work; Portfolio Index is a directory of published portfolios. See [Portfolio](../website/portfolio/README.md). - An optional account adds a dashboard, cross-device sign-in, plan purchases and API keys. See [Account and billing](../website/account-and-billing/README.md).

title: What Auric Artisan is
heading: The VS Code extensions
text: Seventeen free extensions for Visual Studio Code, listed at https://auricartisan.com/vscode/ and on the Visual Studio Marketplace under the publisher auric-artisan . They cover colour themes, file and library icons, emoji, colour and WCAG linting, a secrets scanner, a live server, a file organiser, a font hub and a code formatter. The site describes every one as free, needing no account and sending no telemetry. Two extension packs install most of them in one step: text code --install-extension auric-artisan.auric-artisan-icon-pack code --install-extension auric-artisan.auric-artisan See [VS Code extensions](../vscode-extensions/README.md).

title: What Auric Artisan is
heading: The browser extension
text: A colour, accessibility and developer toolkit for your browser: an eyedropper, contrast checks, palettes, an accessibility audit, an element inspector and vision simulation, all working on the page you are looking at. The extension page (https://auricartisan.com/extension.html) describes version 1.0.1 as having 18 tools, 80 accessibility rules and 12 vision simulations, with English and हिन्दी interfaces and no network calls or telemetry. It installs from the Chrome Web Store (which also serves Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi) and from Firefox Add-ons. Press Alt + Shift + A to open it on the current tab. See [Browser extension](../browser-extension/README.md).

title: What Auric Artisan is
heading: Services for developers
text: - Public REST API — programmatic access to colour conversion, palettes, contrast, vision simulation, rendering and more, metered in API credits. API access is part of the Specialist plan and above. See [Public API](../services/public-api/README.md). - Font and icon delivery — the Font Library and Icon Library on the website offer CDN-ready code for embedding their fonts and icons. See [Font CDN](../services/font-cdn/README.md) and [Icon CDN](../services/icon-cdn/README.md). - Design-tool plugins — see [Design-tool plugins](../design-tool-plugins/README.md) for the plugins you can actually install.

title: What Auric Artisan is
heading: What Auric Artisan is not
text: The site is explicit about its limits, and so are these docs: - It is an independent private platform, not a government body, standards organisation or certification laboratory. - Vision simulations and the Ishihara-style plate generator are for learning and design. They are not medical tests and do not diagnose anything. - Web analysis results are guidance. They are not a certified accessibility audit, security audit or penetration test. - Colour-science outputs are grounded in published CIE and W3C methods, but they do not replace calibrated instruments for colour-critical industrial work.

title: Accessibility aids
text: Auric Artisan is built for accessibility work, and the site offers the same care to its own visitors. On every page you can: - make text larger or smaller in four steps; - switch to reading mode , a calm, narrow column of large text with the floating controls hidden; - boost contrast , reduce motion , reduce transparency and underline links ; - replace the custom cursor with your system pointer; - choose light, dark or system theme; - use the whole site from the keyboard, with shortcuts for the most common actions; - switch the interface to Hindi. Many of these respond to your device settings as well: the site follows your system's light or dark preference, and it turns off the custom cursor and animated effects when your device asks for reduced motion. For the site's formal accessibility commitment, see the Accessibility statement at https://auricartisan.com/company/accessibility/.

title: Get started with the accessibility aids
text: All of these apply to every page at once and are remembered in this browser.

title: Get started with the accessibility aids
heading: Make text larger
text: - Press Alt + + (one step larger) or Alt + - (one step smaller). Alt + 0 returns to the default. - Or open Settings › Appearance › Text size and choose Small (90%), Default , Large (112%) or X-Large (125%). This scales the site's text. Your browser's own zoom ( Ctrl + + ) also works and scales everything, including layout.

heading: Stronger contrast
text: Settings › Comfort › Boost contrast draws secondary text in the stronger text colour and makes borders darker, in both themes. You can also choose the theme that suits you in Appearance › Theme .

text: - Settings › Comfort › Reduce motion (or Alt + M ) makes animations and transitions finish instantly and turns smooth scrolling into jumps. - If your device's reduced-motion setting is on, the site also hides the custom cursor, stops the eye-rest horizon from animating, shortens the first-visit welcome, and swaps info-bar messages without fading.

title: Keyboard and screen readers
heading: Keyboard access
text: - Skip link. On every page, the first Tab reveals Skip to main content . Press Enter to jump past the header. - Menus. The header menus open with Enter , Space or the arrow keys and close with Esc , returning focus to their button. - Panels and dialogs. Settings, Spotlight, the guide, the right-click menu, the recorder and the kits all open and close from the keyboard. When a panel closes, focus returns to what you used to open it. - Focus stays inside modal dialogs such as the guide, a guided tour and the Settings reset confirmation, so Tab cannot wander behind them. - Shortcuts. The most common actions have shortcuts ( Ctrl + K search, Ctrl + , settings, ? guide, Alt + R reading mode and more). Letter shortcuts with Alt are ignored while you type in a field. See [Keyboard shortcuts](../../keyboard-shortcuts/README.md). - Tooltips appear when a control receives keyboard focus, not only on hover. - Date fields. Where the site shows its calendar for a date field, arrows move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Shift with them by year, Home and End to the start and end of the week, Enter or Space to choose, and Esc to close.

title: Keyboard and screen readers
heading: Screen reader support
text: - Buttons that show only an icon have a spoken name, such as "Open guide" or "Switch language between English and Hindi". - Panels and dialogs have names, for example "User settings", "Search" and "Page actions". - Confirmation messages ("Settings exported", "Page URL copied") are announced without moving focus. - The clock strip's time is not announced every second; its date, day and zone are announced only when they change. - In Hindi, the page is marked as Hindi so screen readers use a Hindi voice. - The language buttons are written in their own languages and are never translated, so you can always find yours. - The custom cursor and decorative effects are hidden from assistive technology.

title: Keyboard and screen readers
heading: Respecting your device settings
text: - Colour scheme: with the theme on System , the site follows your device's light or dark mode. - Reduced motion: the site turns off the custom cursor and animated effects when your device asks for less motion. - Pointer type: on touch screens the custom cursor is never shown.

title: Keyboard and screen readers
heading: Reporting a barrier
text: If something on the site is hard to use with your assistive technology, use the Report a bug form (see [Feedback](../../feedback/README.md)) or the contact details in the Accessibility statement at https://auricartisan.com/company/accessibility/.

title: Reading mode
text: Reading mode is a distraction-free layout with comfortable typography, for articles, documentation and other long pages.

title: Reading mode
heading: Turn it on or off
text: - Press Alt + R (not while typing in a field). - Or Settings › Comfort › Reading mode . - Or right-click the page, choose View , then Reading mode ( Leave reading mode when it is on). - Or, on card pages, right-click a card and select the Reading pill. To leave it, you can also select the Reading mode ✕ chip at the bottom centre of the screen. Reading mode stays on as you move between pages until you turn it off.

title: Reading mode
heading: What changes
text: Area In reading mode --- --- Text column Centred and limited to a comfortable line length (about 68 to 76 characters) Body text Larger, with generous line spacing Headings Clear sizes and spacing, kept to a readable width Links Underlined for scanning Images and media Kept within the column Header Scrolls away with the page instead of staying pinned Floating controls Kit launchers, the library launcher and the right-edge menu line are hidden Info bars and clock strip Hidden Pointer Your system pointer replaces the custom cursor Decorative animation Stopped Progress A thin bar across the top of the window fills as you scroll Exit Reading mode ✕ chip at the bottom of the screen

title: Reading mode
heading: What does not change
text: Tools keep working normally. The Settings panel, Spotlight ( Ctrl + K ), the guide ( ? ) and the right-click menu remain available.

title: Troubleshooting the accessibility aids
heading: The Alt shortcuts do not work
text: Why: they are ignored while you type in a field, and when Ctrl or Cmd is also held. On some keyboards, Alt + + needs Shift as well; Alt + = also works. What to do: click an empty part of the page first, or use the Settings panel.

title: Troubleshooting the accessibility aids
heading: Text size did not change everywhere
text: Why: the text size setting scales the site's text. Some tools draw text inside images or canvases, which it cannot resize. What to do: use your browser's zoom ( Ctrl + + ) for those.

title: Troubleshooting the accessibility aids
heading: Something still moves with Reduce motion on
text: Why: Reduce motion stops animations and transitions defined by the site's styles. A tool that animates a canvas as its purpose (for example a live simulation) may keep doing so. What to do: turn on your device's reduced-motion setting as well, which the site also follows.

title: Troubleshooting the accessibility aids
heading: My screen reader announces too much or too little
text: What to do: report it with Report a bug (see [Feedback](../../feedback/README.md)), naming the page, your screen reader and browser.

title: Troubleshooting the accessibility aids
heading: Reading mode did not change a page much
text: Why: reading mode is designed for text pages. On a tool page it hides floating controls and adjusts text, but the tool's own layout stays.

title: Accessibility aids FAQ
heading: Do I need an account to use these aids?
text: No. All of them work signed out and are kept in your browser.

title: Accessibility aids FAQ
heading: Can I carry my setup to another computer?
text: Yes. Use Export in the Settings panel, then Import on the other computer.

title: Accessibility aids FAQ
heading: Is there a dyslexia-friendly font?
text: The site does not offer a font switch. Reading mode, larger text and underlined links can make long text easier to read.

title: Accessibility aids FAQ
heading: Where is the site's accessibility statement?
text: At https://auricartisan.com/company/accessibility/, also reachable from the Company menu and the footer.

title: Accessibility aids FAQ
heading: Are the colour tools themselves accessible?
text: The tools have their own documentation, which describes their keyboard and screen reader support where it differs from the site's.

They are not sent to Auric Artisan or attached to an account. - The site reads your device's colour-scheme and reduced-motion preferences only to adjust the page; it does not record them. - A page link you copy can carry appearance settings that differ from the defaults, such as text size (see [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md)).

title: Right-click menu
text: When you right-click a page on auricartisan.com, the site opens its own menu instead of your browser's. It is built around what you clicked: the top of the menu names the thing under your pointer (the page, a link, an image, a selection of text or a colour) and its own actions come first. Everything else is grouped into a few rows that open submenus, so the whole menu fits on one screen. A quick bar of one-click buttons sits across the top. It starts with Back, Forward, Reload, Home and Copy URL, and you can pin any action to it with the star on that action's row. A filter field lets you type part of an action's name to find it anywhere in the menu, submenus included. A gear button opens the menu's own preferences: a longer "Everything" layout, a compact row height, or handing right-click back to your browser for good. Your browser's menu is always one keystroke away: hold Shift while you right-click.

title: Right-click menu
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone who wants quick actions on the thing they are looking at: copy a colour as HEX, RGB, HSL or OKLCH; copy a link as Markdown; copy an image's palette; search the web for a selection. - Keyboard users: the menu can be driven entirely from the keyboard and searched by typing. - People who prefer their browser's menu: one setting makes the browser's menu the default.

title: Right-click menu
heading: Where to find it
text: On any page of https://auricartisan.com: - right-click anywhere that is not a text field; - or rest your pointer on the thin gold line at the middle of the right edge of the window for a moment; - or press the menu key on your keyboard ( Shift + F10 on many keyboards), which your browser treats as a right-click.

title: Right-click menu
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Right-click an empty part of any page. The heading shows Page and the page's title. 2. Select Copy URL in the quick bar. A message confirms "Page URL copied". 3. Select some text on the page and right-click on it. The heading now reads Selection with a word and character count. 4. Choose Search the web , then DuckDuckGo . A new tab opens with your selection searched. 5. Right-click again and start typing dark . The list filters to Switch theme . Press Enter to run it. 6. Right-click again, find Split view under View , and select the star on its row. Split view now appears in the quick bar. 7. To use your browser's menu once, hold Shift and right-click.

title: Right-click menu
heading: What you can do
text: - Copy the page URL, title or a Markdown link; share or print the page; open the URL Analyzer on it. - Copy, search, translate or read aloud selected text. - Open, copy or share links, including as Markdown. - Open, copy, save and extract the palette of images. - Copy any colour on the site in four formats and send it to the colour tools. - Reach View actions (scroll, reading mode, split view, full screen, theme) and Site actions (home, search, settings, shortcuts, website update). - Pin up to six actions to the quick bar. - Choose a Focused or Everything layout and a Standard or Compact row height. - Make the browser's own menu the default.

title: Get started with the right-click menu
Get started with the right-click menu
heading: Open the menu
text: - Right-click anywhere on a page, except inside a text field, a drop-down or an editable area. Those keep your browser's menu so that spelling suggestions, paste and similar options still work. - Hover the right edge. A short, thin gold line sits halfway down the right edge of the window. Rest your pointer on it for a moment and the menu opens beside it, showing the actions for the page. Move away and it closes. - Keyboard. The menu key, or Shift + F10 on many keyboards, sends a right-click to the page and opens the same menu. To get your browser's menu instead, hold Shift while you right-click.

title: Get started with the right-click menu
heading: The parts of the menu
text: From top to bottom: 1. Header. An icon and two lines that describe what you clicked: - the kind ( Page , Link , Image , Selection or Colour ) and a detail, such as the page address, "This site" or "Another site" for a link, the pixel size and file type of an image, the word and character count of a selection, or the RGB value of a colour; - a label: the page title, the link address, the image file name, the quoted selection, or the colour's hex code. For a colour, the icon is a swatch of that colour. 2. Quick bar. A row of one-click buttons, each with an icon and a short label. By default: Back , Forward , Reload , Home and Copy URL . Hover a button to see its full name and shortcut. 3. Filter field. It reads "Type to filter N actions", where N is the number of actions available for what you clicked. It has keyboard focus as soon as the menu opens. 4. Website update banner (only sometimes). When a newer version of the site is ready, a highlighted row such as Update available appears here. 5. The list. - First, the actions for what you clicked, under This page for a page (the group heading is hidden in the default layout). - Then More : one row per group — Page (not shown when you clicked the page itself, whose actions are already listed), Colour tools , View and Site . Each row shows how many actions it holds. Hover it, or press the Right arrow, to open its submenu. - Last, Browser’s own menu . 6. Footer. Hints for the keys ( ↑↓ move, ↵ run, → submenu, the star to pin) and the gear button, Customise this menu . After an action such as pinning, the hints briefly give way to a confirmation. Every action row has a star at its right-hand end. Select it to pin that action to the quick bar.

title: Get started with the right-click menu
heading: Try it
text: 1. Right-click an empty part of the homepage. The header reads Page with the page's address and title. 2. Hover View under More . The View submenu opens to the side. 3. Select Scroll to bottom . The menu closes and the page scrolls to the end. 4. Right-click a link in the footer, such as Privacy . The header reads Link · This site with the link's address. 5. Select Copy as Markdown . A message confirms "Markdown link copied". Paste it into a document: it reads [Privacy](https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/) .

title: Get started with the right-click menu
heading: Close the menu
text: The menu closes when you run an action, press Esc , click anywhere outside it, scroll the page, resize the window or switch to another window. Scrolling inside the menu does not close it.

title: Get started with the right-click menu
heading: Next steps
text: - [Actions for what you clicked](actions-for-what-you-clicked.md) - [Quick bar and pinning](quick-bar-and-pinning.md) - [Menu preferences](menu-preferences.md)

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: How the menu decides what you clicked
text: The menu checks, in this order, and uses the first that fits: 1. Colour — you right-clicked a colour: a selected hex code (such as d3af37 , or six hex characters that include at least one digit), a swatch or chip that carries a colour, or a short piece of text that is a hex code starting with . 2. Selection — you right-clicked on text you have selected. A selection made earlier elsewhere on the page does not count unless your click lands on it. 3. Image — you right-clicked an image. 4. Link — you right-clicked a link. 5. Page — anything else. Plain words that happen to be valid hex, such as "decade" or "facade", are not treated as colours.

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Page
text: The actions for a page appear first when you right-click an empty area. For the other kinds, the same actions are in the Page row under More . Action Short label What it does --- --- --- Copy page URL Copy URL Copies the page's full address. Message: "Page URL copied". Copy page title Title Copies the page title. Message: "Page title copied". Copy as Markdown link Markdown Copies [Page title](address) . Message: "Markdown link copied". Share page… Share Opens your device's share sheet. Without one, copies the address ("Link copied"). Print… — Opens your browser's print dialog ( Ctrl + P ). Analyze this page Analyze Opens the URL Analyzer panel with this page's address, ready to audit. Some pages add actions of their own at the top of this list, and some remove actions that do not apply. For example, a published portfolio page shows fewer site actions.

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Link
text: Action What it does --- --- Open in new tab Opens the link in a new tab (same as Ctrl + click) Open in new window Opens the link in a new window (same as Shift + click) Copy link address Copies the link's full address ("Link address copied") Copy link text Copies the visible text of the link (shown only when the link has text) Copy as Markdown Copies [link text](address) ("Markdown link copied") Share link… Shares the link through your device's share sheet, or copies it The header says This site for a link on auricartisan.com and Another site for an external link.

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Image
text: Action What it does --- --- Open image in new tab Opens the image file on its own Copy image Copies the picture itself as a PNG, or its address when the browser does not allow that (see below) Copy image address Copies the image's address Copy alt text Copies the image's text alternative, shown beside the action. Greyed out with "None" when the image has none. Copy its palette Copies up to four main colours of the image as HEX codes, separated by commas. Four small swatches preview them. Save image Downloads the image under its own file name Copy its palette appears only when the browser allows the site to read the image's pixels, which is true for images on auricartisan.com and for images from sites that permit it. When Copy image cannot copy the picture, it copies the address and shows "Image address copied (the image itself can’t be copied)". If the image is inside a link, two more actions follow: Open link in new tab and Copy link address .

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Selection
text: Action What it does --- --- Copy Copies the selected text ( Ctrl + C ) Copy as plain text Copies the selection with all line breaks and extra spaces collapsed to single spaces Search this site Opens the site's search page in a new tab with your selection as the query Search the web A submenu: Google , Bing , DuckDuckGo , Wikipedia , YouTube . Each opens a new tab. Translate Opens Google Translate in a new tab, translating the selection into the page's language Read aloud / Stop reading Reads the selection with your device's speech voice; selecting it again while speaking stops it Share… Shares the page with the selection as its text Read aloud appears only if your browser offers speech. If speech fails, the message reads "Reading aloud is not available".

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Colour
text: The header shows a swatch of the colour, its RGB value and its hex code. Action Example of what is copied --- --- Copy HEX D3AF37 Copy RGB rgb(211 175 55) Copy HSL hsl(46 64% 52%) Copy OKLCH oklch(76.6% 0.138 91.6) Check its contrast Opens the contrast tool with this colour Build harmonies Opens the harmony tool with this colour Find its name Opens the colour-name tool with this colour Inspect in Colour Tools Opens the colour inspector with this colour Each copy row shows the value it will copy, in a fixed-width font. The examples are the values for the site's gold, D3AF37 ; the menu computes them for the colour you clicked. OKLCH is a way of writing colour as lightness, chroma (colourfulness) and hue that matches how people perceive colour more closely than HSL.

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: The groups under More
text: Shown on pages where the site's colour tools are available. - All colour tools… (short label Colour tools , Ctrl + Shift + C ) opens the colour tools menu at the spot you clicked. - Contrast System , Accessibility Lab , Harmony Studio , Color Space Converter , Color Name Finder , Gradient Library , Color Library open that tool as a floating panel. If you right-clicked a colour, the tool opens with that colour already loaded. If the tools cannot open on the page, you are taken to the Basic Tools page instead. Action What it does --- --- Scroll to top Scrolls to the top of the page ( Home ) Scroll to bottom Scrolls to the end of the page ( End ) Reading mode / Leave reading mode Turns reading mode on or off ( Alt + R ) Split view Opens or closes split view ( Ctrl + Shift + D ) Full screen / Exit full screen Enters or leaves full screen ( F11 ) Switch theme Toggles light and dark. The row shows the current theme, Light or Dark . Action What it does --- --- Home Goes to the homepage Search the site Opens Spotlight search ( Ctrl + K ), or the search page if Spotlight is not available Settings Opens the Settings panel Keyboard shortcuts Opens the Settings panel on its Shortcuts section Update website Checks for a newer version of the site and applies it ( Ctrl + Shift + U ) The Update website row changes with the update state: Update available with a version number and "Ready", Updating website while it runs, and Retry update after an error. A message reads "Checking for updates…" when you start it. The update itself is handled by the Update Kit (see [Kits](../../../kits/README.md)). Back ( Alt + Left ), Forward ( Alt + Right ) and Reload page ( F5 ) do not have a group of their own. They are in the default quick bar and can be found with the filter. The last row, Browser’s own menu ( Shift + right-click), closes the site menu and shows the message "Right-click again for the browser’s menu". Your next right-click opens the browser's menu; the one after that opens the site menu again.

title: Actions for what you clicked
heading: Actions that depend on the page
text: Some rows appear only where the page supports them. Settings , Keyboard shortcuts and Reading mode need the Settings panel; the Colour tools group needs the colour tools; Switch theme needs a theme control. Pages that do not load these, such as published portfolios, show a shorter menu.

title: Filter and keyboard
heading: Find an action by typing
text: The filter field below the quick bar has keyboard focus as soon as the menu opens, so you can start typing straight away. 1. Right-click the page. 2. Type part of an action's name, for example mark . 3. The list is replaced by matching actions from every group, submenus included, each tagged with the group it belongs to (for example Page or Link ). The field shows how many matched, for example "2 of 27". 4. The first match is highlighted. Press Enter to run it, or use the arrow keys to choose another. How matches are found: - The filter matches the action's name, the name of its group, and a few extra words for some actions. For example, dark or light finds Switch theme , audit or seo finds Analyze this page , and colors finds Copy its palette . - Names that start with what you typed are listed first, then names that contain it, then matches on the extra words. - Up to 12 results are shown. - If nothing matches, the list reads "No actions match" followed by your text. Typing works from anywhere in the menu: if a row has focus and you type a letter, it goes into the filter. Press Esc once to clear the filter.

title: Filter and keyboard
heading: Keyboard reference
text: Keys What they do --- --- Letters and digits Type into the filter Down from the filter Move to the highlighted result or the first action Up / Down Move between rows and quick-bar buttons; the list wraps round Up from a quick-bar button Return to the filter field Right on a group row Open its submenu and move into it Right on an action row Move to that row's pin star Left on a pin star Move back to its row Left or Esc in a submenu Close the submenu and return to its group row Enter or Space Run the focused action, open a focused group, or toggle a focused star Enter in the filter Run the highlighted result Esc Close a submenu; otherwise clear the filter; otherwise close the menu Esc in the preferences view Return to the action list When the menu closes, keyboard focus goes back to where it was before you opened it.

title: Filter and keyboard
heading: Mouse behaviour
text: - Hovering a group row opens its submenu after a short pause. Moving to another row closes it. - Submenus open to the right of the menu, or to the left when there is no room. - Selecting a group row also opens its submenu.

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
text: The gear button at the bottom right of the menu, Customise this menu , replaces the action list with the menu's preferences. Every change is saved as soon as you make it; the footer confirms "Saved". Select Done , the gear again, or press Esc to return to the actions. Typing in the filter field also returns to the actions.

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: Quick bar
text: Shows your pinned actions as chips, each with an X to unpin it, and a Reset chip that restores the default five. See [Quick bar and pinning](quick-bar-and-pinning.md).

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: Layout
text: Option Description on screen What it looks like --- --- --- Focused (default) What you clicked, then one row per group Your context's actions, then a More section with one row per group that opens a submenu Everything Every group open in one list Every group's actions listed in full, each under its own heading, with no submenus Choose Everything if you prefer to see all actions at once and do not mind a longer menu.

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: Row height
text: Option Effect --- --- Standard (default) Comfortable rows, easier to hit with a pointer or a finger Compact Shorter rows, so more actions fit in the same space

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: Right-click on this site
text: This choice decides which menu a plain right-click opens. Option Description on screen --- --- This menu (default) Hold Shift for the browser’s menu The browser’s menu Hold Shift for this one 1. Right-click the page and select the gear. 2. Under Right-click on this site , select The browser’s menu . 3. The footer confirms "Right-click now opens the browser’s menu". From now on a plain right-click opens your browser's menu everywhere on the site. To reach the site menu, hold Shift while you right-click. You can also rest your pointer on the thin line at the right edge of the window. 1. Hold Shift and right-click the page. The site menu opens. 2. Select the gear, then This menu under Right-click on this site .

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: One-off use of the browser's menu
text: Without changing any preference: - hold Shift while you right-click; or - choose Browser’s own menu at the foot of the site menu, then right-click again. Right-clicking in a text field, drop-down or editable area always opens the browser's menu.

title: Menu preferences and turning it off
heading: Where preferences are kept
text: Your layout, row height, right-click choice and quick-bar pins are kept in this browser and apply on every page of the site. They are not part of the Settings panel's export file.

title: Other right-click menus on the site
text: A few parts of the site have a small right-click menu of their own, with actions for that one thing. Right-clicking them opens that menu instead of the main one. They share a look: a heading, labelled groups of buttons, and sometimes a Reset button and an All settings link. All of these close with Esc , a click elsewhere, a scroll or a window resize.

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Clock strip
text: Right-click the clock strip at the top of a page (when it is switched on) to open Clock settings : a live preview, Format ( 12h , 24h ), Date ( Long , D/M/Y , M/D/Y , ISO ), Show switches ( Seconds , Weekday , Zone ), a searchable Time zone list, Reset and All settings → . Details are in [Info bars and notices › Clock strip](../../info-bars-and-notices/docs/clock-strip.md).

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Info bars
text: Right-click the welcome, announcement or quick-links bar to open a menu headed with the bar's name ("Welcome messages", "Site announcements" or "Site tools"). Under This bar : Button What it does --- --- Open Goes to the link you right-clicked, or the bar's first link Copy link Copies that link's address Hide bar Hides this bar everywhere (same as its ✕) Settings Opens the Settings panel on the Comfort section

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Cards on browsing pages
text: On pages with a grid of cards (the homepage, Collections, Blog, Changelog, Documentation and Learn), right-clicking a card opens a Card settings menu headed with the card's title: - Card : Pin (or Unpin ), Open , New tab , Copy link ; - View : Grid or List ; - Density : Cozy or Compact ; - Columns : Auto , 2 , 3 or 4 ; - Sort : the sort orders the page offers; - System : Theme and Reading switches; - Reset and All settings → . This menu is part of the card libraries and is described fully in [Collections › Card menu](../../../library/collections/docs/card-menu.md).

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Footer contact card
text: Right-click the "Start a conversation" card in the footer to open a menu headed Start a conversation . Under Contact : Button What it does --- --- Email us Opens your email app with a message to the studio address Copy email Copies the email address (the button briefly reads "Copied") Copy link Copies the address of the page you are on LEACB Opens the studio's portfolio site in a new tab

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Inside the Settings panel
text: Right-clicking inside the Settings panel opens a menu with Turn on or Turn off for the switch you clicked, and Export , Import , Reset section and Reset all . See [Settings panel › Back up, restore and reset](../../settings-panel/docs/back-up-restore-and-reset.md use-the-panels-right-click-menu).

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Inside the Library Kit
text: The Library Kit's panel has its own right-click menu for your saved items. See [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Other right-click menus on the site
heading: Places that keep the browser's menu
text: The main menu never opens, and your browser's menu appears instead, in: - text fields, text areas, drop-down lists and other editable areas; - the accessibility checklist's evidence drawing tool; - any spot a page has marked as needing the browser's own menu.

title: Quick bar and pinning
text: The quick bar is the row of one-click buttons across the top of the right-click menu. Each button shows an icon and a short label; hover it to see the full action name and its shortcut. By default it holds five actions: Back , Forward , Reload , Home and Copy URL .

title: Quick bar and pinning
heading: Pin an action
text: 1. Right-click the page and find the action you use most, for example Split view under View , or Copy HEX on a colour. 2. Select the star at the right-hand end of its row ( Pin to the quick bar ). 3. The star fills, the footer confirms "Pinned to the quick bar", and the action appears at the end of the quick bar. With the keyboard: move to the action's row, press the Right arrow to move onto its star, and press Enter or Space .

title: Quick bar and pinning
heading: Unpin an action
text: - Select the filled star on the action's row ( Unpin from the quick bar ). The footer confirms "Unpinned from the quick bar". - Or open the gear ( Customise this menu ) and select the X on the action's chip under Quick bar .

title: Quick bar and pinning
heading: Limits
text: - The quick bar holds six actions. With six pinned, selecting another star shows "The quick bar holds 6: unpin one first". - Group rows (Page, Colour tools, View, Site), greyed-out actions and Browser’s own menu have no star and cannot be pinned.

title: Quick bar and pinning
heading: Why a pinned action is sometimes missing
text: The quick bar shows only pinned actions that make sense for what you clicked. Copy HEX appears only when you right-click a colour, Open in new tab only on a link, Copy only on a selection, and so on. The pin is kept; the button returns the next time the action applies. Actions that belong to every page, such as Copy URL , Split view or Settings , always appear.

title: Quick bar and pinning
heading: Reset the quick bar
text: 1. Right-click the page and select the gear ( Customise this menu ) at the bottom right. 2. Under Quick bar , select Reset . 3. The bar returns to Back , Forward , Reload , Home and Copy URL , and the footer confirms "Quick bar reset". When nothing is pinned, the Quick bar area of the preferences reads "Empty: pin actions with the star", and the bar itself is hidden from the menu. Your pins are kept in this browser and apply on every page.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: I get my browser's menu instead of the site menu
text: Possible causes and fixes: - You right-clicked inside a text field, drop-down or editable area. These always keep the browser's menu. Right-click outside the field. - You held Shift . Right-click again without it. - You chose Browser’s own menu on your previous right-click. That lasts for one right-click only; try again. - You set Right-click on this site to The browser’s menu . Hold Shift and right-click to reach the site menu, then change it back under the gear. - The page has only just loaded. The menu arrives a moment after the page; wait and try again. - You right-clicked something with its own menu, such as the clock strip or a card. See [Other right-click menus](other-right-click-menus.md).

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: I cannot get my browser's menu
text: Hold Shift while you right-click. If you often need it, make it the default under the gear ( Right-click on this site › The browser’s menu ).

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: A copy action says "Could not copy"
text: Why: the browser blocked access to the clipboard. This can happen in some embedded views, when the page is not in focus, or when a browser setting blocks clipboard access. What to do: click the page once so it has focus and try again, or select the text and use Ctrl + C .

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: Copy image copies the address instead of the picture
text: Why: some browsers do not let web pages put images on the clipboard, and images from other websites often cannot be read by the page. What to do: use Open image in new tab and copy it from there, or Save image .

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: Copy its palette is missing
text: Why: the browser does not allow the page to read that image's pixels (usually an image from another website), or the image has not finished loading. What to do: wait for the image to load and right-click again. For images from elsewhere, save the image and use the site's Image Picker tool.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: The Colour tools group is missing
text: Why: the colour tools are not loaded on this page, for example on a published portfolio. What to do: open a tool page such as Basic Tools, or use Ctrl + Shift + C where the tools are available.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: Right-clicking a word gave me a colour
text: Why: the word is also a valid hex code and contains a digit (for example a1b2c3 ), or the element you clicked carries a colour. What to do: use the Page row under More for the page actions, or select the text and choose from the Selection actions if you right-click on the selection.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: A pinned action does not show in the quick bar
text: Why: the action only applies to certain things, such as a colour or a link. It appears when you right-click one.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: The menu closed while I was using it
text: Why: scrolling the page, resizing the window, switching windows or clicking outside the menu closes it. What to do: keep the pointer inside the menu while scrolling its list.

title: Troubleshooting the right-click menu
heading: Read aloud does nothing
text: Why: your device has no speech voice for the page's language, or speech is turned off in the browser. What to do: check your operating system's text-to-speech settings. If speech fails, the menu shows "Reading aloud is not available".

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Can I turn the site menu off?
text: Yes. Right-click, select the gear, and under Right-click on this site choose The browser’s menu . The site menu is then available only with Shift + right-click or from the line at the right edge of the window.

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Does the menu work on phones and tablets?
text: A long press on a touch screen is handled by the browser and usually opens the browser's own menu or text selection. The site menu is designed for a mouse, trackpad or keyboard.

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Where do Search the web and Translate send my text?
text: Only where you ask. Search the web opens the search engine you pick in a new tab with the selected text in the address. Translate opens Google Translate in a new tab. Nothing is sent until you choose one of them.

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Is my quick bar the same in every browser?
text: No. Pins and preferences are kept in the browser you set them in.

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Why does the same menu look shorter on some pages?
text: Some rows depend on what the page loads. Published portfolio pages, for example, have no colour tools and remove some site actions, so their menu is shorter.

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Is the browser extension's menu the same thing?
text: No. The Auric Artisan browser extension has its own right-click menu for other websites. On auricartisan.com the extension steps aside and the site's own menu is the one you see. See [Browser extension](../../../../browser-extension/README.md).

title: Right-click menu FAQ
heading: Can I see the colour formats before copying?
text: Yes. Each colour copy row shows the exact value it will copy.

title: Right-click menu glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Context The thing you right-clicked: a page, link, image, selection or colour. Context menu A menu that opens on right-click and offers actions for what is under the pointer. Quick bar The row of one-click buttons at the top of the menu. Holds up to six pinned actions. Pin To add an action to the quick bar with the star on its row. Group A set of related actions (Page, Colour tools, View, Site) shown as one row that opens a submenu. Submenu The small panel that opens beside a group row, listing that group's actions. Filter The field that narrows the menu to actions whose names match what you type. Focused layout The default layout: your context's actions, then one row per group. Everything layout A layout that lists every group's actions in full, with no submenus. Markdown link Text written as [label](address) , which many editors turn into a link. HEX, RGB, HSL Common ways of writing a colour: a hex code, red-green-blue values, or hue-saturation-lightness. OKLCH A way of writing colour as lightness, chroma and hue that follows human perception closely. Alt text The text alternative of an image, read by screen readers and shown when the image cannot load. Share sheet Your device's own panel for sending a link to an app or contact.

title: Right-click menu privacy
heading: Stored in your browser
text: - Your quick-bar pins, layout, row height and right-click choice, in local storage for auricartisan.com. - Nothing about what you right-click or copy is stored or sent.

title: Right-click menu privacy
heading: Actions that leave the site
text: These open another website in a new tab and pass it the text you chose: - Search the web › Google , Bing , DuckDuckGo , Wikipedia or YouTube — sends the selected text as the search query. - Translate — sends the selected text to Google Translate. - Open in new tab , Open in new window and Open image in new tab — open the address you right-clicked.

title: Right-click menu privacy
heading: Actions that stay on your device
text: - The copy actions put text or an image on your clipboard. - Read aloud uses your device's own speech voice. - Share… hands the link to your device's share sheet; what happens next depends on the app you pick. - Copy its palette reads the image's colours inside your browser.

title: Right-click menu privacy
heading: Actions that use the site
text: - Search this site opens the site's search page. - Analyze this page opens the URL Analyzer with the address of the page you are on, ready to audit it. - Update website checks the site for a newer version.

title: Cookie consent and privacy choices
text: On your first visit, after the short welcome animation, a bar appears at the bottom of the page: We value your privacy . It explains that Auric Artisan uses cookies and local storage to keep the site secure, remember your preferences and understand basic, anonymous usage, and it offers three choices: Accept All , Reject All and Customise . The page stays readable and usable while the bar is showing. Your choice covers four categories: Essential (always on), Functional , Analytics and Marketing . You can change it at any time on the Cookie Policy page, which lists every cookie in each category with its purpose and how long it lasts, and where you can also clear the site's non-essential cookies or withdraw your consent.

title: Cookie consent and privacy choices
heading: Who it is for
text: Every visitor. The choice decides whether the site may measure how pages are used, and which optional cookies it may set.

title: Cookie consent and privacy choices
heading: Where to find it
text: - The consent bar on your first visit. - The Cookie Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/, section Manage Cookie Preferences . - The Cookies link in the footer.

title: Cookie consent and privacy choices
heading: Quick start
text: 1. On your first visit, read the bar at the bottom of the page. 2. Select Customise . The Cookie Policy page opens at Manage Cookie Preferences . 3. Switch Analytics Cookies on or off as you prefer. Essential Cookies are always on. 4. Select Save Preferences . A message confirms "Cookie preferences saved successfully." 5. The section now shows Consent recorded with the date and time.

title: Cookie consent and privacy choices
heading: What you can do
text: - Accept all optional cookies, reject them, or choose by category. - See every cookie the site lists, with its purpose, duration and type. - Change your choice at any time. - Clear all non-essential cookies, or withdraw your consent.

title: Get started with cookie consent
heading: When the bar appears
text: The consent bar appears at the bottom of the page on your first visit, once the short welcome animation has finished. It stays until you choose. It does not dim or block the page, so you can read the page before deciding. It does not appear on the sign-in and verification pages, and it does not appear again once you have made a choice in this browser.

title: Get started with cookie consent
heading: What it says
text: We value your privacy The bar explains that Auric Artisan uses cookies and local storage to keep the platform secure, remember your preferences (theme, accent colour, language and tool settings) and understand basic, anonymous usage. Essential cookies are always on; analytics and other optional cookies run only with your consent, and your data is never sold. It links to the full Cookie Policy .

title: Get started with cookie consent
heading: The three buttons
text: Button What it does --- --- Accept All Turns on every category: Essential, Functional, Analytics and Marketing Reject All Keeps only Essential, turns the others off, and deletes the site's non-essential cookies Customise Opens the Cookie Policy page at Manage Cookie Preferences , where you choose each category After Accept All or Reject All , the bar slides away and your choice is recorded with the date and time. Note: The bar says you can change your choice "from Settings". The cookie controls are on the Cookie Policy page, not in the Settings panel. See [Manage your cookie preferences](manage-cookie-preferences.md).

title: Get started with cookie consent
heading: What your choice affects
text: - Analytics: with Analytics on, the site may record anonymous usage events, such as which pages and features are used. With it off, no usage events are recorded. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md) for details, including Do Not Track. - Functional: covers remembering preferences such as theme, language and layout. - Marketing: reserved for campaign attribution if the site enables it later. The policy states that Auric Artisan does not currently use marketing pixels or cross-site advertising profiles. - Essential: signing in, security and remembering your consent choice. Always on.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
text: All cookie controls are in the Manage Cookie Preferences section of the Cookie Policy page.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
heading: Open the preferences
text: - Select Customise on the consent bar; or - open https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/ cookies-preferences; or - select Cookies in the footer, then Manage Cookie Preferences in the page's section rail. The section opens and scrolls into view.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
heading: Choose by category
text: Each category is a card with a title, a count of listed cookies, a description and a switch: - Essential Cookies — marked Always Active ; the switch cannot be turned off. - Functional Cookies - Analytics Cookies - Marketing Cookies Select Show cookies under a card to see a table of that category's cookies (Cookie, Purpose, Duration, Type), and Hide cookies to fold it away. To save a choice: 1. Turn the switches on or off. 2. Select Save Preferences . Result: "Cookie preferences saved successfully." Cookies from any category you switched off are deleted, and the Consent recorded line shows the new date and time. Important: Accept All and Reject All on this page only set the switches. Select Save Preferences afterwards to apply them. If you have never made a choice, the switches start with Functional on and Analytics and Marketing off.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
heading: Clear all non-essential cookies
text: Select Clear All Cookies . The site deletes its non-essential cookies, forgets your consent choice and turns off the optional switches: "All non-essential cookies have been cleared." The consent bar will appear again on your next page.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
heading: Withdraw consent
text: Once you have made a choice, a Consent recorded line appears with the date, beside Withdraw Consent . Select it to forget your choice and delete non-essential cookies: "Cookie consent withdrawn. Preferences reset." The consent bar appears again on your next page, so you can choose afresh.

title: Manage your cookie preferences
heading: Where your choice applies
text: Your choice is kept in this browser. Another browser or device asks again. Clearing your browser's data for auricartisan.com also removes it.

title: Troubleshooting cookie consent
heading: The consent bar keeps coming back
text: Why: your choice is kept in this browser's storage. It is lost if the browser clears site data on exit, if you use a private window, or if storage is blocked for the site. What to do: allow auricartisan.com to keep site data, or accept that a private window asks each time.

title: Troubleshooting cookie consent
heading: I cannot find the cookie settings in the Settings panel
text: Why: the consent bar mentions Settings, but the controls are on the Cookie Policy page. What to do: open https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/ cookies-preferences.

title: Troubleshooting cookie consent
heading: I pressed Accept All or Reject All on the Cookie Policy page and nothing changed
text: Why: on that page, those buttons only set the switches. What to do: select Save Preferences .

title: Troubleshooting cookie consent
heading: My settings survived Reject All
text: Why: your preferences (theme, accent, language and the Settings panel's choices) are kept in your browser's local storage so that the features you use keep working. Rejecting optional cookies does not reset them. What to do: use Reset all in the Settings panel, or clear the site's data in your browser, to remove them.

title: Troubleshooting cookie consent
heading: The bar does not appear on the sign-in page
text: Why: the notice is not shown over sign-in and verification pages. It appears on the next ordinary page.

title: Cookie consent FAQ
heading: Does the site sell my data?
text: The consent notice states that your data is never sold. The full terms are in the Privacy Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/.

title: Cookie consent FAQ
heading: Are the cookies third-party?
text: All cookies listed on the Cookie Policy page are first-party (set by auricartisan.com).
