title: Cookie consent glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Cookie A small piece of data a website stores in your browser and receives back on later visits. Local storage Browser storage that a website's pages can read, but which is not sent to the website automatically. First-party Set by the website you are visiting (here, auricartisan.com), not by another company. Consent Your recorded choice about which optional categories the site may use. Essential Needed for the site to work securely; cannot be turned off. Functional Remembers your preferences. Analytics Measures how the site is used, in aggregate or pseudonymously. Marketing Campaign attribution and advertising measurement; not currently used. Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control Browser settings that ask websites not to track you. Pseudonymous Linked to a random identifier rather than to your name or account.

title: What the site measures
heading: With Analytics consent
text: The site's own, first-party analytics may record usage events: the name of an event (such as a feature being used), the page's path, and a few small details. It does not record what you type into fields, email addresses, or the query part of addresses. No third-party analytics scripts are used for this. With the same consent, the site also measures whether a visit behaves like a person rather than an automated script, from how pointer and keyboard input vary during the visit. It does not record what you clicked, what you typed, where you came from or who you are.

title: What the site measures
heading: Without Analytics consent
text: - No usage events are recorded. - The site still counts that a page was viewed: the page's path and the site's host name, with nothing about how you used the page and no identifier stored on your device.

title: What the site measures
heading: Browser privacy signals
text: If your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control , the site's analytics stays off and page views are not counted at all, whatever your cookie choice.

title: What the site measures
heading: Your preferences
text: Settings you choose (theme, language, accent colour, comfort options and similar) are kept in your browser's local storage so that the features work. They are not sent to Auric Artisan. The full, binding descriptions are in the Privacy Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/ and the Cookie Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/.

title: Custom cursor
text: On a computer with a mouse or trackpad, Auric Artisan replaces your system pointer with its own: a thin ring that follows your pointer smoothly, and a small dot at the exact point you are aiming. The ring changes shape to tell you what the thing under it does: it grows over links and buttons, becomes an I-beam over text, a double arrow over a resize handle, a crosshair over precise controls, and so on. The ring also picks its colour from what is under it. It keeps the hue of the surface but pushes its lightness away from it, so the ring stays visible on a dark photo, a light page or a colourful canvas. Over grey or neutral surfaces it uses your accent colour. The custom cursor is on by default and can be turned off at any time in Settings. It is never shown on touch screens, on devices without a hovering pointer, or when your device asks for reduced motion.

title: Custom cursor
heading: Who it is for
text: Mouse and trackpad users. If you prefer your system pointer, for example because you use a large or high-contrast system cursor, turn the custom cursor off.

title: Custom cursor
heading: Where to find it
text: Settings ( Ctrl + , ) › Comfort › Custom cursor .

title: Custom cursor
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Move your mouse over a page. The ring and dot follow it. 2. Point at a link. The ring grows slightly. 3. Point at a paragraph of text. The ring becomes a tall, narrow I-beam. 4. Press Ctrl + , , select Comfort , and switch off Custom cursor . Your system pointer returns at once. 5. Switch it back on to see the ring again.

title: Custom cursor
heading: What you can do
text: - Turn the custom cursor on or off instantly. - Read what a control does from the cursor's shape.

title: Get started with the custom cursor
Get started with the custom cursor
heading: The two parts
text: - The dot is where you are pointing. Clicks happen at the dot. - The ring trails slightly behind and changes shape to show what the element under it does.

title: Get started with the custom cursor
heading: How it reacts
text: - Hover: over links, buttons and other clickable things, the ring grows and softly glows (the "magnetic" look). Over text it becomes an I-beam. - Click: the ring shrinks briefly. - Fast movement: the ring stretches in the direction you move. - Rest: when you stop moving for a moment, or the pointer leaves the window, the ring fades to half strength. - Loading: while a page or tool is busy, the ring turns dashed and spins. - Colour: the ring's colour follows the surface under it, and the dot switches between dark and light so it is always visible. The full list of shapes is in the [Reference](reference.md).

title: Get started with the custom cursor
heading: When the custom cursor is not shown
text: Your system pointer is used instead when: - you switched off Custom cursor in Settings › Comfort; - your device uses touch, or has no pointer that can hover (such as most phones and tablets); - your device's reduced-motion setting is on; - reading mode is on. When the custom cursor is off, the site still shows the right system pointer: a hand over links and buttons, an I-beam over text fields, and a left-right arrow over sliders.

title: Get started with the custom cursor
heading: Turn it off or on
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , and select Comfort . 2. Switch Custom cursor ("The ring and dot that follow your pointer. Turn off for your system cursor.") off or on. The change is immediate, with no reload, and applies to every page and open tab.

title: Troubleshooting the custom cursor
heading: The cursor feels slow or lags behind
text: Why: the ring follows the pointer smoothly on purpose, and on a busy page or a slower computer it can fall further behind. What to do: aim with the dot, which is exact. If the lag bothers you, switch off Custom cursor in Settings › Comfort.

title: Troubleshooting the custom cursor
heading: I cannot see the cursor
text: Possible causes and fixes: - The ring fades when you stop moving. Move the mouse. - The page is still loading. Wait a moment. - Switch off Custom cursor in Settings to use your system pointer.

title: Troubleshooting the custom cursor
heading: My large or high-contrast system pointer is replaced
text: Why: the custom cursor hides the system pointer. What to do: switch off Custom cursor in Settings › Comfort. Your system pointer, with its size and colour, returns everywhere on the site.

title: Troubleshooting the custom cursor
heading: The custom cursor does not appear at all
text: Why: it is off in Settings, your device has no hovering pointer, your device asks for reduced motion, or reading mode is on. This is intended.

title: Troubleshooting the custom cursor
heading: Screen recordings show a ring and dot
text: Why: the custom cursor is part of the page, so recordings of the page include it. What to do: switch it off before recording, or use the recorder's Highlight the cursor option with the custom cursor off.

title: Custom cursor FAQ
heading: Does the custom cursor change where I click?
text: No. Clicks happen at the dot, exactly where your system pointer would be.

title: Custom cursor FAQ
heading: Does Reduce motion in Settings turn it off?
text: No. The custom cursor follows your device's reduced-motion setting, not the site's Reduce motion switch. Use the Custom cursor switch to turn it off.

title: Custom cursor FAQ
heading: Why does the ring change colour?
text: It reads the colour of the surface under it and picks a version of that colour that stands out, so it stays visible on any background.

title: Custom cursor FAQ
heading: Is it shown on my phone?
text: No. Touch screens use the device's normal behaviour.

title: Custom cursor FAQ
heading: Does it work in the installed app?
text: Yes, on computers with a mouse or trackpad, the same as in the browser.

title: Eye rest
text: Eye rest is an optional reminder to look away from the screen. When it is on, a small card appears after a set time on a page, "Time to look away", and invites you to rest your eyes for a few seconds. Select Rest now and the screen dims to a quiet horizon with one instruction: look at something about twenty feet away. A line on the horizon shrinks as the seconds pass, and when the rest is over the whole screen brightens, so you can tell it has finished without looking back at it. Reminders are off by default . You choose how often they come (every 20, 35, 45 or 60 minutes) and how long each rest lasts (5 to 30 seconds). Every reminder can be put off with Later , silenced for the session, or turned off for good.

title: Eye rest
heading: Who it is for
text: People who spend long stretches looking at colours, contrast checks or code on the site and want a gentle prompt to look away now and then.

title: Eye rest
heading: Where to find it
text: Settings ( Ctrl + , ) › Comfort › Eye-rest reminders .

title: Eye rest
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , and select Comfort . 2. Switch on Eye-rest reminders . 3. Under Reminder interval , select 20m . 4. Keep working on a page. After 20 minutes the card "Time to look away" appears. 5. Select Rest now . The screen dims; look at something far away until it brightens. 6. The page returns and the next reminder is scheduled.

title: Eye rest
heading: What you can do
text: - Choose how often reminders come and how long each rest lasts. - Start a rest straight from the reminder, or put it off with Later . - End a rest early. - Silence reminders for the rest of the session, or turn them off.

title: Get started with eye rest
heading: Turn reminders on
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , to open Settings, then select Comfort . 2. Switch on Eye-rest reminders ("Gentle reminders to rest your eyes on a schedule."). 3. Under Reminder interval (minutes between reminders), select 20m , 35m , 45m or 60m . The countdown starts at once. Changing the interval later restarts it.

title: Get started with eye rest
heading: How the countdown works
text: - The countdown runs while a page is open. It starts again whenever you load a page, including moving to another page or reloading. - It keeps running while the tab is in the background, so a reminder can be waiting when you come back. - After a reminder, the next countdown starts when you finish, end or put off the rest.

title: Get started with eye rest
heading: Turn reminders off
text: Any of these: - Settings › Comfort › switch off Eye-rest reminders . This is the most reliable way. - On a reminder card, select Turn these off . - For this session only, select Not this session on a reminder card. Note: Turn these off on the card stops the reminders but does not move the switch in Settings. If you later change any setting while that switch still shows on, the reminders come back. Switch it off in Settings as well to keep them off.

title: Get started with eye rest
heading: Next step
text: [The reminder and the rest](the-reminder-and-the-rest.md) explains the card and the rest screen.

title: The reminder and the rest
heading: The reminder card
text: When the countdown ends, a card appears: - Time to look away - "You have been at this for 20 minutes. 30 seconds looking into the distance is enough." (with your own interval and rest length) - Rest now and Later - a quieter row: Change , Not this session , Turn these off - a thin bar that empties over 60 seconds If you do nothing, the card leaves by itself after 60 seconds (when the bar is empty), and the next countdown starts. Button What it does --- --- Rest now Starts the rest straight away Later Closes the card; the next reminder comes after a full interval Change Shows the timing options (below) Not this session No more reminders until you close this browser tab Turn these off Stops reminders (see the note in [Getting started](getting-started.md turn-reminders-off))

title: The reminder and the rest
heading: Change how often and how long
text: Select Change . The card becomes How often, and how long : 1. Remind me every : 20m , 35m , 45m or 60m . This changes the same setting as Reminder interval in Settings, and the card's sentence updates. 2. Rest for : 5s , 10s , 15s , 20s , 25s or 30s . 3. Select Rest now to start a rest with these timings, or Later or Turn these off below. This view also leaves by itself after 60 seconds. Note: The rest length you pick here applies until you move to another page or reload. It then returns to 30 seconds.

title: The reminder and the rest
heading: During the rest
text: - The screen fills with a dark sky and ground, divided by a horizon line. - Above the line: Look past the screen — "Something about twenty feet away — a doorway, a window, the far wall. The screen will brighten when the rest is over." - Below the line: the seconds remaining, counting down. - The horizon line slowly shrinks towards the centre as the rest passes. With your device's reduced-motion setting on, it stays still. - The floating buttons, kits, dock and info bars are hidden. The pointer stays visible. - End early stops the rest. It does not turn reminders off; the next countdown starts.

title: The reminder and the rest
heading: When the rest ends
text: The whole screen brightens to a warm off-white, a change you can notice from the corner of your eye. It shows Rest complete , Welcome back and "Next reminder in 20 minutes." (with your interval). After about 2.6 seconds the page returns and the next countdown starts.

title: Troubleshooting eye rest
heading: I switched reminders on but none appear
text: Possible causes and fixes: - The countdown restarts on every page load. If you move between pages often, a 20-minute reminder may never be reached. Stay on one page, or choose a shorter interval. - You selected Not this session earlier in this tab. Open the site in a new tab. - You selected Turn these off earlier. Switch Eye-rest reminders off and on again in Settings › Comfort. - A few pages do not include the eye-rest reminder. Try another page.

title: Troubleshooting eye rest
heading: Reminders came back after I turned them off
text: Why: Turn these off on the card does not change the switch in Settings. Changing any setting while that switch shows on brings the reminders back. What to do: switch off Eye-rest reminders in Settings › Comfort.

title: Troubleshooting eye rest
heading: The rest always lasts 30 seconds
text: Why: the Rest for choice lasts only until you move to another page or reload. What to do: choose it again under Change on the card.

title: Troubleshooting eye rest
heading: The horizon line does not move
text: Why: your device's reduced-motion setting is on, so the line stays still. The countdown number still shows the time left, and the screen still brightens at the end.

title: Troubleshooting eye rest
heading: The screen went white at the end of a rest
text: That is the end signal. It lasts about 2.6 seconds, then the page returns.

title: Eye rest FAQ
heading: Why are reminders off by default?
text: They interrupt what you are doing, so the site leaves the choice to you.

title: Eye rest FAQ
heading: Why twenty feet?
text: Looking into the distance gives your eyes a break from focusing close up. The reminder's wording follows the common "20-20-20" habit: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet (6 metres) away for about 20 seconds. The site's default interval is 20 minutes and its default rest is 30 seconds.

title: Eye rest FAQ
heading: Does eye rest work when the tab is in the background?
text: The countdown keeps running, so the reminder can be waiting when you return. It is shown on the page, not as a system notification.

title: Eye rest FAQ
heading: Is eye rest the same as the screen saver?
text: No. Eye rest reminds you on a schedule while you work. The screen saver appears after you stop using the page for a while. See [Screen saver](../../screen-saver/README.md).

title: Eye rest FAQ
heading: Can I trigger a rest without waiting?
text: Not directly. Choose the shortest interval, 20m , or wait for the next reminder.

Rest The few seconds (5 to 30) during which the screen dims and invites you to look away. Reminder card The small card that appears when the interval ends: "Time to look away". Horizon The line across the rest screen that shrinks to show how much of the rest is left. Dawn The brightening of the whole screen that marks the end of a rest. title: Eye rest limits and accuracy
text: - Not medical advice. Eye rest is a comfort reminder. It does not diagnose, treat or prevent any eye condition. If your eyes are uncomfortable, talk to an eye-care professional. - Per page. The countdown runs per page and restarts whenever a page loads. It does not track your total screen time, or time spent in other apps or other websites. - Timings. Reminders appear after the chosen interval measured from the page load or the previous reminder. Browsers may delay timers in background tabs, so a reminder in a background tab can arrive a little late. - Where it appears. Only on auricartisan.com, and only in the tab where the countdown ran. It is not a system notification. - Rest length. The Rest for choice is not saved and returns to 30 seconds on the next page load.

title: Eye rest privacy
text: - Your on or off choice and your interval are kept in this browser, as part of your settings. Turn these off is remembered in this browser too, and Not this session in this tab only. - Eye rest does not record when you rest, how often you skip, or anything about your activity, and it sends nothing over the network. - The cookie policy lists the eye rest preference under Functional storage.

title: Feedback
text: Auric Artisan asks for feedback rarely and quietly. After you have spent twenty minutes of active time on a page, a small Feedback panel may appear: "You have been here a little while — how is it going?" You can give a star rating and a comment, open a six-question survey, or report a bug with details of what happened. You can also put it off with Maybe later , or tell the site never to ask again with Don't ask again . Contact details are always optional. You can send any feedback anonymously, and adding your name or email is a separate, equal choice. The site does not ask on pages where a prompt would get in the way: signing in, checking out, paying, or reading legal pages. After any prompt, it waits at least a week before asking again on this device. To give feedback whenever you like, use the Feedback panel in the Feature Kit (see [Kits](../../kits/README.md)).

title: Feedback
heading: Who it is for
text: Anyone with something to say: praise, a complaint, a missing feature, or a bug.

title: Feedback
heading: Where to find it
text: - The automatic prompt, occasionally, after twenty minutes of active use. - The Feature Kit's Feedback panel, at any time.

title: Feedback
heading: Quick start
text: 1. When the Feedback panel appears, select a number of stars (or press 1 to 5 ). 2. The question below changes to suit your rating. Type an answer if you like. 3. Select Continue . 4. Choose Send anonymously , or Add contact details to give a name or email. 5. A thank-you message confirms that your feedback has been received.

title: Feedback
heading: What you can do
text: - Rate your experience from one to five stars, with an optional comment. - Answer a short, optional six-question survey. - Report a bug with what happened, what you expected, how to reproduce it, and how badly it affects you. - Choose whether to be contacted. - Put the prompt off, or stop it for good.

title: Get started with feedback
heading: Give feedback at any time
text: The automatic prompt is not the only way. Open the Feature Kit ( Ctrl + Shift + K , or Feature in the page utilities bar) and choose Feedback . See [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Rate, survey and report a bug
Rate, survey and report a bug
heading: Quick rating
text: The panel asks "You have been here a little while — how is it going?" (or "How is Auric Artisan working for you?"). 1. Select one to five stars, or press 1 to 5 (when you are not typing in the comment box). 2. The comment question changes with your rating: Stars Question Hint --- --- --- 1 What went wrong? We would like to fix it. The more specific, the better 2 What let you down? What would have made this work for you? 3 What would move this from fine to good? Optional 4 Anything that would have made it a five? Optional 5 What worked well? It helps us keep it that way. Optional Before you rate, it reads "Anything you would like to add?". 3. With one or two stars, the Report a bug button is highlighted and reads Something broke? , in case a bug report fits better. 4. Select Continue . It becomes available once you have chosen a rating or typed a comment.

title: Rate, survey and report a bug
heading: Choose whether to be contacted
text: The next screen asks "Would you like us to contact you about this feedback?" and notes that contact information is completely optional. - Send anonymously sends your rating and comment straight away, without asking again. - Add contact details shows two optional fields: - Name — optional ("How should we address you?", up to 120 characters); - Email — optional ( you@example.com , up to 254 characters). Select Send feedback , or Back to return. If the email does not look valid, the message reads "That email does not look right. Correct it, clear it, or go back to send anonymously." Either way, a thank-you screen confirms "Thank you for your feedback" and closes by itself.

title: Rate, survey and report a bug
heading: The survey
text: Select Full survey in the Feedback panel. A few questions : "Six questions, about a minute. Every answer is optional." Question Answer type --- --- What brings you here most often? One of: Design work, Development, Accessibility testing, Learning, Something else How easy was it to find what you needed? 1 to 5 How would you rate the speed and performance? 1 to 5 How does the design feel to use? 1 to 5 Is anything missing that you expected to find? Text ("A tool, an export format, a colour space…") Anything you particularly liked? Text (optional) A counter shows how many you have answered, for example "3 of 6 answered". Select Send answers , or Not now to close. The thank-you screen reads "Your responses have been received."

title: Rate, survey and report a bug
heading: Report a bug
text: Select Report a bug (or Something broke? ) in the Feedback panel. 1. What happened? (required) — for example "Export HTML did nothing when I pressed it". 2. What did you expect instead? — for example "A file should download". 3. How can we reproduce it? — numbered steps. 4. How badly does it affect you? — Minor , Normal (default) or Blocking . 5. Select Send report . It becomes available once What happened? has text. Cancel closes the form. What you type is saved as a draft on this device as you go. If you close the form and open it again, it reads "Restored what you had written earlier." The report is sent with details of the page, so the problem can be reproduced: the page address, the window and screen size, your browser and platform, your language, the theme and, where available, a few recent error messages from the page. The thank-you screen reads "Your report has been received, with the page details attached. We review reports as part of improving the site."

title: Rate, survey and report a bug
heading: When you are offline
text: Feedback you send while offline is kept on your device and sent when the connection returns.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: The prompt never appears
text: Why: it needs 20 minutes of active time on one page, it does not appear on sign-in, checkout, payment or legal pages, it waits at least a week between prompts, and it stops for good after Don't ask again . What to do: use the Feature Kit's Feedback panel whenever you want to give feedback.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: I chose Don't ask again by mistake
text: Why: the choice is kept in this browser. What to do: use the Feature Kit's Feedback panel, which is always available. Clearing the site's data in your browser also resets the choice.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: Continue is greyed out
text: Why: it needs a star rating or a comment.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: Send report is greyed out
text: Why: What happened? is required.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: Pressing a number changed my rating
text: Why: the keys 1 to 5 set the rating when the comment box does not have focus. What to do: click in the comment box before typing numbers.

title: Troubleshooting feedback
heading: I was offline when I sent feedback
text: It is kept on your device and sent automatically when you are back online.

title: Feedback FAQ
heading: Do I have to give my name or email?
text: No. Send anonymously is always available and sends your feedback without contact details.

title: Feedback FAQ
heading: Will I get a reply?
text: Only if you add contact details and the team decides to follow up. A bug report is not a promise of a fix, but reports are reviewed.

title: Feedback FAQ
heading: Can I attach a screenshot or recording?
text: Not in the feedback panel. You can describe the problem, or contact the team through https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/.

title: Feedback FAQ
heading: Why does the site wait so long before asking?
text: So that it asks people who have actually used the site, and does not interrupt short visits.

title: Feedback FAQ
heading: Does the prompt appear on every device?
text: The timing and your choices are kept per browser, so each browser counts separately.

title: Feedback glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Automatic prompt The feedback panel the site shows by itself after 20 minutes of active use. Active time Time with the page visible on screen; time in a background tab does not count. Quiet period The time after a prompt during which the site does not ask again. Anonymous feedback Feedback sent without a name or email. Bug report A description of something that went wrong, sent with details of the page. Severity How badly a bug affects you: Minor, Normal or Blocking. Draft Text you have typed but not sent, kept on your device.

title: Feedback privacy
heading: Sent when you submit
text: - Rating and comment: your stars and what you typed, and the page you were on. - Survey: your answers. - Bug report: what you typed, the severity, and page details: the page address, window and screen size, browser and platform, language, theme, and recent page errors where available. - Contact details: only if you choose Add contact details and fill them in. Nothing is sent until you select a send button.

title: Feedback privacy
heading: Kept on this device
text: - When you were last asked and how you answered (to respect the quiet periods and Don't ask again ). - Unsent bug-report drafts. - Feedback waiting to be sent while you are offline. To remove these, clear the site's data in your browser.

title: Guide and page outline
text: The guide is a help panel for the page you are on. Press ? (or select the question-mark Guide button in the header) and it opens by saying what the page is and what it is for. It offers a guided tour of the page, which highlights each important area in turn with a short explanation; a map of the tour's stops; quick links to other parts of the site; and recommended paths for common jobs, such as running an audit or finding a tool. The guide remembers how far you got in each page's tour, so you can pick up where you left off. Long company, pricing, legal and trust pages also have a section rail : a row of section links pinned under the header, labelled "On this page", which highlights the section you are reading and jumps to any other. A third outline, the Page outline button in the navigation dock, lists any page's headings; it is described in [Navigation dock › Page outline](../navigation-dock/docs/page-outline.md).

title: Guide and page outline
heading: Who it is for
text: - First-time visitors who want to know what a page does. - Anyone who prefers a short walkthrough to exploring alone. - Readers of long policy and company pages who want to jump between sections.

title: Guide and page outline
heading: Where to find it
text: - Press ? on any page (when you are not typing in a field). - Select Guide (the question mark) in the header. - In the mobile drawer, tap Guide (Tours and shortcuts) under Your work . - In Spotlight, type and choose Open the page guide . The section rail appears by itself on the pages that have one.

title: Guide and page outline
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/tool/analyzer/ and press ? . 2. The guide opens with Analyzer guide and a summary of the page. 3. Select Take the guided tour . 4. The first area of the page is highlighted with an explanation. Select Next , or press the Right arrow, to move on. 5. Press Esc to leave the tour at any point. 6. Press ? again later: the tour card now offers Pick up where you left off .

title: Guide and page outline
heading: What you can do
text: - Learn what any page is for, in one sentence. - Take, pause, resume and replay a guided tour of the page. - Jump straight to any tour stop. - Filter the guide by typing, or by tab: All, Tour, Tools, Pages, Learn, Help. - Follow quick links and recommended paths. - Jump between sections of long pages with the section rail.

title: Get started with the guide
heading: Open and close the guide
text: - Open: press ? , select Guide in the header, tap Guide in the mobile drawer, or choose Open the page guide in Spotlight's commands. - Close: press Esc , select the X ( Close guide ) or the ESC button beside the filter box, or click outside the panel. The guide opens only when you ask for it. It never opens by itself when you visit a page. While the guide is open, Tab stays inside it.

title: Get started with the guide
heading: The panel
text: From top to bottom: 1. What this page is. A kicker naming the kind of guide (for example Home guide , Analyzer guide , Collections guide , Search guide , Workspace guide , Library guide , Tool guide , Company guide , Policy guide or Site guide ), the page's title, and a one-sentence summary. 2. Filter box. Type to narrow everything below. The placeholder reads "Filter this guide…". 3. Tabs. All , Tour , Tools , Pages , Learn and Help . Each shows only that kind of item. With a tab focused, Left and Right move between tabs. 4. Tour card. Starts, resumes or replays the guided tour of this page, with a progress bar (see [Guided tours](guided-tours.md)). 5. On this page. The tour's stops for this page, numbered. A tick marks stops you have already seen. Select a stop to start the tour there. 6. Getting around. The stops that are the same on every page (the header, search, your library, the theme button), folded under "The same stops on every page" with a count such as "2/4 seen". Once you have seen them all, the group starts folded. 7. Elsewhere. Quick links: Full Search , Analyze a website , Find the right tool , Open saved work , Read documentation , Learn color concepts , Install the PWA and Install the extension . 8. Recommended paths. Short recipes for common jobs: Run a quick audit , Build color assets , Check accessibility and Find a feature fast , most with numbered steps. 9. Footer hints. Type to filter, ↑ ↓ navigate, ↵ open, ESC close.

title: Get started with the guide
heading: Find something in the guide
text: 1. Open the guide and type a word, for example export . 2. Only matching items remain. If nothing matches: "Nothing in the guide matches that. Try a shorter word, another tab, or clear the box." 3. Press Down to move to the first result, then Enter to open it. Pressing Enter in the filter box opens the top match directly. Home and End jump to the first and last item (when the filter box is not focused).

title: Get started with the guide
heading: What the tabs contain
text: Tab Shows --- --- All Everything Tour The tour card, the stops and the recommended paths Tools Quick links to tools (Analyze a website, Find the right tool) Pages Quick links to site pages (Open saved work) Learn Documentation and Learn links Help Full Search and the install links

title: Guided tours
text: A guided tour walks through the important areas of the page you are on. Each stop highlights one area and explains it in a small card beside it.

title: Guided tours
heading: Start a tour
text: 1. Press ? to open the guide. 2. The tour card at the top reads Take the guided tour , with the number of stops, for example "11 stops · leave at any point". 3. Select it (its action reads Start the tour ). To start at a particular stop, select that stop under On this page or Getting around .

title: Guided tours
heading: The tour card
text: What it shows When --- --- Take the guided tour — "N stops · leave at any point" You have not taken this page's tour Pick up where you left off — "You stopped at X of N · leave at any point", action Resume at stop X You left this page's tour part-way Replay the tour — "N stops on this page · you have finished this one" You finished this page's tour Start over from stop 1 (below the card) You left part-way and want the whole tour again A progress bar on the card shows how much of the tour you have seen. Progress is kept for each page separately. If a page has nothing to tour, the guide says "This page has no tourable sections yet, but the paths below will still help you move around."

title: Guided tours
heading: Move through a tour
text: The highlighted area is outlined on the page, which scrolls to bring it into view. The card beside it shows: - a rail of dots, one per stop; - the position, for example "3 of 11", and whether the stop is about this page or the whole site; - the stop's title and explanation; - sometimes a note; - What to look for : a list of details you can open. Controls: Control Key What it does --- --- --- Next Right Next stop Back Left Previous stop (unavailable on the first stop) Finish — On the last stop, ends the tour and marks it finished X ( Leave the tour ) Esc Leaves the tour; your place is remembered Skip to this page’s N stops — Shown on the site-wide stops at the start, to jump to the stops about this page While the tour is running, Tab stays inside the tour card.

title: Guided tours
heading: The stops every page shares
text: Every tour includes a few stops about the site itself, the same everywhere: - Start from the top — the header; - Search when the path is unclear — search and Ctrl + K ; - Keep useful work close — your library and workspace; - Match the viewing mode — the theme button; - Use footer links for trust and support — the footer. Once you have seen them, the guide folds them away under Getting around , and Skip to this page’s N stops lets you pass them.

title: Guided tours
heading: When an eye rest appears
text: A tour is hidden while an eye rest is on screen, and reappears afterwards.

title: The section rail
text: Long pages about the company, pricing, policies and security have a section rail : a row of links to the page's sections, labelled "On this page", near the top of the page.

title: The section rail
heading: Where it appears
text: - Company pages: About, Pricing, Accessibility and FAQ. - Every legal page, such as Privacy, Terms, Cookies, Refund Policy, Licenses, Security, Transparency, Acceptable Use Policy, Content & Intellectual Property, Data Retention & Deletion, Subscription & Billing and the Extension privacy policy. - The Trust Center at https://auricartisan.com/security/.

title: The section rail
heading: How it behaves
text: - Pinned. As you scroll down, the rail sticks just below the site header, so it is always in reach. It gains a shadow once it is pinned. - Shows where you are. The link for the section you are reading is highlighted. A section counts as "current" once its heading has passed a line a little below the rail. - Jumps. Select a link to scroll to that section. On legal pages, whose sections can be folded, jumping to a folded section opens it. - Narrow screens. The rail scrolls sideways, and keeps the current section's link in view. - At the very end of the page, the last section is highlighted. The links are ordinary page links, so they also work with the keyboard ( Tab and Enter ), and you can copy one to share a link straight to a section. Opening such a link on a legal page opens that section.

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: Pressing ? does nothing
text: Possible causes and fixes: - The cursor is in a text field. Click an empty part of the page first. - A modifier key is held, or your keyboard layout needs Shift for ? (that is fine) but also another key such as Alt Gr (which is not). Use the header's Guide button instead. - The page is still loading. Wait a moment. - A tour or the guide is already open.

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: The tour highlights nothing, or the wrong place
text: Why: a stop points at an area the page has not shown yet, for example one that loads late, is hidden on small screens or is folded away. What to do: select Next to move on, or widen the window and try again.

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: The tour card says I finished, but I want to see it again
text: Select Replay the tour .

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: The tour starts in the middle
text: Why: you left part-way through last time. The card offers Pick up where you left off . What to do: select Start over from stop 1 .

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: The section rail covers part of a heading after jumping
text: Why: on some pages the header scrolls away during the jump, leaving the heading slightly lower than expected. What to do: scroll a little; the correct section stays highlighted.

title: Troubleshooting the guide and section rail
heading: A legal section stayed folded
text: What to do: select its heading to open it. Jumping from the rail or a direct link normally opens it for you.

title: Guide and page outline FAQ
heading: Will the guide pop up by itself?
text: No. It opens only when you press ? or select a Guide button.

title: Guide and page outline FAQ
heading: Is the tour the same on every page?
text: No. Each kind of page (home, analyzer, collections, search, workspace, library, tools, company and policy pages) has its own stops, plus a few site-wide stops shared by all.

title: Guide and page outline FAQ
heading: Does finishing one page's tour mark others as finished?
text: No. Progress is kept separately for each page.

title: Guide and page outline FAQ
heading: What is the difference between the three outlines?
text: The guide explains the page and tours it. The section rail is the pinned row of section links on long company, legal and trust pages. The navigation dock's Page outline lists the headings of any page.

title: Guide and page outline FAQ
heading: Is the guide available in Hindi?
text: Yes. When the site is in Hindi, the guide and its tours are shown in Hindi.

title: Header and navigation
text: Every page on auricartisan.com opens with the same header. On a computer it shows the Auric Artisan name, three menus ( Company , Tools and Learn ), a row of quick tools (the app, the browser extension, the VS Code extensions, search, the guide, your library, language and theme) and a Sign in button. On a phone or a narrow window, the menus and tools fold into a drawer that opens from the menu button, with every item labelled. Two more pieces of navigation float over every page. The page utilities bar sits at the bottom-left: one button that opens a row of launchers for the kits, the navigation dock and Settings. The navigation dock is a slim rail on the left or right edge with Back, Forward, Reload and scrolling controls; it has its own guide in [Navigation dock](../navigation-dock/README.md). At the bottom of every page, the footer gathers product links, policies, trust pages, contact details and social links.

title: Header and navigation
heading: Who it is for
text: Everyone who visits the site. The header is the quickest way to find a tool, the documentation or your saved work, and to switch theme or language.

title: Header and navigation
heading: Where to find it
text: - The header is at the top of every page. It stays pinned to the top as you scroll (except in reading mode). - The page utilities bar button is at the bottom-left corner of the window. - The footer is at the end of every page.

title: Header and navigation
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Select Tools in the header. A menu opens listing every tool, grouped under headings such as Core tools and Colour science . 2. Select a tool, for example Vision Simulation , to open it. The menu closes. 3. Select the magnifier ( Search ) to open Spotlight search, or press Ctrl + K . 4. Select the sun or moon button to switch between light and dark. 5. On a phone, tap the three-line menu button. The drawer opens with Browse , Your work , Get Auric and Preferences . 6. Select the page utilities button at the bottom-left, then Settings , to open the Settings panel.

title: Header and navigation
heading: What you can do
text: - Reach every company page, every tool and every learning and library page from three menus. - Open search, the guide and your library from any page. - Download the app, the browser extension or the VS Code extensions. - Switch language and theme in one click. - Sign in, or reach your account once signed in. - Use a labelled drawer on small screens, with tools grouped behind chips. - Launch the kits, the navigation dock and Settings from the page utilities bar.

title: Get started with the header and navigation
Get started with the header and navigation
heading: A tour of the page frame
text: Every page has the same frame around its content: 1. Header (top). The Auric Artisan name on the left returns you to the homepage. The rest depends on the width of your window: - 960 pixels wide or more: the Company , Tools and Learn menus, the quick-tools icons and Sign in . - Narrower than 960 pixels: a Search button and the three-line menu button, which opens the drawer. 2. Info bars (below the header, homepage by default). Optional strips such as the announcements bar and the clock strip. See [Info bars and notices](../../info-bars-and-notices/README.md). 3. Page content. 4. Floating controls. The page utilities button at the bottom-left, and the navigation dock on the left or right edge. 5. Footer (bottom).

title: Get started with the header and navigation
heading: Open a tool from the header
text: 1. Select Tools in the header. 2. The menu lists All Tools under Overview , then the tools under group headings: Core tools , Creative utilities , Colour science , Gamut & rendering , Perception , Spectral and Utilities . 3. Scroll the menu if needed. While there is more below, a SCROLL DOWN hint shows at its foot. 4. Select a tool. Result: the tool page opens. The menu closes by itself.

title: Get started with the header and navigation
heading: Open a tool on a phone
text: 1. Tap the three-line button at the top right. The drawer opens. 2. Under Browse , tap Tools . The section opens in place and shows a row of group chips, each with a count. 3. Tap a chip, for example Utilities . Only that group's tools are listed, with All Tools always at the top. 4. Tap a tool. Result: the tool page opens and the drawer closes.

title: Get started with the header and navigation
heading: Get back to where you were
text: - Select the Auric Artisan name to go to the homepage. - Use the navigation dock's Back button, your browser's back button, or Alt + Left . - Right-click the page and use Back in the quick bar.

title: Get started with the header and navigation
heading: Find something without the menus
text: - Select Search in the header, or press Ctrl + K , and type what you want. See [Search and Spotlight](../../search-and-spotlight/README.md). - Select Guide (the question mark), or press ? , for a map of the page and its tour. See [Guide and page outline](../../guide-and-page-outline/README.md).

title: The desktop header
text: On windows 960 pixels wide or more, the header shows everything in one row: the brand, three menus, the quick-tools icons and Sign in .

title: The desktop header
heading: Sign in
text: Sign in opens the sign-in page, where you can also create a free account. Once you are signed in, the button is replaced by your account menu. Accounts are covered in [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: The desktop header
heading: When the header scrolls
text: The header stays pinned to the top of the window as you scroll. In reading mode it scrolls away with the page, to leave more room for text.

title: The mobile drawer
text: When the window is narrower than 960 pixels, for example on a phone, a tablet in portrait, or a narrow desktop window, the header menus and quick tools move into a drawer . The drawer is the same content as the desktop header, with every item labelled in words.

title: The mobile drawer
heading: The bar
text: The header bar on a narrow screen holds: - the Auric Artisan name (to the homepage); - a Search button. On screens 600 pixels wide or more it also shows the word "Search" and a Ctrl K hint; on phones it is an icon; - your account button, once you are signed in; - the menu button (three lines). Its label is Open navigation , and Close navigation while the drawer is open, when it shows an X.

title: The mobile drawer
heading: Open and close the drawer
text: 1. Tap the menu button. The drawer opens: - on phones, as a full-width sheet from under the bar to the bottom of the screen; - on screens from 600 to 959 pixels wide, as a sheet 400 pixels wide on the right. 2. While it is open, the page behind it does not scroll, and the floating buttons are hidden. 3. To close it, tap the menu button again, tap the dimmed page outside the drawer, press Esc , or open any link in it. It also closes if you widen the window past 960 pixels or go back or forward in your history.

title: The mobile drawer
heading: What is in the drawer
text: From top to bottom: Search tools, colours and pages . Tap it to open Spotlight search. Company , Tools and Learn , each with a count of its entries. Tap one to open it in place, like an accordion. Opening one section does not close the drawer, and tapping a switch further down does not fold the section away. In Tools , a row of group chips sits above the list: Core tools , Creative utilities , Colour science , Gamut & rendering , Perception , Spectral and Utilities , each with a count. Only the selected group's tools are listed, with All Tools always at the top. The drawer selects the group of the page you are on, or Core tools if you are not on a tool page. Tap another chip to switch group. - Library — Saved palettes and exports. Opens your library panel. - Guide — Tours and shortcuts. Opens the page guide. - The app — Works offline in a browser tab. Opens the Download page. - Browser extension — The Auric toolbar in your browser. - VS Code — Icon collections and colour themes. - Theme : Auto , Light , Dark . Auto follows your device, like System in the Settings panel. - Language : English , हिन्दी . Each language is written in its own script, so you can find yours even if you cannot read the current one. The highlighted buttons always show your current choice, including changes made elsewhere, such as in Settings. Pinned to the foot of the drawer: Sign in and Create account when you are signed out, or your account once you are signed in.

title: The mobile drawer
heading: With the keyboard
text: The drawer works with Tab , Enter and Space like the rest of the page. Inside an open section, Up , Down , Home and End move between the visible entries. Esc closes an open section first, then the drawer, and returns focus to the menu button.

title: The page utilities bar
text: The page utilities bar is a single round button at the bottom-left corner of every page. Select it to open a bar of labelled launchers: Launcher Opens --- --- Feature The Feature Kit Menu The Menu Kit Advanced The Advanced Kit Status The Status Kit Library The Library Kit Navigate The navigation dock (Back, Forward, Reload, outline, split view and more) Settings The Settings panel The kits are documented in [Kits](../../../kits/README.md), which also covers this bar in more depth. The dock is documented in [Navigation dock](../../navigation-dock/README.md), and the panel in [Settings panel](../../settings-panel/README.md).

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Open and close the bar
text: 1. Select the button at the bottom-left. Its tooltip reads Page utilities : "Show navigation, settings, and the Feature, Menu, Advanced, Status and Library kits." 2. The bar opens along the bottom of the window. The first button now reads Close ( Hide page utilities ). 3. Select a launcher. The bar closes and that kit or panel opens. To close the bar without choosing, select Close , press Esc , or click anywhere else on the page. Closing the bar does not close a kit you already opened; an open kit's launcher stays visible so you can close the kit from it.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: On a phone
text: On screens up to about 580 pixels wide the bar fills the width of the screen in two rows: the five kits, a thin line, then Navigate , Settings and Close . The page leaves room at its end so the bar does not cover the last lines of content. On a phone, the navigation dock has no button of its own on the screen; Navigate in this bar is the way to open it.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Things to know
text: - The bar is hidden while the screen saver, an eye rest or the mobile drawer is showing. In reading mode the kit launchers are hidden. - Each kit also has a keyboard shortcut (for example Ctrl + Shift + L for the Library Kit). See [Keyboard shortcuts](../../keyboard-shortcuts/README.md).

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: The header shows a menu button instead of Company, Tools and Learn
text: Why: your window is narrower than 960 pixels, or your browser is zoomed in far enough to make the page that narrow. What to do: use the drawer, or widen the window or zoom out ( Ctrl + - ) to see the full header.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: A header menu closed before I could click an entry
text: Why: menus close when keyboard focus or a click moves outside them. What to do: open the menu again and select the entry directly. On a touch screen, use the drawer, whose sections stay open until you close them.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: I cannot see the bottom of a long menu
text: Why: tall menus scroll inside themselves. What to do: scroll inside the menu. The SCROLL DOWN hint shows while more entries are below.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: The page does not scroll while the drawer is open
text: Why: this is intended, so that swiping inside the drawer does not move the page behind it. What to do: close the drawer with the menu button, Esc , or a tap on the dimmed area.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: The floating buttons disappeared
text: Why: the page utilities button and other floating buttons are hidden while the mobile drawer, the screen saver or an eye rest is showing. What to do: close the drawer, move the mouse or press a key to leave the screen saver, or finish or end the eye rest.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: The theme buttons in the drawer do not match what I see
text: Why: the drawer shows the stored choice: Auto follows your device, so a dark page can show Auto selected. What to do: select Light or Dark to fix the theme regardless of your device.

title: Troubleshooting the header and navigation
heading: The Library button does nothing
text: Why: the library panel loads a moment after the page. What to do: wait until the page has finished loading and select it again, or use Ctrl + Shift + L .

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: Is there a page that lists every tool?
text: Yes. All Tools at the top of the Tools menu opens https://auricartisan.com/collections/, which shows every tool with filters.

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: Do the menus open when I hover over them?
text: No. They open when you click or tap their button, or press Enter , Space or Down on it, and they stay open until you choose an entry or move away.

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: Can I hide the page utilities bar?
text: The bar collapses to a single button when you close it, and that button cannot be removed. Reading mode hides the kit launchers.

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: Where is the navigation dock on my phone?
text: On phones the dock has no button of its own. Open the page utilities bar and select Navigate .

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: What does the flag in the footer do?
text: Double-click it to play a short celebration animation. It does nothing else.

title: Header and navigation FAQ
heading: How do I contact Auric Artisan?
text: Use Email our studio in the footer ( hello@auricartisan.com ), or the Contact page in the Company menu.

title: Header and navigation glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Header The strip at the top of every page with the brand, menus, quick tools and sign-in. Menu (header) The Company, Tools or Learn list that opens below its button. title: Header and navigation privacy
text: - The header's menus and the drawer do not store anything themselves. - The Theme and Language switches in the header and drawer store your choice in this browser, the same way the Settings panel does. - The header checks whether you are signed in, so it can show your account menu instead of Sign in . For visitors who are not signed in, no account request is made. - The page utilities bar does not store whether it was open. - The footer's social links open other websites (Product Hunt, LinkedIn, GitHub, X) in a new tab only when you select them. Explore our portfolio, LEACB opens the studio's own portfolio site.

title: Info bars and notices
text: Around the content of a page, the site can show a few slim strips and small notices: - the welcome bar , which cycles through short introductions to the platform; - the announcement bar , with the latest news, such as roadmap updates and offline support; - the quick-links bar , a scrolling row of cards for Documentation, Changelog, Timeline, Blog and Learn; - the clock strip , a live clock with the date and your time zone; - the hero notice on the homepage, and demo chips that mark live or demo sections. By default the three bars appear on the homepage only, and the clock strip is off, so ordinary pages start with their own content. Every bar and notice has a ✕ to hide it, and the Settings panel's Highlights section switches each one on or off, for the homepage or for every page. The site also shows short status messages : a brief welcome animation on your first visit, "Offline mode" and "Back online" when your connection changes, and prompts when the installed app has an update.

title: Info bars and notices
heading: Who it is for
text: Everyone. Keep the bars if you like to see news and shortcuts; hide them for a quieter page.

title: Info bars and notices
heading: Where to find it
text: - The bars and the clock strip appear under the header. - Their switches are in Settings ( Ctrl + , ) › Highlights . - Right-click a bar or the clock strip for its own small menu.

title: Info bars and notices
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open the homepage. The announcement bar sits under the header, cycling its messages. 2. Point at the bar: it pauses. Select a message to open it. 3. Select the ✕ at the end of the bar. It disappears from every page. 4. Press Ctrl + , , select Highlights , and switch Announcement bar back on. It now shows on every page. 5. Switch on Clock strip . A live clock appears under the header. 6. Right-click the clock and choose 24h .

title: Info bars and notices
heading: What you can do
text: - Show or hide each bar on the homepage only, on every page, or nowhere. - Pause a bar by pointing at it; open, copy or hide it from its right-click menu. - Show a live clock and set its format, date style, weekday, zone label and time zone. - Hide the hero notice and the demo chips.

title: Get started with info bars and notices
Get started with info bars and notices
heading: What appears by default
text: Item Default --- --- Welcome bar Homepage only Announcement bar Homepage only Quick-links bar Homepage only (also at the foot of the Collections page) Clock strip Off Hero notice On (homepage) Demo chips On (where a page has them) On every page, the announcement bar sits directly under the header, followed by the clock strip, then the page content.

title: Get started with info bars and notices
heading: Hide something
text: Select the ✕ at the end of a bar, on the hero notice, or on a demo chip. It disappears at once, and the matching switch in Settings › Highlights turns off. A demo chip's ✕ hides every demo chip on the site.

title: Get started with info bars and notices
heading: Show something again, or everywhere
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , and select Highlights . 2. Switch on the item you want. For the three bars, switching on shows the bar on every page. To return to the homepage-only default, select Restore section defaults . Details are in [Settings panel › Highlights and clock](../../settings-panel/docs/highlights-and-clock.md).

title: Get started with info bars and notices
heading: Changes apply everywhere at once
text: A change made with a ✕ or in Settings applies straight away to every page, including pages already open in other tabs.

title: Get started with info bars and notices
heading: In reading mode and the screen saver
text: The bars and the clock strip are hidden in reading mode and while the screen saver is showing.

title: The clock strip
text: The clock strip is a live clock under the header. It is off by default .

title: The clock strip
heading: Turn it on
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , and select Highlights . 2. Switch on Clock strip ("Off by default. Turn this on for a live clock, date and timezone above every page."). It appears under the header (and under the announcement bar, if shown) on every page.

title: The clock strip
heading: What it shows
text: - The flag of your time zone's country, or a globe for other zones. - The zone's name, for example "India Standard Time" (it reads Local time for a moment while the clock starts). "(default)" is added when the site could not match your zone and used a close one. - The time, ticking every second, for example 10:42:07 AM . - The date, the weekday, and the zone's abbreviation with its offset from UTC, for example "EDT · UTC-4" for New York in summer. Where the browser has no abbreviation for a zone, the offset is shown in both places. Screen readers can read the time on demand; it is not announced every second.

title: The clock strip
heading: The Clock settings menu
text: Right-click anywhere on the clock strip to open Clock settings : Part Options --- --- Preview The clock and date as they will look Format 12h , 24h Date Long , D/M/Y , M/D/Y , ISO Show Seconds , Weekday , Zone (each on or off) Time zone A search box ("Search time zone…") and a list: Auto-detect , then common cities with their offsets Reset Returns the clock to its defaults All settings → Opens Settings on the Clock section Each change applies at once to the strip and the preview. 1. Right-click the strip. 2. Under Time zone , choose a city from the list, or type part of a city, zone or region name (for example tokyo or Europe ). Up to 60 matches are listed; if none match, the list reads "No zones match." 3. Select a zone. The strip switches to it; the list marks your current choice. Choose Auto-detect to follow your device's zone again. Reset returns the format to 12-hour, shows seconds, weekday and zone, sets the date to Long , and returns the zone to Auto-detect .

title: The clock strip
heading: How it relates to Settings › Clock
text: The clock strip and Settings › Clock share the same choices: 24-hour time, seconds, date format and time zone. A change in one shows in the other. The menu adds three choices that Settings does not have: the ISO date format, and the Weekday and Zone switches. Settings adds Show date , which hides the date line.

title: The clock strip
heading: Turn it off
text: Switch off Clock strip in Settings › Highlights.

title: The info bars
heading: The welcome bar
text: A single-line bar that shows one message at a time and cross-fades to the next every six seconds. Its seven messages introduce the platform: colour science, colour-space tooling, accessibility, vision simulation, palettes, research tools such as Ishihara plates, and what comes next. Each message links to the welcome article on the blog. Hover a message for a short tooltip.

title: The info bars
heading: The announcement bar
text: Also one message at a time, every six seconds. It carries the latest platform news, for example: - "New library updates and workflow improvements are in progress — read the roadmap." (to the roadmap article) - "Every tool works offline — install Auric Artisan as an app from the Download page." (to the Download page) - "Early access: accounts, pricing, and sync are rolling out in stages." (to the roadmap article) Highlighted messages are featured news.

title: The info bars
heading: The quick-links bar
text: A row of cards that scrolls continuously across the page: Card Subtitle Goes to --- --- --- Documentation Guides & API reference /library/documentation/ Changelog What's new lately /library/changelog/ Timeline Milestones & history /company/timeline/ Blog Posts & site news /library/blog/ Learn Tutorials & resources /library/learn/

title: The info bars
heading: Pausing and motion
text: - Point at the welcome or announcement bar to pause it on the current message. It resumes when you move away. - Rotation also pauses while the tab is hidden. - With Reduce motion on (Settings › Comfort) or your device's reduced-motion setting, messages change instantly instead of fading.

title: The info bars
heading: Hide a bar
text: Select the ✕ at the end of the bar ( Hide this bar (re-enable in Settings) ). The bar is hidden on every page, and its switch in Settings › Highlights turns off. Note: The tooltip on the ✕ says "Turn it back on in Settings → Comfort". The switches are in the Highlights section.

title: The info bars
heading: The bar's right-click menu
text: Right-click a bar, or a message in it, to open a small menu headed with the bar's name ("Welcome messages", "Site announcements" or "Site tools"). Under This bar : Button What it does --- --- Open Goes to the message you right-clicked, or the bar's first link Copy link Copies that link's address Hide bar Hides this bar everywhere Settings Opens the Settings panel (on the Comfort section) Esc , a click elsewhere, a scroll or resizing the window closes the menu.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Hero notice
text: A highlighted notice banner in the homepage's opening section. Select its ✕ ( Dismiss (re-enable in Settings → Comfort) ) to hide it. Switch it back on with Hero notice in Settings › Highlights .

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Demo chips
text: Small labels with an information mark that sit above sections showing a live demo, marking them as "live" or "demo" content. Select the ✕ on any chip ( Hide demo chips (re-enable in Settings → Highlights) ) to hide every demo chip on the site. Switch them back on with Live demo chips in Settings › Highlights.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: First-visit welcome
text: The first time you open the site in a browser, a short animated welcome plays over the page for about a second (shorter if your device asks for reduced motion). Click it, or press Esc , Enter or Space , to skip it. It plays only once per browser. The cookie consent bar appears after it.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Loading screen
text: While a page is loading, a brief screen with the Auric Artisan logo and the line "Preparing local color tools." may show, with a progress bar. It disappears when the page is ready.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Connection messages
text: A small message appears at the edge of the screen when your connection changes: Message Meaning --- --- Offline mode Your device has lost its connection. The message stays while you are offline. Saved pages and tools keep working. Back online The connection has returned.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: App messages
text: When the site is installed as an app or prepared for offline use, you may see: Message Meaning --- --- Update ready — "Refresh to use the newest offline cache." ( Refresh / Later ) A new version of the site is ready Saving for offline — N% An offline download you asked for is in progress Full offline app ready The offline download has finished Auric Artisan installed The app was installed N files ready / Could not open file Files opened with the installed app These are explained in [Download and offline](../../../download-and-offline/README.md). Website updates can also be announced by the Update Kit; see [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Confirmation messages
text: Many actions show a short confirmation that fades after a couple of seconds, for example "Settings exported", "Page URL copied" or "Theme: Dark". They are announced to screen readers without moving focus. Each feature's reference page lists its messages.

title: Notices and status messages
heading: Notifications
text: The site does not send system or push notifications. Everything above appears on the page itself.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: A bar I hid is back
text: Why: someone switched it on in Settings › Highlights, or you restored the section's defaults, which brings the bars back on the homepage. What to do: select its ✕ again.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: A bar now shows on every page, not just the homepage
text: Why: switching a bar on in Settings shows it everywhere. What to do: select Restore section defaults in Settings › Highlights to go back to homepage only.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: The ✕ tooltip says Comfort, but I cannot find the switch there
text: Why: the switches are in the Highlights section of Settings, not Comfort.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: The clock shows the wrong time zone
text: Why: a fixed zone was chosen in the clock menu or in Settings › Clock, or your device reports a zone the site could not match exactly (the label then shows "(default)"). What to do: right-click the strip and choose Auto-detect , or pick your zone from the list.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: The clock strip is missing
text: Why: it is off by default, and it is hidden in reading mode. What to do: switch on Clock strip in Settings › Highlights.

title: Troubleshooting info bars and notices
heading: "Offline mode" will not go away
text: Why: your device reports that it has no connection. The message stays until the connection returns. What to do: check your connection. Saved pages keep working meanwhile.

title: Info bars and notices FAQ
heading: Why are the bars only on the homepage?
text: They are an introduction. On other pages they would push the content down, so by default they stay on the homepage. You can show them everywhere from Settings › Highlights.

title: Info bars and notices FAQ
heading: Can I see the first-visit welcome again?
text: It plays once per browser. It plays again only if you clear the site's data in your browser.

title: Info bars and notices FAQ
heading: Does the site send notifications?
text: No. All messages appear on the page itself.

title: Info bars and notices FAQ
heading: Can I show a world clock for another city?
text: Yes. Right-click the clock strip and choose that city's time zone. The strip shows one zone at a time.

title: Info bars and notices FAQ
heading: Does the clock strip use my Settings clock choices?
text: Yes. The strip and Settings › Clock share 24-hour time, seconds, date format and time zone.

title: Info bars and notices glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Info bar A slim strip under the header: welcome, announcement or quick links. Clock strip A live clock under the header with the date and time zone. Hero notice A highlighted banner in the homepage's opening section. Demo chip A small label marking a live or demo section. Time zone A region's standard time, such as Asia/Kolkata or Europe/London. UTC offset How far a time zone is ahead of or behind Coordinated Universal Time. ISO date A date written year-month-day, for example 2026-09-24. Status message A short message at the edge of the screen about the connection or the app.

title: Info bars and notices privacy
text: - Which bars and notices you show or hide, and your clock choices, are kept in this browser as part of your settings. - The first-visit welcome remembers that it has played, in this browser. - The clock uses your device's time and time zone. Nothing about them is sent to Auric Artisan. - Nothing is recorded when you open, copy or hide a bar.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Almost everything on auricartisan.com can be reached from the keyboard. This section gathers every site-wide shortcut in one place: search, settings, the guide, reading mode, theme, text size, split view, the recorder, the kits and the right-click menu, followed by the keys that work inside each panel. On a Mac, use Cmd where this list says Ctrl for the shortcuts marked "Ctrl or Cmd". Shortcuts that use Alt use the Option key on a Mac. Letter shortcuts are ignored while you are typing in a text field, so they never interfere with what you type.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
heading: Who it is for
text: Keyboard users, power users, and anyone who wants to move faster around the site.

title: Troubleshooting keyboard shortcuts
heading: A shortcut does nothing
text: Possible causes and fixes: - You are typing in a field. Alt letter shortcuts and ? are ignored in text fields. Click an empty part of the page, or press Esc to leave the field, then try again. - The page is still loading. Most panels load a moment after the page. Wait, then try again. - The feature is not on this page. A few simple pages (for example sign-in pages) do not load every panel. - Another panel has focus. Some panels use keys for themselves while open; close the panel first.

title: Troubleshooting keyboard shortcuts
heading: The browser did something else instead
text: Why: browsers and operating systems reserve some combinations. For example, Ctrl + Shift + D can bookmark all tabs, Ctrl + Shift + A can search tabs, and Cmd + M minimises a window on a Mac. The site claims its shortcuts where the browser allows it, but some browsers keep certain combinations for themselves. What to do: use the on-screen control instead (the navigation dock for split view, the page utilities bar for kits and Settings).

title: Troubleshooting keyboard shortcuts
heading: ? does not open the guide
text: Why: on some keyboard layouts, ? needs a modifier the site does not accept, such as Alt Gr . What to do: use the Guide button in the header.

title: Troubleshooting keyboard shortcuts
heading: Alt shortcuts open the browser's menu bar
text: Why: in some browsers on Windows, pressing and releasing Alt alone moves focus to the menu bar. What to do: hold Alt while pressing the second key; the site's shortcut takes effect.

title: Troubleshooting keyboard shortcuts
heading: Alt + + does not enlarge text
text: Why: on many keyboards + needs Shift . What to do: press Alt + = instead, which does the same.

title: Language
text: Auric Artisan is available in English and Hindi (हिन्दी). English is the default. When you switch to Hindi, the page you are on is translated in place, without a reload, and every page you open afterwards appears in Hindi too, until you switch back. The translation covers the site's interface and its pages: menus, buttons, labels, tooltips, messages, settings, kits and the text of articles and tool pages. The site's own brand and product names are written in Devanagari (for example ऑरिक आर्टिज़न for Auric Artisan), while names of other companies and products, code, hex values and keyboard keys stay as they are. Hindi text uses Devanagari fonts chosen for each platform, with slightly taller line spacing for comfortable reading. Switching back to English reloads the page in English.

title: Language
heading: Who it is for
text: Hindi readers, and anyone who prefers to use the site in Hindi. The language choice also sets how dates and times are written (Indian Hindi conventions).

title: Language
heading: Where to find it
text: - The globe button in the header (tooltip Language / भाषा ). It switches between the two languages. - Settings › Appearance › Language : English or हिन्दी . - The mobile drawer › Preferences › Language . - Spotlight: press Ctrl + K , type , and choose Switch language . - A link ending in ?lang=hi (or ?lang=en ).

title: Language
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Select the globe button in the header. 2. The page switches to Hindi. Menus, buttons and the page text now read in Devanagari. 3. Open any other page: it is in Hindi too. 4. Select the globe again. The page reloads in English.

title: Language
heading: What you can do
text: - Use the whole site in Hindi, including the header, footer, kits, Settings, Spotlight, the right-click menu and page content. - Share a link that opens in Hindi by adding ?lang=hi . - Keep Hindi available offline in the installed app.

title: Get started with languages
heading: Switch to Hindi
text: Use any one of these: - Header: select the globe button. Its tooltip reads Language / भाषा with the description in both languages. - Settings: press Ctrl + , , and under Appearance › Language (भाषा — interface and articles) select हिन्दी . - Drawer (narrow screens): open the menu, and under Preferences › Language tap हिन्दी . - Spotlight: press Ctrl + K , type , and choose Switch language (English ⇄ हिन्दी). What happens: 1. The site downloads the Hindi text for the page you are on. On a first switch this can take a moment on a slow connection. 2. The page is translated where it stands. You stay at the same place on the page and nothing you typed is lost. 3. Text that appears later, such as a kit you open or a tool's results, is translated as it appears. 4. Every page you open afterwards loads in Hindi.

title: Get started with languages
heading: Switch back to English
text: Use the same controls: the globe, English in Settings or the drawer, or Switch language in Spotlight. The page reloads in English. Translation changes the page's text in place, so a reload is how the site returns to the original English. If you were typing into a form, finish or copy your text first.

title: Get started with languages
heading: Share a link that opens in Hindi
text: Add ?lang=hi to the end of any page address, for example: text https://auricartisan.com/tool/vision-simulation/?lang=hi Anyone who opens the link sees the page in Hindi, and their browser remembers Hindi for later visits. ?lang=en does the same for English. If the address already has a ? , add &lang=hi instead.

title: Get started with languages
heading: Language buttons are always readable
text: The language buttons show each language in its own script, English and हिन्दी , and are never translated. You can find your language even if you cannot read the one on screen.

title: What is translated
heading: Translated into Hindi
text: - Site chrome: the header, drawer, footer, info bars, cookie notice, navigation dock and page utilities bar. - Panels: the Settings panel, the kits, Spotlight, the guide and tours, the right-click menu and the eye-rest reminder. - Page content: the text of company and legal pages, tool pages, Learn articles, documentation, blog posts and library pages. - Hidden text: tooltips, placeholders in empty fields, image descriptions and the labels read out by screen readers. - Messages built from live values, such as labels that include a colour code or a count, for the common kinds of message. - The logo: the Auric Artisan wordmark is shown in Devanagari. - Promotional images with text in them are swapped for Hindi versions where one exists. - Dates and times are written the Hindi (India) way, for example on the clock strip. Pages that open without the rest of the site around them, such as sign-in, checkout, the offline page and the "page not found" page, are translated too.

title: What is translated
heading: Written in Devanagari rather than translated
text: The site's own brand and product names are transliterated, not translated: Auric Artisan becomes ऑरिक आर्टिज़न, and names such as Auric Icons and the kit names (फ़ीचर किट, मेन्यू किट and so on) are written the same way.

title: What is translated
heading: Kept as they are
text: - Code, keyboard keys and values: anything shown as code, key caps such as Ctrl , hex codes, numbers with units, and file names. - Names of other companies and products that people type or search for: Google, GitHub, VS Code, Open VSX, Figma, Razorpay, Cloudflare and similar. - Technical and scientific names that are used internationally, such as CIELAB, xyY, YCbCr, Von Kries, Bradford, and font names such as Inter. - The language buttons themselves, which always show English and हिन्दी. - Web addresses: a page has the same address in both languages. - Your own content: names you give to saved items, text you type into tools, and portfolio text. - Social preview images (the picture shown when a link is shared) stay in English.

title: What is translated
heading: Not covered by this switch
text: - The browser extension is a separate product with its own language support. See [Browser extension](../../../../browser-extension/README.md). - Search results are matched against the English text of pages, so searching with English words works best. - A small number of messages assembled from several live values may still appear partly in English.
