title: Language reference
heading: Opting parts of a page out
text: Some elements are deliberately never translated: the language buttons, code, keyboard keys, and the header detail lines of the right-click menu that show addresses, hex codes and quoted text.

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: The page stays in English after I choose Hindi
text: Why: the Hindi text is downloaded when you switch. On a slow or broken connection it may not arrive. What to do: check your connection and reload the page; the site remembers Hindi and translates again on load. In the installed app offline, Hindi is available only if you prepared the offline version while the site was in Hindi.

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: Some words are still in English
text: Why: some names and terms are kept in English on purpose (see [What is translated](what-is-translated.md)), and a few messages made up of several live values are not yet translated.

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: Switching to English reloaded the page and I lost what I typed
text: Why: returning to English needs a reload. What to do: before switching back, finish or copy your text. Many tool pages keep their inputs in the page address, so a reload restores them (see [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md)).

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: Devanagari text looks like boxes or a plain font
text: Why: your device has no Devanagari font, or not one of those the site asks for. What to do: install a Devanagari font such as Noto Sans Devanagari, or add the Hindi language pack in your operating system's language settings.

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: The site opened in Hindi although I never chose it
text: Why: you followed a link that ended in ?lang=hi , which switches the site to Hindi and remembers it. What to do: select the globe button, or choose English in Settings.

title: Troubleshooting languages
heading: Search does not find anything when I type in Hindi
text: Why: page search matches the English text of pages. What to do: search with English words. Spotlight commands can be found in either language.

title: Language FAQ
heading: Which languages are available?
text: English and Hindi.

title: Language FAQ
heading: Is the Hindi version a separate website?
text: No. Every page has one address, and the same page is shown in the language you chose.

title: Language FAQ
heading: Does switching language change my other settings?
text: No. Theme, accent, text size and your other settings stay as they are.

title: Language FAQ
heading: Does my account remember the language?
text: The language is kept in your browser, not in your account. Choose it once on each browser you use, or open a link with ?lang=hi .

title: Language FAQ
heading: Why are some brand names written in Devanagari?
text: The site writes its own brand and product names in Devanagari so that Hindi pages read in one script. Names of other companies and tools that you would type into a search engine stay in Latin letters.

title: Language FAQ
heading: Can I read an article in Hindi and a tool in English?
text: Not at the same time. The language applies to the whole site in this browser.

text: Term Meaning --- --- Devanagari The script used to write Hindi (हिन्दी). Transliteration Writing a name in another script by its sound, not its meaning, such as ऑरिक आर्टिज़न for Auric Artisan. title: Language limits and accuracy
text: - Coverage. The site's interface and page text are translated across the site. A small number of strings stay in English: terms that are international (such as CIELAB or OKLCH-style colour notations), third-party names, code, and some messages built from several live values. - Emphasis. Where an English heading has part of it styled differently (for example in italics), the Hindi heading may show it as plain text. - Layout. Hindi text can be longer or shorter than English. Lines use slightly taller spacing to keep Devanagari marks clear. - Search. Page search matches English text. - Technical terms. Names used internationally, such as CIELAB, xyY or Bradford, are kept in Latin letters so they match the literature and other tools.

title: Language privacy
text: - Your language choice is kept in this browser's local storage for auricartisan.com. The cookie policy lists it under Functional storage as the language and locale preference. - Switching to Hindi downloads the Hindi text for the pages you open, from auricartisan.com. No text from the page, and nothing you type, is sent anywhere to be translated: translation happens in your browser from those downloaded files. - Nothing about your language is sent to an account.

title: Navigation dock
text: The navigation dock is a slim floating rail on the edge of every page. It gathers the controls you reach for while reading or working: Back , Forward and Reload ; a Page outline that lists the page's headings and jumps to them; Open split view ; Record screen ; Copy link and Share ; and Scroll to top (with a ring that fills as you read) and Scroll to bottom . The dock is independent of the header, so it stays with you as you scroll. When you are not using it, it tucks away to a thin gold line at the edge of the window and slides out when you point at it. You can drag it up or down, and move it to the other side of the screen; it remembers where you put it. On phones it becomes a horizontal bar at the bottom of the screen, opened from the page utilities bar.

title: Navigation dock
heading: Who it is for
text: - Readers of long pages who want to jump between sections or back to the top. - Anyone using the site as an installed app, where the browser's own Back and Reload buttons may be hidden. - People who share pages often.

title: Navigation dock
heading: Where to find it
text: - Desktop and tablets: a thin gold line halfway down the left edge of the window (or the right edge, if you moved it). Point at it to open the dock. - Phones: open the page utilities bar at the bottom-left and select Navigate .

title: Navigation dock
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Move your pointer to the thin line at the left edge of the window. The dock slides out. 2. Select Page outline (the list icon). A panel titled On this page lists the page's headings. 3. Select a heading. The page scrolls to it and the panel closes. 4. Select Scroll to top . The ring around it shows how far down the page you were. 5. Drag the dotted grip at the top of the dock to the right-hand half of the screen. The dock moves to the right edge and stays there on every page. 6. Move your pointer away. After a moment the dock tucks back into a thin line.

title: Navigation dock
heading: What you can do
text: - Go back, go forward and reload, even when the browser's own buttons are hidden. - Jump to any heading on the page and see which section you are in. - Open split view or the screen recorder. - Copy the page link, including what you have changed on the page, or share it. - Scroll to the top or bottom, and see your reading progress. - Move the dock and keep it where you like.

title: Get started with the navigation dock
Get started with the navigation dock
heading: Open the dock
text: When a page loads on a computer, the dock shows fully for a moment and then tucks itself away into a thin gold line at the edge of the window. To bring it back: - point at the line; or - click it; or - move keyboard focus into it with Tab . It tucks away again about half a second after your pointer leaves, unless the page outline is open or a button in the dock has keyboard focus. On a phone, open the page utilities bar at the bottom-left and select Navigate .

title: Get started with the navigation dock
heading: The buttons
text: From top to bottom (left to right on a phone): Button What it does --- --- Grip (six dots) Drag to move the dock. Tooltip: "Drag to move". Not shown on phones. Back Goes back one page. Greyed out when there is nothing to go back to. Forward Goes forward one page. Greyed out when there is nothing ahead. Reload Reloads the page. Page outline Opens the On this page list of headings. Open split view Opens split view with this page (see [Split view](../../split-view/README.md)). Record screen (Alt+Shift+R) Opens the screen recorder (see [Screen recorder](../../screen-recorder/README.md)). Copy link Copies the page's address. The icon briefly becomes a tick. Share Opens your device's share sheet; without one, copies the link and shows a tick. Scroll to top Scrolls smoothly to the top. The ring around it shows how far down you are. Scroll to bottom Scrolls smoothly to the end of the page. Flip dock side Moves the dock to the other edge. Not shown on phones. Hover or focus a button to see its name in a tooltip. Note: Copy link and Share copy the address exactly as it is in the address bar, which can include the page's remembered state, such as your scroll position and the values you typed into a tool. See [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md).

title: Get started with the navigation dock
heading: Try it
text: 1. Open a long page, such as https://auricartisan.com/company/about/. 2. Scroll halfway down. Point at the dock: the ring around Scroll to top is half full. 3. Select Page outline . The heading of the section you are reading is highlighted. 4. Select the first heading. The page scrolls up to it. 5. Select Copy link and paste the address somewhere. Opening it later returns you to the same place on the page.

title: Move and collapse the dock
heading: Move the dock up or down
text: 1. Point at the dock so it opens. 2. Press and hold the grip (six dots) at its top. 3. Drag up or down. The dock can sit anywhere between 10% and 90% of the window's height. 4. Let go. Result: the dock stays at that height on every page, in this browser.

title: Move and collapse the dock
heading: Move the dock to the other side
text: Either: - drag the grip across the middle of the window, then let go; or - select Flip dock side (the arrow at the bottom of the dock). Result: the dock moves to the other edge and stays there on every page. The outline panel opens on the side facing the page.

title: Move and collapse the dock
heading: How the dock collapses
text: On screens wider than 700 pixels: - after a page loads, the dock stays open for about 1.6 seconds so you can see it, then collapses; - collapsed, it is a thin gold line, 64 pixels tall, flush with the edge. It is faint until you point at it; - it opens when you point at it, click it or tab into it, and collapses about half a second after you move away; - it stays open while the page outline is open, while you are dragging it, and while a button in it has keyboard focus.

title: Move and collapse the dock
heading: On a phone
text: On screens 700 pixels wide or narrower: - the dock is a horizontal bar centred at the bottom of the screen. If its buttons do not fit, swipe it sideways; - the grip and Flip dock side are not shown, and the dock cannot be dragged; - it starts collapsed. Open it from the page utilities bar with Navigate (on the narrowest phones this is the only way). On slightly wider screens, a round button with a list icon ( Show navigation ) also opens it; - it closes again when you tap anywhere outside it, and a dock opened with its round button closes by itself after about five seconds.

title: Move and collapse the dock
heading: When the dock is hidden
text: - While the screen saver or an eye rest is showing. - While the mobile drawer is open. - Inside the panes of split view, which have their own toolbar. - On the sign-in and verification pages.

title: Jump around with the page outline
text: The Page outline button opens a panel titled On this page beside the dock. It lists the headings of the page you are on and highlights the one you are reading.

title: Jump around with the page outline
heading: Open the outline and jump to a section
text: 1. Point at the dock and select Page outline (the list icon). 2. The On this page panel opens. Main headings are listed normally; sub-headings are indented and slightly smaller. 3. The heading of the section you are reading is highlighted in the accent colour. As you scroll, the highlight moves with you. 4. Select a heading. Result: the page scrolls smoothly to that heading, leaving room for the site header above it, and the panel closes.

title: Jump around with the page outline
heading: Close the outline
text: Select Page outline again, press Esc , or click anywhere outside the panel and the dock.

title: Jump around with the page outline
heading: What the outline lists
text: - The main headings and their sub-headings (heading levels 1, 2 and 3) in the page's main content. - Headings in the header, footer and navigation areas are left out, as are hidden headings and headings longer than 90 characters. - The list is rebuilt every time you open it, so headings that appear later (for example in a tool's results) are included. - On a page without headings, the panel reads "No sections on this page".

title: Jump around with the page outline
heading: Other outlines on the site
text: Long company, pricing, legal and security pages also have a section rail pinned under the header. It is described in [Guide and page outline](../../guide-and-page-outline/docs/section-rail.md). The page guide ( ? ) lists the page's tour stops. See [Guide and page outline](../../guide-and-page-outline/README.md).

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: I cannot find the dock
text: Why: it collapses to a thin, faint line at the edge of the window a moment after the page loads. On phones it has no visible button on the narrowest screens. What to do: look halfway down the left edge (or the right edge, if you moved it) and point at the line. On a phone, open the page utilities bar and select Navigate .

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: The dock closes before I can use it
text: Why: it collapses half a second after the pointer leaves it. What to do: keep the pointer over the dock, or tab into it with the keyboard; it stays open while a button in it has focus. The outline keeps it open too.

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: Back and Forward are greyed out
text: Why: there is no page in that direction in this tab's history. If you opened the page in a new tab, there is nothing to go back to.

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: Share only copied the link
text: Why: your browser or device has no share sheet available to web pages, so the dock copies the link instead and shows a tick. What to do: paste the link into the app you want to share it with.

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: The copied link is very long
text: Why: the address includes the page's remembered state after p= , such as your scroll position and values you entered. See [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md). What to do: to share a clean link, scroll to the top of the page and clear any values you typed before copying, or delete the part from p= onwards after pasting.

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: The outline says "No sections on this page"
text: Why: the page's main content has no headings the outline can list. What to do: use Scroll to top and Scroll to bottom , or the page guide ( ? ).

title: Troubleshooting the navigation dock
heading: The dock covers part of the page
text: What to do: drag it up or down with the grip, or move it to the other side with Flip dock side . On a phone, tap outside it to close it.

title: Navigation dock FAQ
heading: Can I turn the dock off?
text: There is no switch to remove it. It collapses to a thin line when you are not using it, and you can move it wherever it is least in the way.

title: Navigation dock FAQ
heading: Can I keep the dock open all the time?
text: No. On desktop it opens when you point at it or tab into it, and collapses when you move away.

title: Navigation dock FAQ
heading: Does the dock work in the installed app?
text: Yes. It is especially useful there, where the browser's own Back, Forward and Reload buttons may not be visible.

title: Navigation dock FAQ
heading: Is the dock the same as the header menus?
text: No. The header takes you to other pages; the dock moves you around the page you are on and through your history.

title: Navigation dock FAQ
heading: Why is there no dock inside split view?
text: Each pane of split view has its own Back, Forward and Reload buttons, so the dock stays out of the panes.

title: Screen recorder
text: Every page on auricartisan.com has a built-in recorder. Press Alt + Shift + R , choose what to record, and start. You can capture: - Screen or window — any screen, window or tab you pick in your browser's sharing dialog; - This tab — the page you are on; - Region of this page — a rectangle you draw, or a part of the page you click; - Tool canvas — a tool's drawing surface, captured pixel for pixel. While you record, a small bar shows the time and file size, with pause, stop and discard buttons. When you stop, the recording is kept on your device under My recordings , where you can play it, rename it, trim it, and export it as a video file, an animated GIF, a ZIP of PNG frames or a single PNG still. Recordings are made and stored entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

title: Screen recorder
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers and developers showing a tool, a palette or a bug to someone else. - Teachers and writers making short clips or GIFs of colour tools. - Anyone filing a bug report who wants to show what happened.

title: Screen recorder
heading: Where to find it
text: - Press Alt + Shift + R on any page. - Select Record screen in the navigation dock. The recorder works in desktop browsers that let web pages capture the screen, such as Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Mobile browsers generally cannot capture the screen; the Tool canvas source can still work where a page has a canvas.

title: Screen recorder
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Alt + Shift + R . The Your Recorder dialog opens. 2. Under Recording source , choose This tab . 3. Leave the capture settings as they are and select Start recording . 4. Your browser asks to share this tab. Allow it. 5. After a 3-second countdown, recording starts and the recording bar appears. 6. Do what you want to show, then select Stop and save on the bar (or press Alt + Shift + R ). 7. My recordings opens with your new clip at the top. Select GIF to export it as an animated GIF.

title: Screen recorder
heading: What you can do
text: - Record a screen, window, tab, page region or tool canvas. - Choose frame rate, quality, maximum resolution and a countdown. - Add microphone narration and the page's own sound; highlight the pointer. - Pause, resume, stop or discard a recording. - Play, rename, trim, download and delete recordings. - Export an animated GIF, a ZIP of PNG frames or a PNG still.

title: Get started with the screen recorder
Get started with the screen recorder
heading: Open the recorder
text: - Press Alt + Shift + R on any page. - Or point at the navigation dock and select Record screen (Alt+Shift+R) . The first time, the recorder takes a moment to load. The Your Recorder dialog opens. It floats over the page without blocking it.

title: Get started with the screen recorder
heading: A tour of the dialog
text: 1. Header. A grip to move the dialog, the title Your Recorder , Reset dialog position and Close . 2. Recording source (choose what enters the frame): Screen or window , This tab , Region of this page , Tool canvas . Each has a one-line description. A source the page or browser cannot use is greyed out with the reason. 3. Capture settings (video output): Frame rate , Quality , Resolution cap and Countdown . 4. Audio & pointer (optional capture layers): Microphone , Tab audio and Highlight the cursor . 5. A note saying which video format this browser records: "Recording to MP4 — plays anywhere." or "Recording to WebM. Export to GIF or frames from My recordings." 6. Footer. My recordings , Reset setup , the Alt Shift R reminder, and Start recording . Your choices are remembered for next time.

title: Get started with the screen recorder
heading: Your first recording
text: 1. Open the recorder. 2. Choose Screen or window . 3. Select Start recording . Your browser's sharing dialog opens. 4. Pick the window or screen to record and confirm. 5. A large countdown (3, 2, 1) shows on the page. Recording then starts, and the recording bar appears with a timer and the file size so far. 6. Select Stop and save on the bar, press Alt + Shift + R , or use your browser's own Stop sharing button. Result: a message such as "Recording saved — 00:42, 6.3 MB." appears, and My recordings opens with the new clip highlighted.

title: Get started with the screen recorder
heading: Move or reset the dialog
text: - Drag the header to move the dialog. With the grip focused, the arrow keys move it; hold Shift for finer steps. - Reset dialog position , or a double-click on the grip, returns it to the centre ("Recorder returned to the center."). - On narrow screens the dialog cannot be dragged.

title: Get started with the screen recorder
heading: Close the dialog
text: Select Close or press Esc . If a drop-down list in the dialog is open, the first Esc closes the list.

title: My recordings and export
text: My recordings lists every recording kept in this browser. It opens after each recording, or from My recordings in the recorder dialog.

title: My recordings and export
heading: The list
text: The panel header has a grip to move it, the title My recordings , New recording (opens the setup dialog) and Close . Esc closes it. Each recording shows: - a thumbnail; select it to play the recording; - its title, which you can edit in place (an empty title becomes "Untitled recording"); - details: length, file size, pixel size, and "with audio" when it has sound; - actions: Download video , GIF , Frames , Still , Trim and Delete . The foot of the panel shows the total, for example "4 recordings · 38.2 MB used · 1.1 GB free". With no recordings, the panel reads "No recordings yet." with a Record something button.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Play a recording
text: Select the thumbnail. A player opens with the recording's title and standard video controls. Esc or Close closes it.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Download the video
text: Select Download video . The file downloads as MP4 or WebM, whichever format this browser recorded.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Export an animated GIF
text: 1. Select GIF (Export as an animated GIF). 2. A progress bar shows "Encoding GIF…". 3. The GIF downloads, and the message gives its size, for example "GIF exported — 2.4 MB." GIFs are made at 10 frames per second, at most 640 pixels wide, with up to 300 frames, and they loop. Longer recordings are sampled evenly across their length.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Export frames
text: Select Frames (Export every frame as PNG (ZIP)). A progress bar shows "Exporting frames…", then a ZIP file downloads containing PNG images named frame-0001.png , frame-0002.png and so on. Frames are taken five times per second, at most 1,280 pixels wide, up to 120 frames.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Save a still
text: Select Still (Save the current frame as a PNG). A progress bar shows "Grabbing frame…", then a PNG downloads. The still is taken one second into the recording (or halfway through a recording shorter than two seconds), at most 1,280 pixels wide.

title: My recordings and export
heading: Trim a recording
text: 1. Select Trim . The player opens with the trim controls showing (or select Trim… in the player). 2. Enter Start and End in seconds (to one decimal place). End starts as the full length. 3. Select Export trimmed clip . 4. The trimmed clip downloads as a new file with "-trimmed" added to its title: "Trimmed clip exported." Trimming re-encodes in real time, so a 30-second clip takes about 30 seconds. The original recording is not changed. If End is not after Start , the message reads "End must be after start."

title: My recordings and export
heading: Delete a recording
text: Select Delete (the bin), then select it again within four seconds ("Click again to delete permanently"). The recording is removed from this browser. This cannot be undone.

title: My recordings and export
heading: File names
text: Downloads are named from the recording's title and the time it was made, for example Recording-Sep-24-1042-AM-2026-09-24-05-12-33.mp4 . The date in the title follows your browser's language settings; the time stamp at the end is in UTC. Characters other than letters, numbers, spaces and hyphens are removed, spaces become hyphens, and the title part is limited to 48 characters.

title: My recordings and export
heading: If an export fails
text: The message explains why, for example "That recording could not be read.", "No frames could be read from that recording." or "The ZIP library could not be loaded." (frames export needs to load a small helper from the site the first time).

Either drag a rectangle, or move over the page (a box outlines the element under the pointer) and click to use that element. 4. Your browser asks to share this tab. Allow it. Only the region is recorded; the rest of the tab is cropped away. A click or a very small drag (under 12 pixels) counts as choosing the element under the pointer.

title: Record a take

Collapse to a dot / Expand controls Shrinks the bar to a small dot, or restores it; remembered Click a collapsed dot to expand it again.

title: Record a take
heading: When a recording stops by itself
text: - Your browser's own Stop sharing button ends the recording and saves it. - A recording stops at 30 minutes : "Time limit reached — recording stopped." - If you try to leave or reload the page during a recording, the browser asks you to confirm.

text: - The recording is saved to My recordings , titled "Recording" with the date and time, and the list opens with it highlighted. - If there is little browser storage left (under about 50 MB), the recorder warns before you start: "Storage is nearly full — this recording may not save. Delete some clips first." - If the browser refuses to store it, the file is downloaded straight away instead: "Saved to your downloads (browser storage was unavailable)." - If nothing was captured, the message reads "Nothing was recorded."

heading: Reset your setup

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: The screen sources are greyed out
text: Why: "This browser cannot capture the screen." Most mobile browsers, and some older desktop browsers, do not let web pages capture the screen. What to do: use a current desktop browser such as Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or use Tool canvas on a tool page.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: Tool canvas is greyed out
text: Why: "No recordable canvas on this page." The page has no visible canvas larger than 80 by 80 pixels. What to do: open a tool that draws on a canvas, or choose another source.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: Nothing happened after Start recording
text: Why: you cancelled or closed your browser's sharing dialog, or denied permission. What to do: select Start recording again and allow sharing. If you denied it permanently, allow screen sharing for auricartisan.com in your browser's site settings.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: The recording bar is in my video
text: Why: with This tab , the bar is part of the page, so it is recorded. What to do: collapse it to a dot, record a Region of this page that leaves it out, or use Screen or window and pick another window.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: There is no sound
text: Possible causes: - Tab audio was off, or the page made no sound. - In your browser's sharing dialog, the option to share audio was not ticked (some browsers only offer audio for tabs). - The microphone was refused ("Microphone unavailable — recording without it.").

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: The recording stopped by itself
text: Why: it reached 30 minutes, you pressed your browser's Stop sharing , or the shared window was closed.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: The recording was downloaded instead of saved
text: Why: the browser refused to store it, usually because storage is full or the browser is in a private mode. What to do: delete old recordings in My recordings , or keep the downloaded file.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: Exporting a GIF is slow or the GIF is large
text: Why: GIFs are made in your browser and hold every frame as an image. What to do: trim the recording first, record at a lower resolution, or download the video instead.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: Trimming takes a long time
text: Why: trimming re-encodes the clip in real time, so it takes as long as the part you keep.

title: Troubleshooting the screen recorder
heading: My recordings disappeared
text: Why: they are stored in this browser. Clearing site data, using a private window, or a different browser or profile means they are not there. What to do: download recordings you want to keep.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Are my recordings uploaded?
text: No. They are recorded and stored in your browser on this device. They leave it only when you download them.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Are recordings saved in my Library?
text: No. Recordings have their own list, My recordings , separate from the library of palettes and assets.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Can I record other websites or apps?
text: Yes, with Screen or window : your browser lets you pick any screen, window or tab to share.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Why MP4 in one browser and WebM in another?
text: The recorder uses MP4 where the browser can record it, because it plays almost everywhere. Otherwise it records WebM. The dialog tells you which.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Can I keep recording while I move to another page on the site?
text: No. Leaving or reloading the page ends the recording; the browser asks you to confirm first. Record with Screen or window if you need to move between pages, and pick the browser window.

title: Screen recorder FAQ
heading: Does the custom cursor appear in recordings?
text: Yes, when you record the page itself. Switch it off in Settings › Comfort for a clean system pointer, and use Highlight the cursor if you want the pointer emphasised.

title: Screen recorder glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Source What the recorder captures: a screen or window, this tab, a region, or a tool canvas. Take One recording, from start to stop. Frame rate (fps) How many images per second a video holds. Higher is smoother and larger. Resolution cap The largest width a recording is allowed; bigger sources are scaled down. Canvas A drawing surface that tools use for graphics and animation. Region A rectangle of the page, or one element, that a recording is cropped to. MP4, WebM Video file formats. MP4 plays almost everywhere; WebM is widely supported by browsers. GIF An animated image format that plays in most apps and web pages without a player. Re-encode To play a video and record it again, which is how trimming makes a new file. Sharing dialog The browser's own window asking which screen, window or tab to share.

title: Screen recorder limits and accuracy
text: - Length. A recording stops at 30 minutes. - Storage. Recordings use your browser's storage for this site, which the browser limits. A minute of high-resolution video can take several megabytes to tens of megabytes. The list shows how much is used and free. - Video length metadata. Browsers do not always write a length into recorded files. Some players may show an unknown length or seek slowly in a downloaded WebM file; the recorder's own player and exports account for this. - GIF. Up to 300 frames at 10 per second and 640 pixels wide, with at most 255 colours. Long recordings are sampled, not played frame by frame, and subtle gradients can band. - Frames. Up to 120 PNG images, five per second, up to 1,280 pixels wide. It is a sampling of the recording, not every frame. - Trim. Runs in real time and makes a new file; the quality matches the original recording's format. - Region crop. Where the browser can crop the shared tab itself, it does so; otherwise the recorder crops each frame, which uses more processing power. - Browser support. Screen capture depends on the browser. Most mobile browsers cannot capture the screen.

title: Screen recorder privacy
text: - Permission first. Nothing is captured until you start a recording and, for screen, window, tab and region sources, allow sharing in your browser's dialog. The microphone is used only if you switch it on and allow it. - What is captured. Exactly what you shared: a screen or window can include other apps, notifications and personal information. Check what is visible before you record. - Where recordings live. In your browser's storage for auricartisan.com, on this device only. They are not uploaded, not added to your account and not placed in your Library. - Sharing. A recording leaves your device only when you download it and send the file yourself. - Preferences. Your recorder settings and the dialog position are kept in this browser. - Deleting. Delete in My recordings removes a recording. Clearing site data for auricartisan.com removes them all.

title: Screen saver
text: The screen saver is an optional idle screen. When you have not touched the page for a while, it fills the window with a single colour from the site's colour atlas, laid out as seven bands from its darkest shade to its lightest, with the colour itself sitting on its own step. A readout names the colour and gives its hex code, its OKLCH value, the mood it reads as, the art movement associated with it, and its contrast against black. A new colour arrives every twelve seconds, and a small clock shows the time. Move the mouse, press a key, scroll or touch the screen, and the page comes back exactly as you left it. The screen saver is off by default . You choose whether it runs and how long the page must be idle first (1, 5, 10, 20 or 30 minutes).

title: Screen saver
heading: Who it is for
text: People who leave the site open on a second screen or in a studio, and anyone who enjoys a slow tour of the site's colour atlas.

title: Screen saver
heading: Where to find it
text: Settings ( Ctrl + , ) › Comfort › Screen saver .

title: Screen saver
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , and select Comfort . 2. Switch on Screen saver . 3. Under Start after , select 1m to try it. 4. Leave the page alone for a minute or so. 5. The screen fills with a colour and its readout. Wait twelve seconds to see the next one. 6. Move the mouse. The page returns.

title: Screen saver
heading: What you can do
text: - Turn the screen saver on or off. - Choose how long the page must be idle before it starts. - Read the name, hex, OKLCH, mood, movement and contrast of a new colour every twelve seconds.

title: Get started with the screen saver
Get started with the screen saver
heading: Turn it on
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , to open Settings, then select Comfort . 2. Switch on Screen saver ("Ambient animation after long periods of inactivity."). 3. Under Start after (minutes of inactivity), select 1m , 5m , 10m , 20m or 30m . The default is 10m .

title: Get started with the screen saver
heading: When it starts
text: The screen saver starts when the page has had no mouse movement, click, key press, scroll, touch or wheel movement for the time you chose. The site checks every ten seconds, so it can start up to about ten seconds after the time is reached. It counts activity on this page only. Time spent in other tabs or apps counts as idle time for this page, so the screen saver may already be showing when you come back to the tab.

title: Get started with the screen saver
heading: Return to the page
text: Do any of these: move the mouse, click, press a key, scroll, use the wheel, or touch the screen. The page comes back as you left it. A hint, Move to return , shows at the bottom of the screen saver for its first minute, then fades.

title: Get started with the screen saver
heading: Turn it off
text: Switch off Screen saver in Settings › Comfort. If it is showing at that moment (for example in another window you can see), it closes at once.

title: Reading the screen
heading: The colour bands
text: The whole screen is seven bands of one colour, from its darkest shade to its lightest. On a wide screen the bands run side by side; on a narrow or portrait screen they run top to bottom. - The bands are steps of lightness in OKLCH: 0.22, 0.35, 0.48, 0.61, 0.74, 0.85 and 0.94. Each band shows its step number. - The fourth band (0.61) is the colour's own step, marked as the sample. - The darkest step is pure black for every colour. - Colourfulness tapers towards both ends, because very dark and very light shades cannot hold a strong colour. - Each step number sits on a small chip that keeps it readable on its band. OKLCH describes a colour by its lightness (L), chroma or colourfulness (C) and hue (H), in a way that follows how people see colour. Stepping lightness in OKLCH gives even-looking shades.

title: Troubleshooting the screen saver
heading: The screen saver never starts
text: Possible causes and fixes: - It is off. Switch on Screen saver in Settings › Comfort. - Something keeps registering as activity, for example a mouse that drifts slightly or a page that scrolls itself. Keep the mouse still. - A few pages do not include the screen saver. Try another page. - The idle check runs every ten seconds, so allow a few seconds beyond your chosen time.

title: Troubleshooting the screen saver
heading: It starts too soon or too late
text: What to do: change Start after in Settings › Comfort. The new time applies at the next check.

title: Troubleshooting the screen saver
heading: My computer's own screen saver or sleep takes over first
text: Why: your operating system's power settings are separate from the site. If the system dims or sleeps sooner than the site's delay, you will not see the site's screen saver. What to do: choose a shorter Start after , or a longer delay in your system settings.

title: Troubleshooting the screen saver
heading: The colour readout is missing and only a plain colour shows
text: Why: the colour list is downloaded the first time the screen saver starts. If that fails, the screen saver uses a small built-in set of colours instead. What to do: nothing is needed; it still works. Check your connection if you want the full atlas.

title: Screen saver FAQ
heading: Does the screen saver stop my computer from sleeping?
text: No. It is part of the web page. Your computer's own power and sleep settings still apply.

title: Screen saver FAQ
heading: Can I choose which colours it shows?
text: No. It picks a random starting colour from the atlas and moves on every twelve seconds.

title: Screen saver FAQ
heading: Where do the colours come from?
text: From the site's colour atlas of 8,192 named colours, each with a mood and an art movement associated with it.

title: Screen saver FAQ
heading: Does it use much power?
text: It is drawn with plain page elements rather than animation-heavy graphics, and it pauses while its tab is hidden.

title: Screen saver FAQ
heading: Is the screen saver the same as eye rest?
text: No. Eye rest reminds you to look away while you are working; the screen saver appears when you have stopped. See [Eye rest](../../eye-rest/README.md).

title: Screen saver: supporting material
text: File What it covers --- --- [glossary.md](glossary.md) Terms used in the screen saver guides [limits-and-accuracy.md](limits-and-accuracy.md) What the readout's values mean and how precise they are [related.md](related.md) Related features and libraries [privacy.md](privacy.md) What the screen saver stores and downloads The screen saver has no keyboard shortcut: any key press closes it.

title: Screen saver glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Idle No mouse, keyboard, scroll, wheel or touch activity on the page. Colour atlas The site's collection of 8,192 named colours with mood and movement notes. OKLCH A way of writing colour as lightness (L), chroma (C) and hue (H) that follows human perception. Lightness step One of the seven bands, each a fixed OKLCH lightness from 0.22 to 0.94. Chroma How colourful a colour is, from grey (0) upwards. Contrast on black The WCAG contrast ratio between the colour and pure black.

title: Screen saver limits and accuracy
text: - Values. The OKLCH values are shown to two decimal places for lightness and chroma and to whole degrees for hue. The contrast against black uses the WCAG 2 formula, to two decimal places. - Shades. The seven bands are drawn in OKLCH where your browser supports it; very colourful shades may be outside what your screen can show and are drawn as close as the screen allows. - Mood and movement. "reads as" and "movement" are descriptive notes from the colour atlas, not measurements. - Timing. The idle check runs every ten seconds, so the screen saver can start up to about ten seconds after your chosen delay. - Scope. It runs only in the page's own tab and does not replace your operating system's screen saver or power settings.

title: Screen saver privacy
text: - Your on or off choice and delay are kept in this browser, as part of your settings. - The screen saver watches for activity only to know when you are idle. It does not record or send what you do. - The first time it starts, it downloads a small list of atlas colours from auricartisan.com. Nothing is sent in return.

title: Related to the screen saver
text: - [Settings panel › Comfort options](../../settings-panel/docs/comfort-options.md) — the switch and the delay. - [Settings panel › Highlights and clock](../../settings-panel/docs/highlights-and-clock.md) — the 24-hour setting used by its clock. - [Eye rest](../../eye-rest/README.md) — reminders to look away while you work. - [Colour libraries](../../../library/colour-libraries/README.md) — the site's colour collections, including the Color Library.

title: Search and Spotlight
text: Spotlight is the search box that floats over any page when you press Ctrl + K ( Cmd + K on a Mac) or select Search in the header. Type a few letters and it lists matching pages, tools, documentation and Learn articles from across the site, with a preview of the highlighted result and the reasons it ranked there. Tabs narrow the search to Pages , Tools , Docs or Learn , and a Web tab searches trusted sources beyond the site. Spotlight also answers some questions directly. Type a hex colour such as 2f5eaa and it shows that colour's values and its contrast on black and white. Type two hex colours and it judges them as a text-and-background pair against WCAG. Type and it becomes a command palette that can switch the theme, open the guide, the library or Settings, switch language, and more. For a larger results page with filters, Spotlight hands your query to the full search page at https://auricartisan.com/search/, which is documented in [Search](../../search/README.md).

title: Search and Spotlight
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone looking for a tool, article or page without browsing the menus. - Keyboard users who want to reach site actions without the mouse. - Designers who want a quick reading of a colour or a colour pair.

title: Search and Spotlight
heading: Where to find it
text: - Press Ctrl + K ( Cmd + K ) on any page. - Select the magnifier ( Search ) in the header, or Search on a narrow screen. - In the mobile drawer, tap Search tools, colours and pages . - Right-click the page and choose Site , then Search the site .

title: Search and Spotlight
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + K . Spotlight opens with your recent searches and a list of Quick Actions . 2. Type gamut . Results appear as you type, with matching words highlighted. 3. Press Down to move through the results. The preview on the right shows each one. 4. Press Enter to open the highlighted result, or Ctrl + Enter to open it in a new tab. 5. Press Ctrl + K again and type d3af37 . The preview shows the colour, its RGB value and its contrast on black and white. 6. Clear the box, type , and choose Toggle light and dark . 7. Press Esc to clear the box, and Esc again to close Spotlight.

title: Search and Spotlight
heading: What you can do
text: - Search the whole site, or only pages, tools, documentation or Learn articles. - Search trusted sources on the wider web. - Re-run recent searches. - Read a colour's values and contrast, or check a colour pair against WCAG, straight from the search box. - Use field filters such as title: and path: . - Run site commands with . - Open the full search page for more results and filters.

title: Get started with Spotlight
heading: Open and close Spotlight
text: - Open: press Ctrl + K ( Cmd + K on a Mac), or select Search in the header. - Close: press Esc (the first press clears what you typed, the second closes), press Ctrl + K again, or click the dimmed page around Spotlight. While Spotlight is open, the page behind it does not scroll.

title: Get started with Spotlight
heading: The parts of Spotlight
text: 1. Search box. A magnifier, an optional mode chip (for example Colour or Command ), the text box, an ESC hint and an X to clear the box. The box's placeholder names the current scope, for example "Search Auric Artisan…". 2. Scope tabs. All , Pages , Tools , Docs , Learn and Web . 3. Results list on the left. 4. Preview pane on the right. It shows details of the highlighted result, or the answer when you type a colour. 5. Footer. Key hints ( ↑ ↓ navigate, ↵ open, TAB filter, ESC close) and, on the right, a count such as "12 results · 3ms".

title: Get started with Spotlight
heading: Your first search
text: 1. Open Spotlight. Before you type, it shows: - Recent : up to six of your recent searches, with a Clear button; - Quick Actions : shortcuts to Full Search, Collections, URL Analyzer, Color Science Lab, Documentation, Learn Color, Vision Simulations, Install the PWA and Install Extension. 2. Type at least two characters, for example contrast . 3. Results appear under Results . Each shows an icon for its kind, the title with your words highlighted, a short excerpt and the page address. 4. Move through them with Up and Down , or point at them. The preview pane shows the highlighted page's type, title, address, description and a Why it ranks here chart. 5. Press Enter to open the highlighted result. Hold Ctrl ( Cmd on a Mac) as you press Enter to open it in a new tab. Result: the page opens and Spotlight closes. Your search is added to Recent . The first time you open Spotlight on a page, it prepares the site index in the background. For a moment the list may read "Search engine is loading…"; results then appear as you type.

title: Get started with Spotlight
heading: Go further
text: - At the foot of the results, View all results for "…" opens the full search page with filters and previews. - Press Tab to move to the next scope tab. See [Scopes and results](scopes-and-results.md). - Type a hex colour or two. See [Colour answers and filters](colour-answers-and-filters.md). - Type for commands. See [Commands](commands.md).

title: Colour answers and filters
text: Spotlight reads what you type and, for some kinds of query, answers directly. A small mode chip at the start of the search box says how it read your query. You type Chip What Spotlight does --- --- --- Ordinary words none Searches the site One hex colour, such as 2f5eaa Colour Shows the colour's values in the preview Two hex colours, such as ffffff 2f5eaa Contrast pair Judges the pair against WCAG in the preview followed by anything Command Lists commands (see [Commands](commands.md)) A field filter such as title:gamut title:gamut Searches only that field

title: Colour answers and filters
heading: Read a colour
text: 1. Open Spotlight and type a colour as and six hex digits, for example 2f5eaa , with nothing else. 2. The chip reads Colour . The preview pane shows: - a swatch of the colour with its OKLCH value; - Hex , RGB , On black and On white (the WCAG contrast ratio of the colour against black and against white); - a link, Check it against a background , which opens the Contrast Checker with this colour. 3. The list shows Pages that mention it (up to three pages whose text contains that hex code), or the note "Nothing in the index mentions this colour by name — the answer is on the right."

title: Colour answers and filters
heading: Check a colour pair
text: 1. Type two hex colours, for example ffffff 2f5eaa . The first is treated as the text colour and the second as the background. 2. The chip reads Contrast pair . The preview pane shows: - two swatches with "Aa" drawn in each colour on the other; - the contrast ratio; - three verdicts: AA body (pass or fail at 4.5), AAA body (7.0) and AA large (3.0); - Open in the checker , which opens the Contrast Checker with both colours. Only six-digit hex codes with a are recognised. Three-digit codes, colour names and other formats are searched as text.

title: Colour answers and filters
heading: Field filters
text: Start the query with a field name and a colon to search one part of each page: Filter Searches --- --- title: Page titles desc: Page descriptions tag: Page tags path: Page addresses, for example path:/tool/ type: The kind of content category: The page category Put a phrase in quotes after the colon to match it exactly, for example title:"colour vision" . The chip shows the filter you used.

title: Colour answers and filters
heading: Phrases and exclusions
text: - Put words in double quotes to require that exact phrase: "contrast ratio" . - Put a minus sign before a word to leave out pages that contain it: palette -gradient . These work in the full search page too.

title: Scopes and results
heading: Scope tabs
text: The tabs under the search box decide where Spotlight looks. The box's placeholder changes to match. Tab Searches Placeholder --- --- --- All Everything on the site Search Auric Artisan… Pages Site pages such as home, collections, company and security (not tools, documentation or Learn) Search pages… Tools Every tool page Search tools… Docs Documentation and developer references Search documentation… Learn Learn colour-science guides Search learn guides… Web Trusted sources on the wider web Search the web… Switch scope by selecting a tab, or press Tab (next) and Shift + Tab (previous) while the search box has focus. Your query re-runs in the new scope at once. Spotlight remembers the scope you chose until you reload the page. With an empty box, each scope shows its own launch points: Scope Heading Launchers --- --- --- All Quick Actions Full Search, Collections, URL Analyzer, Color Science Lab, Documentation, Learn Color, Vision Simulations, Install the PWA, Install Extension Pages Jump to Pages Home, Collections, About, Pricing, FAQ, Contact, Security Tools Jump to Tools URL Analyzer, Color Science Lab, Vision Simulations, ASCII, Ishihara Plates, General Tools Docs Jump to Docs Documentation Home, Changelog Learn Jump to Learn Learn Color, Blog Web Web search A hint: "Type at least 2 characters to search trusted sources across the web."

title: Scopes and results
heading: Reading the results
text: - Searching starts once you have typed two characters. - Up to 8 results are listed, under Results . The footer shows the total and how long the search took, for example "23 results · 2ms". - Each result shows an icon for its kind (page, documentation, tool, article and so on), the title with your words highlighted, an excerpt, and the page address. - The last row, View all results for "…" , opens https://auricartisan.com/search/ with your query, where you can see every result with filters and previews.

title: Scopes and results
heading: The preview pane
text: When a result is highlighted (by the arrow keys or by pointing at it), the pane on the right shows: - the kind of page, its title, address and description; - Why it ranks here : up to four bars, one for each part of the page your words matched (such as its title, tags, description or body text), each labelled with how heavily that part counts, for example ×6 for the title. Longer bars contributed more.

title: Scopes and results
heading: When nothing is found
text: The list reads "No results for "…"", with "in Pages" (or the scope you chose) when a scope is active. Under Try instead : - Show all N results — shown when the query matches elsewhere on the site but not in this scope. Selecting it switches to All . - Search the web for "…" — switches to the Web tab. - Open full search page — opens the full search page with your query.

title: Scopes and results
heading: Searching the web
text: The Web tab searches a curated set of trusted sources beyond auricartisan.com. 1. Select Web (or Search the web for "…" under Try instead ). 2. Type at least two characters. The list reads "Searching trusted sources…". 3. Up to 8 results appear, each with its title, an excerpt and the source's name. The footer shows the count, the time taken and how many pages were checked. 4. Select a result. It opens in a new tab. If the web search service cannot be reached, the list reads "Global search is unavailable right now". If no trusted source matches, it reads "No trusted web results for "…"". Web search needs a network connection.

title: Scopes and results
heading: Recent searches
text: - When you open a result, the query that found it (if at least two characters) is added to Recent , most recent first. Up to six are kept, without duplicates. - Recent shows whenever the box is empty. Select an entry to run it again. - Select Clear beside the heading to remove them all. Recent searches are kept in this browser only.

title: Scopes and results
heading: How results are ranked
text: Results are ranked by how well your words match, with more weight for matches in the title and tags than in the body text. Pages whose title starts with or contains your whole query rank higher, and pages that you have opened from search before get a small boost in this browser. Close spelling mistakes are still matched, and common alternative words are understood: for example color finds "colour", a11y finds accessibility pages, and audit finds the Analyzer.

title: Commands
text: Type at the start of the Spotlight box to switch to command mode . The chip reads Command , and the list shows actions you can run on this page instead of pages you can open.

title: Commands
heading: Run a command
text: 1. Press Ctrl + K and type . 2. The list shows every command available on this page, under the heading Commands . The footer counts them, for example "7 commands". 3. Keep typing to narrow the list, for example theme . 4. Select a command, or highlight it and press Enter . If nothing matches, the list reads "No command matches that on this page."

title: Commands
heading: The site's commands
text: Command Description Shows --- --- --- Toggle light and dark The header's theme button The current theme, and ⌥T Open the page guide What this page is, and its tour — Open the library Saved palettes, gradients and reports — Open settings Theme, motion, density, language ⌘, Switch language English ⇄ हिन्दी The current language Open the full search page The whole index, with filters and instant answers — Install the app Offline cache and an app window — A command appears only when the page has the control it drives. For example, Open the library is missing on a page without the library button. The key hints are shown in Mac notation: ⌥T is Alt + T , and ⌘, is Ctrl + , on Windows and Linux.

title: Commands
heading: Commands a page adds
text: Some tools add their own commands, listed first under their own headings. For example, the Portfolio Builder uses Spotlight as its toolbar and adds commands for its sections, typefaces and publishing. These appear only on that tool's page. See the tool's own documentation for its commands.

title: Commands
heading: Commands in Hindi
text: When the site is in Hindi, commands are shown in Hindi, and you can type either the Hindi or the English name to find them.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: Ctrl + K opens my browser's address bar or search
text: Why: Spotlight loads a moment after the page. A shortcut pressed before that goes to the browser. What to do: wait for the page to finish loading, or select Search in the header.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: The list says "Search engine is loading…"
text: Why: the first time you open Spotlight on a page, it builds its search index in the background. What to do: wait a moment and keep typing; results appear once the index is ready. On a slow connection this takes longer.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: A page I know exists does not appear
text: Possible causes and fixes: - A scope tab is hiding it. Select All , or Show all N results under Try instead . - You typed only one character. Type at least two. - Only 8 results are listed. Select View all results for "…" for the full list. - A -word in your query excluded it, or a quoted phrase is too strict. Remove it.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: Web search says "Global search is unavailable right now"
text: Why: the Web tab needs a network connection and the site's web search service. What to do: check your connection and try again later, or search the site with All .

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: Typing a colour does not show a colour answer
text: Why: only six-digit hex codes with a , and nothing else in the box, are read as a colour. fff , rebeccapurple or rgb(...) are searched as text. What to do: type the full six-digit form, for example ffffff . For other formats, use the Contrast Checker or the colour tools.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: A command is missing
text: Why: commands appear only when the page has the control they drive. What to do: go to a page that has it, or use the control directly, for example the header's theme button.

title: Troubleshooting Spotlight
heading: Recent searches are gone
text: Why: they are kept in this browser and are lost if you clear site data, use a private window, or select Clear .

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: What is the difference between Spotlight and the search page?
text: Spotlight is the quick box that floats over any page and shows up to 8 results. The search page at https://auricartisan.com/search/ shows every result with filters, previews and answers. View all results for "…" moves your query from one to the other. The search page is documented in [Search](../../../search/README.md).

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: Does Spotlight work offline?
text: Searching the site can work offline once you have prepared the offline version on the Download page, because the site's search index is part of it (see [Download and offline](../../../download-and-offline/README.md)). Opening a result offline works only for pages that were saved. The Web tab always needs a connection.

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: Can I search in Hindi?
text: Commands can be found by their Hindi or English names. Page search matches the English text of pages, so English words give the best results.

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: Why does a result I open often move up?
text: Spotlight gives a small boost to pages you have opened from search before, in this browser.

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: Does Spotlight show ads?
text: It can show a compact sponsored strip while ads are running on the site. The Ads in panels & search setting controls it on plans that include ad preferences (see [Settings panel › Tooltips and ads](../../settings-panel/docs/tooltips-and-ads.md)).

title: Spotlight FAQ
heading: What does Ctrl + Shift + K do?
text: It opens the Feature Kit (calculator, converter and other small tools), which is separate from Spotlight. See [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Spotlight glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Spotlight The floating search box opened with Ctrl + K . Scope The part of the site a search covers: All, Pages, Tools, Docs, Learn or Web. Launcher A shortcut row shown when the search box is empty. Index The list of the site's pages and their words that Spotlight searches. Preview pane The panel beside the results showing details of the highlighted result or a colour answer. Field filter A prefix such as title: that limits a search to one part of each page. Exclusion A word with a minus sign in front, such as -gradient , which removes matching pages. Command mode The mode entered by typing , which lists actions instead of pages. Contrast ratio The WCAG measure of lightness difference between two colours, from 1:1 to 21:1. AA, AAA WCAG contrast levels: AA body text needs 4.5:1, AAA needs 7:1, AA large text needs 3:1. OKLCH A way of writing a colour as lightness, chroma and hue that follows human perception closely.

title: Spotlight limits and accuracy
heading: What is searched
text: - Spotlight searches the site's own search index: the titles, descriptions, tags, categories, addresses and text of the site's pages. It does not search inside your saved library items or inside tool results. - The Web tab searches a curated set of trusted outside sources through the site's web search service, not the whole web. - Scopes are decided by page address: Tools is every page under /tool/ , Docs is under /library/documentation/ , Learn is under /library/learn/ , and Pages is everything else.

title: Spotlight limits and accuracy
heading: Result limits
text: - Searches start at two characters. - Spotlight lists up to 8 results; the full search page lists all of them. - Up to six recent searches are kept. - Web results are limited to 8.

title: Spotlight limits and accuracy
heading: Colour answers
text: - Contrast ratios use the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula and are shown to two decimal places. - Only plus six hex digits is recognised as a colour. Colours are treated as sRGB. - The pass and fail verdicts use the WCAG 2 thresholds: 4.5:1 for AA body text, 7:1 for AAA body text and 3:1 for AA large text. - The answer is a quick reading, not an audit. For a page-wide check, use the Analyzer.

title: Spotlight limits and accuracy
heading: Language
text: The index holds the English text of pages. Searching in Hindi finds commands, but page results depend on English words.

title: Spotlight privacy
heading: Stored in your browser
text: - Your last six searches (the Recent list). Select Clear to delete them. - A small record of which results you have opened from search, used only to rank those pages a little higher for you next time. Both stay in this browser and are not sent to Auric Artisan.

title: Spotlight privacy
heading: Uses the network
text: - Site searches run inside your browser against the site's search index, which is downloaded from auricartisan.com. Your query is not sent anywhere. - Web searches send your query to the site's web search service to find matches in trusted outside sources. - Opening a web result opens that outside website in a new tab.

title: Related to Spotlight
text: - [Search](../../../search/README.md) — the full search page at https://auricartisan.com/search/. - [Contrast Checker](../../../tools/accessibility-and-vision/contrast-checker/README.md) — where colour answers lead. - [Analyzer](../../../tools/accessibility-and-vision/analyzer/README.md) — a full accessibility audit of a page. - [Guide and page outline](../../guide-and-page-outline/README.md) — the guide has its own filter box for the current page. - [Context menu](../../context-menu/README.md) — Search the site and, for a selection, Search this site and Search the web . - [Kits](../../../kits/README.md) — the Menu Kit and Status Kit have their own search fields.

title: Settings panel
text: The Settings panel, titled Your Settings , is a floating panel that changes how the whole site looks and behaves for you. It holds your accent colour, theme, language and text size; comfort options such as reading mode, reduced motion and eye-rest reminders; which info bars appear; how clocks show the time; how tooltips behave; ad preferences; and a list of keyboard shortcuts. Every change applies at once, on the page you are on and on every page you open afterwards. The panel keeps your choices in this browser, so they work without an account. If you have the site open in several tabs, a change in one tab is picked up by the others. You can also save all your settings to a file and load them again on another browser or device. The panel is modeless: it floats over the page without dimming it, so you can keep reading and clicking the page while it is open. You can drag it, widen it, collapse it to its title bar and close it.

title: Settings panel
heading: Who it is for
text: - Everyone who uses the site: the defaults suit most people, and every choice can be undone. - People who need larger text, stronger contrast, underlined links or less motion. - People who prefer the site in Hindi, a 24-hour clock or a particular time zone. - Anyone who wants to move their setup to another browser.

title: Settings panel
heading: Where to find it
text: On any page of https://auricartisan.com: - press Ctrl + , (or Cmd + , on a Mac); - open the page utilities bar at the bottom-left of the screen and select Settings ; - right-click the page and choose Site , then Settings (or Keyboard shortcuts to open the Shortcuts section); - press Ctrl + K , type and choose Open settings ; - right-click the clock strip and choose All settings , which opens the Clock section.

title: Settings panel
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , to open Your Settings . 2. In Appearance , select an accent swatch, for example Emerald . The whole site recolours. 3. Under Theme , select Light , Dark or System . 4. Under Text size , select one of the four A buttons to make type smaller or larger across the site. 5. Select Comfort in the section list and switch on anything you need, such as Reduce motion or Underline links . 6. Select Export at the bottom of the panel to keep a copy of your settings as auric-settings.json . 7. Press Esc or select the close button to put the panel away. Your choices stay in place on every page.

title: Settings panel
heading: What you can do
text: - Recolour the site with 13 preset accents, any custom colour, or a shade from the live accent ramp, and keep up to 18 saved colours. - Check that your accent is readable with a live WCAG contrast readout. - Choose light, dark or system theme, English or Hindi, and one of four text sizes. - Turn on reading mode, reduced motion, reduced transparency, boosted contrast and underlined links; turn the custom cursor off. - Schedule eye-rest reminders and set up the idle screen saver. - Choose which info bars, notices and demo chips appear, and whether the clock strip is shown. - Set 12 or 24-hour time, seconds, date display, time zone and date format. - Turn tooltips off, or make them more or less detailed. - Adjust ad preferences (a paid perk). - Restore one section, or everything, to its defaults; export and import your settings as a file.

title: Get started with the Settings panel
Get started with the Settings panel
heading: Open the panel
text: Use whichever way is closest: Where you are What to do --- --- Anywhere, with a keyboard Press Ctrl + , ( Cmd + , on a Mac). Press it again to close the panel. Anywhere, with a mouse or touch Select the page utilities button at the bottom-left of the screen, then Settings . Right-clicking the page Choose Site , then Settings . Choose Keyboard shortcuts to open the Shortcuts section directly. In Spotlight search Press Ctrl + K , type , and choose Open settings . On the clock strip Right-click the strip and select All settings . The panel opens on the Clock section. On an info bar Right-click the bar and select Settings . The panel opens on the Comfort section. The page utilities bar is the launcher row that also holds the kits. It is described in [Header and navigation](../../header-and-navigation/docs/page-utilities-bar.md) and, in more depth, in [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Get started with the Settings panel
heading: A tour of the panel
text: The panel has four parts. 1. The title bar. It reads Your Settings . Drag it to move the panel; the position is remembered. On the right are four buttons: - Focus mode — the pin-style button shared with the kits. Its tooltip reads "Keep Settings open through navigation and while opening other kits." - Resize — switches between the normal size and a wider size (up to 980 pixels, or the width of your window). - Minimize — collapses the panel to its title bar. Select the title bar, or the same button (now Restore ), to bring it back. - Close settings — the X. 2. The section list. Appearance, Comfort, Highlights, Clock, Tooltips, Ads and Shortcuts. Each shows how many controls it holds. With a section selected, press the Left and Right arrow keys to move between sections. 3. The section body. The controls for the selected section. Most sections end with Restore section defaults . 4. The footer. Export and Import on the left; Reset all and a reminder of the Ctrl + , shortcut on the right. The panel does not dim or block the page. You can scroll and click the page while it is open. Note: The Ads section appears only while the site is showing ads. If ads are switched off site-wide, the section is not shown at all.

title: Get started with the Settings panel
heading: Make your first change
text: 1. Open the panel with Ctrl + , . 2. In Appearance , look at the Preview card at the top. It shows a heading, an accent chip, a link, a line of text and a button in your current look. 3. Under Accent color , select Sapphire . The preview, the panel and the whole page change to blue at once. 4. Under Text size , select the largest A ( X-Large ). The text across the site grows. 5. Select Comfort in the section list and switch on Underline links . 6. Close the panel with Esc . Result: every page you open now uses the sapphire accent, extra-large text and underlined links in articles. To undo the three changes, open the panel again and use Restore section defaults in Appearance and in Comfort, or select Reset all .

title: Get started with the Settings panel
heading: Close the panel
text: - Press Esc . If a drop-down list inside the panel is open, the first Esc closes the list and the second closes the panel. - Press Ctrl + , again. - Select the X in the title bar. When the panel closes, keyboard focus returns to whatever you used to open it.
