title: Back up, restore and reset
text: Your settings live in this browser only. Clearing the browser's site data, using a private window or switching to another browser starts you from the defaults. A settings file lets you carry them across.

title: Back up, restore and reset
heading: Export your settings
text: 1. Open the panel ( Ctrl + , ). 2. Select Export in the footer. 3. Your browser downloads a file named auric-settings.json . A message confirms "Settings exported". The file contains every setting in the panel, including your saved colours. It is plain JSON (see [Reference](reference.md the-settings-file) for its fields). It contains no account details.

title: Back up, restore and reset
heading: Import settings from a file
text: 1. Open the panel on the browser you want to set up. 2. Select Import in the footer. 3. Choose an auric-settings.json file (any .json file is accepted for selection). 4. The settings apply at once, including the theme. A message confirms "Settings imported". What happens to the file's contents: - Only settings the panel knows are read. Anything else in the file is ignored. - A setting missing from the file is set to its default. - A value that is not allowed (for example a text size that does not exist) is replaced by that setting's default. - If the file is not valid JSON, nothing changes and the message reads "That file isn't valid settings". If the file cannot be read, the message reads "Couldn't read that file". You can import the same file again later; the panel accepts a repeat of the same file.

title: Back up, restore and reset
heading: Restore one section
text: Every section except Shortcuts ends with Restore section defaults . It resets only that section's settings. For example, in Comfort it turns every switch back to its default and leaves your accent colour alone. A message names the section, for example "Clock restored to defaults". Section What its restore resets --- --- Appearance Accent, theme and text size (not language, not saved colours) Comfort Reading mode, reduce motion, reduce transparency, boost contrast, underline links, custom cursor, eye-rest reminders and interval, screen saver and delay Highlights Live demo chips, welcome bar, announcement bar, quick links bar, clock strip, hero notice Clock 24-hour time, show seconds, show date, timezone, date format Tooltips Show tooltips, detailed tooltips, advanced tooltips Ads Show ads, ad density, ads in panels & search

title: Back up, restore and reset
heading: Reset everything
text: 1. Select Reset all in the footer. 2. A confirmation covers the panel: "Reset all settings to their defaults? Your accent, theme, comfort and clock preferences will be cleared." 3. Select Reset all to confirm, or Cancel (or press Esc , or click outside the card) to keep your settings. After a reset, a message confirms "All settings reset to defaults". Your saved colours are kept , because they are a palette you built rather than a preference. Remove them one by one with the X on each swatch if you want them gone. Tip: Export your settings before a reset if you might want them back.

title: Back up, restore and reset
heading: Use the panel's right-click menu
text: Right-clicking inside the Settings panel opens a small menu of its own instead of the site's page menu. - The heading shows the name of the setting you right-clicked, or Settings if you right-clicked elsewhere in the panel. - This setting (only when you right-clicked a switch row): Turn on or Turn off . - Panel : Export , Import , Reset section and Reset all . Reset section is unavailable in the Shortcuts section, which has nothing to reset. Reset all still asks for confirmation. Press Esc , click elsewhere, scroll or resize the window to close the menu. Esc closes only the menu, not the panel.

title: Change the appearance
text: The Appearance section controls the site's accent colour, theme, language and text size. It opens first whenever you open the panel. The accent is the site's highlight colour: the gold of links, active tabs, buttons, focus rings, kit launchers and tooltip borders. Changing it recolours all of those at once.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Read the preview and the contrast readout
text: At the top of the section are two live readouts. - Preview (live appearance) shows a heading, an Accent chip, A link , a sample sentence and a Primary button drawn in your current accent, theme and text size. - Accent accessibility (live WCAG contrast) shows two rows: - Accent on background — the contrast between your accent and the page background of the current theme. - Text on accent — the contrast between the accent and the text colour the site places on it. The site picks a dark or a light text colour automatically, whichever reads better. Each row shows a ratio such as 4.87:1 and a badge. Contrast ratio is the WCAG measure of how far apart two colours are in lightness, from 1:1 (identical) to 21:1 (black on white). Badge Ratio Meaning --- --- --- AAA 7:1 or more Meets the strictest WCAG level for body text AA 4.5:1 or more Meets the standard WCAG level for body text AA Large 3:1 or more Meets WCAG only for large text and interface parts Fail below 3:1 Too little contrast for text Below the rows is a strip of seven shades of your accent, from darker to lighter. Select any shade to use it as your accent.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Choose a preset accent
text: 1. Open the panel ( Ctrl + , ). Appearance is selected. 2. Under Accent color (gold + 12 premium tones), select a swatch. Hover a swatch to see its name. The page recolours at once. The presets are: Swatch Hex --- --- Gold (default) D3AF37 Champagne DEC68A Rose Gold B76E79 Silver C4C7CE Platinum Grey 8A8F99 Bronze B08D57 Copper B87333 Brown 8B5A2B Maroon 800020 Pink E75480 Emerald 3EA882 Sapphire 2F5EAA Amethyst 9966CC Note: In the light theme, the default Gold accent is drawn as a slightly darker gold so that it stays readable on a light page. A colour you choose yourself, including Gold picked from a saved colour, is used exactly as chosen.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Use any colour you like
text: 1. Under Custom color (any color you like), select the round colour chip. Your browser's colour picker opens. 2. Choose a colour. While you drag, the panel previews the colour; when you let go, the whole site takes it. 3. The hex value appears next to the chip, for example 2E8B57 . If your browser supports it, an Eyedropper button appears next to the chip. Select it, then click any pixel on your screen to make that colour your accent. Press Esc to cancel. Browsers without an eyedropper do not show the button. You can also select any shade in the Accent accessibility shade strip to use it as a custom accent.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Keep colours in Saved colors
text: Saved colors is a palette of accents you want to come back to. Nothing is added to it unless you ask. 1. Set a custom colour as above. 2. Select the + button ( Save this color ) next to the hex value. 3. The colour appears at the front of Saved colors , and the hint reads, for example, "3 of 18 kept". To use a saved colour, select its swatch. To remove one, select the small X on its corner. - The palette holds up to 18 colours. When it is full, the + button is disabled; remove a colour first. - The + shows as done ( Already saved ) when the current colour is already in the palette. - Restore section defaults and Reset all keep your saved colours. Only the X removes them.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Choose a theme
text: Under Theme , select Light , Dark or System . System follows your device's light or dark setting and changes with it. The full story, including the header button and shortcuts, is in [Theme](../../theme/README.md).

title: Change the appearance
heading: Choose a language
text: Under Language (भाषा — interface and articles), select English or हिन्दी . Choosing Hindi translates the page in place; choosing English reloads the page in English. See [Language](../../language/README.md) for what is translated.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Change the text size
text: Under Text size (scales type across the site), select one of the four A buttons, from smallest to largest: Button Size --- --- Small 90% of the default Default 100% Large 112% X-Large 125% You can also use the keyboard anywhere on the site (not while typing in a field): - Alt + + makes text larger by one step. - Alt + - makes text smaller by one step. - Alt + 0 returns to the default size. A short message such as "Text size: Large" confirms each change.

title: Change the appearance
heading: Restore the section
text: Select Restore section defaults at the bottom of Appearance to return the accent, theme and text size to their defaults (Gold, System, Default). Your language and your saved colours are not changed. A message confirms "Appearance restored to defaults".

title: Comfort options
text: The Comfort section holds switches that make the site easier to read and calmer to use. Each switch takes effect at once and applies to every page. Open it with Ctrl + , , then select Comfort .

title: Comfort options
heading: Reading mode
text: Reading mode gives a distraction-free layout with comfortable typography. While it is on: - floating chrome is hidden: the kit launchers, the right-edge menu strip, the info bars and the clock strip; - the custom cursor is replaced by your system cursor; - the main text sits in a narrower, centred column with larger type and more generous line spacing; - the header no longer sticks to the top of the screen; - a thin bar across the very top of the window fills as you scroll down the page; - a Reading mode ✕ chip appears near the bottom of the screen. Select it to leave reading mode. Ways to switch it on or off: - the Reading mode switch in Comfort; - Alt + R anywhere on the site (not while typing in a field); - right-click the page, choose View , then Reading mode (or Leave reading mode ); - on card pages (home, collections, blog, changelog, documentation, learn), right-click a card and select the Reading pill. A short message ("Reading mode on" or "Reading mode off") confirms a change made from the right-click menu.

title: Comfort options
heading: Reduce motion
text: Reduce motion minimises animations and transitions across the site. Animations finish instantly, smooth scrolling becomes an instant jump, and the rotating info bars swap messages without fading. Toggle it with Alt + M anywhere on the site. A message confirms "Reduced motion on" or "Reduced motion off". Note: This switch is the site's own setting. The site also respects your operating system's reduced-motion preference: with that on, the custom cursor is not shown and the eye-rest horizon does not animate, whatever this switch says.

title: Comfort options
heading: Reduce transparency
text: Reduce transparency turns off blur and translucency, so panels and overlays are drawn as solid surfaces. This can make text over panels clearer and can help on slower devices.

title: Comfort options
heading: Boost contrast
text: Boost contrast strengthens secondary text and borders for easier reading. Muted text is drawn in the stronger secondary text colour, and borders use a darker line.

title: Comfort options
heading: Underline links
text: Underline links always underlines links inside articles and prose: paragraphs, list items, definitions, quotations and captions. Navigation menus and buttons are not changed.

title: Comfort options
heading: Custom cursor
text: Custom cursor controls the ring and dot that follow your pointer. It is on by default. Switch it off to use your system cursor everywhere; the change is immediate, with no reload. See [Custom cursor](../../custom-cursor/README.md).

title: Comfort options
heading: Eye-rest reminders
text: Eye-rest reminders are gentle reminders to rest your eyes on a schedule. They are off by default. 1. Switch on Eye-rest reminders . 2. Under Reminder interval (minutes between reminders), select 20m , 35m , 45m or 60m . The default is 20 minutes. The interval buttons are dimmed while the switch is off. Changing the interval restarts the countdown at once. The reminder itself, and its own options, are described in [Eye rest](../../eye-rest/README.md).

title: Comfort options
heading: Screen saver
text: Screen saver shows an ambient colour screen after a period of inactivity. It is off by default. 1. Switch on Screen saver . 2. Under Start after (minutes of inactivity), select 1m , 5m , 10m , 20m or 30m . The default is 10 minutes. The delay buttons are dimmed while the switch is off. Switching the screen saver off while it is showing closes it at once. See [Screen saver](../../screen-saver/README.md).

title: Comfort options
heading: Restore the section
text: Select Restore section defaults to return every Comfort switch and both timings to their defaults: everything off except Custom cursor , a 20-minute reminder interval and a 10-minute screen saver delay. A message confirms "Comfort restored to defaults".

title: Highlights and clock
heading: Highlights: bars, notices and chips
text: The Highlights section decides which extra strips and labels appear around page content. The bars themselves are described in [Info bars and notices](../../info-bars-and-notices/README.md). Switch What it shows Default --- --- --- Live demo chips The highlighted "live / demo" chips above demo sections On Welcome bar The rotating welcome bar above the page Homepage only Announcement bar The site announcements bar Homepage only Quick links bar The quick-links bar (documentation, changelog, timeline, blog, learn) Homepage only Clock strip A live clock, date and time zone above every page Off Hero notice The highlighted notice banner on the homepage hero On The Welcome, Announcement and Quick links bars start in a third state: shown on the homepage only. In that state the switch appears on. - Switch it off to hide that bar everywhere, including the homepage. - Switch it on again to show that bar above every page, not only the homepage. - To get back to "homepage only", select Restore section defaults . The Quick links bar also shows by default at the foot of the Collections page, where it is part of the layout. Each bar, the hero notice and each demo chip has its own ✕ button. Selecting it has the same effect as switching the matching setting off, so the switch in Highlights moves to off as well. For demo chips, one ✕ hides every demo chip on the site. Note: The tooltip on a bar's ✕ says you can turn it back on in "Settings → Comfort". The switches are in the Highlights section. Restore section defaults returns all six switches to the defaults in the table above. A message confirms "Highlights restored to defaults".

title: Highlights and clock
heading: Clock: time and date display
text: The Clock section controls the live clock strip at the top of pages (when Clock strip is on in Highlights). The 24-hour choice is also used by the clock on the screen saver. At the top, Live preview (your clock right now) shows the time and date exactly as your settings will draw them, updating every second. Control What it does Values Default --- --- --- --- 24-hour time Shows clocks in 24-hour format instead of AM / PM On, off Off Show seconds Includes seconds on the live clock On, off On Show date Shows the calendar date next to the clock On, off On Timezone The time zone the clock shows (defaults to your location) Auto-detect , or any time zone your browser lists Auto-detect Date format How the date is written Long , DD/MM/YYYY , MM/DD/YYYY Long The Auto-detect entry names the zone your device reports, for example "Auto-detect (Asia/Kolkata)". Long writes the weekday, month, day and year in words, for example "Thursday, September 24, 2026". 1. Open the panel and select Clock . 2. Open the Timezone list and choose a zone, for example Europe/London . 3. The preview switches to that zone at once. To follow your device again, choose Auto-detect at the top of the list. Right-click the clock strip itself for a small Clock settings menu with a few extra choices (an ISO date format, and switches for the weekday and the zone label). It is described in [Info bars and notices](../../info-bars-and-notices/docs/clock-strip.md). Its All settings link opens this Clock section. Restore section defaults returns all five clock settings to their defaults. A message confirms "Clock restored to defaults".

title: Tooltips and ads
heading: Tooltips
text: Most buttons, links and cards on the site show a tooltip when you hover over them or move keyboard focus to them: a small card with a title, a description and sometimes a picture, tags, a keyboard shortcut and extra details. The Tooltips section starts with a Live preview (how tooltips will look). It shows a sample tooltip for the Design System Generator with a picture, three tags, a description, the Ctrl + K shortcut and a details table, and it changes as you flip the switches below it. Switch What it does Default --- --- --- Show tooltips Shows the rich hover and focus tooltips across the site. Off hides them; the preview reads "Tooltips are turned off". On Detailed tooltips Expands the collapsible details: preview image, metadata and tags. Off keeps tooltips compact: title, description and shortcut. On Advanced tooltips Always expands the data section (category, route, read time). Off keeps it collapsed. Off With Advanced tooltips off, a tooltip that has extra data shows an Alt — More details hint at its foot. While the tooltip is open, press Alt to expand the data section for that tooltip only. The next tooltip starts collapsed again. Restore section defaults returns the three switches to their defaults.

title: Tooltips and ads
heading: Ads
text: The Ads section appears only while the site is showing ads. It opens with the note Ad preferences — "paid perk — free plan shows standard ads". Control What it does Values Default --- --- --- --- Show ads Shows sponsored slots across the site On, off On Ad density How many in-content slots appear per page Standard , Reduced Standard Ads in panels & search Shows the compact sponsored strip inside kits, Spotlight and search results On, off On Ad density is dimmed while Show ads is off. Ad preferences are a paid perk. Every tool on the site stays free on every plan either way. - Signed out or on the free plan: the controls are shown but disabled. Selecting one opens an upgrade message: "Ad preferences are a paid perk — upgrade to hide ads or tune where they appear. Every tool stays free either way." Nothing changes until you upgrade. - On a plan that includes the ad-free perk: the controls work like any other setting. Plans and the ad-free perk are explained in [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md). Restore section defaults returns the three ad controls to their defaults.

heading: Shortcuts
text: The Shortcuts section lists the panel's own keyboard shortcuts. It has no settings. Keys Action --- --- Ctrl + , Open or close settings Alt + R Toggle reading mode Alt + T Switch theme (light, then dark, then system) Alt + + Increase text size Alt + - Decrease text size Alt + 0 Reset text size Alt + M Toggle reduced motion Esc Close the dialog The Alt shortcuts do nothing while you are typing in a text field. On a Mac, Cmd + , also opens the panel. The whole site's shortcuts are in [Keyboard shortcuts](../../keyboard-shortcuts/README.md).

title: Settings panel reference
heading: The settings file
text: Export writes a JSON file named auric-settings.json . It starts with two marker fields and then lists every setting: json { " aa": "auric-settings", "v": 1, "accent": "sapphire", "savedColors": [" 2e8b57"], "themeMode": "system", "textScale": 1.12, "reduceMotion": false, "customCursor": true, "eyeRest": true, "eyeRestInterval": 35, "time24": true, "clockTz": "", "dateFormat": "dmy" } The example is shortened. A real export also includes the remaining switches: reduceTransparency , contrast , underlineLinks , reading , screenSaver , screenSaverDelay , showWelcome , showAnnouncements , showQuickLinks , showTimeStrip , showHeroNotice , showDemoBadges , showSeconds , showDate , tipEnabled , tipDetails , tipAdvanced , adsEnabled , adsDensity and adsInPanels , plus recentColors , an older colour history that is only read to fill Saved colors once. Field Accepted values --- --- accent A preset name ( gold , champagne , rose-gold , silver , platinum , bronze , copper , espresso , maroon , rose , emerald , sapphire , amethyst ) or a rrggbb colour savedColors Up to 18 rrggbb colours themeMode light , dark , system textScale 0.9 , 1 , 1.12 , 1.25 eyeRestInterval 20 , 35 , 45 , 60 screenSaverDelay 1 , 5 , 10 , 20 , 30 dateFormat long , dmy , mdy clockTz Empty for auto-detect, or a time zone name such as Europe/London showWelcome , showAnnouncements , showQuickLinks true , false or "home" adsDensity standard , reduced Other switches true or false The preset names in the file are fixed identifiers: espresso is the Brown swatch, rose is Pink , and platinum is Platinum Grey . The language is not part of the file; it is kept separately (see [Language](../../language/README.md)).

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: My settings are gone
text: Why: settings are kept in this browser's local storage. They are lost when you clear site data or cookies for auricartisan.com, when you use a private or incognito window (which forgets everything when it closes), or when you open the site in a different browser or on another device. What to do: set them again, or import a settings file you exported earlier ( Import in the panel footer). Export a file now so you have a copy next time.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: Ctrl + , does nothing
text: Why: the panel loads a moment after the page. A shortcut pressed while the page is still loading can be missed. Some browser extensions also claim Ctrl + , . What to do: wait until the page has finished loading and try again, or open the panel from the page utilities bar at the bottom-left ( Settings ).

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: The Alt shortcuts do nothing
text: Why: Alt + R , Alt + T , Alt + M , Alt + + , Alt + - and Alt + 0 are ignored while your cursor is in a text field, so they cannot interfere with typing. They are also ignored when Ctrl or Cmd is held. What to do: click an empty part of the page first, then press the shortcut.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: A change in one tab did not reach another tab
text: Why: other open tabs pick up a change when the browser tells them about it. This works in normal windows but not between a normal window and a private window, which keep separate storage. What to do: reload the other tab.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: My theme, accent or text size changed after I opened a link
text: Why: a page link copied from the site can carry the sender's appearance settings when they differ from the defaults (see [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md)). Opening it applies those settings in your browser. What to do: set them back in Appearance, or select Restore section defaults .

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: The Ads controls are greyed out
text: Why: ad preferences are a paid perk. For signed-out and free-plan visitors the controls are disabled, and selecting one shows an upgrade message. What to do: nothing is broken. Upgrading unlocks the controls; every tool stays free either way.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: I cannot find the Ads section
text: Why: the section appears only while the site is showing ads.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: The Eyedropper button is missing
text: Why: it appears only in browsers that offer a screen colour picker to web pages, which at present means desktop Chromium-based browsers such as Chrome and Edge. What to do: use the Custom color chip instead, or pick a colour with a colour tool on the site and paste its hex into your browser's picker.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: The + button next to my custom colour is disabled
text: Why: either the colour is already in Saved colors (the button reads Already saved ), or the palette already holds 18 colours. What to do: remove a saved colour with the X on its swatch, then try again.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: The Settings panel does not stay open when I move to another page
text: Why: the panel closes when you leave a page, even with the Focus mode button on. What to do: press Ctrl + , on the new page. Your settings themselves carry over.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: Import says "That file isn't valid settings"
text: Why: the file is not valid JSON, for example because it was edited by hand and a comma or bracket is missing, or because it is a different kind of file. What to do: export a fresh file from a browser that has the settings you want, or fix the JSON. See [Reference](reference.md the-settings-file) for the format.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: After Reset all my saved colours are still there
text: Why: this is intended. Saved colours are a palette you built, so neither Reset all nor Restore section defaults removes them. What to do: remove them one by one with the X on each swatch.

title: Troubleshooting the Settings panel
heading: A bar I switched on shows on every page, not just the homepage
text: Why: the Welcome, Announcement and Quick links bars start in a "homepage only" state. Switching one off and on again shows it everywhere. What to do: select Restore section defaults in Highlights to go back to homepage only.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Do I need an account to use Settings?
text: No. Every setting works signed out and is kept in this browser. The only exception is the Ads section, whose controls need a paid plan.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Do my settings follow me to another device?
text: Not automatically. Export them with Export and load the file on the other device with Import .

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Does the accent colour change the colours inside the tools?
text: No. The accent recolours the site's interface: links, buttons, focus rings, tabs, kit launchers and tooltip borders. Colours you are working with in a tool, and colours shown in libraries, are not changed.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Why is the default gold darker in the light theme?
text: Plain gold on a near-white page has too little contrast to read comfortably, so the light theme uses a darker gold for the default accent. Colours you pick yourself are used as chosen. The Accent accessibility readout shows how your accent performs.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: What is the difference between Restore section defaults and Reset all?
text: Restore section defaults resets only the section you are in. Reset all resets every section after asking you to confirm. Neither removes your saved colours.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Is language included in an exported settings file?
text: No. The language is kept separately. Choose it again on the new browser, or open any page with ?lang=hi added to its address (see [Language](../../language/README.md)).

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Can I open the panel on a specific section?
text: Yes, from a few places: the right-click menu's Keyboard shortcuts opens Shortcuts, the clock strip's All settings opens Clock, and an info bar's Settings opens Comfort.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Does Reduce motion affect the custom cursor?
text: No. The custom cursor follows your operating system's reduced-motion preference, not this switch. To remove it, switch off Custom cursor in Comfort.

title: Settings panel FAQ
heading: Why does the panel look different on my phone?
text: On screens narrower than about 900 pixels, the section list becomes a strip across the top of the panel that you scroll sideways, and the control counts are hidden. All the same settings are there.

title: Settings panel glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Accent The site's highlight colour for links, buttons, active tabs, focus rings, kit launchers and tooltip borders. Gold by default. Contrast ratio The WCAG measure of how different two colours are in lightness, from 1:1 (none) to 21:1 (black on white). WCAG The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international standard for accessible web content. AA, AAA WCAG contrast levels for body text: AA needs 4.5:1, the stricter AAA needs 7:1. AA Large A contrast of at least 3:1, accepted by WCAG for large text and interface parts but not body text. Eyedropper A browser tool that lets you click any pixel on your screen to read its colour. Hex colour A colour written as and six hexadecimal digits for red, green and blue, for example D3AF37 . Local storage A small store inside your browser where a website keeps data on your device. Modeless A panel that does not block the page behind it. You can keep using the page while it is open. Reading mode A distraction-free layout with a narrow text column, larger type and no floating controls. Saved colors Your own palette of up to 18 accent colours, added only when you select the + button. Section One of the groups in the panel's list: Appearance, Comfort, Highlights, Clock, Tooltips, Ads, Shortcuts. System theme A theme setting that follows your device's light or dark preference and changes when it changes. Toast A short message that appears briefly to confirm an action, such as "Settings exported". Tooltip The small card that appears when you hover over or focus a control, explaining what it does.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The accent contrast readout
text: - Formula. Both rows use the WCAG 2 relative-luminance contrast formula, and the badges use the WCAG 2 thresholds (7:1, 4.5:1, 3:1). - Accent on background compares your accent with the background colour of the page you are on, read from the page itself. On a page with a coloured or image background under a particular block, the real contrast in that block can differ. - Text on accent compares your accent with the text colour the site places on it. The site chooses between a very dark and a very light text colour, whichever gives more contrast. - Precision. Ratios are shown to two decimal places. Colours are treated as sRGB with no transparency. - The readout is a guide for choosing an accent, not a certified accessibility audit. For a full check of a page, use the Analyzer or the Contrast Checker tools.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The shade strip
text: The seven shades are three darker steps, your accent itself in the middle, and three lighter steps, made by mixing the accent towards black or towards white in sRGB. They are not a perceptual (OKLCH) ramp; use the site's shade and design tools for that.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Storage and scope
text: - Settings are kept per browser and per device. They are not synced to your account. - A private window starts from the defaults and forgets its changes when it closes. - Saved colors holds at most 18 colours. - The language setting is kept separately from the other settings and is not in the exported file.

title: Settings panel privacy
heading: What stays on your device
text: - Every setting in the panel, including your saved colours, is kept in your browser's local storage for auricartisan.com. - The panel's position and size are kept the same way. - Nothing is sent to Auric Artisan when you change a setting. The settings work signed out and are not attached to an account. - Export creates a file on your own device. It contains only your settings.

title: Settings panel privacy
heading: What uses the network
text: - Opening the Ads section checks your plan in the background, to decide whether the ad controls are unlocked. If you are signed in, this uses your existing session. - Choosing हिन्दी downloads the Hindi dictionaries for the pages you visit (see [Language](../../language/README.md)).

title: Settings panel privacy
heading: Links can carry settings
text: If you copy a page link from the site, it can include your appearance settings that differ from the defaults (for example your accent and text size), so the person you send it to sees the page as you do. See [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md) for what a link contains and how to share a clean one.

title: Settings panel privacy
heading: Removing your settings
text: - Reset all in the panel returns everything to the defaults (saved colours are kept until you remove them). - Clearing site data for auricartisan.com in your browser removes all stored settings. The site's full policies are on https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/ and https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/.

title: Settings panel release notes
text: The site's changelog at https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/ records releases. Entries that concern the settings controls: Date Release Change --- --- --- 2026-06-05 v0.9.9 Added user settings controls, alongside guide content, PWA app support and the UX Kit. 2026-05-02 v0.9.8 Added complexity management, which lets you control how many advanced tools the site shows (through the Advanced Kit). The panel as documented here (seven sections, saved colours, the accent contrast readout, the Custom cursor switch, the Highlights section and the panel's right-click menu) reflects the site as of September 2026. Later changes appear in the changelog.

title: Shareable links
text: As you use a page on auricartisan.com, the site quietly keeps the page's state in the address bar, after p= : how far you have scrolled, what you have typed or chosen in the page's fields, which tabs and toggles are selected, which panels are open, and your appearance settings where they differ from the defaults. Reload the page and it comes back as you left it. Copy the address and send it, and the other person sees the same view. The site also understands a few other additions to an address: ?lang=hi opens a page in Hindi, ?color= opens a colour inspector over any page, and split= restores a split view.

title: Shareable links
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone who wants a reload to keep their place and their inputs. - People sharing a specific tool setup, a scroll position in a long article or a filled-in form. - Teachers and support staff pointing someone to an exact view.

title: Shareable links
heading: Where to find it
text: It works on its own on every page. To copy the current address, use your browser's address bar, Copy link in the navigation dock, or Copy URL in the right-click menu.

title: Shareable links
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open a tool, for example https://auricartisan.com/tool/basic-tools/, and change a few inputs. 2. Scroll down a little. After a moment the address gains a p= part. 3. Reload the page. Your inputs and scroll position come back. 4. Point at the navigation dock and select Copy link . 5. Paste the link into a message. Whoever opens it sees the same inputs and position.

title: Shareable links
heading: What you can do
text: - Keep your place and inputs through a reload. - Share an exact view of a page. - Open any page in Hindi or English with ?lang= . - Inspect any colour over any page with ?color= . - Share a split view with split= .

title: Get started with shareable links
heading: What happens as you work
text: On every page, about a third of a second after you scroll, type or change a control, the site updates the address in your browser's address bar. It adds p= followed by a short code that describes the page's state. For example: text https://auricartisan.com/tool/basic-tools/ p=eyJ2IjoxLCJ5IjoxNjkwLCJ4IjowfQ The code is not secret or encrypted: it is the page's state written compactly. The update replaces the current address rather than adding a new entry, so it does not fill your Back button with steps. When you are at the top of the page and have changed nothing, the address stays clean, with no p= .

title: Get started with shareable links
heading: What comes back when you open the address
text: When you reload the page or open the address later, the site restores the state in this order: 1. Panels that were open (the Settings panel and the Feature, Menu, Advanced and Status Kits) open again. 2. Tool-specific state is applied, on tools that save their own. 3. Field values are put back, and the page recalculates as if you had typed them. 4. Selected tabs and toggles are selected again. 5. The page scrolls back to where you were. Some parts of a page load late, such as kits and tool panels; the site keeps trying for a few seconds until they are ready.

title: Get started with shareable links
heading: Share an exact view
text: 1. Set up the page the way you want to show it. 2. Copy the address: select Copy link in the navigation dock, choose Copy URL in the right-click menu's quick bar, or copy it from the address bar. 3. Send it. The person who opens it sees the same page, inputs, tabs, open panels and scroll position. Important: The link also carries your appearance settings that differ from the defaults, such as accent colour, theme mode and text size, and applies them in the other person's browser. It carries whatever you typed into the page's fields, apart from passwords and search boxes. Check the view before you share it.

title: Get started with shareable links
heading: Share a clean link
text: To share just the page: - scroll to the very top and undo any changes before copying; or - delete everything from p= onwards in the copied address.

title: Get started with shareable links
heading: Pages that use their own #
text: Some pages keep their own information after , for example a section link such as about-intro , the Vision Simulation tool's shareable state, or a shared library item. On those pages the site does not add p= , so it never overwrites them.

title: Other link options
heading: Open a page in Hindi or English: ?lang=
text: Add ?lang=hi to any page address to open it in Hindi, or ?lang=en for English. The browser that opens the link remembers the choice for later visits. text https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/?lang=hi If the address already contains ? , use &lang=hi . See [Language](../../language/README.md).

title: Other link options
heading: Inspect a colour over any page: ?color=
text: Add ?color= and a colour to any page address, and a floating colour inspector opens over that page with a full reading of the colour. text https://auricartisan.com/?color=CEA1B5 https://auricartisan.com/library/palette/?colour=%23d3af37&on=ffffff - Parameter names: color , colour or hex for the colour; on , bg , against or vs for a background to compare it with. - Colour formats: hex with or without (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits; must be written %23 in an address), a CSS colour name such as rebeccapurple , or a CSS colour function such as oklch(…) , lab(…) or rgb(…) . - Short or partial hex still works: ?color=CEA is read as a colour. - Several colours: separate them with or ; (or , when no colour function is used). - The inspector reports contrast against the page it opens on unless you give a background with on= . The inspector itself is part of the colour tools; see [Basic colour tools](../../../tools/colour-workspace/basic-colour-tools/README.md).

title: Other link options
heading: Restore a split view: #split=
text: While split view is open, the address holds split= and a description of both panes. Opening that address restores the split. See [Split view › Share a split](../../split-view/docs/share-a-split.md).

title: Other link options
heading: Search: /search/?q=
text: The full search page accepts a query in its address, for example https://auricartisan.com/search/?q=gamut . Spotlight's View all results uses it. See [Search](../../../search/README.md).

text: - When the address already has another part (a section anchor, the Vision Simulation state, a shared library item). The site still restores its own p= if present. - On pages that turn the feature off. - Inside split view panes, each pane keeps its own state, which is included in the split= address.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: The link opened but my inputs were not restored
text: Possible causes and fixes: - The field has no identity on the page, so it cannot be saved. Nothing can be done from your side. - It was a password, file or search field, which are never saved. - The state was too long (over about 3,600 characters), so only the scroll position and open panels were kept. - The page uses its own part, so no p= was added. Use the tool's own sharing option if it has one. - The page had not finished loading when the link was copied. Wait a moment after your last change before copying.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: Opening a link changed my theme, accent or text size
text: Why: the link carried the sender's appearance settings that differ from the defaults. What to do: change them back in Settings, or use Restore section defaults in Appearance.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: A panel opened by itself when I loaded a page
text: Why: the address had a p= part recorded while that panel was open. What to do: close the panel. The address updates and it will not reopen.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: The address changes as I scroll
text: That is the page saving your position. It does not add steps to your Back button.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: I want a link without the extra part
text: Scroll to the top and undo your changes before copying, or delete everything from p= onwards.

title: Troubleshooting shareable links
heading: ?color= did not open the inspector
text: Why: the value is not a colour the site can read, or the was not written as %23 . What to do: write the hex without ( ?color=d3af37 ) or as %23d3af37 .

title: Shareable links FAQ
heading: Is the #p= part sent to Auric Artisan?
text: No. Browsers do not send the part of an address after to the website. It is read by the page in the browser that opens it.

title: Shareable links FAQ
heading: Is it encrypted?
text: No. It is the page's state written compactly. Anyone who has the link can read what it contains.

title: Shareable links FAQ
heading: Can I turn it off?
text: There is no switch for it. It only affects the address; it does not store anything elsewhere. Share a clean link if you prefer.

title: Shareable links FAQ
heading: Does it work offline?
text: Yes, for pages that are saved on your device: reloading restores the state without a connection.

title: Shareable links FAQ
heading: Does it include what I saved in my library?
text: No. It includes what is on the page, not your saved library items.

title: Shareable links glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Address (URL) The web address shown in the browser's address bar. Fragment The part of an address after . Browsers keep it on your device and do not send it to the site. Query parameter A part of an address after ? , such as ?lang=hi , which the page reads. Page state The scroll position, inputs, selections and open panels of a page. p= The fragment in which the site keeps a page's state. Restore Putting a page back into the state its address describes. Clean link An address without the p= part.

title: Shareable links privacy
text: - Stays in the address. The page state is kept only in the address bar of your browser tab. It is not stored elsewhere and, because it follows , it is not sent to Auric Artisan when the page loads. - Travels with the link. When you copy and share the address, the state goes with it: what you typed into the page's fields (except passwords and search boxes), your selections, open panels, your scroll position, and your appearance settings that differ from the defaults. - Readable by anyone with the link. The state is written compactly, not encrypted. - Browser history. The latest state of each page can appear in your browser history and bookmarks, like any address. To share safely, share a clean link: scroll to the top and undo changes, or delete everything from p= onwards.

title: Split view
text: Split view shows two pages side by side (or one above the other) in the same browser tab. The left pane, the live pane, is a working copy of the page you were on, scrolled to where you were. The right pane, the companion , can show any other page: a tool next to its documentation, two palettes, or the same page in light and dark. Both panes are complete, working pages, and each one behaves like a real window: make a pane narrow and the page inside it switches to its phone layout. Each pane has its own Back, Forward, Reload and address bar, and its own theme, device width and zoom. A toolbar across the top lets you change the layout, swap the panes, overlay them in Compare mode to see differences, sync their scrolling, send links from one pane to the other, and watch live performance numbers. The address of the page changes as you work, so you can copy it and share the exact split. Your original page keeps running untouched behind split view. When you close it, you are back where you were, or on the page the live pane moved to.

title: Split view
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers checking a page or palette in light and dark, or at desktop and phone width, at the same time. - Developers comparing two versions of a page. - Learners reading an article next to the tool it describes.

title: Split view
heading: Where to find it
text: - Press Ctrl + Shift + D on any page. - Select Open split view in the navigation dock. - Right-click the page and choose View , then Split view . - Hold Alt and click a link to another page on the site: split view opens with that page in the companion pane.

title: Split view
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/tool/basic-tools/ and press Ctrl + Shift + D . 2. The live pane shows Basic Tools; the companion shows your last companion page or the homepage. 3. Select the companion's address bar, type docs , and choose Documentation from the list. 4. Open the companion's More menu (three dots) and select Theme until it reads dark. 5. Drag the divider between the panes to give the tool more room. A badge shows the split, for example "62 38". 6. Press Alt + V to stack the panes, and Alt + V again to put them side by side. 7. Press Esc to close split view.

title: Split view
heading: What you can do
text: - Show two site pages at once, each fully interactive and responsive. - Give each pane its own theme, device width (desktop, tablet, phone) and zoom. - Stack or place panes side by side, swap them, resize them, maximise one. - Compare two panes visually, with differences highlighted. - Sync scrolling, mirror the live page into the companion, and route links into the companion. - Watch frame rate, CPU and memory while you work. - Share the whole split as a link.

title: Get started with split view
heading: Open split view
text: How What opens --- --- Ctrl + Shift + D Live pane: this page. Companion: your last companion page, or the homepage Navigation dock › Open split view The same Right-click › View › Split view The same Alt + click a link to another site page Live pane: this page. Companion: the page the link points to The first time, split view takes a moment to load. The live pane opens scrolled to where you were on the page.

title: Get started with split view
heading: The screen
text: Split view covers the whole window: - Toolbar across the top, in three groups: - the live pane's controls (its tab, Back , Forward , Reload , address bar and More menu); - the companion pane's controls (the same set); - the global controls: the performance chip, Toggle layout , Swap panes , Compare , Mirror , Route links , Scroll sync , Equal split and Close . - Two panes below it, with a divider between them that you can drag. On windows narrower than about 900 pixels, the toolbar wraps: each pane's controls take a full row. Your original page stays behind split view and keeps running; nothing on it is changed.

title: Get started with split view
heading: Close split view
text: - Press Esc (if a pane's More menu is open, the first Esc closes the menu; if you are editing an address bar, the first Esc puts back the address). - Or select Close at the right end of the toolbar. - Or press Ctrl + Shift + D again. When split view closes: - if the live pane is still on the page you started from, you return to that page, scrolled to where the live pane was; - if you moved the live pane to another page, the browser goes to that page.

title: Get started with split view

text: - [Panes and their controls](panes-and-controls.md) - [Layout, compare and sync](layout-compare-and-sync.md)

title: Layout, compare and sync
text: These are the global controls at the right of the split view toolbar.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Side by side or stacked
text: Select Toggle layout or press Alt + V to switch between panes side by side and panes one above the other.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Resize the panes
text: - Drag the divider between the panes. A badge follows the pointer showing the split as two percentages, for example "62 38". - The divider snaps when you pass near 25%, 33%, 50%, 66% or 75%. - A pane cannot be made smaller than 80 pixels. - Double-click the divider, select Equal split , or press Alt + E to return to 50 50. The sizes you choose are remembered separately for side-by-side and stacked layouts.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Swap the panes
text: Select Swap panes or press Alt + S . The panes trade places; both pages keep running, with nothing reloaded.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Maximise one pane
text: Use Maximize in a pane's More menu to give it the whole area, and select it again to restore.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Compare two pages
text: Compare overlays the two panes and highlights what differs: 1. Load the two pages you want to compare, for example the same page with one pane in light theme and the other in dark, or two palettes. 2. Select Compare . 3. A note appears: "Compare mode — matching areas go dark, differences light up. Scroll is synced." Areas where the two pages are identical turn black; anything different shows in colour. Scroll sync is switched on while comparing, and returns to your previous choice when you leave. Select Compare again to leave.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Mirror
text: Mirror loads the live pane's page into the companion, so you can show the same page twice, for example at two widths or in two themes.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Route links
text: When Route links is on (highlighted), links you click in the live pane open in the companion pane instead, so the live pane stays put. Whether it is on or off, holding Alt while clicking a link in either pane opens it in the other pane.

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Scroll sync
text: When Scroll sync is on (highlighted), scrolling one pane scrolls the other to the same relative position (for example, halfway down both pages).

title: Layout, compare and sync
heading: Performance chip
text: The first global control shows the frame rate, for example "58 fps", with a coloured health dot. - Point at it (or focus it) to see the Performance panel: FPS , Frame time , CPU busy (long tasks) , Event-loop lag , JS heap (RAM) where the browser reports it, DOM nodes · live and DOM nodes · pane 2 . - Click it to pin the panel open; click again to unpin. Two full pages at once can be heavy. When readings stay poor for a few seconds (frame rate below 32, CPU busy above 65%, or lag above 400 milliseconds), split view switches both panes, and the page behind, to the site's low-performance mode, which turns off decorative effects. The panel then reads "Eco mode active — panes switched to the low performance tier until readings recover." When readings stay good for a few seconds, normal mode returns. Otherwise it reads "Optimizer on standby — kicks in automatically when FPS drops or lag builds up."

title: Panes and their controls
text: Each pane has the same row of controls in the toolbar.

title: Panes and their controls
heading: The pane tab
text: The tab at the start of each row names the pane: by default the page's own title (for example "Basic Tools"). A dot shows its state: amber and pulsing while the page loads, green when it is ready. Rename a pane: double-click its tab, type a name and press Enter (or click elsewhere). Press Esc to cancel. An empty name returns to the page title. Your name stays on the pane while you browse in it, until you close split view.

title: Panes and their controls
heading: Back, Forward and Reload
text: Each pane has its own history. Back and Forward move through the pages that pane has shown; Reload reloads just that pane.

title: Panes and their controls
heading: The address bar
text: Each pane has an address bar showing its page's address on the site, for example /library/palette/ . To load another page: 1. Select the address bar. A list of destinations opens, grouped under Home , Tools , Libraries , Account , Company , Legal and your Recent pages. 2. Type to narrow the list: page names, addresses and keywords all match (for example oklch finds the Colour Science Lab). 3. Use Up and Down to choose and Enter to load, or click an entry. You can also type an address that is not in the list: a site path such as /tool/icon/ (the list offers Go to that path) or a full https:// address ( Open external URL ). Press Ctrl + Enter to open the typed address in a new browser tab instead. Press Esc to close the list, and again to put back the current address. Loading a new page in the live pane means closing split view will take you to that page. The companion's address bar tooltip reads "Edit the companion pane's URL and press Enter to load it." Pages you load are added to Recent (up to 10 site pages), and split view uses your most recent companion page the next time it opens.

title: Panes and their controls
heading: The More menu
text: Select the three dots ( More pane controls ) at the end of a pane's row: Control What it does --- --- Theme Cycles Auto , Light and Dark for this pane only. Light and dark apply instantly. Viewport Cycles desktop (full pane width), tablet (820 pixels) and phone (400 pixels). The page inside reflows to that width. Zoom Cycles 100% , 125% , 150% and 75% for this pane. Focus this pane Moves keyboard focus into the pane and outlines it ( Alt + 1 for live, Alt + 2 for companion). Select again to clear. Maximize Gives this pane the whole area. Select again to restore. Open in new tab Opens this pane's page in a new browser tab. Copy URL Copies this pane's page address, without the split details. Controls that differ from their default (a forced theme, a device width, a zoom other than 100%) are highlighted. The menu stays open while you cycle theme or zoom; click elsewhere or press Esc to close it. Your own site theme setting is not changed by a pane's theme. When you switch a pane back to Auto , it reloads to follow your site theme again.

title: Panes and their controls
heading: Keyboard inside a pane
text: Keyboard shortcuts pressed inside a pane (such as Esc , Alt + S or Ctrl + Shift + D ) still reach split view.

title: Share a split
text: While split view is open, the browser's address bar keeps a description of the split after split= . It records: - the live pane's page and the companion pane's page, including where each is scrolled and what you entered on them; - side-by-side or stacked layout; - the divider position; - each pane's theme, viewport and zoom; - whether the panes are swapped.

title: Share a split
heading: Share or bookmark a split
text: 1. Set up split view the way you want it. 2. Copy the address from your browser's address bar (or bookmark it). 3. Open the address later, or send it to someone. Result: the page opens straight into split view, with both panes, the layout and the pane settings restored.

title: Share a split
heading: Things to know
text: - The address updates as you work, including as you scroll either pane. - Pane names you typed are not part of the address. - Closing split view removes the split details from the address. - Copy URL in a pane's More menu copies only that pane's page, without the split. - A shared split contains the addresses of both pages and the values entered on them. Check it before sending it to someone.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: Ctrl + Shift + D does nothing, or bookmarks the page
text: Why: in some browsers Ctrl + Shift + D also means "bookmark all tabs". Split view claims the shortcut once the page has loaded; pressed too early, the browser may act on it instead. What to do: wait for the page to finish loading, or use Open split view in the navigation dock.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: An outside website shows as a blank pane
text: Why: many websites do not allow themselves to be shown inside another page. External pages that do load are not controlled by split view, so the pane's theme, zoom and history buttons may not affect them. What to do: use Open in new tab from the pane's More menu.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: A pane is slow or the page stutters
text: Why: two full pages are running at once. What to do: let eco mode switch on, close heavy tools in one pane, or use a smaller viewport. The performance chip shows what is happening.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: Closing split view took me to a different page
text: Why: you loaded another page in the live pane. Closing follows the live pane. What to do: use your browser's Back button to return.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: The Theme control shows Auto but the pane is not following my theme
text: Why: switching a pane back to Auto reloads it. If the reload has not finished, wait a moment.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: Compare shows everything in colour
text: Why: the two pages differ everywhere, for example because they are scrolled to different places or use different themes on purpose. What to do: load the same page in both panes ( Mirror ), then change one thing, such as the theme, to see just that difference.

title: Troubleshooting split view
heading: A shared split opened as a normal page
text: Why: the link lost the part after split= , for example because an app shortened it. What to do: copy the full address again from the address bar.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Is the live pane a screenshot?
text: No. It is the real page, fully working, in its own window area. You can click, type and scroll in it.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Does split view change my page?
text: No. Your original page keeps running untouched behind split view.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Can I see a page at phone width?
text: Yes. Set the pane's Viewport to phone (400 pixels) in its More menu. The page reflows as it would on a phone.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Can I compare light and dark?
text: Yes. Use Mirror so both panes show the same page, then set one pane's Theme to Light and the other to Dark. Compare then highlights every difference.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Can I have more than two panes?
text: No. Split view shows two panes.

title: Split view FAQ
heading: Does split view work on a phone?
text: It opens, but two pages on a small screen are cramped. It is designed for larger windows.

title: Split view glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Live pane The pane that starts with the page you were on. Closing split view follows it. Companion pane The second pane, for any other page. Divider The bar between the panes that you drag to resize them. Viewport The width a pane's page is laid out for: desktop, tablet (820 px) or phone (400 px). Responsive A page that rearranges itself to fit the width it is given. Compare mode An overlay of both panes in which identical areas turn black and differences show. Route links A mode in which links clicked in the live pane open in the companion. Scroll sync Scrolling one pane scrolls the other to the same relative position. Eco mode Automatic low-performance mode that turns off decorative effects when the panes run slowly. FPS Frames per second: how smoothly the screen is updating.

title: Split view privacy
text: - Stored in your browser: your recent pane destinations (up to 10 site pages) and the divider sizes. - In the address bar: while open, the address describes both panes, including each page's remembered state (scroll position and values entered). Anyone you send the address to sees those pages and values. - Not sent anywhere: split view runs entirely in your browser. Opening an external address in a pane loads that website directly, as a normal visit would. - Performance readings are measured in your browser and shown only to you.

title: Theme
text: Auric Artisan has a light theme and a dark theme. A third choice, System (called Auto in the mobile drawer), follows your device: when your operating system switches between light and dark, the site switches with it, even on a page that is already open. System is the default. You can change the theme from several places: the sun and moon button in the header, the Settings panel, the mobile drawer, a keyboard shortcut, the right-click menu, Spotlight's commands and the card menu. They all change the same setting, which applies to every page in this browser and to every open tab. The site also applies your theme before the page is drawn, so a page does not flash the wrong theme as it loads. Some panels can override the theme for themselves: each kit has its own light and dark button, and each pane of split view can be forced light or dark. These do not change the site's theme.

title: Theme
heading: Who it is for
text: Everyone. Dark suits low light and long sessions; light suits bright rooms, printing and checking colours against white. When you compare colours or contrast, it can help to check them in both.

title: Theme
heading: Where to find it
text: - The sun or moon button at the right of the header. - Settings › Appearance › Theme ( Ctrl + , ). - The mobile drawer › Preferences › Theme . - Alt + T anywhere on the site.

title: Theme
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Select the moon in the header. The page turns dark and the button now shows a sun. 2. Select the sun. The page turns light. 3. Press Alt + T three times and watch the message: "Theme: Light", "Theme: Dark", "Theme: System" (the order depends on where you start). 4. Open Settings with Ctrl + , and select System under Theme . 5. Change your device between light and dark mode. The page follows.

title: Theme
heading: What you can do
text: - Choose Light, Dark or System. - Switch quickly from the header, the keyboard, the right-click menu, Spotlight or the card menu. - Keep a kit, or a split-view pane, in a different theme from the page.

title: Get started with themes
heading: The three modes
text: Mode What you see --- --- Light Light pages with dark text, always Dark Dark pages with light text, always System ( Auto in the drawer) Light or dark to match your device's setting, changing when it changes System is the default for a new visitor.

title: Get started with themes
heading: Choose a mode
text: 1. Press Ctrl + , to open Settings. Appearance is selected. 2. Under Theme , select Light , Dark or System . The page changes at once, and every other page and open tab follows.

title: Get started with themes
heading: How System mode follows your device
text: With System selected, the site asks your browser whether your device is set to dark mode, and uses dark if it is. When the device switches (for example on a schedule at sunset), the site switches too, without a reload. Where to change your device's setting: - Windows: Settings › Personalisation › Colours › Choose your mode. - macOS: System Settings › Appearance. - Android: Settings › Display › Dark theme. - iOS and iPadOS: Settings › Display & Brightness.

title: Get started with themes
heading: What the header button does to System mode
text: The header's sun and moon button always switches to the opposite of what you see now, and makes that choice fixed. If you were on System and the page was dark, selecting the sun sets the theme to Light , and the Settings panel moves from System to Light . To follow your device again, choose System in Settings or Auto in the drawer.

title: Get started with themes
heading: What changes with the theme
text: - The page background, text, borders and panels. - The default gold accent is drawn slightly darker in the light theme to stay readable. A custom accent is not changed. Tool results, images and colour swatches are not recoloured.

title: Every way to switch the theme
text: All of these change the same site-wide setting, except the last two, which affect only one panel.

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Header button
text: The sun or moon at the right of the header (tooltip Theme : "Switch between light and dark mode"). - It shows a moon while the page is light (select it to go dark) and a sun while the page is dark. - It always switches to the opposite of what you see, and fixes that choice (it leaves System mode).

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Settings panel
text: Settings ( Ctrl + , ) › Appearance › Theme : Light , Dark , System . This is the only place, with the drawer, that can set System .

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Mobile drawer
text: On narrow screens, open the drawer and use Preferences › Theme : Auto , Light , Dark . Auto is the same as System . The highlighted button shows your current choice.

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Keyboard
text: Alt + T anywhere on the site (not while typing in a field) moves one step through Light , Dark and System , in that order, and shows a message such as "Theme: Dark".

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Right-click menu
text: Right-click the page, open View , and choose Switch theme . The row shows the current theme ( Light or Dark ). It works like the header button. You can pin it to the quick bar with its star, and filter for it by typing dark or light .

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Spotlight command
text: Press Ctrl + K , type , and choose Toggle light and dark . The row shows the current theme. It works like the header button.

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: Card menu
text: On pages with card grids, right-click a card and select the Theme pill under System . It works like the header button.

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: A kit's own theme button
text: Each kit has a sun or moon button in its title bar, labelled for example "Switch Status Kit to light mode". It changes the theme of that kit only and is remembered for it. Until you use it, a kit follows the site theme. See [Kits](../../../kits/README.md).

title: Every way to switch the theme
heading: A split-view pane
text: In split view, each pane has a Theme control in its More menu that cycles Auto , Light and Dark for that pane only, so you can compare the two themes side by side. It does not change your setting. See [Split view](../../split-view/README.md).

title: Troubleshooting themes
heading: The site does not follow my device any more
text: Why: a light/dark toggle (the header button, the right-click menu, Spotlight or the card menu) fixes the theme and leaves System mode. What to do: choose System in Settings › Appearance, or Auto in the mobile drawer.

title: Troubleshooting themes
heading: The site is dark but my device is light (or the other way round)
text: Possible causes: - You chose Light or Dark at some point, so System mode is off. Open Settings and check Theme . - Your browser has its own theme setting that overrides the device. In some browsers you can set the website appearance separately from the operating system.

title: Troubleshooting themes
heading: One panel is in a different theme from the page
text: Why: kits remember their own theme once you use their theme button, and split-view panes can be forced light or dark. What to do: use the kit's own theme button to match the page. For split view, set the pane's theme back to Auto .

title: Troubleshooting themes
heading: My theme changed after I opened a link someone sent me
text: Why: page links copied from the site can carry the sender's appearance settings, including the theme mode. See [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md). What to do: set your theme again in Settings.

title: Troubleshooting themes
heading: The theme resets every time I close the browser
text: Why: you are using a private window, or your browser clears site data on exit. What to do: use a normal window, or allow auricartisan.com to keep site data.

title: Theme FAQ
heading: Is there a high-contrast theme?
text: There is no separate theme, but Settings › Comfort › Boost contrast strengthens text and borders in both themes. See [Accessibility aids](../../accessibility-aids/README.md).

title: Theme FAQ
heading: Does the theme change colours in the tools?
text: No. The theme changes the site's interface. Colours you are working with, swatches and images are shown as they are.

title: Theme FAQ
heading: Does my account remember my theme?
text: The site theme is kept in your browser, not in your account. Your account dashboard has its own theme preference; see [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: Theme FAQ
heading: Can I set a different theme for one kit?
text: Yes. Use the sun or moon button in that kit's title bar. It affects only that kit.

title: Theme FAQ
heading: Why does the page not flash when it loads?
text: The site reads your saved theme before it draws the page, so it starts in the right theme.

title: Theme privacy
text: - Your theme mode is kept in this browser's local storage for auricartisan.com, along with the last light or dark choice made with a toggle. The cookie policy lists this under Functional storage. - Each kit's own theme choice is kept the same way. - Nothing about your theme is sent to Auric Artisan when you change it. - A page link copied from the site can include your theme mode (see [Shareable links](../../shareable-links/README.md)).

title: Accessibility and vision tools
text: This group covers the tools on auricartisan.com that help you make a design or a website usable by more people. Some of them measure a live page against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), the W3C standard that most accessibility laws point at. Others show you how colour looks to people with colour-vision deficiencies or low vision, so you can catch problems that a number alone does not reveal. The tools range from a one-question checker to a full audit console. Use the small tools when you already know what you are asking, and the Analyzer when you want to find the problems you do not know about yet. Every tool here is free to use. A few actions that run on Auric Artisan's servers, such as rendering someone else's website or crawling a whole site, need an account and are metered in tokens. Each tool's own docs say exactly which actions those are.

title: Accessibility and vision tools
heading: Which tool should I open?
text: - You have two colours and want a yes or no: open the [Contrast Checker](contrast-checker/README.md). - You have a URL and want every problem on the page: open the [Analyzer](analyzer/README.md). - You are preparing a manual audit or an accessibility statement: open the [Accessibility Checklist](accessibility-checklist/README.md). - You want to see a palette or an image the way someone with a colour-vision deficiency sees it: open the [Vision Lab](vision-simulation/README.md). - You are teaching how colour-vision tests work: open the [Ishihara Plate Generator](ishihara-plate-generator/README.md). Important: None of these tools gives a legal certification or a medical diagnosis. Automated testing finds real problems quickly, but a conformance claim needs manual review as well, and a vision simulation is an approximation, not an eye test.

title: Accessibility Checklist
text: The Accessibility Checklist is a free working checklist of 50 accessibility checks, grouped into nine areas, from semantics and keyboard focus to forms, media, colour, motion, ARIA, zoom and testing. Each check is explained in full: what it means, who it affects, how to test it, what the fix looks like in code, and what usually breaks it. You work through it in the Inspector : a list of every check beside the selected check in full. Mark each one Pass , Fail or N/A , attach annotated screenshots as evidence, and watch a meter count what is left. When you are done, print the findings or copy them as Markdown into your issue tracker. Everything stays in your browser; there is no account and nothing is uploaded. The page also carries a Reference of what the WCAG levels mean and what the law asks for in 15 jurisdictions, India first, with links to the primary sources.

title: Accessibility Checklist
heading: Who it is for
text: - Front-end developers, designers and accessibility testers preparing or running a manual review. - Teams who want evidence of a process to go with an automated audit. - Anyone who needs to know which accessibility law applies where, and to which WCAG version.

title: Accessibility Checklist
heading: Where to find it
text: - Address: https://auricartisan.com/resources/accessibility-checklist/ - From any page: open the Learn menu in the site header and select Accessibility Compliance ("WCAG checks & guidance"). - The old addresses https://auricartisan.com/accessibility-compliance/ and https://auricartisan.com/compliance forward here. See [Accessibility Compliance](../accessibility-compliance/README.md). - A single check: add check- and the check's ID, for example https://auricartisan.com/resources/accessibility-checklist/ check-k2 .

title: Accessibility Checklist
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/resources/accessibility-checklist/. The first check, "Landmarks wrap every region of the page", is selected. 2. Optionally run the automated pass first: select Run the automated pass first → to open the [Analyzer](../analyzer/README.md) on your page. 3. Read the check in the pane on the right (on a phone, tap a row to open it). 4. Test your page as the How to test it block describes. 5. Select Pass , Fail or N/A . With focus in the list or the pane, you can press Space , F or N . 6. Press J to move to the next check, and repeat. 7. For a failure, select Attach screenshot , add a screenshot and mark it up. 8. Open the Export tab and select Copy as Markdown or Export the report .

title: Accessibility Checklist
heading: What you can do
text: - Read 50 checks, each tied to a WCAG 2.2 success criterion or marked as good practice, with a code example for most. - See which checks the Analyzer can decide for you ( AUTO ), narrow down ( PARTLY ), or cannot judge ( BY HAND ). - Mark each check Pass , Fail or N/A , and clear a mark by pressing it again. - Filter to Required (Level A and AA), AAA or Practice checks, or hide passed checks with Open only . - Attach any number of screenshots to a check and annotate them with a pen, highlighter, arrows, boxes, redaction and numbered callouts. - Print the flagged findings, or copy them as Markdown for Jira, Linear or GitHub. - Look up the accessibility law for India, the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Japan and eight more countries. - Work entirely from the keyboard.

title: Getting started with the Accessibility Checklist
Getting started with the Accessibility Checklist
heading: Open it
text: Go to https://auricartisan.com/resources/accessibility-checklist/, or open the Learn menu in the site header and select Accessibility Compliance . No account is needed.

title: Getting started with the Accessibility Checklist
heading: The screen, top to bottom
text: The kicker "Auric Artisan · Accessibility", the title The accessibility checklist , and a line: "Fifty checks across the whole of WCAG 2.2, each one explained: what it means, who it affects, how to test it, and what the fix looks like in code." A note under it says: "The analyzer decides 11 of these outright and narrows 23 more. The rest needs a person, which is what the explanations are for." Two links follow: - Run the automated pass first → opens the [Analyzer](../../analyzer/README.md). - Wire it into CI → opens the public API documentation. Three tabs: Checklist , Export and Reference . With a tab focused, Left and Right move between tabs (wrapping round), and Home and End jump to the first or last. Beside the tabs is the meter : "0 passed · 0 flagged · 50 left", a two-colour bar (passed and flagged), and "of 50". The meter always counts all 50 checks, whatever filter is on. When a filter is on, a small chip beside it names the filter and how many rows it shows, for example "REQUIRED · 35". On wide screens the tab rail and meter stay pinned under the site header as you scroll. On screens at least 1080 pixels wide, the Checklist tab is two columns: - The index , on the left: filter buttons, then nine numbered areas, each with a header showing how many of its checks you have decided (for example "0 / 6"), then one row per check. Each row shows a state symbol, the check title and its tag (for example "A 1.3.1" or "PRACTICE"). Required checks show their tag in gold. - The pane , on the right: the selected check in full. It stays in view while the index scrolls. The first check is selected when you arrive, unless the address names another one. On narrower screens you see the index only. Tapping a row opens that check full-screen, with an All checks button to go back. See [Work through the checklist](work-through-the-checklist.md). From top to bottom: 1. A bar with the check's position ("3 of 50") and Previous check and Next check buttons. 2. The area, for example "01 Semantics & structure". 3. The check title. 4. Chips: the criterion tag, Required for Level A and AA checks, and AUTO , PARTLY or BY HAND with a sentence saying how much the Analyzer can decide. 5. A one-sentence summary of the check. 6. The verdict buttons: Pass , Fail , N/A and Attach screenshot . 7. Evidence , once you have attached screenshots. 8. The explanation: What it means , Who it affects , How to test it , What the fix looks like (on most checks), Usually breaks when , and links such as "Understanding 1.3.1" to the W3C.

title: Getting started with the Accessibility Checklist
heading: Mark your first check
text: 1. Make sure the first check, "Landmarks wrap every region of the page", is selected in the pane. 2. Open the page you are testing in another tab. 3. Follow How to test it . For this check, you run a short snippet in the browser console and look for exactly one main landmark and a label on every repeated nav . 4. Back in the checklist, select Pass if the page meets it, Fail if it does not, or N/A if it does not apply. 5. Look at the index row: its symbol changes, and the meter updates. 6. Select Next check (or press J with focus in the list or pane) to move on. The result: your mark is saved in this browser straight away. Close the tab and come back later, and it is still there.
