title: Kits
text: Kits are small floating panels that you can open on any page of auricartisan.com without leaving the page you are on. Each kit does one job: the Feature Kit holds a calculator, a unit converter, notes, date tools and developer utilities; the Menu Kit is a start menu for the whole site; the Advanced Kit decides which tools the site shows you; the Status Kit shows the status of pages and your device; the Library Kit holds everything you have saved from the tools. Kits are modeless. A kit floats above the page, and the page underneath stays usable: you can scroll, click and type in a tool while a kit is open. You can drag a kit anywhere in the window, make it larger, shrink it to its title bar, give it its own light or dark theme, and keep it open while you move from page to page. All kits open from one place: the page utilities bar in the bottom-left corner of the window. A few kits also have keyboard shortcuts, and the Library Kit has a button in the site header.

title: Kits
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone using the site's tools who wants a quick calculation, conversion or note without opening another tab. - Designers and developers who save palettes, gradients, reports and presets and want to find, compare and reuse them. - Visitors who want a simpler or a more technical view of the site's tools. - Anyone who wants to see how a page or their device is doing: page status, connection, memory, frame rate.

title: Kits
heading: Where to find it
text: - On every page of https://auricartisan.com, select the round Page utilities button in the bottom-left corner. The bar opens and shows one labelled launcher per kit. - Keyboard shortcuts open some kits directly. See [Keyboard shortcuts](others/shortcuts.md). - The Library Kit also opens from the Library button in the site header, from a link ending in library , and from https://auricartisan.com/library/workspace/.

title: Kits
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open any page on https://auricartisan.com. 2. Select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner. The bar opens with the launchers Feature , Menu , Advanced , Status , Library , Navigate and Settings , and the hub button now reads Close . 3. Select Menu . The bar folds away and the Menu Kit opens in the bottom-left corner with its search box ready. 4. Drag the kit by its title bar to move it somewhere convenient. 5. Select the four-arrow Resize button in the kit's title bar to make it wider and taller. 6. Select the target-shaped Focus mode button if you want the kit to stay open when you go to another page. 7. Select the cross ( Close ) in the title bar, or press Esc , to close the kit.

title: Getting started with kits
text: A kit is a floating panel that opens over the page you are on. This guide opens one, walks through the parts every kit shares, and closes it again.

title: Getting started with kits
heading: Before you start
text: - Kits work on desktop and on phones. On a narrow screen the launcher bar wraps into two rows. - Kits need JavaScript. Each kit loads the first time you open it, so the first open can take a moment on a slow connection. While it loads, its launcher looks dimmed and shows a busy pointer. - Nothing needs an account. Kits keep their preferences in your browser. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Getting started with kits
heading: Open your first kit
text: 1. Go to any page, for example https://auricartisan.com. 2. Find the round button in the bottom-left corner of the window. Its tooltip reads Page utilities . 3. Select it. A bar slides open with labelled launchers: Close , Feature , Menu , Advanced , Status , Library , Navigate and Settings . 4. Select Feature . The bar folds away and the Feature Kit opens in the bottom-left corner of the window, showing six cards. 5. Select Scientific Calculator , type 2+3 with your keyboard and press Enter . You see 5 in the calculator's display. You have opened a kit, switched to one of its tools and used it.

title: Getting started with kits
heading: The parts of a kit panel
text: Every kit panel has the same frame. - Title bar. The kit's name sits on the left. Drag the title bar to move the panel. - Title-bar buttons. On the right: Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize and Close , in that order. The Library Kit puts all but Close in a Panel options menu. - Body. The kit's own content: cards, tabs, a search box, results. The body scrolls when there is more than fits. - Launcher. The labelled button in the page utilities bar that opens the kit. While a kit is open, its launcher shows a cross, and selecting it again closes the kit. [Panel controls](panel-controls.md) explains each button in detail.

title: Getting started with kits
heading: Keep working while a kit is open
text: Kits do not block the page. While a kit is open you can scroll the page, click links and type into tools. Clicking on the page does not close the kit. The Feature Kit is the one exception: when Focus mode is off, it dims the page behind it, and clicking the dimmed page closes it. Turn on Focus mode in the Feature Kit to work on the page while it stays open.

title: Getting started with kits
heading: Open more than one kit
text: Opening a kit normally closes whichever kit was already open. To keep two kits open side by side: 1. Open the first kit and select its Focus mode button. The button turns gold. 2. Open the second kit from the page utilities bar. 3. Drag the two panels apart by their title bars. Both kits stay open. The Status Kit is an exception: it closes when another kit opens, even with Focus mode on.

title: Getting started with kits
heading: Close a kit
text: Use any of these: - Select Close (the cross) in the kit's title bar. - Press Esc . In the Feature Kit, the first Esc goes back to the Feature Kit menu and the second closes the kit. In the Menu Kit and the Library Kit, the first Esc clears the search box if it has text in it. - Select the kit's launcher again. While the Feature Kit's Focus mode is on, its launcher moves keyboard focus into the kit instead of closing it. If Focus mode is on, a closed kit can open again by itself on the next page you visit. Turn Focus mode off first if you want it to stay closed. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

title: Panel controls
text: Every kit panel has a title bar with the same set of controls: move, Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize and Close . This page explains each control, what the kits remember between visits, and the places where a kit does something different.

title: Panel controls
heading: Sizes and starting position
text: A kit opens in the bottom-left corner of the window, just above the page utilities bar, until you move it. It opens at its normal size unless you left it expanded. Kit Normal width Expanded width --- --- --- Feature Kit 560 px 640 px Menu Kit 680 px 820 px Advanced Kit 480 px 720 px Status Kit 560 px 760 px Library Kit 680 px 940 px - An expanded kit is never wider than the window, less a small margin. - An expanded Menu, Advanced, Status or Library Kit grows to at most 900 px tall, and always leaves room for its title bar at the top of the window. An expanded Feature Kit grows to at most 900 px or 90% of the window height, whichever is smaller. - On a phone (580 px wide or narrower) every kit spans the width of the screen, less a small margin.

title: Panel controls
heading: Move a panel
text: With a pointer or touch: 1. Press on the kit's title bar, away from the buttons. 2. Drag the panel to where you want it. 3. Release. The panel stays inside the window: you cannot drag it past an edge. The kit remembers its position as a proportion of the window, so it returns to the same relative place next time you open it, on any page, and it moves back inside the window if the window becomes smaller. Differences between kits: - Feature Kit. Drag by the title text itself ("Feature Kit", or the name of the tool you have open). - Library Kit. Drag the title bar or the six-dot grip at its left end. With the keyboard (Library Kit only): 1. Press Tab until the six-dot grip at the left of the title bar has focus. It announces itself as Move library panel . 2. Press an arrow key to move the panel 12 pixels in that direction. 3. Hold Shift with an arrow key to move 1 pixel at a time. Put a panel back in its corner: - Library Kit: open Panel options and select Reset position . A message confirms "Library returned to its default position." - Other kits: drag the panel back. There is no reset button. Clearing this site's stored data in your browser also returns every kit to its corner, but it clears your other kit preferences too.

title: Panel controls
heading: Focus mode
text: The Focus mode button has a target icon and sits first in the row of title-bar buttons. Its tooltip reads "Keep [kit name] open through navigation and while opening other kits." When it is on, the button turns gold. The kit remembers the setting in your browser. What Focus mode does depends on the kit: Kit Stays open when another kit opens Opens again on the next page Closing the kit turns Focus mode off --- --- --- --- Feature Kit Yes Yes, on the tool you were using Yes Menu Kit Yes Yes No Advanced Kit Yes Yes No Status Kit No Yes No Library Kit Yes Yes No In practice: - Feature Kit. Focus mode also changes how the kit sits on the page. With Focus mode off, the page behind the Feature Kit is dimmed, Tab keeps moving within the kit, and clicking the dimmed page closes the kit. With Focus mode on, the page is not dimmed and stays fully usable, and selecting the Feature launcher moves keyboard focus into the kit instead of closing it. Closing the Feature Kit with Close or Esc turns Focus mode off. - Menu, Advanced, Status and Library Kits. Focus mode stays on until you turn it off. If you close one of these kits while its Focus mode is on, it opens again on the next page you load. Turn Focus mode off before closing if you want it to stay closed. - Library Kit. The control is called Keep open in the Panel options menu, described as "Stay visible while opening other kits".

title: Panel controls
heading: Theme
text: The Theme button switches the kit between light and dark. The icon shows the mode you will switch to: a sun while the kit is dark, a moon while it is light. The tooltip reads "Switch this kit between light and dark mode." (In the Menu Kit it says "this menu", and in the Library Kit "this panel".) - Until you use the button, a kit follows the site's theme and changes when the site changes. - Once you use it, the kit keeps its own choice, even on a page whose theme is different. A light kit on a dark page, or the other way round, is expected. - Each kit remembers its own choice. The kit's launcher in the page utilities bar follows the same choice. - There is no button that hands a kit back to the site theme. Set the kit to match the site, or clear this site's stored data. The accent colour you choose in the site settings panel also colours the kits' gold highlights. See [Site features](../../site-features/README.md).

title: Panel controls
heading: Resize
text: The Resize button, with four arrows, switches between the normal and the expanded size shown in the table above. The icon changes to arrows pointing inwards while the kit is expanded. Its tooltip reads "Switch [kit name] between normal and expanded size." The kit remembers the choice and opens expanded next time, on any page. In the Library Kit the control is Panel size in Panel options , described as "Toggle the wider workspace view". In the Feature Kit, expanding also gives the calculator's graph more room.

title: Panel controls
heading: Minimize
text: The Minimize button, a short dash, shrinks the kit. - Menu, Advanced, Status and Library Kits. The kit collapses to its title bar. The button changes to a restore icon (a square with a line). Select the restore button, or select anywhere on the title bar that is not a button, to bring the kit back. The tooltip reads "Collapse [kit name] to its title bar — click the bar to restore." A minimised kit is not remembered: it opens at full height next time. - Feature Kit. The kit shrinks to a small round icon where the panel was, and the Feature launcher hides. Select the icon, or give it focus and press Enter or Space , to reopen the kit at its menu. If the kit was expanded before, it comes back expanded.

title: Panel controls
heading: Close
text: The Close button is a cross at the right end of the title bar. You can also: - press Esc (see each kit's guide for how Esc interacts with search boxes and sub-panels); - select the kit's launcher in the page utilities bar. Closing does not lose your work in the kits that keep it: calculator history, notes, library items and settings stay in your browser. What a closed kit forgets is listed in each kit's reference.

title: Panel controls
heading: What the title bar holds in each kit
text: Kit Left side Buttons, left to right --- --- --- Feature Kit Back (only inside a tool), then the title Graph and History (calculator only), Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize , Close Menu Kit Menu Kit and a site status chip, for example Beta Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize , Close Advanced Kit Advanced Kit Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize , Close Status Kit Status Kit Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize , Close Library Kit Six-dot grip, Your Library and an item count Panel options ( Keep open , Theme , Panel size , Minimize , Reset position ), Close On a phone, the Menu Kit's title bar stacks its title, status chip and buttons in a centred column.

title: Panel controls
heading: What the kits remember
text: All kits keep these preferences in your browser, per kit: Preference Remembered Notes --- --- --- Position after dragging Yes Stored as a proportion of the window size Expanded size Yes Opens expanded next time Focus mode Yes Feature Kit turns it off when you close the kit Theme Yes, once you use the button Until then the kit follows the site Minimised No A kit always opens at full height Each kit also remembers things of its own, such as the Menu Kit's last tab or the Library Kit's sort order. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md) for the full list.

title: Panel controls
heading: Other things you may see in a kit
text: Depending on your cookie choices and your plan, a small sponsored strip can appear in the Feature Kit menu, the Menu Kit and the Advanced Kit. The Ads in panels & search switch in the site settings panel controls it; changing ad settings is a paid-plan convenience. See [Site features](../../site-features/README.md) and [Account and billing](../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: The page utilities bar
text: The page utilities bar is the one place every kit opens from. It sits in the bottom-left corner of every page. Closed, it is a single round button; open, it is a row of labelled launchers.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Closed and open
text: Closed , the bar is one round button with a gold outline. Its tooltip reads Page utilities : "Show navigation, settings, and the Feature, Menu, Advanced, Status and Library kits." Open , the bar becomes a single card with one cell per launcher. Each cell shows an icon with a one-word name under it: Cell What it opens Tooltip --- --- --- Close Folds the bar away. This is the same round button, relabelled while the bar is open. Hide page utilities Feature [Feature Kit](../feature-kit/README.md) Calculator, converter, graph tools, and feedback. Menu [Menu Kit](../menu-kit/README.md) Open site navigation, grouped pages, and quick search. Advanced [Advanced Kit](../advanced-kit/README.md) Choose Basic, Advanced, or Everything tool visibility. Status [Status Kit](../status-kit/README.md) View the current page status and scan page status entries. Library [Library Kit](../library-kit/README.md) Browse, search and restore everything you have saved across the tools. Navigate The page navigation dock Back, forward, reload, outline, split view and jump to top or bottom. Settings The site settings panel Settings Thin dividers separate the three groups: the Close button, the five kits, and the two page controls ( Navigate and Settings ). Navigate and Settings are site features rather than kits; see [Site features](../../site-features/README.md).

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Open the bar and a kit
text: 1. Select the round Page utilities button. 2. Select a launcher, for example Status . The bar folds away and the kit opens. On a desktop screen the kit panel appears in the bottom-left corner, just above the round button, unless you have moved it before.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Close the bar
text: Any of these folds the bar back into its round button: - Select Close , the first cell. - Press Esc . - Click anywhere on the page outside the bar. - Select any launcher. The kit opens and the bar closes. Folding the bar away does not close any kit. The tooltip says so: "Put the bar away. The kits stay where they are."

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Launchers of open kits
text: While a kit is open, its launcher shows a cross instead of its icon. Selecting it closes the kit. The Feature Kit, the Advanced Kit and the Library Kit go one step further: while one of them is open, its launcher gets a gold tint and stays on screen beside the round button even after the bar folds away, so you can close the kit from there. For the Menu Kit and the Status Kit, open the bar again or use the kit's own Close button.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Loading
text: Each kit loads the first time you open it on a page. Until it has loaded, its launcher is dimmed, shows a busy pointer and ignores further clicks. Hovering over a launcher or giving it keyboard focus starts loading early, so the kit usually opens without a wait.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: On a phone
text: On screens 580 pixels wide or narrower, the bar changes shape: - The round button is slightly smaller and sits closer to the corner. - Open, the bar stretches across the bottom of the screen and wraps into two rows. The top row holds the five kits. A thin line separates it from the bottom row, which holds Navigate , Settings and Close . - While the bar is open, the page gains extra space at the bottom, so the end of the page is not hidden under the bar. - The page navigation dock does not show its own collapsed tab on a phone. Open it with Navigate . Kit panels also adapt: on a phone every kit opens across the full width of the screen, less a small margin on each side.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Keyboard use
text: - Tab reaches the round button like any other button. Press Enter or Space to open the bar, then Tab through the launchers. - Esc closes the bar. - Several kits have their own shortcuts that work without the bar. See [Keyboard shortcuts](../others/shortcuts.md).

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Accessibility
text: - The round button announces itself as Show page utilities or Hide page utilities and reports whether the bar is expanded. - The bar is a toolbar named Page utility launchers . - Each launcher has a visible name as well as an icon, and a gold focus ring when it has keyboard focus. - If your system asks for reduced motion, the bar opens and closes without animation.

title: The page utilities bar
heading: Related
text: - [Panel controls](panel-controls.md) — what you can do with a kit once it is open - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) — if the bar or a launcher does not respond

title: Troubleshooting kits
text: This page covers problems that affect all kits. Each kit also has its own troubleshooting page for problems inside that kit.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: The Page utilities button is missing
text: Why: The bar is added by the site's scripts after the page has loaded. It does not appear if JavaScript is blocked, if a content blocker removes the site's scripts, or while the page is still loading on a slow connection. What to do: 1. Wait a few seconds after the page appears. The button is added once the page is ready. 2. Check that JavaScript is allowed for auricartisan.com. 3. Pause content-blocking extensions for the site and reload.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: A launcher is dimmed and does nothing
text: Why: The kit is still loading. A launcher is dimmed, with a busy pointer, from the moment you select it until the kit has loaded. It ignores further clicks during that time. What to do: Wait for the kit to open. If the launcher stays dimmed for a long time, or returns to normal without opening anything, the kit could not load, usually because the connection dropped. Reload the page and try again.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: A kit opens by itself on every page
text: Why: Its Focus mode is on. The Menu, Advanced, Status and Library Kits keep Focus mode on after you close them, and open again on the next page you load. What to do: Open the kit, select Focus mode (the target icon) so it is no longer gold, then close the kit. In the Library Kit, open Panel options and turn off Keep open .

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: Opening one kit closes another
text: Why: This is expected. Opening a kit closes any other open kit unless that kit's Focus mode is on. What to do: Turn on Focus mode in the kit you want to keep. The Status Kit is the exception: it always closes when another kit opens, whatever its Focus mode setting.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: The page goes dark behind the Feature Kit
text: Why: With Focus mode off, the Feature Kit dims the page behind it and keeps Tab inside the kit. Clicking the dimmed page closes the kit. What to do: Turn on Focus mode in the Feature Kit if you want to use the page while the kit is open. The dimming goes away.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: A kit is off to one side, or I cannot find it
text: Why: Kits remember where you dragged them, as a proportion of the window. On a much smaller window the saved position can look odd, although a kit never goes outside the window. What to do: - Drag the kit by its title bar to where you want it. - In the Library Kit, open Panel options and select Reset position . - If a kit is minimised, look for its title bar alone (or, for the Feature Kit, a small round icon) and select it to restore the kit.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: A kit is light on a dark page, or dark on a light page
text: Why: You have used the kit's own Theme button. From then on the kit keeps its own light or dark setting and no longer follows the site theme. What to do: Select the kit's Theme button to switch it to the mode you want. There is no button that makes a kit follow the site again; clearing this site's stored data in your browser does that, but also clears your other kit preferences.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: A keyboard shortcut does nothing
text: Why: Some shortcuts are also used by browsers or operating systems, which can take the key press first. For example, on a Mac Cmd + M minimises the browser window, and some desktop environments use Ctrl + Shift + U to type special characters. What to do: Open the kit from the page utilities bar instead. See [Keyboard shortcuts](../others/shortcuts.md) for every shortcut.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: Ctrl + K opens the site search instead of the kit's search
text: Why: Ctrl + K opens the site-wide search on every page, even while the Menu Kit or the Status Kit is open. What to do: Press / instead. While the Menu Kit is open, / puts the cursor in its search box. While the Status Kit is open, / puts the cursor in its path box, or in its results search after a scan.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: Esc closed more than one kit
text: Why: With Focus mode, several kits can be open at once, and Esc is heard by every open kit. What to do: Use each kit's Close button when you want to close only one of them.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: My kit settings are not remembered
text: Why: Kits keep their preferences in your browser's storage. In a private window, or when the browser blocks site storage, nothing is kept after you close the page. Clearing this site's data also removes them. What to do: Use a normal window and allow site storage for auricartisan.com. The kits still work without storage; they simply start fresh each time.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: The launcher bar covers the bottom of the page on a phone
text: Why: The open bar takes two rows at the bottom of the screen. What to do: The page gains extra space at the bottom while the bar is open, so you can scroll the last content above it. Select Close or press anywhere on the page to fold the bar back into its round button.

title: Troubleshooting kits
heading: Still stuck
text: See the kit's own troubleshooting page, or [Help](../../../help/README.md) for how to contact support. - [Feature Kit troubleshooting](../feature-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Menu Kit troubleshooting](../menu-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Advanced Kit troubleshooting](../advanced-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Status Kit troubleshooting](../status-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Library Kit troubleshooting](../library-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Update Kit troubleshooting](../update-kit/docs/troubleshooting.md)

title: Kits FAQ
heading: What is a kit?
text: A floating panel that opens over any page of the site and does one job: calculations and utilities (Feature Kit), site navigation (Menu Kit), tool visibility (Advanced Kit), page and device status (Status Kit), or your saved work (Library Kit).

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Do I need an account to use the kits?
text: No. Every kit works without signing in. The Library Kit keeps your saved items in your browser, not in an account.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Are the kits free?
text: Yes. Every kit is available on every plan. Your plan only sets how many active items the Library Kit can keep; see the [Library Kit FAQ](../library-kit/docs/faq.md).

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Where do I find the kits?
text: Select the round Page utilities button in the bottom-left corner of any page. See [The page utilities bar](the-kit-dock.md).

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Can I have two kits open at once?
text: Yes. Turn on Focus mode in the first kit before opening the second. Without Focus mode, opening a kit closes the one already open. The Status Kit always closes when another kit opens.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Will a kit stay open when I go to another page?
text: Only with Focus mode on. Each page load starts fresh, and kits with Focus mode on open again automatically.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Does a kit block the page?
text: No, with one exception. Kits float above the page and you can keep using the page. The Feature Kit dims the page while its Focus mode is off; turn Focus mode on to keep the page usable.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Why does a kit look different from the rest of the page?
text: Each kit can have its own light or dark theme, set with its Theme button. Once you use that button, the kit keeps its own choice instead of following the site.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Can I move a kit back to the corner?
text: In the Library Kit, yes: Panel options Reset position . For other kits, drag the panel back by its title bar.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Do kits work on a phone?
text: Yes. On a narrow screen the launcher bar wraps into two rows, and kits open across the width of the screen.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Can I use kits with the keyboard only?
text: Yes. The round Page utilities button and every launcher can be reached with Tab . The Feature, Menu, Advanced and Library Kits also have their own shortcuts; see [Keyboard shortcuts](../others/shortcuts.md). Moving a panel with the arrow keys is possible only in the Library Kit.

title: Kits FAQ
heading: What is the "UX Kit" in the changelog?
text: It is not a panel. It is the part of the site that changes wording and shows or hides sections when you pick a mode in the Advanced Kit. See [What each mode changes](../advanced-kit/docs/what-each-mode-changes.md).

title: Kits FAQ
heading: Is the Update Kit a panel?
text: No. It shows an Update available notice at the top of the page when a new release is out, and it runs the Update website command. See [Update Kit](../update-kit/README.md).

title: Kits FAQ
heading: What do the kits store about me?
text: Only preferences and content in your own browser, such as positions, themes, calculator history, notes and saved items. Feedback you send from the Feature Kit is sent to Auric Artisan. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Advanced Kit
text: Auric Artisan has tools for everyday colour work and tools for colour science, vision research and diagnostics. The Advanced Kit decides which of them the site puts in front of you. You choose one of four modes: Basic , Advanced , Everything or Custom . The choice applies across the whole site and is remembered in your browser. It changes which tools appear in the Menu Kit and in the tool collections, which keypads the Feature Kit calculator offers, and some of the wording on the home page and on several tool pages. In Custom mode you tick individual tools on or off from a searchable checklist. No tool is ever locked or removed: every tool page still opens from its address, and Everything mode shows all of them.

title: Advanced Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - New visitors who want a short, friendly list of tools ( Basic , the default). - Scientists, researchers and specialists who want the diagnostic and scientific tools up front ( Advanced ). - People who want to see the full range ( Everything ). - Regular users who want exactly their own set of tools ( Custom ).

title: Advanced Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: - On any page of https://auricartisan.com, select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner, then Advanced . - Or press Ctrl + Shift + A .

title: Advanced Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + Shift + A . The Advanced Kit opens, showing Tool visibility and your Current mode . 2. Under Default visibility , select the Everything card. A tick appears on it and Current mode changes to Everything . 3. Open the Menu Kit ( Ctrl + M ). A Design tab is now present with the scientific tools. 4. Back in the Advanced Kit, select the Custom card. The Choose your tools checklist appears. 5. Type lut in Filter tools… and untick LUT Lab . 6. Open the Menu Kit again: LUT Lab is no longer listed. 7. Select Basic in the Advanced Kit to return to the default.

title: Advanced Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - Switch the whole site between Basic, Advanced and Everything tool sets in one click. - Build a Custom tool set by ticking tools, with Enable all , Disable all and Reset . - Filter the checklist by name. - Open three example tools from quick cards: Analyze URLs , Image Color Picker and Generate Ishihara Plates .

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: Open the kit
text: Use either: - Page utilities (bottom-left corner) Advanced , or - Ctrl + Shift + A . The launcher's tooltip reads "Choose Basic, Advanced, or Everything tool visibility." The kit opens with keyboard focus on the card for your current mode.

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: The screen, top to bottom
text: 1. Title bar. Advanced Kit and the buttons Focus mode , Theme , Resize , Minimize and Close . 2. Heading. Tool visibility , with the line "Choose which tools stay visible by default." 3. Current mode. A badge showing Basic , Advanced , Everything or Custom . 4. Mode summary. An illustration of the current mode, a one-line title, a short description and one or two buttons to switch mode. 5. Default visibility. Four illustrated cards, one per mode. The Basic card carries a Recommended tag. The selected card shows a tick. 6. Choose your tools. The Custom checklist. It appears only in Custom mode. 7. Quick cards. Links to example tools that fit the current mode.

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: Change the mode
text: 1. Select a card under Default visibility , for example Advanced . 2. The tick moves to that card, Current mode updates, and the summary changes to "Advanced tools are on". The change applies at once to the whole site, on this page and every page you open next. You do not need to save.

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: If you have never chosen a mode
text: New visitors see the site in Basic mode. The Advanced Kit shows Basic as the current mode until you pick another card.

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: Close the kit
text: Press Esc , select Close , or select the Advanced launcher again. Your mode stays as you set it.

title: Getting started with the Advanced Kit
heading: Next steps
text: - [Choose a mode](choose-a-mode.md) - [Build a custom tool set](build-a-custom-tool-set.md) - [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md)

title: Build a custom tool set
text: In Custom mode you decide tool by tool what the site lists. Unticked tools disappear from the Menu Kit and from the tool collections, on every page of the site.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Open the checklist
text: 1. Open the Advanced Kit. 2. Select the Custom card under Default visibility . A section called Choose your tools appears below the cards. The first time, it shows Loading tools… while it gathers the list. Every tool starts ticked.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: The checklist
text: - Tools are grouped by category, for example Accessibility , Colorimetry , Generators , Perception , Spectral and Utilities , with categories in alphabetical order and tools in alphabetical order within each. - The list covers the site's tool pages only. Account, library, company and legal pages are not in it and always stay visible. - Some names differ slightly from the Menu Kit, because the checklist uses the collections' names where it can. For example the URL Analyzer appears as Analyze URLs and the Ishihara plate tool as Generate Ishihara Plates .

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Turn tools on or off
text: 1. Untick a tool to hide it. The change applies at once, across the site. 2. Tick it again to show it. There is no save button.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Find a tool in the list
text: Type part of a name in Filter tools… . Rows that do not match hide, and categories with no matching rows hide too. Clear the box to see the whole list.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Change many tools at once
text: Button What it does --- --- Enable all Ticks every tool in the list Disable all Unticks every tool in the list Reset Forgets all your custom choices, so every tool is ticked again Enable all and Disable all act on the whole list, not only the rows a filter is showing.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Where your custom set applies
text: In Custom mode, unticked tools are hidden from: - the Menu Kit's tiles and search results; - tool collections, such as https://auricartisan.com/collections/. The tool pages themselves still open if you visit them directly or follow a link from elsewhere. In Custom mode the Feature Kit calculator shows all three keypads, and page wording follows the Basic wording. See [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md).

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Your ticks are kept when you switch mode
text: Switching to Basic, Advanced or Everything does not delete your ticks. They take effect only while Custom is the current mode. Select Custom again to bring your set back.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Example: a palette-only set
text: 1. Select Custom . 2. Select Disable all . 3. Type basic in Filter tools… and tick Basic Tools . 4. Clear the filter, type gradient and tick M-Gradient Palette . 5. Clear the filter, type picker and tick Image Picker . 6. Open the Menu Kit. The Tools tab shows Basic Color Tools alongside pages that are not individual tools, such as All Tools , Collections , Search and the portfolio pages. Image Picker and M-Gradient Palette appear under Utility Labs in the Design tab.

title: Build a custom tool set
heading: Related
text: - [Choose a mode](choose-a-mode.md) - [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md) - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

title: Choose a mode
text: The tool visibility mode is one site-wide setting with four values. It decides which tools the site lists for you. Every tool can still be opened from its own address in any mode.

title: Choose a mode
heading: The four modes
text: Mode Card description Summary shown when active --- --- --- Basic (Recommended) Beginner-friendly tools stay visible while deeper scientific tools are hidden. Advanced tools are hidden — "Science, research, and precision tools stay tucked away until you need them." Advanced Scientific, diagnostic, and power-user tools stay visible while simple tools are hidden. Advanced tools are on — "Keep the scientific set visible, or open the full platform when you want more." Everything Every tool stays available, including removed or not-yet-used cards. Everything is available — "Removed and not-yet-used tools come back while Everything is active." Custom Turn individual tools on or off — your picks apply across the whole site. Your custom tool set is active — "Tick the tools you want — your picks apply across the menu and every tool grid, site-wide."

title: Choose a mode
heading: How tools are sorted into Basic and Advanced
text: Each tool is treated as basic , advanced or both : - Both tools show in every mode. They include the URL Analyzer, the Vision Deficiency Simulator, the Design System Generator, and all account, library, company and legal pages. - Basic tools are the everyday colour tools, such as Basic Color Tools, ASCII Art, Icon Library and the general colour tools. - Advanced tools are the scientific and diagnostic ones, such as the Color Science Lab, Colorimetry, Gamut and Rendering, Perception and Neuroscience, Spectral and Material tools, and the Utility Labs. Basic mode shows basic and both tools. Advanced mode shows advanced and both tools. Everything shows all tools. Custom shows every tool except the ones you untick. The full effect on each part of the site is in [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md).

title: Choose a mode
heading: Switch mode
text: Select a card under Default visibility . The change is immediate and site-wide. Or use the buttons in the mode summary, which offer the natural next step: Current mode Buttons --- --- Basic Switch to Advanced Advanced Show everything Everything Use Basic , Use Advanced Custom Show everything

title: Choose a mode
heading: Which mode to pick
text: - Start with Basic if you are new to the site or want palettes, gradients and pickers without the scientific tools. - Choose Advanced if you work with colorimetry, gamuts, spectral data or perception experiments. - Choose Everything when you are exploring, or cannot find a tool you know exists. - Choose Custom if you use a handful of tools regularly and want the menus to show only those. See [Build a custom tool set](build-a-custom-tool-set.md).

title: Choose a mode
heading: Where the mode is stored
text: The mode is stored in your browser, not in your account. Each browser and device starts in Basic until you choose. Changing the mode in one tab updates your other open tabs of the site.

title: Choose a mode
heading: Other places that change the same setting
text: A few tools have their own mode switch that changes this same site-wide setting: - The URL Analyzer 's Simple and Advanced modes set the site to Basic and Advanced . Opening the URL Analyzer also sets the site to one of these two to match its own mode. - The Vision Simulation lab's mode buttons, and resetting its filters, which sets Everything . - The Colour Science Lab 's mode buttons. After using one of them, the Advanced Kit shows the new mode.

title: Choose a mode
heading: Related
text: - [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md) - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

title: What each mode changes
text: The mode you pick in the Advanced Kit is read by several parts of the site. This page lists each one and what it does in each mode.

title: What each mode changes
heading: Summary
text: Part of the site Basic Advanced Everything Custom --- --- --- --- --- Menu Kit tiles and search Basic and both tools Advanced and both tools All All except unticked tools Tool collections Basic and both tools Advanced and both tools All, including cards hidden earlier All except unticked tools Feature Kit calculator keypads Basic only Scientific , Programmer All three All three Page wording (see below) Basic wording Advanced wording Everything wording Basic wording

title: What each mode changes
heading: Menu Kit
text: The Menu Kit shows only the tools the mode allows, in its tiles and in its search results. A tab with nothing to show is hidden: - Basic: the Design tab disappears. - Advanced: the Design tab appears, and the General Color Tools section of the Tools tab is hidden. - Everything: every tab and page. - Custom: every page except unticked tools. See [Find a page](../../menu-kit/docs/find-a-page.md).

title: What each mode changes
heading: Tool collections
text: Tool collection grids, such as the one at https://auricartisan.com/collections/, show only the tools the mode allows. In Everything mode they also bring back cards that were hidden, whether you hid them or the grid hid them because you had not used them. While you search a collection, every matching tool shows, whatever the mode. See [Collections](../../../library/collections/README.md).

title: What each mode changes
heading: Feature Kit calculator
text: The calculator's keypad tabs follow the mode: - Basic: only the Basic keypad. - Advanced: the Scientific and Programmer keypads; the Basic keypad is hidden. - Everything and Custom: all three. The expression bar works the same in every mode. See [Calculator](../../feature-kit/docs/calculator.md).

title: What each mode changes
heading: Page wording
text: Some pages switch between plainer and more technical wording. Page titles in the browser tab and search-engine descriptions do not change. title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
text: For problems shared by every kit, see [Troubleshooting kits](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: My mode changed by itself
text: Why: Some tools have their own mode switch that sets the same site-wide mode. Opening the URL Analyzer sets the site to Basic or Advanced to match the Analyzer's Simple or Advanced mode. The Vision Simulation lab and the Colour Science Lab can also change it, and resetting the Vision Simulation filters sets Everything . What to do: Open the Advanced Kit and choose your mode again. If you were in Custom mode, your ticks are still there; select Custom to use them again.

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: A tool I unticked still appears
text: Why: Your ticks only apply while the current mode is Custom . Another mode may be active, or a tool may have changed the mode (see above). What to do: Check Current mode in the Advanced Kit and select Custom .

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: A tool I want is missing from the menu
text: Why: The current mode hides it, or you unticked it in Custom mode. What to do: Select Everything , or tick the tool in Custom mode. Every tool also opens from its own address.

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Custom checklist says "No tools found."
text: Why: The tool list could not be downloaded. What to do: Check your connection, reload the page, and open the Advanced Kit again.

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: The checklist names do not match the Menu Kit
text: Why: The checklist uses the names from the tool collections where it can, such as Analyze URLs for the URL Analyzer and Basic Tools for Basic Color Tools. What to do: Search for a word in the tool's name, such as analy or basic .

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + Shift + A does nothing
text: Why: Some browsers use this key combination for their own features and act on it first. What to do: Open the kit from Page utilities Advanced .

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: The mode is different on my other computer
text: Why: The mode is stored in each browser, not in your account. What to do: Choose the mode once in each browser you use.

title: Advanced Kit troubleshooting
heading: Page wording did not change
text: Why: Only some pages have mode-dependent wording, and the browser tab title and search-engine description never change. See [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md). What to do: Nothing is wrong. Tool lists, the Menu Kit and the calculator keypads still follow the mode.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Does Basic mode lock the advanced tools?
text: No. It only hides them from the menus and collections. Every tool page opens from its address in every mode.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Is the Advanced Kit a paid feature?
text: No. All modes are available to everyone, signed in or not.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Which mode do new visitors get?
text: Basic , which the kit marks as Recommended .

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Is my mode saved to my account?
text: No. It is stored in your browser. Each browser and device keeps its own mode.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Do my Custom ticks survive if I switch to another mode?
text: Yes. They apply again whenever you select Custom . Reset is the only thing that clears them.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: What does Everything bring back that Basic and Advanced do not?
text: Every tool, plus collection cards that were hidden earlier, whether you hid them or the collection hid them because you had not used them yet.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Why does the calculator lose its Scientific keypad in Basic mode?
text: The Feature Kit calculator follows the mode: Basic shows only the Basic keypad. Choose Everything to see all three. The expression bar still accepts every function in any mode.

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: What is the "UX Kit"?
text: The name the changelog uses for the part of the site that changes page wording when you switch mode. It has no panel; you control it from the Advanced Kit. See [What each mode changes](what-each-mode-changes.md).

title: Advanced Kit FAQ
heading: Does the mode affect the site-wide search?
text: No. The site-wide search shows results for every tool whatever the mode.

title: Advanced Kit glossary
text: Tool visibility mode — The site-wide setting that decides which tools are listed: Basic, Advanced, Everything or Custom. Sometimes called complexity mode. Basic mode — Shows everyday, beginner-friendly tools and hides the scientific ones. The default. Advanced mode — Shows scientific, diagnostic and power-user tools and hides the simplest ones. Everything mode — Shows every tool, including collection cards that were hidden earlier. Custom mode — Shows every tool except the ones you untick in the checklist. Basic, advanced and both tools — The level each tool is given. Both tools show in every mode. Custom checklist — The Choose your tools list of tick boxes shown in Custom mode. Quick cards — The three example tool links at the bottom of the kit. Mode summary — The illustrated panel under Current mode that describes the active mode and offers switch buttons. UX Kit — The changelog's name for the part of the site that changes page wording when the mode changes. It has no panel of its own. Colorimetry — The measurement of colour as numbers, such as chromaticity and colour spaces. Gamut — The range of colours a device or colour space can show. Spectral — To do with light broken into its wavelengths. Psychophysics — The study of how physical stimuli, such as light, relate to what people perceive.

title: Feature Kit
text: The Feature Kit is a floating toolbox that opens on any page of auricartisan.com. It holds six tools behind one menu: a Scientific Calculator with graphing and history, a Unit Converter with 1,344 units in 70 categories, a Feedback form, a Markdown Notes scratchpad, a Date & Time workbench and a set of Developer Tools . The calculator is more than a keypad. Its expression bar understands variables, functions you define yourself (such as f(x) = x^2 + 1 ), statistics, number theory, physical constants and numerical calculus: derivatives, integrals, equation solving, sums and products. Results show as exact fractions when a tidy one exists, and any function can be plotted on a graph you can pan and zoom. Everything except sending feedback and loading the unit list runs in your browser. Calculator history and notes are kept in your browser between visits.

title: Feature Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers and developers who need a quick calculation, conversion, timestamp or hash while working in a tool. - Students checking maths, including derivatives, integrals and statistics. - Anyone who wants a scratchpad or a date calculator that stays one click away on every page. - Visitors who want to tell the Auric Artisan team what works and what does not.

title: Feature Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: - On any page of https://auricartisan.com, select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner, then Feature . - Or press Ctrl + Shift + K ( Cmd + Shift + K on a Mac).

title: Feature Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + Shift + K . The Feature Kit opens on its menu with six cards. 2. Press 1 to open Scientific Calculator . 3. Select the expression bar (the long box with the calculator icon) and type integral(sin(x), 0, pi) . 4. Press Enter . The display shows 2 . 5. Type f(x) = x^2 - 2 and press Enter . The display confirms ƒ f(x) defined . 6. Type solve(f(x), 1) and press Enter . The display shows 1.41421356237 , the square root of 2. 7. Select the Graph button in the title bar and type f(x) in the y = box to see the curve. 8. Press Esc to go back to the menu, and Esc again to close the kit.

title: Feature Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - Calculate with a Basic, Scientific or Programmer keypad, or type full expressions. - Use variables, ans , your own functions, constants such as pi , c and NA , and memory keys. - Differentiate, integrate, solve equations, and add or multiply series numerically. - Work out mean, median, standard deviation, greatest common divisor, primes and more. - Plot a function, pan and zoom the graph. - Reuse or delete past calculations from the history. - Convert between 1,344 units in 70 categories, from length and temperature to radiation dose and typography. - Keep several Markdown notes that save as you type, preview them, copy them or export them as .md files. - Pick dates on a calendar, count days and business days between dates, add or subtract days, weeks, months or years, and watch clocks in eight time zones. - Format and inspect JSON, encode Base64 and URLs, hash text, generate UUIDs, decode JWTs, convert timestamps, test regular expressions, explain cron schedules, change text case and encode HTML entities. - Send quick or detailed feedback about the site.

title: Calculator functions
text: This page lists everything you can type into the calculator's expression bar. The keypad uses the same rules; it simply types the symbols for you.

title: Calculator functions
heading: How expressions are read
text: - Spaces are ignored. 2 + 3 and 2+3 are the same. This also means sin 30 is read as the unknown name sin30 ; always use brackets: sin(30) . - Multiplication must be written. Type 2 pi , not 2pi . A missing operator gives Unexpected token after expression . - Names are case-sensitive. sin works, SIN does not; NA is Avogadro's number, na is not defined. - Brackets must balance. A missing ) gives Expected ) . From the loosest to the tightest binding: 1. bitwise OR 2. xor( ) bitwise exclusive OR, written after a value: 5 xor(3) 3. & bitwise AND 4. << and bit shifts 5. + and - (the keypad's − is the same as - ) 6. or × , / or ÷ , and % 7. A leading - or + sign 8. ^ power, which groups from the right 9. ! factorial Things that follow from this order: - -2^2 is -4 , because the power is worked out before the sign. - 2^3^2 is 2^9 , which is 512 . - 2^-1 is 0.5 . - % is the remainder , not a percentage: 10 % 3 is 1 . To take 15% of 80, type 80 15/100 . - Dividing by zero gives the error Division by zero . A remainder by zero gives NaN . You type Meaning Example result --- --- --- 42 , 3.14 , .5 Decimal numbers .5 is 0.5 2e3 , 1.5E-4 Scientific notation 2000 , 0.00015 0xFF Hexadecimal (digits 0 to 9 and A to F) 255 0b1010 Binary (digits 0 and 1) 10 Because e is also a constant, a number cannot end in a bare e : 2e gives Invalid numeric literal . Write 2 e for two times e.

title: Calculator functions
heading: Functions
text: Call a function with brackets and separate arguments with commas: atan2(1, 1) . Calling with the wrong number of arguments gives a message such as sin expects 1 argument or stdev expects at least 2 arguments . Angles follow the RAD or DEG setting on the display. Function Returns --- --- sin(a) , cos(a) , tan(a) Sine, cosine, tangent of angle a asin(v) , acos(v) , atan(v) Inverse sine, cosine, tangent, as an angle atan2(y, x) The angle of the point (x, y), as an angle sinh(v) , cosh(v) , tanh(v) Hyperbolic sine, cosine, tangent (not affected by RAD or DEG) asinh(v) , acosh(v) , atanh(v) Inverse hyperbolic functions (not affected by RAD or DEG) deg(r) Converts radians to degrees: deg(pi) is 180 rad(d) Converts degrees to radians: rad(180) is 3.14159265359 Function Returns --- --- sqrt(v) Square root. sqrt(-1) gives NaN cbrt(v) Cube root nthroot(v, n) The nth root. An odd root of a negative number is negative: nthroot(-27, 3) is -3 pow(a, b) a to the power b , the same as a^b exp(v) e to the power v ln(v) Natural logarithm log(v) Base-10 logarithm: log(1000) is 3 log2(v) Base-2 logarithm logb(v, base) Logarithm in any base: logb(8, 2) is 3 Function Returns --- --- abs(v) Absolute value round(v) Nearest whole number roundto(v, digits) Rounded to that many decimal places. Negative digits round to tens, hundreds and so on: roundto(1234.5, -2) is 1200 floor(v) , ceil(v) Round down, round up trunc(v) Drop the fractional part sign(v) -1 , 0 or 1 mod(a, b) Remainder of a divided by b , the same as a % b max(a, b, ...) , min(a, b, ...) Largest, smallest of any number of values clamp(v, low, high) v limited to the range: clamp(15, 0, 10) is 10 hypot(a, b, ...) Square root of the sum of squares: hypot(3, 4) is 5 Function Returns --- --- n! or fact(n) Factorial. Works for non-whole numbers too, through the gamma function: 0.5! is 0.886226925453 gamma(v) The gamma function: gamma(5) is 24 nPr(n, r) or npr(n, r) Permutations: ordered choices of r from n nCr(n, r) or ncr(n, r) Combinations: unordered choices of r from n Function Returns --- --- gcd(a, b, ...) Greatest common divisor of any number of values (rounded to whole numbers first) lcm(a, b, ...) Least common multiple of any number of values isprime(n) 1 if n is prime, otherwise 0 nextprime(n) The first prime greater than n fib(n) The nth Fibonacci number: fib(10) is 55 Each takes any number of values: mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) . Function Returns --- --- mean(...) or avg(...) Arithmetic mean median(...) Middle value (mean of the two middle values for an even count) stdev(...) Sample standard deviation. Needs at least 2 values stdevp(...) Population standard deviation variance(...) Sample variance. Needs at least 2 values varp(...) Population variance geomean(...) Geometric mean rms(...) Root mean square total(...) Sum of the values Function Returns --- --- rand() A random number from 0 up to, but not including, 1 randint(a, b) A random whole number from a to b , both included These work on whole numbers as 32-bit values. Results show in decimal. - a & b — bits set in both. - a b — bits set in either. - xor(a, b) , or a xor(b) — bits set in one but not both: xor(5, 3) is 6 . - not(a) — every bit flipped: not(0) is 4294967295 . - a << n and a n — shift left or right by n bits: 1 << 4 is 16 .

title: Calculator functions
heading: Constants
text: Name Value Meaning --- --- --- pi or π 3.14159… Pi e 2.71828… Euler's number phi or φ 1.61803… The golden ratio tau 6.28318… Two pi inf ∞ Infinity c 299792458 Speed of light, m/s G 6.6743e-11 Gravitational constant, SI units g0 9.80665 Standard gravity, m/s² NA 6.02214076e23 Avogadro constant, per mole kB 1.380649e-23 Boltzmann constant, J/K qe 1.602176634e-19 Elementary charge, C me 9.1093837015e-31 Electron mass, kg mp 1.67262192369e-27 Proton mass, kg eps0 8.8541878128e-12 Vacuum permittivity, F/m mu0 1.25663706212e-6 Vacuum permeability, N/A² ans Your last result Updated after each calculation You cannot assign a new value to a constant's name: pi = 3 gives an error.

title: Calculator functions
heading: Variables
text: Store a value with name = expression : 1. Type r = 4 and press Enter . The display shows 4 , and a chip r = 4 appears under the expression bar. 2. Type pi r^2 and press Enter . The display shows 50.2654824574 . - A name starts with a letter or an underscore and can continue with letters, digits and underscores. - Assigning to an existing name replaces its value. - Using a name that has no value gives Unknown variable: name . - Variables last until you leave or reload the page, or until you select Clear in the variables strip.

title: Calculator functions
heading: Your own functions
text: Define a function with name(parameters) = expression : 1. Type f(x) = x^2 + 1 and press Enter . The display shows ƒ f(x) defined , and a chip ƒ f(x) appears. 2. Type f(3) and press Enter . The display shows 10 . - Functions can take several parameters: area(w, h) = w h , then area(3, 4) . - The body can use constants, built-in functions, variables and your other functions. - Variables in the body are read when you call the function. With h(x) = a x , changing a changes what h(5) returns. - Calling with the wrong number of values gives a message such as f expects 1 argument . - You cannot reuse the name of a built-in function or constant: sin(x) = 2 gives Cannot redefine sin . Defining a function you already made replaces it. - A function that calls itself stops with Recursion too deep after 128 levels. - Your functions also work in the graph and inside calculus functions. - Functions last until you leave or reload the page, or until you select Clear .

title: Calculator functions
heading: Calculus and series
text: These functions take an expression as their first argument and work it out many times with a changing variable. By default the variable is x . You can name a different variable as an extra argument. You type Returns --- --- diff(expr, at) The slope (first derivative) of expr with respect to x , at x = at diff(expr, var, at) The same, with respect to the variable var derivative(...) Another name for diff diff2(expr, at) or diff2(expr, var, at) The second derivative Examples: diff(x^3, 2) shows 12.0000000001 (exactly 12 in theory); diff(sin(x), 0) shows 1 . Derivatives are estimated numerically, so the last digits can show tiny rounding noise, more so for diff2 . You type Returns --- --- integral(expr, a, b) The area under expr from x = a to x = b integral(expr, var, a, b) The same, integrating over var integrate(...) Another name for integral Examples: integral(sin(x), 0, pi) is 2 ; integral(t^2, t, 0, 3) is 9 ; integral(1/x, 1, e) is 1 . When a equals b the result is 0 ; when a is greater than b the result changes sign. solve finds a value of the variable that makes the expression equal to zero. You type How it searches --- --- solve(expr, guess) Starts at guess and homes in on a nearby root solve(expr, low, high) Searches between low and high . Best when the expression changes sign in that range solve(expr, var, guess) or solve(expr, var, low, high) The same, for a variable other than x root(...) Another name for solve Examples: solve(x^2 - 9, 1) is 3 ; solve(cos(x) - x, 0, 1) is 0.739085133215 . - To solve f(x) = 5 , move everything to one side: solve(f(x) - 5, 1) . - If there is no nearby root, you see solve: no convergence (try lo, hi bounds) . Try a different guess, or give a range that brackets the root. Some expressions, such as x^2 + 1 , have no real root at all. - If the range you give does not change sign, solve starts from its middle and searches as if you had given a guess. - A result within a hair of a whole number is shown as that whole number. You type Returns --- --- sum(expr, var, from, to) expr added up for var = from , from + 1 , and so on to to product(expr, var, from, to) expr multiplied together over the same range Examples: sum(k^2, k, 1, 10) is 385 ; product(k, k, 1, 5) is 120 ; sum(1/2^n, n, 0, 50) is 2 . - from and to are rounded to whole numbers, and swapped if from is larger. - A range of more than 1,000,000 steps gives sum: too many terms (or product: too many terms ). - The variable you name can reuse a constant's name inside the function: sum(e, e, 1, 3) is 6 . - They can be nested: integral(diff(x^2, x), 0, 1) is 1 . - Very heavy expressions stop with Expression too complex instead of freezing the page.

title: Calculator functions
heading: How results are shown
text: - Whole numbers under 10^15 show in full. - Other results show up to 12 significant digits, with trailing zeros removed. - Very small (under 10^-10) or very large (over 10^15) results show in scientific notation, for example 1.2345678901e+17 . - Results are rounded to 14 significant digits internally, so 0.1+0.2 shows 0.3 . - Infinite results show as ∞ or -∞ ; undefined results show as NaN . - In the expression bar, a result with a small exact fraction also shows the fraction, such as 0.875 = 7/8 . See [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md) for the ranges each function can handle.

title: Use the calculator
text: The Scientific Calculator gives you two ways to calculate: a keypad (which you can also drive from your keyboard) and an expression bar for full expressions with variables, your own functions and calculus. Both share one result display, one ans value and one history. Open it from the Feature Kit menu with the Scientific Calculator card or the 1 key.

title: Use the calculator
heading: The screen, top to bottom
text: 1. Display. A small expression line, a large result line, and the angle buttons RAD and DEG . 2. Expression bar. A long text box with a calculator icon and an ƒx button at its right end. Its placeholder reads f(x) = x^2 · integral(sin(x), 0, pi) · solve(x^2−2, 1) . 3. Function reference. Hidden until you select ƒx . 4. Variables strip. Appears once you have defined a variable or a function. 5. Graph and History areas. Hidden until you select Graph or History in the title bar. 6. Keypad tabs: Basic , Scientific , Programmer . 7. Memory row: MC , MR , M+ , M− . 8. Keypad for the selected tab.

title: Use the calculator
heading: Calculate with the keypad
text: 1. Select keys, or type on your keyboard while the cursor is not in a text box. 2. Watch the result line: it previews the answer as you type. 3. Select = or press Enter to finish. The result becomes ans , and the calculation goes into the history. After a result, typing a digit starts a new calculation. Typing an operator adds it to the end of the expression you just worked out, not to the result, so 2+3 followed by ×2 becomes 2+3×2 . To build on a result, start with Ans instead: Ans×2 . Keyboard keys the keypad understands: Key Enters --- --- 0 to 9 The digit + - / Add, subtract, multiply (shown as ×), divide (shown as ÷) . Decimal point ( ) Brackets ^ Power % Remainder (modulo) ! Factorial Enter or = Work out the expression Backspace Delete the last character Delete Clear everything If an expression cannot be worked out, the result line shows the reason, such as Division by zero , and flashes red.

title: Use the calculator
heading: The three keypads
text: Select a tab to switch keypad. Which tabs you see depends on the site's tool visibility mode, set in the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md): Mode Tabs shown --- --- Basic Basic only Advanced Scientific and Programmer Everything or Custom All three text C ( ) ÷ 7 8 9 × 4 5 6 − 1 2 3 + 0 . = C clears the expression. The Basic keypad has no backspace key; use Backspace on your keyboard. text d/dx ∫ solve Σ Π nCr gcd lcm x̄ σ sin cos tan π e sin⁻¹ cos⁻¹ tan⁻¹ φ ^ ln log log₂ √ ∛ exp x n! % ⌫ C ( ) ÷ × 7 8 9 − + 4 5 6 . Ans 1 2 3 0 = Function keys insert the function name and an opening bracket, for example sin inserts sin( and d/dx inserts diff( . Close the bracket yourself. x̄ inserts mean( , σ inserts stdev( , x inserts abs( , √ inserts sqrt( , ∛ inserts cbrt( , log₂ inserts log2( , Σ inserts sum( and Π inserts product( . π , e and φ insert the constants. n! adds the factorial sign. Ans inserts the previous result. ⌫ deletes one character. What each function does is listed in [Calculator functions](calculator-functions.md). text AND OR XOR NOT << 0x 0b A B C D E F ⌫ AC 7 8 9 + 4 5 6 − 1 2 3 × 0 . = - 0x starts a hexadecimal number and 0b a binary one, for example 0xFF or 0b1010 . A to F enter hexadecimal digits. - AND and OR combine numbers bit by bit. << and shift bits left and right. - XOR inserts xor( and NOT inserts not( . The Programmer keypad has no bracket keys, so type the closing ) on your keyboard. For example 5 xor(3) gives 6 . - AC clears the expression. - Results always show in decimal: 0xFF shows 255 .

title: Use the calculator
heading: Calculate with the expression bar
text: The expression bar takes a whole expression as text, including things the keypad cannot enter. 1. Select the expression bar. 2. Type an expression, for example mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) . 3. Press Enter . The expression appears on the display's top line and the result on the large line. The result becomes ans and goes into the history. When a result has a tidy exact fraction, the display shows it too: 0.875 shows as 0.875 = 7/8 . Fractions are found for denominators up to 10,000. While the cursor is in the expression bar, keys go to the bar, not to the keypad. Use the bar for: - variables: r = 4 , then pi r^2 ; - your own functions: f(x) = x^2 + 1 , then f(3) ; - calculus and series: diff(x^3, 2) , integral(sin(x), 0, pi) , solve(x^2-2, 1) , sum(k^2, k, 1, 10) ; - statistics and number theory: stdev(2, 4, 4, 5) , gcd(12, 18) , isprime(97) . The full language is in [Calculator functions](calculator-functions.md).

title: Use the calculator
heading: The function reference (ƒx)
text: Select ƒx at the end of the expression bar to show a panel of insertable chips, grouped by topic. Selecting a chip adds its text to the end of the expression bar. Group Chips --- --- Calculus diff(x², at) , diff2 , ∫ integral(f, a, b) , solve(f, guess) , Σ sum(f, n, 1, 99) , Π product Statistics mean , median , stdev , variance , geomean , rms Numbers gcd , lcm , isprime , nextprime , fib , nCr , nPr , roundto(x, digits) , nthroot(x, n) , logb(x, base) Define x = 5 , f(x) = x^2 , ans Constants π , e , φ , τ , c (light) , G , g₀ , Nᴀ , kʙ Select ƒx again to hide the panel.

title: Use the calculator
heading: The variables strip
text: After you define a variable or a function, a strip of chips appears under the expression bar: - A variable chip shows its value, for example r = 4 . Selecting it inserts r into the expression bar. - A function chip shows ƒ and its name, for example ƒ f(x) . Hovering shows its definition. Selecting it inserts f( . - Clear removes every variable and function you have defined. Variables and functions last until you leave or reload the page. They are not saved.

title: Use the calculator
heading: Angle mode: RAD and DEG
text: RAD (the default) treats angles in radians; DEG treats them in degrees. The setting affects sin , cos and tan (their input) and asin , acos , atan and atan2 (their output). It also applies to the graph. It resets to RAD each time the page loads.

title: Use the calculator
heading: Memory keys
text: Key What it does --- --- MC Clears the memory to 0 MR Adds the memory value to the end of the current expression M+ Adds the number on the result line to the memory M− Subtracts the number on the result line from the memory Memory lasts until you leave or reload the page.

title: Use the calculator
heading: Copy a result
text: Select the large result line. A Copied! message confirms that the result is on your clipboard. Only the decimal result is copied, not the fraction.

title: Use the calculator
heading: Use the history
text: 1. Select History (the clock icon) in the title bar. The history area opens under the graph area, newest calculation first. 2. Each entry shows the expression and = result . 3. Select an entry, or focus it and press Enter , to load it back into the keypad display. Press Enter (with the cursor outside text boxes) or = to work it out again. 4. Select the bin icon on an entry to delete that calculation. 5. Select the bin icon in the History heading to delete every calculation. There is no confirmation. The history keeps your last 100 calculations in your browser, including calculations from the keypad and the expression bar. When it is empty it reads No calculations yet . Select History again to hide it.
