text: - [Calculator functions](calculator-functions.md) — the full list of what you can type - [Graphing](graphing.md) — plot a function - [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md) — precision and numeric limits - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) — what each error message means

title: Work with dates and times
text: Date & Time is a small date workbench with four tabs: Calendar , Difference , Add / Subtract and Timezones . Dates are written in the format of the site's language, or of your browser if the site has no preference. Open it with the Date & Time card on the Feature Kit menu, or press 5 on the menu.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: The calendar picker
text: All four tabs use the same calendar: - The month and year sit at the top, with ‹ (previous month) on the left and « (previous year), » (next year) and › (next month) on the right. - The week starts on Sunday: Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa . - Today is marked. The selected day is highlighted. Weekends and days from the neighbouring months look different. - Clear removes the selection. Today selects today and jumps to its month.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: Calendar tab: read a date in every format
text: 1. Select the Calendar tab (it opens first). 2. Pick a day. Today is selected when you arrive. 3. Set the time of day in the Time box if it matters. Under the calendar you see the date in ISO form with a relative description ( Today , Tomorrow , Yesterday , in 12 days , 3 days ago ), then one row per format, each with a Copy button: Row Example --- --- Full (culture) The full date and short time in your locale, for example Thursday 24 September 2026 at 14:05 Long date 24 September 2026 ISO 8601 2026-09-24T14:05 Unix (s) Seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, for your local date and time Day of year 267 ISO week W39 · 2026 Weekday Thursday Selecting Copy copies that row's value; the button briefly shows a tick. If copying is blocked it shows Failed . Every day you pick is added to a Recent row of chips, newest first, up to 8. Each chip shows the month and day. Select a chip to jump back to that date. The list is kept in your browser. If you select Clear , the details read No date selected. Pick a day above.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: Difference tab: count the time between two dates
text: 1. Select Difference . 2. Select the From field and pick a date. It starts on today. 3. Select the To field and pick a date. It starts 30 days from today. The result shows six figures: Figure How it is worked out --- --- Days Calendar days from From to To . Negative if To is earlier Weeks Days divided by 7, to 2 decimal places Months (≈) Days divided by 30.437, to 2 decimal places Years (≈) Days divided by 365.25, to 3 decimal places Business days Days that are Monday to Friday, counting the To date but not the From date. Public holidays are not taken into account Hours Days multiplied by 24 If either field is empty, you see Pick two dates. Each date field shows the chosen date written out in full. Select it to open its calendar; picking a day closes the calendar again.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: Add / Subtract tab: shift a date
text: 1. Select Add / Subtract . 2. Pick the Start date . It starts on the date selected in the Calendar tab, or today. 3. Type a whole number in Amount (it starts at 30). 4. Choose a Unit : days , weeks , months or years . 5. Choose a Direction : after (+) or before (−) . The result shows the new date in ISO form and written out in full, and updates as you change any field. When you add months or years and the day does not exist in the target month, the date moves to that month's last day. For example, 31 January plus 1 month gives 28 or 29 February. If the start date is empty, you see Pick a date.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: Timezones tab: world clocks
text: Select Timezones to see live clocks, updating every second, in 24-hour time with seconds and the local date for each place: - UTC - New York - Los Angeles - London - Berlin - Kolkata - Tokyo - Sydney Daylight saving time is applied automatically for each place. The list of places is fixed. The clocks stop updating while you are in another Feature Kit tool and restart when you come back.

title: Work with dates and times
heading: Related
text: - [Developer Tools](developer-tools.md) — the Epoch tool converts Unix timestamps in both directions - [Reference](reference.md)

title: Use the developer tools
text: Developer Tools gathers eleven small utilities behind one row of tabs. Everything runs in your browser: nothing you paste is sent anywhere or kept after you leave the page. Open it with the Developer Tools card on the Feature Kit menu, or press 6 on the menu. It opens on JSON . Select a tab to switch tool. Most tools share one layout: an input box, a row of buttons, and an output box. Copy copies the output box. It briefly reads Copied , or Copy failed if your browser blocked the clipboard. Errors show in the output box in a warning colour.

title: Use the developer tools
heading: JSON
text: Paste JSON into the box (the placeholder shows { "hello": "world", "n": 1 } ), then choose: Button Output --- --- Format The JSON indented with two spaces Minify The JSON on one line with no spaces Sort keys Indented, with every object's keys sorted alphabetically, at every depth → TypeScript A TypeScript interface Root (or type Root for arrays and plain values) describing the data Stats Size in bytes, number of keys, objects, arrays, and the deepest nesting level Escape Your input as a quoted JSON string, ready to embed Copy Copies the output If the input is not valid JSON, the output reads Invalid JSON: with the browser's message and, where the browser gives a position, the line and column: → line 3, column 7 . An empty box is treated as null .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Base64
text: Button Output --- --- Encode Standard Base64 of the text (UTF-8, so accented letters and symbols work) URL-safe Base64 with - and instead of + and / , and no = padding Decode The text inside a Base64 string. Accepts standard and URL-safe forms, with or without padding → Hex Each UTF-8 byte of the text in hexadecimal, and the byte count Copy Copies the output A string that cannot be decoded shows Not valid Base64 .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: URL
text: Paste a URL or text (placeholder https://example.com/path?q=a b&x=1 top ). Button Output --- --- Parse The protocol, host, port ( (default) if none), path and hash, then each query parameter as name = value . A URL without a scheme is treated as https:// Encode The text percent-encoded for use inside a URL Decode Percent-encoding turned back into text; + is read as a space Copy Copies the output Errors: Enter a URL. , Could not parse URL , Malformed URI sequence .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Hash
text: Type or paste the text to hash. The second box, HMAC key , is only used by the HMAC button. Button Output --- --- Hash all SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 of the text in hexadecimal, plus CRC32 HMAC-SHA256 The HMAC-SHA256 signature of the text with your key, in hexadecimal Copy Copies the output Without a key, HMAC-SHA256 says Enter an HMAC key first. Hashes are computed on the text's UTF-8 bytes by your browser's built-in cryptography. SHA-1 and CRC32 are shown for checking against older systems; do not use them for security.

title: Use the developer tools
heading: UUID
text: A UUID is a 128-bit identifier written as 36 characters in five groups separated by hyphens. The tool shows one new version 4 UUID when it opens. Button Output --- --- v4 One random UUID v4 ×10 Ten random UUIDs, one per line v7 One time-ordered UUID (version 7), which starts with the current time so values sort by creation v7 ×10 Ten version 7 UUIDs NIL The all-zero UUID Copy Copies the output To inspect a UUID, paste it into Paste a UUID to inspect… . The output shows its version and variant (RFC 4122, Microsoft or NCS), and for version 7 the timestamp it carries, with how long ago that was. Anything that is not a UUID shows Not a valid UUID .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: JWT
text: A JWT (JSON Web Token) is a signed token in three dot-separated parts. Paste one into the box. It decodes as you paste, or select Decode . The output shows: - HEADER — the decoded header JSON; - PAYLOAD — the decoded payload JSON; - TIMES — the exp (expires), iat (issued at) and nbf (not before) claims, if present, as dates with how far away they are; - Signature — its length, marked "not verified — decoding only". Important: The tool does not check the signature. A token that decodes is not proven genuine. Pasting a live token into any web page is a risk; this tool keeps it in your browser, but clear the box when you are done. Errors: Not a JWT (need header.payload.signature) , Could not decode JWT segments .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Epoch
text: Converts between Unix timestamps and dates. It shows the current time when it opens. 1. Type a value in Unix seconds/millis or ISO date… . 2. Press Enter or select Convert . How the value is read: - 1 to 10 digits: Unix seconds. - Exactly 13 digits: Unix milliseconds. - Anything else: a date your browser can read, such as 2026-09-24T09:30:00Z . The output lists Unix (s) , Unix (ms) , ISO , UTC , Local , Relative and Day (weekday and day of the year, DOY). Now shows the current time. Convert with an empty box also shows the current time. A value that cannot be read shows Could not parse date/timestamp .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Regex
text: Tests a JavaScript regular expression against sample text, live. 1. Type the pattern between the two slashes. 2. Type flags in the small box after the second slash (it starts with g ). Common flags: g all matches, i ignore case, m multi-line, s dot matches new lines, u Unicode, y sticky. 3. Type or paste the text to search in Test string… . 4. Optionally type a replacement in Replacement (optional — $1, $<name )… . As you type: - the highlight box shows the test text with each match marked (an empty match shows as ∅ ); - the output box shows the number of matches, then each one with its position ( 1 @4: text ), its numbered groups and its named groups; - with a replacement, the output ends with REPLACED and the text after replacement. Test re-runs it and Copy copies the output. The list shows the first 200 matches. An invalid pattern shows Invalid regex: and the browser's reason. Without a pattern the output reads Enter a pattern. ; with no matches it reads No matches.

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Cron
text: Explains a standard five-field cron schedule and lists its next five run times in your local time. 1. Type an expression: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. The box starts with /15 9-17 MON-FRI . 2. Press Enter or select Explain . The output starts with a plain-language summary, such as "Runs every 15 minutes during hour 9-17, on MON-FRI", then Next runs (local time): with five dates and how far away each is. Preset buttons fill in and explain common schedules. Each button is labelled with its expression: Button Schedule --- --- 0 At the start of every hour /5 Every five minutes 0 9 MON-FRI 09:00 on weekdays 0 0 1 Midnight on the 1st of each month What the fields accept: - , single values, ranges ( 9-17 ), lists ( 1,15 ) and steps ( /15 , 10-50/10 ). - Month names JAN to DEC and day names SUN to SAT . Day of week 7 also means Sunday. - When both day of month and day of week are restricted, a day matching either one runs, as in standard cron. - Times that do not exist because of a daylight-saving change are skipped. Errors: Expected 5 fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week , Bad field , Out of range . The Cron tool has no Copy button.

title: Use the developer tools
heading: Text
text: Type or paste text. A line under the box counts characters, words, lines and bytes as you type. Buttons put the transformed text in the output box: Button Result for "hello big world" --- --- camelCase helloBigWorld PascalCase HelloBigWorld snake case hello big world kebab-case hello-big-world slug hello-big-world (lower case, accents removed, anything else becomes hyphens) Title Case Hello Big World UPPER HELLO BIG WORLD lower hello big world reverse dlrow gib olleh sort lines Lines sorted alphabetically dedupe lines Repeated lines removed, first copy kept trim lines Spaces removed from the start and end of every line Copy Copies the output The case buttons also split words at capital letters, underscores, hyphens, dots and slashes, so myVariable name becomes my variable name with snake case .

title: Use the developer tools
heading: HTML
text: Button Output --- --- Encode & , < , , " and ' replaced with HTML entities Decode Entities turned back into characters. Real tags in the input are dropped Strip tags Only the text, with tags removed and runs of blank lines reduced Copy Copies the output The placeholder shows an example: <a href="/" Fish & Chips</a . Decoding and stripping read the input as HTML without running any scripts in it.

text: - [Date & Time](date-and-time.md) for calendar-based date work - [Reference](reference.md) - [Privacy](../others/privacy.md)

title: Send feedback
text: The Feedback tool in the Feature Kit lets you tell the Auric Artisan team how the site is working for you. A quick rating takes one click; a detailed form takes about a minute. Both are optional.

title: Send feedback
heading: Open the feedback form
text: Select the Feedback card on the Feature Kit menu, or press 3 on the menu. You may also see a small prompt inside the Feature Kit that reads Feedback when you're ready with the line "The full form lives in Feature Kit and stays out of the way." Select Open form to go to the form, or Later to dismiss it. The prompt hides by itself after 10 seconds.

title: Send feedback
heading: Send quick feedback
text: 1. Read the question at the top. It depends on what you did last in the kit, for example How's your experience so far? , How was the calculator? or How was the unit converter? 2. Choose one of five faces: Terrible , Bad , Okay , Good or Amazing . 3. A comment box appears: Tell us more (optional)... . Type a comment if you like. 4. Select Submit . It reads Sending... while it sends. A thank-you message appears, matched to your rating: Thank you! , We hear you. or Thanks for sharing! . Select Done , or wait 5 seconds, to return to the Feature Kit menu. Submit stays disabled until you choose a face.

title: Send feedback
heading: Send detailed feedback
text: 1. On the quick feedback screen, optionally choose a face, then select Give Detailed Feedback . 2. Answer each question. A progress bar and a counter such as 2/8 show where you are. 3. Use Next → to continue, Skip to leave a question unanswered, or ← Back to return to the previous question. 4. On the last question, the forward button reads Submit with a tick. Select it to send. The questions, in order: Question How you answer --- --- How easy was it to find what you needed? A scale of 1 to 5, from Very hard to Very easy How would you rate the speed & performance? A scale of 1 to 5, from Very slow to Lightning How do you feel about the design? Five faces: Love it , Nice , Okay , Meh , Needs work Follow-up questions Depend on your quick rating (see below) What features would you like to see? Pick any of: Dark/Light themes , More tools , Keyboard shortcuts , Mobile improvements , Accessibility , Import/Export , Other Would you recommend this to a colleague? A scale of 0 to 10, from Not likely to Very likely Anything else you'd like to share? Free text Follow-up questions: - After a 4 or 5 rating: "What do you like most?" (free text) and "Would you share this with others?" ( Definitely! , Maybe , Probably not ). - After a 1 or 2 rating, or no rating: "What frustrated you the most?", "What did you expect to happen?" (both free text) and "What should we fix first?" ( Bugs , Performance , Design , Features , Usability ). - After a 3 rating: "What one thing would make this better?" (free text).

title: Send feedback
heading: Not now
text: Select Not now on the quick feedback screen to leave without sending. The kit returns to its menu and the prompts give you more room before they appear again.

title: Send feedback
heading: If sending fails
text: If your feedback cannot be sent, you see Could not send yet with one of these messages: Message What it means --- --- Your feedback is saved on this device. Check your connection and try again. You are offline or the server did not answer. The feedback is kept and will be sent later The server could not accept this feedback. You can try again or return to the menu. The server refused this submission Your feedback could not be sent or saved on this device. Keep this page open and try again. Your browser would not store it, for example in a private window Your feedback is saved, but the current account could not be confirmed yet. Check your connection and try again. You were signed in, and your sign-in could not be checked This feedback belongs to a different signed-in account. Return to that account before retrying. You switched accounts after writing it Select Try again (or Check account ) to retry, or Done to return to the menu. Feedback saved on your device is retried automatically, including when your connection comes back.

title: Send feedback
heading: When the kit asks for feedback
text: The kit asks quietly and rarely: - only while the Feature Kit is open on its menu, never while you are in a tool; - after you have used the calculator or the converter a few times, or after about 15 minutes; - no more than twice in one visit, and no more than once an hour; - less often if you have dismissed several prompts. If a prompt comes due while the kit is closed, it waits and appears the next time you open the menu.

title: Send feedback
heading: What is sent
text: See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md). In short: your rating, comment and answers, the page you were on, and which tool you used last. If you are signed in, the feedback is linked to your account. For feedback outside the Feature Kit, see [Site features](../../../site-features/README.md).

title: Plot a function
text: The calculator can draw the graph of any expression in x . The graph redraws as you type, uses the same functions and constants as the calculator, and can use the variables and functions you have defined.

title: Plot a function
heading: Show the graph
text: 1. Open Scientific Calculator in the Feature Kit. 2. Select Graph (the wave icon) in the title bar. The button turns gold and a graph area opens under the expression bar. 3. The y = box already holds sin(x) , and its curve is drawn. The graph shows a grid with numbered axes, the curve in gold, and a label in its top-left corner such as y = sin(x) .

title: Plot a function
heading: Plot your own expression
text: 1. Select the y = box. 2. Replace the text with your expression, for example x^3 - 3 x . 3. The graph redraws as you type. Rules: - Use x as the variable. Inside the graph, x always means the horizontal position, even if you have a variable called x . - Write every multiplication: 3 x , not 3x . - You can use your own functions and variables: after f(x) = x^2 - 2 in the expression bar, type f(x) in the y = box. - Trigonometric functions follow the RAD or DEG setting. - Where the expression is undefined or infinite (for example 1/x at x = 0 , or sqrt(x) for negative x ), the curve simply has a gap. Very steep jumps, such as those of tan(x) , are drawn as separate pieces rather than joined by a vertical line. - If the expression has a mistake, nothing is drawn. Fix it and the curve appears. The graph shows one expression at a time.

title: Plot a function
heading: Move around the graph
text: Action How --- --- Pan Drag on the graph with a mouse, pen or one finger Zoom in or out Scroll with a mouse wheel or trackpad over the graph Zoom with touch Pinch with two fingers Zoom in one step Select the magnifier with a plus sign in the graph's corner Zoom out one step Select the magnifier with a minus sign Reset Select the circular-arrow button to return to the starting view The starting view is centred on the origin at 50 pixels per unit. Zooming stops at 5 pixels per unit at the widest and 5,000 pixels per unit at the closest. The grid spacing adjusts as you zoom so labels stay readable.

title: Plot a function
heading: Make the graph bigger
text: Select Resize in the title bar. The expanded Feature Kit gives the graph more height.

title: Plot a function
heading: Hide the graph
text: Select Graph again. The graph also closes when you close the Feature Kit. Your y = expression is kept while the page stays open.

title: Keep notes
text: Notes is a scratchpad inside the Feature Kit. You can keep several notes, write them in Markdown, preview the formatting, and copy or export any note. Notes save automatically in your browser, so they are there the next time you open the kit on any page.

title: Keep notes
heading: Open Notes
text: Select the Notes card on the Feature Kit menu, or press 4 on the menu. The first time, you see one note called Scratchpad containing a short example.

title: Keep notes
heading: The screen
text: - Note tabs along the top, one per note, named after the note's first line. A + button at the end adds a note. - A toolbar with Edit and Preview on the left and Copy , Export and Delete on the right. - The editor, or the preview when Preview is selected. - A status line at the bottom: Saving… while you type, then Saved · and the time.

title: Keep notes
heading: Write a note
text: 1. Select the editor. 2. Type. The placeholder reminds you of the syntax: Title , bold , italic , code , - lists , - [ ] tasks . 3. Stop typing for a moment. The status changes from Saving… to Saved · and the time. The note's tab takes its name from the first non-empty line, without any leading , cut to 24 characters. An empty note is called Untitled .

title: Keep notes
heading: Add a note
text: Select + ( New note ). An empty note opens at the front of the tabs, in edit mode, with the cursor in the editor.

title: Keep notes
heading: Switch between notes
text: Select a note's tab.

title: Keep notes
heading: Preview the formatting
text: Select Preview to see the note formatted. Select Edit to go back to editing. The preview understands this Markdown: You type You get --- --- Heading to Heading Headings, levels 1 to 4 bold Bold text italic Italic text code Inline code A line of three backticks before and after A code block - item or item A bulleted list - [ ] task and - [x] task An open task and a done task, shown with empty and ticked boxes [label](https://example.com) A link that opens in a new tab (only links starting with http: or https: ) Anything else shows as plain paragraphs. Any HTML you type is shown as text, not run.

title: Keep notes
heading: Copy a note
text: Select Copy . The status line reads Copied (or Copy failed if your browser blocked clipboard access). The raw Markdown is copied.

title: Keep notes
heading: Export a note
text: Select Export . Your browser downloads the note as a Markdown file named after the note's title, for example Scratchpad.md . Characters that are not letters, digits, hyphens or underscores in the title become hyphens in the file name.

title: Keep notes
heading: Delete a note
text: Select Delete . The note is removed at once, without a confirmation, and the first remaining note opens. If it is your only note, Delete empties it instead and renames it Untitled . Important: Deleting cannot be undone. Export a note first if you might need it.

title: Keep notes
heading: Where notes are kept
text: Notes are saved in your browser for auricartisan.com. They are not sent anywhere and not linked to your account. They are lost if you clear the site's data in your browser, and they are not available in another browser or on another device. Export notes you want to keep.

title: Convert units
text: The Unit Converter converts a value from one unit to another within a category, such as metres to feet or Celsius to Fahrenheit. It has 70 categories and 1,344 units, including every metric prefix from yocto to yotta for the units that take them.

title: Convert units
heading: Open the converter
text: Select the Unit Converter card on the Feature Kit menu, or press 2 on the menu. The first time you open it on a page, the kit downloads the unit list. A loading message reads Loading units — Preparing the converter. It takes a moment on a slow connection.

title: Convert units
heading: Convert a value
text: 1. Select a category pill, for example Temperature . The converter starts on Length . 2. Type a number in the From box (placeholder Enter value ). 3. Choose the unit you have in the From unit list, for example celsius (°C) . 4. Choose the unit you want in the To unit list, for example fahrenheit (°F) . The result appears in the To row as you type, for example 98.6 , with a sentence under it: 37 celsius = 98.6 fahrenheit . When you pick a category, the converter preselects its first two units.

title: Convert units
heading: Swap the units
text: Select the swap button (two opposing arrows) between From and To . The two units change places and the result updates.

title: Convert units
heading: Copy the result
text: Select the result value. A Copied! message confirms it is on your clipboard.

title: Convert units
heading: Find a unit
text: 1. Type part of a unit's name or symbol in Search units... , for example psi or parsec . 2. The category pills narrow to the categories that contain a matching unit. If nothing matches, you see No matches . 3. Select a category pill to switch to it, then pick the unit from the list. The search finds categories; it does not choose the unit for you. Clear the search box to see every category again. With the cursor outside a text box, pressing / puts the cursor in the search box.

title: Convert units
heading: The categories
text: The converter's 70 categories, in the order the pills appear: Length, Area, Volume, Mass, Speed, Acceleration, Temperature, Time, Energy, Power, Pressure, Force, Frequency, Density, Fuel Economy, Electric Charge, Voltage, Electric Current, Resistance, Capacitance, Magnetic Field, Magnetic Flux, Inductance, Torque, Angular Velocity, Angular Acceleration, Momentum, Impulse, Digital Storage, Data Transfer Rate, Typography, Astronomy, Concentration, Radiation Dose, Radiation Equivalent, Radioactivity, Dynamic Viscosity, Kinematic Viscosity, Volumetric Flow Rate, Mass Flow Rate, Luminous Flux, Illuminance, Luminance, Luminous Intensity, Sound Level, Cooking Volume, Angle, Specific Heat Capacity, Thermal Conductivity, Electric Conductance, Surface Tension, Amount of Substance, Permeability, Permittivity, Electric Field, Moment of Inertia, Molar Mass, Heat Flux Density, Entropy, Energy Density, Specific Energy, Electrical Resistivity, Linear Charge Density, Number, Magnetic Field Strength, Catalytic Activity, Absorbed Dose Rate, Radiation Exposure, Wavenumber, Spectral Power. The number of units available shows at the bottom of the converter: 1344 units available . Most categories convert by a fixed factor. Three do not: - Temperature converts through kelvin and handles offsets correctly. Units: kelvin (K), celsius (°C), fahrenheit (°F), rankine (°R), delisle (°De), newton (temp) (°N), réaumur (°Ré), rømer (°Rø). - Fuel Economy handles units that run in opposite directions. Units: kilometer per liter (km/L), miles per gallon (US) (mpg), miles per gallon (UK) (mpg uk), liters per 100 km (L/100km), miles per liter (mi/L), gallons per 100 miles (gal/100mi). A value of 0 in a per-distance unit converts to ∞ . - Sound Level uses approximate relationships. Units: decibel (dB), bel (B), neper (Np), decibel (milliwatt) (dBm), decibel (watt) (dBW), sone (sone), phon (phon). See [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md).

title: Convert units
heading: How results are shown
text: - Whole-number results show with thousands separators, for example 1,000,000 . - Very small (under 10^-10) or very large (over 10^12) results show in scientific notation with 8 decimal places. - Other results show up to 12 significant digits.

title: Convert units
heading: Things to know
text: - Use a dot for decimals. The box reads a number from the start of what you type, so 1,5 is read as 1 . - Scientific notation works in the From box: 1e3 is 1,000. - Unit names appear as the converter lists them, with US spellings such as "meter" and "liter".

title: Convert units
heading: If the units do not load
text: If the unit list cannot be downloaded, you see Units could not be loaded. Check your connection, then try again. with a Try again button. Reconnect and select Try again .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
text: For problems shared by every kit, such as a missing launcher or a panel in the wrong place, see [Troubleshooting kits](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The page goes dark and I cannot click it
text: Why: With Focus mode off, the Feature Kit dims the page and keeps keyboard focus inside the kit. What to do: Click the dimmed page to close the kit, or select Focus mode in the kit's title bar to keep it open without dimming.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Feature launcher does not close the kit
text: Why: With Focus mode on, the launcher and Ctrl + Shift + K move focus into the kit instead of closing it. What to do: Select Close in the title bar, or press Esc twice (once to leave a tool, once to close).

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: Typing numbers does nothing on the calculator
text: Why: Keyboard typing reaches the keypad only while the Scientific Calculator is open and the cursor is not in a text box. If the cursor is in the expression bar, the y = box or a page field, your keys go there instead. What to do: Click an empty part of the calculator, or the display, then type. Or type into the expression bar and press Enter .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Scientific or Programmer tab is missing
text: Why: The site's tool visibility mode is Basic , which shows only the Basic keypad. In Advanced mode, the Basic keypad is hidden instead. What to do: Open the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md) and choose Everything to see all three tabs.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: My variables and functions disappeared
text: Why: Variables, your own functions and the memory value last only while the page is open. Moving to another page or reloading clears them. What to do: Keep definitions you reuse in [Notes](notes.md) and paste them into the expression bar. Calculations themselves stay in the history.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The result of 2+3×2 is 8, not 10
text: Why: After a result, typing an operator adds to the end of the previous expression rather than to the result, and multiplication comes before addition. What to do: Start the next step with Ans : Ans×2 .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: % does not give a percentage
text: Why: % is the remainder operator: 10 % 3 is 1 . What to do: Work out percentages with multiplication and division: 80 15/100 .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: A derivative shows 12.0000000001 instead of 12
text: Why: diff and diff2 estimate derivatives numerically. The last digits can carry tiny rounding noise. What to do: Round the result with roundto(diff(x^3, 2), 6) . See [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md).

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The graph is empty
text: Why: The y = expression has a mistake, uses something other than x as its variable, or is undefined across the visible range. What to do: Test the expression in the expression bar first, with a value for x , for example x = 2 then your expression. Select the graph's reset button to return to the starting view.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Unit Converter says "Units could not be loaded"
text: Why: The unit list is downloaded the first time you open the converter on a page, and the download failed. What to do: Check your connection and select Try again .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: A conversion shows a strange number
text: Why: The value box reads a number from the start of what you type. A comma is not a decimal separator, so 1,5 is read as 1 . What to do: Use a dot for decimals: 1.5 .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: I cannot find a unit in the search results
text: Why: The search narrows the category pills; it does not pick the unit. What to do: Select the category pill it shows, then choose the unit from the From or To list.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: A note disappeared
text: Why: Delete removes a note immediately, without asking. Notes are also lost if you clear the site's data in your browser, and they do not move between browsers or devices. What to do: There is no undo. Use Export regularly for notes you want to keep.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: Copy does not work
text: Why: Your browser blocked clipboard access, which can happen outside a secure connection or with strict permissions. What to do: Allow clipboard access for the site, or select the text and copy it with Ctrl + C .

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: A tool card shows "failed to load"
text: Why: Notes, Date & Time and Developer Tools download the first time you open them on a page. The download failed. What to do: Check your connection and reload the page.

title: Feature Kit troubleshooting
heading: The feedback form keeps saying "Could not send yet"
text: See the message table in [Feedback](feedback.md). Your feedback is usually saved on your device and sent automatically once the connection is back.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Does the Feature Kit work offline?
text: Mostly. Once the kit and its tools have loaded on a page, the calculator, graph, notes, date tools and developer tools work without a connection. The Unit Converter needs a connection the first time you open it on a page, to download its unit list. Feedback waits on your device until you are back online.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Is my calculator history saved?
text: Yes. Your last 100 calculations are kept in your browser and appear in History on any page. Variables, functions you define and the memory value are not saved.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Can I plot more than one function at once?
text: No. The graph shows one expression at a time. Define functions in the expression bar and switch between them in the y = box.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Does the calculator handle complex numbers?
text: No. Results are real numbers. Expressions with no real answer, such as sqrt(-1) , show NaN .

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Is % a percentage?
text: No. It is the remainder after division: 10 % 3 is 1 .

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Can I solve an equation such as x² = 5?
text: Yes. Move everything to one side and use solve : solve(x^2 - 5, 2) returns 2.2360679775 .

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Does the calculator give exact answers?
text: It gives decimal answers rounded to 14 significant digits, shown to 12. In the expression bar it also shows an exact fraction when one with a denominator up to 10,000 matches, such as 0.875 = 7/8 . Calculus results are numerical estimates. See [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md).

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Why can I not see the Scientific keypad?
text: The site is in Basic mode. Choose Everything in the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md).

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Are my notes private?
text: Notes are kept only in your browser for auricartisan.com. They are not sent anywhere and not linked to your account.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Can I move notes to another computer?
text: Export each note with Export and keep the .md files. There is no import button; paste the text into a new note on the other computer.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Is it safe to paste a token or secret into Developer Tools?
text: The Developer Tools run entirely in your browser and do not send or store what you paste. As with any web page, clear the box when you are done, and prefer test tokens over live ones.

title: Feature Kit FAQ
heading: Does the JWT tool check signatures?
text: No. It only decodes the header and payload and marks the signature "not verified — decoding only".

title: Feature Kit FAQ

title: Feature Kit glossary
text: ans — The result of your last calculation. Type ans or select Ans to reuse it. Expression — A calculation written as text, such as 2 (3+4) . Expression bar — The calculator's text box for full expressions, variables, functions and calculus. Variable — A name that holds a value, set with name = value , such as r = 4 . User-defined function — A function you create with name(x) = expression , such as f(x) = x^2 + 1 . Constant — A fixed named value, such as pi , e or the speed of light c . Radians (RAD) and degrees (DEG) — Two units for angles. A full turn is 2π radians or 360 degrees. Remainder (modulo) — What is left after whole division. 10 % 3 is 1 . Factorial — The product of all whole numbers from 1 to n, written n! . 5! is 120 . Gamma function — An extension of the factorial to non-whole numbers. gamma(n) equals (n-1)! for whole numbers. Derivative — The rate of change, or slope, of an expression at a point. diff estimates it. Second derivative — The rate of change of the slope. diff2 estimates it. Integral — The signed area under a curve between two points. integral estimates it. Root — A value where an expression equals zero. solve finds one. Numerical method — A way of computing an answer by repeated approximation rather than by exact algebra. The calculator's calculus functions use numerical methods. Sample and population standard deviation — Measures of spread. Sample ( stdev ) divides by one less than the number of values; population ( stdevp ) divides by the number of values. Geometric mean — The nth root of the product of n values. Root mean square (RMS) — The square root of the mean of the squared values. Greatest common divisor (GCD) — The largest whole number that divides all the given numbers. Least common multiple (LCM) — The smallest whole number that all the given numbers divide. Prime — A whole number above 1 divisible only by 1 and itself. Fibonacci number — A number in the sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, where each is the sum of the two before. Hexadecimal and binary — Base-16 (digits 0–9 and A–F, written with 0x ) and base-2 (digits 0 and 1, written with 0b ). Bitwise operation — An operation that works on each binary digit of a number separately, such as AND, OR, XOR and NOT. Metric prefix — A word or letter before a unit that multiplies it by a power of ten, such as kilo (k, 1,000) or micro (μ, one millionth). Markdown — A plain-text way to write formatting, such as bold or Heading . ISO 8601 — The international date format YYYY-MM-DD , with an optional time after a T . Unix timestamp (epoch) — The number of seconds, or milliseconds, since 1 January 1970 UTC. ISO week — A week number from 1 to 53, where weeks start on Monday and week 1 contains the year's first Thursday. Business day — Monday to Friday. The Feature Kit does not account for public holidays. UTC — Coordinated Universal Time, the time standard the world's time zones are defined against. JSON — A text format for structured data. Base64 — A way of writing any data using 64 safe text characters. Hash — A fixed-length fingerprint of some text. The same text always gives the same hash. HMAC — A hash that also depends on a secret key, used to check that data came from someone who knows the key. CRC32 — A short checksum for spotting accidental changes. Not for security. UUID — A 128-bit identifier. Version 4 is random; version 7 starts with a timestamp so values sort by creation time. JWT (JSON Web Token) — A signed token in three parts: header, payload and signature. Regular expression (regex) — A pattern that describes text to find. Cron expression — Five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) that describe a repeating schedule. Slug — A lower-case, hyphen-separated version of text suitable for a web address. HTML entity — A code such as & that stands for a character with special meaning in HTML. Focus mode — The Feature Kit setting that keeps the kit open across pages and stops it dimming the page.

title: Limits and accuracy
text: The Feature Kit is a quick-use toolbox. Its results are good for everyday design, development and study work. They are not certified for engineering, medical, legal or financial use.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Calculator precision
text: - The calculator uses the browser's standard double-precision numbers, which hold about 15 to 17 significant digits. - Every result is rounded to 14 significant digits to hide floating-point artefacts, so 0.1+0.2 shows 0.3 . - Results are displayed with up to 12 significant digits. Whole numbers under 10^15 are shown in full. - Results smaller than 10^-10 or larger than 10^15 are shown in scientific notation. - Numbers beyond about 1.8 × 10^308 become ∞ . - There are no complex numbers; operations with no real answer give NaN .

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Exact fractions
text: The fraction hint in the expression bar (such as 0.875 = 7/8 ) is found by searching for a fraction with a denominator up to 10,000 that matches the result to within about one part in 10^11. A shown fraction is exact for that decimal; no fraction is shown when none fits. The hint does not appear for keypad results.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Calculus
text: All calculus functions are numerical estimates, not symbolic algebra. Function Method What to expect --- --- --- diff Five-point difference with a step scaled to the point Very close, but the last displayed digits can show rounding noise, for example diff(x^3, 2) shows 12.0000000001 diff2 Three-point second difference Fewer correct digits, for example diff2(x^3, 2) shows 12.0000029666 integral Adaptive Simpson's rule, refining up to 22 levels Very accurate for smooth functions; less reliable across spikes, jumps or infinities inside the range solve with a guess Newton's method, up to 100 steps Finds the root nearest the guess, if any; can miss roots or jump to another one solve with a range Repeated halving, up to 200 steps Reliable when the expression changes sign in the range; otherwise falls back to a guess at the midpoint sum , product Direct addition or multiplication Exact up to floating-point rounding; at most 1,000,000 terms Results within 10^-10 of a whole number are snapped to that whole number by solve .

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Other calculator ranges
text: Function Limit --- --- n! , fact(n) Above 170 the result is ∞ fib(n) Above 1,476 the result is ∞ nextprime(n) Up to 9 × 10^15 isprime(n) Checks by trial division; very large numbers take longer Bitwise operations Work on 32-bit whole numbers stdev , variance Need at least 2 values Your own functions Up to 128 nested calls Any expression Stops with Expression too complex after about 5 million steps rand , randint Use the browser's general-purpose random numbers, not suitable for security

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Graph
text: - The graph samples the expression once per horizontal pixel, so very fast oscillations can look jagged or be missed. - Points where the expression is undefined or infinite are left as gaps. - Zoom ranges from 5 to 5,000 pixels per unit.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Unit Converter
text: - Most categories convert through a base unit with a fixed factor per unit; results are rounded for display to 12 significant digits. - Temperature uses exact formulas through kelvin. - Fuel Economy uses fixed factors (for example 1 US mpg = 0.425144 km/L) and handles the inverse units, such as litres per 100 km. - Sound Level uses approximations: decibels (dB), decibel-milliwatts (dBm) and phons are treated as equal, and sones use the rule that 40 phons is 1 sone and every 10 phons doubles loudness. Treat these as rough equivalents, not physical conversions. - Metric prefixes from yocto (10^-24) to yotta (10^24) are generated for units that take them.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Date & Time
text: - Dates and times use your device's clock and time zone. - Months (≈) and Years (≈) are averages (30.437 and 365.25 days), not calendar months or years. - Business days counts Monday to Friday and ignores public holidays. - Hours in the Difference tab is days × 24; it ignores the time of day and daylight-saving changes. - Unix (s) in the Calendar tab uses the date and time you set, in your local time zone. - World clocks rely on your browser's time zone data.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Developer Tools
text: - Hashes and HMAC use your browser's built-in cryptography and match standard implementations. - JWT decoding does not verify signatures. - The cron explanation reads standard five-field cron only (no seconds or year field, and no L , W or extensions). Next runs are in your local time zone. - The regular expression tool lists the first 200 matches and stops after 10,000. - The Epoch tool reads 1 to 10 digits as seconds and exactly 13 digits as milliseconds; 11- or 12-digit numbers are read as dates, which usually fails.

title: Feature Kit privacy
text: The Feature Kit runs in your browser. Apart from feedback you choose to send and the unit list it downloads, nothing leaves your device.

title: Feature Kit privacy
heading: Kept in your browser
text: What Details How to remove it --- --- --- Calculator history Your last 100 calculations: the expression, the result and the time History bin icon in the heading Notes Every note's text, title and last-saved time Delete on each note Recent dates The last 8 dates you picked in the Calendar tab Clear the site's data in your browser Kit preferences Position, expanded size, Focus mode, the tool that was open while Focus mode was on, and the kit theme Clear the site's data Feedback Each submission, kept so it can be retried until delivered, along with when you were last prompted and how often you dismissed prompts Clear the site's data

title: Feature Kit privacy
heading: Not kept
text: - Calculator variables, functions you define and the memory value (cleared when you leave or reload the page). - The angle setting ( RAD or DEG ) and the graph's y = expression. - Anything you type into the Unit Converter or the Developer Tools. - Text in the feedback form until you send it.

title: Feature Kit privacy
heading: Sent over the network
text: When What is sent or fetched --- --- You open the Unit Converter for the first time on a page The kit downloads the unit list from auricartisan.com. Nothing about you is sent You submit feedback Your rating (1 to 5), your comment or answers, the path of the page you were on (for example /tool/analyzer/ ), and which tool you used last in the kit. If you are signed in, the feedback is linked to your account The Developer Tools never send what you paste. Hashes, HMAC signatures and UUIDs are computed by your browser.

title: Feature Kit privacy
heading: Feedback delivery
text: Feedback is saved on your device first and then sent. If sending fails, it stays on your device and is retried automatically, for example when your connection comes back. Feedback written while signed in to one account is only sent while that same account is signed in.

title: Library Kit
text: The Library Kit is where everything you save from Auric Artisan's tools lives. When you select Save to Library in a tool, the palette, gradient, type scale, preset, plate, report or image lands in your library, and the Library Kit shows it as a tile you can find, reopen and reuse from any page. The kit is a floating panel, so you can open it without leaving what you are doing. Select a tile to restore that item into the tool that made it, or open it in another tool that can use it. Organise items with favourites, collections and the archive; compare two versions side by side with colour-difference figures; share an item as a link; export it, or the whole library, as files; and generate reports in seven formats. Your library is stored in your browser on this device. It is not uploaded to your account. You can export it as a single file, import it elsewhere, and optionally push it to web addresses you control.

title: Library Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone who saves work from the site's tools and wants to find it again. - Designers who iterate on palettes and gradients and want to compare versions. - Teams that want to share a palette or gradient as a link, or back up and move a library between browsers. - Developers who want their library pushed to their own systems as JSON, NDJSON, CSV or reports.

title: Library Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: - On any page of https://auricartisan.com, select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner, then Library . - Select the Library button in the site header. - Press Ctrl + Shift + L ( Cmd + Shift + L on a Mac). - Add library to any page address, or library=favorites , library=recent , library=projects , library=collections , library=archive , library=compare or library=settings to open a particular tab. - Visit https://auricartisan.com/library/workspace/, which opens the panel.

title: Library Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open a tool, for example Basic Color Tools, make a palette and select Save to Library . Give it a name and select Save to Library in the dialog. 2. Press Ctrl + Shift + L . The Library Kit opens on the All tab with your palette as a tile. 3. Type part of its name in Search your library… to find it. 4. Right-click the tile to see everything you can do with it. 5. Select Favourite from that menu. A star appears on the tile and it joins the Favorites tab. 6. Select the tile. The palette opens again in the tool that made it. 7. Back in the Library Kit, select Export in the footer to download a backup of your whole library.

title: Library Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - Browse by tab: All, Recent, Favorites, Projects, Collections, Archive, and one tab per type of item you have saved. - Search, sort, group by project or type, switch between grid and list, and change density. - Restore an item into its tool, or open it in another tool that accepts it. - Rename, describe, tag, favourite, duplicate, collect, archive and delete items, one at a time or in bulk. - Compare two items: palettes with ΔE2000 colour differences and contrast, images side by side, with a wipe or a difference heatmap, settings field by field, audits by score. - Share an item as a self-contained link. - Download an item as JSON, NDJSON, CSV, XML, HTML, Markdown, text, PNG or SVG. - Export and import the whole library as a JSON file, including by drag and drop. - Generate library reports in seven formats. - Push your library automatically to web addresses you configure. - Run any action from a command palette (type ) or a right-click menu.

title: Getting started with the Library Kit
Getting started with the Library Kit
heading: Save something first
text: Items reach your library from the tools: 1. Open a tool, make something (a palette, a gradient, a plate, a report) and select Save to Library . 2. In the dialog, type a name (the box says Name your save ), and optionally a description, a collection (or ＋ New collection… ) and tags separated by commas. 3. Select Save to Library , or press Ctrl + Enter ( Cmd + Enter on a Mac). The item is saved in your browser and appears in the Library Kit straight away, even if the kit is already open.

title: Getting started with the Library Kit
heading: Open the kit
text: Use any of: - Page utilities Library ; - the Library button in the site header ("Open your saved palettes, gradients, presets and exports."); - Ctrl + Shift + L ; - a page address ending in library ; - https://auricartisan.com/library/workspace/. That page shows Opening your library… and opens the panel. If it cannot, it shows an Open library panel button and the hint "Or press Ctrl Shift L anywhere on the site." The kit opens with the cursor in the search box. When you close it, keyboard focus returns to where it was before.

title: Getting started with the Library Kit
heading: The screen, top to bottom
text: 1. Title bar. A six-dot grip (drag it, or use the arrow keys, to move the panel), the title Your Library , an item count such as 12 items , the Panel options button and Close . 2. Tabs. All , Recent , Favorites , Projects , Collections , Archive , Compare , Settings , then one tab per type of item you have saved, such as Palette or Gradient . Each tab except Compare and Settings shows a count. The row scrolls sideways. 3. Search. Labelled Search library with the hint "type for commands"; the box reads Search your library… ( for commands) . 4. Toolbar. A count such as 12 items in All , a Sort list, and three buttons: Group , View and Select . 5. Filter chips. Shown when a collection, tool or tag filter is active. 6. Body. Your items as tiles, in a grid or a list. 7. Bulk bar. Shown while multi-select is on. 8. Footer. New project , Import , Export , the storage used (such as 84 KB ), Settings and Keys .

title: Getting started with the Library Kit
heading: A tile
text: Each tile shows: - a preview: the image, the gradient, up to eight colour swatches, a text sample, or a coloured plate with the item's initials when there is nothing to draw; - a star if it is a favourite; - the item's name; - its type (such as Palette ), the tool it came from, and when it was last changed (such as 3m ago , 2h ago , 5d ago , or a date for anything older than a week). Hovering over a tile shows small action buttons: Favourite , Open details , Share and Delete (in list view also Duplicate and Export JSON ). Right-click a tile for every action.

title: Getting started with the Library Kit
heading: Your first actions
text: 1. Select a tile to reopen the item in its tool. See [Restore and reuse](restore-and-reuse.md). 2. Right-click a tile and choose Rename… to give it a better name. 3. Select Recent to see what you changed in the last seven days. 4. Select Keys in the footer to see the keyboard shortcuts.
