title: Browse and find items
heading: Search
text: Type in Search your library… . After a short pause the view shows only items whose name, description, tool name, type or tags contain your text. Search works within the current tab. - Select the cross in the box, or press Esc , to clear the search. A second Esc closes the kit. - Press Down arrow in the box to jump to the first tile. - Start with to search commands instead of items; see [Commands and right-click menus](commands-and-right-click-menus.md). If nothing matches, you see Nothing matched with a Clear search button.

title: Browse and find items
heading: Sort
text: Choose from the Sort list: Option Order --- --- Newest Most recently changed first (the default) Oldest Earliest created first Name A–Z Alphabetical Name Z–A Reverse alphabetical Type Grouped alphabetically by type Your choice is remembered.

title: Browse and find items
heading: Group
text: The Group button cycles through three settings. Its tooltip tells you which is on: 1. By project (the default) — items under a heading for the collection they belong to. Items in no collection come last under Unfiled . "Grouped by project — press for type". 2. By type — items under a heading per type, such as Palette . "Grouped by type — press for none". 3. None — one list. "Not grouped — press for project". Headings show a count and can be collapsed; the kit remembers which you collapsed. Grouping applies in grid view only. A single group that says nothing new is not given a heading.

title: Browse and find items
heading: Grid or list
text: Select View to switch between a grid of tiles and a list of rows. List rows are wider and show two extra actions: Duplicate and Export JSON . The choice is remembered.

title: Browse and find items
heading: Density
text: Type in the search box and choose Compact density to fit more items on screen, or Comfortable density to go back. The choice is remembered.

title: Browse and find items
heading: Filter by collection, tool or tag
text: - Collection: on the Collections tab, select a collection. The All tab opens filtered to it, with a chip Collection: and its name. - Tool: type and choose Filter: followed by a tool name. The command palette offers up to eight tools you have saved from, with counts. - Tag: type and choose Filter: followed by a tag. Up to eight of your most-used tags are offered. Active filters appear as chips under the toolbar. Select a chip to remove that filter, or Clear all to remove every filter and return to All .

title: Browse and find items
heading: Move with the keyboard
text: - Down arrow from the search box moves to the first tile. - Arrow keys move between tiles: left and right by one, up and down by a row. - Home and End jump to the first and last tile. Moving up from the first row returns to the search box. - Enter or Space restores the focused item (or selects it in multi-select mode); Delete asks to delete it.

title: Browse and find items
heading: The item count
text: The count in the title bar (such as 12 items ) is the number of items that are not archived. The same number shows as a small badge on the Library launcher, up to 99+ .

title: Browse and find items
heading: Related
text: - [Organise your library](organise-your-library.md) - [Reference](reference.md)

title: Commands and right-click menus
text: Two shortcuts put every Library Kit action within reach: a command palette in the search box, and right-click menus.

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: The command palette
text: 1. Select the search box. 2. Type . The tiles are replaced by a list of commands, each with a short hint. 3. Type more to narrow the list, for example export . Commands match on their name or hint. 4. Press Up arrow or Down arrow to move the highlight, and Enter to run the command, or select it with the pointer. The search box clears when a command runs. If nothing matches you see No matching command — "Type part of a command name, or clear the to search items instead." Command Hint shown --- --- New project Bundle several saved items into one project New collection Group saved items into a folder Import library file Merge a previously exported .json Export library snapshot Download everything as a single .json Sync now Push to every configured destination Library settings Storage, sync, defaults and data controls Compare items Open two saved items side by side Switch to list view or Switch to grid view Change how items are laid out Group by type or Stop grouping by type Collapsible sections per asset type Compact density or Comfortable density Fit more items on screen Multi-select items or Leave multi-select Act on several items at once Show archived items or Hide archived items Include archived items in normal views Empty the archive Permanently delete every archived item Show favorites Jump to the starred items Show archive Items you archived rather than deleted Browse collections Folders that group saved items Keyboard shortcuts Every key the panel understands Clear filters Back to every item, unfiltered Filter: and a tool name The number of items saved from that tool (up to 8 tools) Filter: and a tag The number of items with that tag (up to 8 tags) Notes: - New project creates an empty project item; see [Organise your library](organise-your-library.md). - Show archived items changes the library preference; in the Library Kit, archived items remain on the Archive tab. - Group by type moves grouping to the next setting in the Group button's cycle.

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: Right-click an item
text: Right-click a tile. The menu is headed with the item's name, a strip of its colours if it has any, and a line with its type, tool and age. Group Entries --- --- Open Restore into its tool ( Enter ), Open details , up to three Open in [tool] entries, Compare with… Organise Favourite or Remove favourite , Rename… , Add to collection… , Duplicate , Archive or Restore from archive Share & export Copy N colours (for items with colours), Copy item name , Share a link… , Export JSON (below a line) Select this item , Delete ( Del ) When several items are selected and you right-click one of them, the menu is headed N selected and offers Favourite all , Archive all , Add all to collection… , Export all and Delete all .

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: Right-click the panel
text: Right-click empty space in the panel. The menu is headed Library with a line such as "12 items · 3 favourite · 2 collections". Group Entries --- --- Create New project , New collection , Import , Export all View Switch to list or Switch to grid , Multi-select items or Leave multi-select , Show archived or Hide archived , Clear search & filters (disabled when nothing is filtered) Library Sync now , Compare items… , Settings, sync & reports , Empty the archive (disabled when the archive is empty)

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: How the menus behave
text: - Right-clicking inside a text box (such as the search box) shows your browser's normal menu, so copy and paste still work. - The menu closes when you choose an entry, click elsewhere, press Esc , scroll or resize the window. Esc closes only the menu, not the panel. - The menu follows the panel's light or dark theme.

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: Keyboard shortcuts sheet
text: Select Keys in the footer, or run the Keyboard shortcuts command, to see: Keys Action --- --- Ctrl / ⌘ + Shift + L Open or close the library Esc Clear the search, then close ↑ ↓ ← → Move between items Enter Restore the item into its tool Delete Delete the focused item Ctrl / ⌘ + A Select all (in multi-select) Right-click Full actions for an item or the panel … Run a library command Close the sheet with its close button, Esc , or a click outside it.

title: Commands and right-click menus
heading: Related
text: - [Organise your library](organise-your-library.md) - [Library Kit shortcuts](../others/shortcuts.md)

title: Compare two items
text: The Compare tab puts two saved items side by side and shows exactly what changed between them. What you see depends on the kind of items you compare.

title: Compare two items
heading: Open a comparison
text: Any of these opens the Compare tab: - Select the Compare tab. - Right-click a tile and choose Compare with… . That item becomes Before . - In multi-select, select two items, then type and choose Compare items . The first becomes Before and the second After . - Right-click empty space in the panel and choose Compare items… . The workspace is headed Comparison workspace — Compare saved assets , with the line "Choose a before and after asset to inspect exactly what changed."

title: Compare two items
heading: Choose the two items
text: 1. In Before , choose an item from the list ( — Choose an asset — means none). Each entry shows a short type label in brackets and the name, newest first. Archived items are included. 2. In After , choose the second item. 3. Select Swap sides to exchange them. Under the pickers, each side shows its type, tool, name, description and Updated date. Until both are chosen, the comparison area reads Pick assets on both sides to see the diff.

title: Compare two items
heading: Palettes
text: When both items are palettes, or both carry colours, you see: Summary figures Figure Meaning --- --- Swatches Number of colours before → after, and the change Avg ΔE2000 Average colour difference between matched colours, with a verbal rating Max ΔE The largest difference between matched colours Shifted How many matched colours differ by 2 or more, and how many by 10 or more ( distinct ) ΔE2000 is a standard measure of how different two colours look; about 1 is the smallest difference most people notice. The verbal ratings are: ΔE2000 Rating --- --- Under 1 Imperceptible 1 to under 2 Very close 2 to under 5 Close 5 to under 10 Noticeable 10 to under 20 Distinct 20 or more Far Colour-by-colour table. Each row pairs a Left colour with its closest Right colour and shows the ΔE2000 and the Shift : how the lightness and hue moved. Unmatched colours. Colours present on only one side are listed as Removed (only in left) and Added (only in right) . Weakest contrast pair. For each palette, the two colours with the lowest contrast ratio between them, shown as swatches and a ratio such as 1.42:1 , labelled Left palette and Right palette , plus the change ( Δ worst-pair ratio ). A higher ratio means the weakest pair is easier to tell apart. A gradient compared with a palette or another coloured item is treated the same way. If neither side has colours, you see Neither asset has any colors to compare.

title: Compare two items
heading: Images and plates
text: When both items are images or plates, choose a view mode: Mode What it shows --- --- Side Before and After next to each other Wipe The two images stacked, with a slider that reveals more of one or the other ΔE heatmap A map of where the images differ: differences under 2 show as a faint blue, 2 to 10 as yellow, and over 10 as pink ("Pink = where colors differ most (ΔE 10)."). A line reports the number of pixels compared and the average and maximum ΔE The heatmap works on copies scaled down to at most 800 pixels on each side. If the images are different sizes, the heatmap compares the overlapping top-left area and says so. If one side has no image, it shows No image ; if neither does, you see Neither asset has image data. An image that cannot be loaded is reported as "Couldn't load the left image" or "right image".

title: Compare two items
heading: Presets and configurations
text: When both items are presets or configurations, the comparison lists differences in two sections, Settings and Data fields , each with a count of changed, added, removed and identical fields. Changed fields show before → after; added fields are marked with + and removed ones with − . If there are none, the section says No differences. If either item came from the URL Analyzer, a strip at the top shows the URL of each, the Score before → after and the Issues count before → after, coloured by whether it improved.

title: Compare two items
heading: URL Analyzer audits
text: When both items are saved analyses, you see each audit's score in a colour for its band (90 and above, 70 to 89, 50 to 69, below 50), its address, how many versions and issues it holds, and a sentence such as "the second scores 6 higher". A What each holds table compares each section by name, marking sections one side lacks as not stored , and Colours on each page shows up to 12 colours from each.

title: Compare two items
heading: Different kinds of item
text: When the two items are different types and do not both carry colours, the comparison explains that only shared signals are compared and shows Extracted colors (up to 12 from each) and their Tags .

title: Compare two items
heading: Related
text: - [Restore and reuse](restore-and-reuse.md) - [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md) - The URL Analyzer's own comparison of runs: [URL Analyzer](../../../tools/accessibility-and-vision/analyzer/README.md)

title: Organise your library
heading: Favourite an item
text: - Hover over the tile and select the star ( Favourite ), or - right-click the tile and choose Favourite . A star appears on the tile and the item joins the Favorites tab. Do the same again ( Remove favourite ) to unstar it.

title: Organise your library
heading: Rename an item
text: 1. Right-click the tile and choose Rename… . 2. In Rename item , change the Name and select Rename . A message confirms Renamed . You can also rename an item in its details; see [Restore and reuse](restore-and-reuse.md).

title: Organise your library
heading: Add a description and tags
text: 1. Hover over the tile and select the pencil ( Open details ). 2. Type a Description , and Tags (comma-separated) , for example brand, spring, web . 3. Select Save changes . Search matches descriptions and tags, and the command palette offers filters for your most-used tags.

title: Organise your library
heading: Duplicate an item
text: Right-click the tile and choose Duplicate (in list view, the copy icon on the row does the same). The copy is named after the original with " copy" added, and starts neither favourited nor archived.

title: Organise your library
heading: Collections
text: A collection is a folder of saved items. Each item can be in one collection at a time. Grouping by project uses collections as its headings. - On the Collections tab, select the New collection tile ("Group saved items"), or - type and choose New collection , or - right-click empty space in the panel and choose New collection . Type a Collection name (it starts as Untitled collection ) and select Create . A message confirms Created and the name. 1. Right-click a tile and choose Add to collection… . 2. In the Add to collection chooser, select a collection, or New collection… to create one and add the item to it, or No collection to take the item out of its collection. A message confirms, for example "Moved 1 item to" and the collection's name. You can also choose the Collection in the item's details. On the Collections tab, each collection tile shows its name, Collection and the number of items. Select it to see its items on the All tab, with a Collection: filter chip. Select the chip to remove the filter.

title: Organise your library
heading: Projects
text: Select New project in the footer (or type and choose New project ). Type a Project name (it starts as Untitled project ) and select Create . An empty item of the Project type is created and the Projects tab opens. Some tools save projects of their own, which also appear on this tab. The Library Kit does not add existing items to a project; to group items together, use a collection.

title: Organise your library
heading: Archive an item
text: Archiving hides an item without deleting it. - Right-click the tile and choose Archive . - To bring it back, open the Archive tab, right-click it and choose Restore from archive . Archived items appear only on the Archive tab and do not count towards your plan's saved-item allowance. Right-click empty space in the panel and choose Empty the archive , or type and choose Empty the archive . Confirm Delete in the dialog, which says how many items will be removed. This cannot be undone. The option is disabled when the archive is empty.

title: Organise your library
heading: Delete an item
text: - Hover over the tile and select the bin ( Delete ), or right-click and choose Delete , or focus the tile and press Delete . - The dialog Delete item? warns that the item "will be permanently removed. This cannot be undone." Select Delete to confirm or Cancel to keep it.

title: Organise your library
heading: Work with several items at once
text: 1. Select Select in the toolbar (or type and choose Multi-select items ). Tiles show a tick box and a bulk bar appears reading Pick items to act on them . 2. Select tiles to add or remove them. The bar shows 3 selected , for example. 3. Choose a bulk action: Button What it does --- --- All Selects every item in the current view; selecting it again when all are selected clears the selection Favorite Stars the selected items; if all are already starred, unstars them Collect Opens the collection chooser for all selected items Archive Archives the selected items; if all are archived already, restores them Export Downloads each selected item as its own file Delete Asks to confirm, then deletes them all permanently Ctrl + A ( Cmd + A on a Mac) selects all while multi-select is on. Press Esc or select Select again to leave multi-select; the selection is cleared. When several items are selected, right-clicking one of them offers Favourite all , Archive all , Add all to collection… , Export all and Delete all . To select one item from its right-click menu, choose Select this item . Multi-select turns on with just that item selected.

title: Organise your library
heading: Related
text: - [Browse and find](browse-and-find.md) - [Commands and right-click menus](commands-and-right-click-menus.md)

title: Restore and reuse items
heading: Restore an item into its tool
text: Select a tile (or focus it and press Enter ), or right-click it and choose Restore into its tool . - If you are already on that tool's page, the item loads into the tool straight away and the Library Kit closes. - If you are on another page, the site opens the tool's page and loads the item there. - If the item cannot be restored into a tool, its details open instead.

title: Restore and reuse items
heading: Open an item in a different tool
text: Many items can be used by more than one tool. For example, a palette saved in one tool can be opened in another tool that accepts palettes. - Right-click the tile. Under Open , up to three entries read Open in followed by a tool's name. - Or open the item's details: a Use in row lists every tool that accepts the item. Selecting one opens that tool, on this page or another, with the item loaded.

title: Restore and reuse items
heading: Open an item's details
text: Hover over the tile and select the pencil ( Open details ), or right-click and choose Open details . A details dialog opens over the page. - The item's type above its name. - A large preview: the image, the SVG, colour swatches with their values, the gradient or the colour. If there is nothing to preview you see No image stored with a hint. - Editable fields: Name , Description , Collection (with Unfiled for none) and Tags (comma-separated) . - The tool it came from, Created and Updated dates, and an Open in tool link when the item knows its tool page. - Use in buttons for other tools that accept the item. - Saved option values : a collapsible list of the tool settings saved with the item, up to 120 of them. 1. Change the Name , Description , Collection or Tags . 2. Select Save changes . Select Cancel , the close button, or press Esc to leave without saving. Control Downloads --- --- Download PNG The item's image as a file (PNG, or JPEG if that is how it was stored). Disabled when no image is stored Download SVG The item's vector image. Disabled when no SVG is stored Other format list and Download The item in the chosen format: JSON (data + metadata) , NDJSON , CSV , XML , HTML , MD , TXT , PNG (image) or SVG (image) Formats that the item cannot provide are marked — unavailable . File names are made from the item's name. Open in tool in the footer restores the item into its tool, as above. A plate saved without its image shows No image stored . If the plate's generation settings were saved, a Re-render & save image button rebuilds the image from them and stores it; the same seed produces the same plate. If the settings were not saved, an Open Ishihara tool link lets you save it again. To repair every such plate at once, use Repair empty Ishihara plates in [Settings](settings-sync-and-reports.md).

title: Restore and reuse items
heading: Copy colours and names
text: Right-click a tile: - Copy 5 colours (the number matches the item) copies its colour values separated by commas, such as 1f2a44, c79a3a . It appears only for items with colours. - Copy item name copies the name. A message confirms, for example 5 colours copied .

title: Restore and reuse items
heading: Related
text: - [Share, export and import](share-export-and-import.md) - [Compare items](compare-items.md) - [Reference](reference.md)

title: Settings, sync and reports
text: Open the Settings tab (or select Settings in the footer, or type and choose Library settings ). It has five sections, chosen from a row of tabs: Preferences , Reporting , Sync & auto-update , Generate reports and Storage . Changes save as soon as you make them.

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Preferences
text: Setting What it does Values Default --- --- --- --- Autosave drafts as you work Lets tools keep drafts of unsaved work in the library On or off On Show archived items in default views Includes archived items in library views outside the Archive tab. In the Library Kit itself, archived items stay on the Archive tab On or off Off Auto-update: keep all integrations in sync as items change Allows sync destinations to be updated when items change On or off On Autosave interval How often drafts are saved 4, 8, 15 or 30 seconds 8 seconds Keep drafts for How long unsaved drafts are kept before they expire 3, 7, 14, 30 or 90 days 14 days

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Reporting
text: "Controls how much each tool reports back into the library when it saves an asset." Setting What it does Default --- --- --- Capture full output payload from every tool Saves the tool's complete output with each item On Capture the tool's settings/state alongside the asset Saves the tool's settings, so restoring brings them back and Saved option values can list them On Capture export configuration (formats, channels, intent) Saves the export choices you made in the tool On Report defaults Setting Values Default --- --- --- Default report kind full, summary, assets, tool, activity full Default report format JSON, NDJSON, CSV, XML, HTML, MD, TXT JSON Include full asset payloads in reports On or off On Include unsaved drafts On or off Off Turning capture options off makes new saves smaller; items already saved are not changed.

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Sync & auto-update
text: "Send everything in your library to one or more external systems. Supports any HTTP endpoint that accepts JSON/NDJSON/CSV/reports." Sync sends your library from your browser directly to web addresses you choose. Auric Artisan's servers are not involved. Sync is off until you turn it on. Setting What it does Default --- --- --- Sync enabled Master switch for sync Off Auto-push on every change Pushes shortly after items change, and on the poll interval On Include full payloads Sends each item's full data, not only its summary On Include drafts Sends unsaved drafts too Off Redact previews Removes preview images and swatches from what is sent Off Auto-poll interval How often automatic pushes run 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 60 min (default 1 min) Buttons: - Push all destinations now — sends to every active destination and reports "N/M destinations succeeded." - Add destination — adds a new destination named Destination 1 , Destination 2 and so on. - Clear history — empties the activity list. 1. Turn on Sync enabled . 2. Select Add destination . 3. Fill in the destination card: Field What it means Values --- --- --- Name A label for you Text Active Whether this destination is used On or off On change Push to it when items change On or off On interval Push to it on the poll interval On or off Transport How to send webhook or http (send to the URL), console (write to your browser's developer console, for testing), local (keep a temporary log in the page, for testing) Method The HTTP method POST , PUT , PATCH URL Where to send, such as https://example.com/webhook A web address Body format What to send JSON , NDJSON , CSV , REPORT Report kind , Report format Used when the body format is REPORT As for reports Auth bearer token Sent as an Authorization: Bearer header, if filled in Optional 4. Select Test now to send once. The card's status line shows the result (for example idle , or the last success time and any error). A failed test also opens Push failed with the reason. 5. Select Remove to delete a destination (confirm Remove ). Requests are sent from your browser, so the receiving server must accept requests from https://auricartisan.com (cross-origin requests). Your cookies are not sent. Each request carries the header X-Auric-Library-Version: 1 . Recent sync activity lists up to 20 recent pushes with time, destination, reason, and bytes and HTTP status, or the error. You can also push from the command palette ( Sync now ) or the panel's right-click menu. If sync is off you see "Sync is switched off — turn it on in Library settings."; with no destinations, "No sync destinations configured yet."

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Generate reports
text: "Download a detailed report of everything in your library in the format of your choice." 1. Choose a Kind : Kind Contents --- --- full Library statistics, every item's details and data, collections and settings summary Statistics only assets Every item's details tool The items saved from one tool, with their data. A Tool list appears so you can pick the tool; each shows its item count activity Items added and updated per day 2. Choose a Format : JSON , NDJSON , CSV , XML , HTML , MD or TXT . 3. Select Download report . The quick buttons JSON , NDJSON , CSV , XML , HTML , MD and TXT download the default report kind in that format at once. Report files are named auric-library- followed by the kind and the date and time.

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Storage
text: - The line "Using" shows how much space the library takes and across how many entries. - Export library downloads the full backup ( auric-library-backup.json ). - Import library loads a backup, asking whether to Merge or Replace ; see [Share, export and import](share-export-and-import.md). - Purge expired drafts removes drafts older than Keep drafts for and confirms Drafts purged . - Reset library deletes every saved item and collection after the warning "This deletes every saved item and collection. This cannot be undone." Select Reset everything to confirm. Maintenance Repair empty Ishihara plates rebuilds missing images for Ishihara plates that were saved with their generation settings but without an image. It asks to confirm how many plates it will re-render, shows progress, and reports how many it repaired. Plates saved without settings cannot be repaired this way. The last line lists the available sync transports: webhook , http , console , local .

title: Settings, sync and reports
heading: Related
text: - [Privacy](../others/privacy.md) - [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md) - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

title: Share, export and import
heading: Share an item as a link
text: 1. Hover over the tile and select Share , or right-click it and choose Share a link… . 2. The Share link dialog opens with the item's name as its title and the note "Anyone with this link can open a copy. State is encoded in the URL — no account needed." 3. Select Copy (it briefly reads Copied! ), or Share via… to use your device's share sheet where available, or Open in new tab to try the link yourself. 4. Select Close when you are done. The item itself is packed into the link, so the recipient does not need an account and nothing is uploaded. The link opens the tool that can show the item. Under the address, the dialog shows the link's length in characters and the size limit, with the note "safe to paste into chat, docs, or email." Links are limited to 6 KB of packed data. Palettes, gradients and small presets fit easily; large items such as audits and images often do not. When an item is too large, the dialog is titled Too large to share and reads "Encoded payload is" followed by its size and "over the 6 KB share limit", with a bar showing how far over it is. Export the item as a file instead.

title: Share, export and import
heading: Download one item
text: - In list view, select the download icon on the row ( Export JSON ), or - right-click the tile and choose Export JSON . Most items download as a JSON file named after the item. Image and plate items download as the image itself (PNG or JPEG), or as SVG if that is all they hold. For other formats (NDJSON, CSV, XML, HTML, Markdown, text, PNG, SVG) use the item's details; see [Restore and reuse](restore-and-reuse.md).

title: Share, export and import
heading: Download several items
text: Turn on multi-select, select the items and choose Export in the bulk bar, or right-click one of them and choose Export all . Each item downloads as its own file. Your browser may ask you to allow several downloads.

title: Share, export and import
heading: Back up the whole library
text: Select Export in the footer, or right-click empty space and choose Export all , or type and choose Export library snapshot . A file named auric-library-backup.json downloads, containing every item, collection, draft and library setting. A message confirms Library snapshot downloaded . The Settings tab's Storage section has the same action, Export library .

title: Share, export and import
heading: Import a library file
text: Import merges a previously exported library file into the library you have. - Select Import in the footer, or type and choose Import library file , and pick a .json file; or - drag a library .json file onto the Library Kit panel. While you drag, the panel shows "Drop a library .json file to import". A message confirms Imported and the file name, or says "That file could not be imported." if the file is not a library export. The Import library button in the Settings tab's Storage section asks first: "Merge the imported file with your current library, or replace everything?" Choose Merge to keep your existing items, or Replace to remove them and keep only the imported ones. Replacing cannot be undone. The footer button and drag and drop always merge.

title: Share, export and import
heading: Reports
text: To download a report of the whole library in JSON, NDJSON, CSV, XML, HTML, Markdown or text, use the Settings tab's Generate reports section. See [Settings, sync and reports](settings-sync-and-reports.md).

title: Share, export and import
heading: Move a library to another browser or device
text: 1. In the old browser, select Export in the footer. 2. Copy auric-library-backup.json to the new device. 3. In the new browser, open the Library Kit and drag the file onto it, or select Import .

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
text: For problems shared by every kit, see [Troubleshooting kits](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: My saved items are missing
text: Why: The library lives in your browser on this device. It is not in your account, so items saved in another browser, on another device, or in a private window are not here. Clearing this site's data in your browser also deletes the library. What to do: Open the library in the browser where you saved the items. To move items, export them there ( Export in the footer) and import the file here. There is no way to recover a library that was cleared without an export.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: An item is not on the All tab
text: Why: It is archived, a filter is active, or you are searching. What to do: Check the Archive tab, select Clear all under the toolbar, and clear the search box.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Saving is refused because of my plan
text: Why: Each plan allows a number of active saved items (archived items do not count): 20 on Apprentice, 500 on Artisan, 2,500 on Specialist and 10,000 on Industrial Pro. The message reads "Your plan keeps N saved projects, and you have M. Archive or delete one to make room, or upgrade for more." What to do: Archive or delete items you no longer need, or change plan. See [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: "This browser has run out of room for saved projects"
text: Why: Browsers limit how much each site can store, whatever your plan. Images and plates take the most space. What to do: Export the library as a backup, then delete or archive large items, or select Purge expired drafts in Settings Storage . The Status Kit's Memory tab shows how full the site's storage is.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: "Library storage is full. Some image data couldn't be saved."
text: Why: The item was saved, but its image did not fit in the remaining space. What to do: Free space as above. For Ishihara plates saved with their settings, use Re-render & save image in the item's details, or Repair empty Ishihara plates in Settings Storage , once there is room.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Selecting a tile opens the details instead of the tool
text: Why: The site cannot find a tool page that can load this item, so the kit shows its details instead. What to do: Use the details to download the item, or try Open in another tool from its right-click menu.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: "Too large to share"
text: Why: Share links carry the item inside the address and are limited to 6 KB of packed data. Audits, images and large presets exceed it. What to do: Export the item as a file and send the file instead.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Only one file downloaded when I exported several items
text: Why: Browsers often ask before letting a page download several files, or block the extra downloads. What to do: Allow multiple downloads for auricartisan.com when your browser asks, or export items one at a time. To get everything in one file, use Export in the footer.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: "That file could not be imported."
text: Why: The file is not a Library Kit export, or it is damaged. Individual item files (from Export JSON ) are not library backups. What to do: Import a file made with Export in the footer or Export library in Settings, such as auric-library-backup.json .

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Sync reports "Push failed"
text: Why: Common causes: the URL is wrong; the server rejected the method or token; or the server does not accept requests from other websites, which browsers require for sync to work. What to do: Check the URL , Method and Auth bearer token ; make sure the server allows cross-origin requests from https://auricartisan.com; then select Test now . The error text in Recent sync activity shows the server's reply.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: "Sync is switched off"
text: What to do: Open Settings Sync & auto-update and turn on Sync enabled .

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Show archived items does nothing in the kit
text: Why: In the Library Kit, archived items always appear on the Archive tab only. The setting affects other library views. What to do: Use the Archive tab.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: A comparison shows "Couldn't load the image"
text: Why: The image could not be read, for example because it points to another website that does not allow it. What to do: Compare items whose images were saved in the library itself.

title: Library Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + Shift + L does nothing
text: Why: Another program or extension uses that combination. What to do: Use Page utilities Library or the Library button in the site header.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Is my library saved to my account?
text: No. It is stored in your browser on this device. Export it ( Export in the footer) to keep a backup or move it to another browser.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: How many items can I keep?
text: Your plan sets the number of active saved items: 20 on Apprentice, 500 on Artisan, 2,500 on Specialist and 10,000 on Industrial Pro. Archived items do not count. Your browser's storage limit applies on top of that, especially for images.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Are the tools still free if I reach the limit?
text: Yes. The limit only affects saving new items. See [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: What happened to the Library Workspace page?
text: The library now opens as a floating panel on any page. https://auricartisan.com/library/workspace/ still works and opens the panel.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Can other people see my library?
text: No. Only items you share as links, export as files or push to your own sync destinations leave your browser.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: What does a share link contain?
text: The item's data, packed into the address. Anyone with the link can open a copy. Nothing is stored on a server.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: What is the difference between archive and delete?
text: Archiving hides an item and keeps it on the Archive tab, where you can restore it. Deleting removes it for good.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: What is the difference between a collection and a project?
text: A collection is a folder that groups items; each item can be in one. A project is a type of saved item; the Library Kit can create empty ones, and some tools save their own. Use collections to group your items.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Can I undo a delete?
text: No. Deletes, Empty the archive and Reset library cannot be undone.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Does the library work offline?
text: Browsing, searching, organising, comparing and exporting work offline once the kit has loaded, because everything is in your browser. Sync needs a connection, and opening an item in a tool needs that tool's page to load.

title: Library Kit FAQ
heading: Which tools can save to the library?
text: Tools with a Save to Library button. Saved items record which tool made them, and many can also be opened in other tools that accept the same type of item.

title: Library Kit glossary
text: Universal Library — Everything you have saved from the site's tools, kept in your browser. Item (asset) — One saved thing, such as a palette, gradient, image, preset or audit. The kit's dialogs sometimes say "asset". Type — What kind of item it is, such as Palette, Gradient, Plate or Analysis. Each type you have saved gets a tab. Restore — Reopen an item in the tool that made it, with its data and settings. Open in — Load an item into a different tool that accepts its type. Collection — A folder of items. An item belongs to at most one collection. Unfiled — Not in any collection. Project — A type of saved item. The kit can create empty projects; some tools save their own. Favourite — An item marked with a star; listed on the Favorites tab. Archive — A holding area for items you want out of the way without deleting them. Draft — Unsaved work a tool keeps in the library while autosave is on. Drafts expire after the Keep drafts for period. Snapshot (backup) — A single JSON file containing your whole library, made with Export . Share link — A web address that carries a copy of an item inside it, so anyone with the link can open it. Sync destination — A web address you configure to receive copies of your library. Transport — How a sync destination sends: webhook or http (to your URL), console or local (testing only). Bearer token — A secret sent in the Authorization header so your server knows the request is yours. Cross-origin request (CORS) — A request from one website to another. Your server must allow requests from auricartisan.com for sync to work. NDJSON — Newline-delimited JSON: one JSON record per line. ΔE2000 (Delta E 2000) — A standard measure of how different two colours look. Around 1 is barely noticeable. Contrast ratio — How distinct two colours are in lightness, from 1:1 (identical) to 21:1 (black on white). Heatmap — An image that colours each pixel by how much two images differ there. Command palette — The list of commands you get by typing in the search box.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Storage
text: - The library is kept in your browser's storage for auricartisan.com. Browsers typically allow a site only a few megabytes of this kind of storage, whatever your plan, and images use it fastest. - Images saved from some tools are reduced before storing, so what you download from the library can be smaller than what the tool produced. Export from the tool itself for full-size output. - The storage figure in the footer and in Settings Storage is an estimate of the library's own use.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Plan allowance
text: Plan Active saved items --- --- Apprentice 20 Artisan 500 Specialist 2,500 Industrial Pro 10,000 Archived items do not count. Editing an existing item is always allowed, even at the limit. The figures are from https://auricartisan.com/company/pricing/, which is authoritative if they differ.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Share links
text: - Limited to 6 KB of packed data per link. - The link contains a copy of the item at the moment you shared it; later changes are not reflected.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Sync
text: - Runs only in an open page of the site; nothing is sent while the site is closed. - Automatic pushes run no more often than every 15 seconds, whatever interval you choose. - The receiving server must accept cross-origin requests from auricartisan.com. - The console and local transports are for testing and do not send anything off your device. The local log is lost when the page reloads.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Reports
text: - Reports describe the library at the moment you download them. - The tool report covers one tool at a time.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Comparisons
text: - Palette matching pairs each colour with its closest counterpart, so reordering colours does not count as a change. - ΔE2000 values are computed from the stored colour values in sRGB; they indicate visible difference under standard viewing conditions and are not a certified measurement. - Contrast ratios follow the usual relative-luminance formula used by accessibility guidelines. - The image heatmap compares copies scaled to at most 800 pixels a side, and only the overlapping area of different-sized images.

title: Library Kit limits
heading: Details and downloads
text: - Saved option values lists up to 120 settings. - Formats an item cannot provide are marked unavailable.

title: Library Kit privacy
heading: Where your library is kept
text: Every saved item, collection, draft and library setting is stored in your browser's storage for auricartisan.com, on this device. It is not uploaded to Auric Artisan and not linked to your account. Anyone who uses the same browser profile can see it. The Library Kit's own view preferences (tab, grouping, density, collapsed groups, panel position, size, theme and Keep open ) are stored the same way.

title: Library Kit privacy
heading: The only ways your items leave the device
text: Action What leaves, and where it goes --- --- Share a link… A copy of the item, packed into the link. It goes wherever you send the link. Anyone with the link can open the copy Export , Export JSON , downloads, reports Files saved to your device by your browser Sync Your library (with or without full data, drafts and previews, as you choose) sent from your browser to the URLs you configure, with your bearer token if you set one Nothing is sent to Auric Artisan's servers by the Library Kit.

title: Library Kit privacy
heading: Sensitive settings
text: Sync destinations, including any Auth bearer token , are stored in your browser as part of the library settings. They are included in a full library backup ( auric-library-backup.json ) and in full reports. Treat those files as private if you use tokens, or remove destinations before exporting.

title: Library Kit privacy
heading: Removing your data
text: - Delete items individually, empty the archive, or use Settings Storage Reset library to delete everything. - Clearing this site's data in your browser also deletes the library. - Deleted data cannot be recovered unless you exported it.

title: Menu Kit
text: The Menu Kit is a start menu for the whole of auricartisan.com. It opens over any page and lists the site's tools and pages as illustrated tiles, grouped into seven tabs: Tools , Design , Analyze , Account , Library , Company and Trust . Selecting a tile takes you to that page. Type in its search box and the tiles give way to a ranked list of matching pages and quick actions, such as Copy current URL or Open a random tool . The search forgives typos in the middle of words: typing clrlib finds Color Library . Pages you open often rise in the results and fill the Most Used section. The Menu Kit follows the site's tool visibility mode, set in the [Advanced Kit](../advanced-kit/README.md): in Basic mode it shows beginner-friendly tools, in Advanced mode the scientific ones, and in Everything mode the lot.

title: Menu Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - New visitors who want an overview of everything the site offers. - Regular users who want to jump to a tool in a couple of keystrokes from any page. - Anyone looking for account, library, company or legal pages.

title: Menu Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: - On any page of https://auricartisan.com, select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner, then Menu . - Or press Ctrl + M .

title: Menu Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Press Ctrl + M . The Menu Kit opens with the cursor in Search Auric Artisan… . 2. Look at the Tools tab: it starts with Recommended and Most Used sections. 3. Select another tab, for example Library , to see its pages. 4. Select the search box and type icon . The tiles are replaced by a list of results. 5. Press Down arrow to highlight a result and Enter to open it. 6. On the new page, press Ctrl + M again. The Menu Kit remembers the tab you used last. 7. Press Esc to close it.

title: Menu Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - Browse the site in seven tabs, with collapsible sections and a count of pages in each. - See at a glance which tile is the page you are on. - Start from eight recommended entry points and your own most-used pages. - Search pages by name, section or description, with forgiving matching and a result count. - Run quick actions: copy the page URL, scroll to top, go home, go back, reload, open a random tool, or switch the menu's theme. - Navigate entirely with the keyboard. - See the site's status (for example Beta ) in the title bar.

heading: Most Used
text: Most Used follows Recommended . It lists up to eight pages from the Tools tab, ordered by how often you have opened them from the Menu Kit, and never repeats a page already in Recommended . On your first visit, before you have opened anything, it lists pages alphabetically. The counts are kept in your browser. Opening a page any other way does not count.

title: Find a page by browsing
heading: Collapse and expand sections
text: Select a section heading to collapse it; select it again to expand it. The chevron at the right of the heading turns to show the state. With the keyboard, focus the heading and press Enter or Space . The kit remembers which sections you collapsed.

title: Find a page by browsing
heading: Move with the keyboard
text: 1. Press Down arrow from the search box or the tab row to move into the body. 2. Use the arrow keys to move between section headings and tiles, and Home or End to jump to the first or last. 3. Press Enter on a tile to open it.

title: Find a page by browsing
heading: How the tool visibility mode changes the menu
text: The Menu Kit shows only the tools that fit the site's mode, set in the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md). A tab with nothing to show disappears. Mode What changes in the Menu Kit --- --- Basic (the default) The Design tab is hidden. The Tools tab shows every section Advanced The Design tab appears. The Tools tab keeps Start Here and Search but hides General Color Tools Everything Every tab and every page Custom Every page except the tools you have unticked in the Advanced Kit Account, Library, Company and Trust pages, the URL Analyzer and the Vision Deficiency Simulator show in every mode. If the tab you were on has nothing to show in the new mode, the kit switches to the first tab that does.

title: Search and quick actions
text: Typing in the Menu Kit's search box turns the menu into a ranked list of results, like a command palette. Results include pages from every tab and a set of quick actions.

title: Search and quick actions
heading: Search for a page
text: 1. Open the Menu Kit. The cursor is already in Search Auric Artisan… . If it is not, press / or select the box. 2. Type a few letters, for example gamut . 3. The tiles are replaced by a list of up to 16 results, and a count such as 4 results appears. 4. Press Up arrow or Down arrow to highlight a result, or move the pointer over it. 5. Press Enter , or select the result, to open it. The kit closes and the page opens. If you pick the page you are already on, the kit just closes. Each result shows the page's illustration or icon, its name, the section it belongs to, and Open ↵ on the right.

title: Search and quick actions
heading: How matching works
text: - Letters in order. A result matches if the letters you type appear in its name in the same order, with anything in between. clrlib matches Color Library , and tmap matches Tone Mapping . - Section names count. If the name alone does not match, the section and name together are tried, so legal priv finds Privacy in Legal and Security . - Descriptions count. If neither matches, a page whose description contains your exact text still appears, lower down. - Ranking. Matches at the start of words and runs of consecutive letters rank higher, tighter matches rank higher, name matches beat description matches, and pages you open often get a boost. - Mode. Search respects the tool visibility mode, so tools hidden by the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md) do not appear. - One result per page. A page listed in several sections appears once. When nothing matches, the list reads No matches for and your search in quotation marks.

title: Search and quick actions
heading: Quick actions
text: Quick actions appear in the same list when your search matches their name. They show Action ↵ on the right. Action Description shown What it does --- --- --- Copy current URL Copy this page's link to the clipboard Copies the address of the page you are on Scroll to top Jump to the top of the page Scrolls the page to the top Go home Open the Auric Artisan home page Goes to https://auricartisan.com Go back Browser back Goes back one page in your browser history Reload page Refresh the current page Reloads the page Open a random tool Jump to a random tool Opens a randomly chosen tool page from the menu Toggle menu theme Switch this menu light / dark Switches the Menu Kit between light and dark For example, type copy and press Enter to copy the page's address. The kit closes before running the action.

title: Search and quick actions
heading: Clear the search
text: - Select the cross at the right of the search box. - Or press Esc once. A second Esc closes the kit. Clearing the search brings back the tabs and tiles.

title: Search and quick actions
heading: Search the whole site instead
text: The Menu Kit searches its own list of pages. To search the text of pages across the site, or the web, use the site-wide search: press Ctrl + K , or go to https://auricartisan.com/search/. See [Search](../../../search/README.md) and [Site features](../../../site-features/README.md). Note: The footer hint Ctrl K Search refers to that site-wide search. Pressing Ctrl + K while the Menu Kit is open opens the site-wide search. Use / to reach the Menu Kit's own search box.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
text: For problems shared by every kit, see [Troubleshooting kits](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Design tab is missing
text: Why: The site's tool visibility mode is Basic , which is the default. Basic mode hides the scientific tools, and the Design tab has nothing else to show. What to do: Open the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md) and choose Advanced or Everything .

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: A tool I expect is not in the menu or the search results
text: Why: The tool visibility mode hides it, or you unticked it in Custom mode. What to do: Choose Everything in the Advanced Kit, or tick the tool in Custom mode. If the tool still does not appear, it may not be in the Menu Kit's list; try All Tools in the Tools tab or the site-wide search ( Ctrl + K ).

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + M does nothing
text: Why: Your browser or operating system uses that key combination first. On a Mac, Cmd + M minimises the window. What to do: Open the Menu Kit from Page utilities Menu .

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + K opens a different search
text: Why: Ctrl + K opens the site-wide search, even while the Menu Kit is open. What to do: Press / to put the cursor in the Menu Kit's own search box.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: The menu says "Menu unavailable"
text: Why: The list of pages could not be downloaded, usually because the connection dropped. What to do: Check your connection and reload the page, then open the Menu Kit again.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: Most Used shows pages I have never opened
text: Why: Until you have opened pages from the Menu Kit, Most Used has no counts to go on and lists pages alphabetically. What to do: Nothing; it fills with your own pages as you use the menu.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: A section is empty or missing
text: Why: You collapsed it earlier (the kit remembers), or every page in it is hidden by the tool visibility mode. What to do: Select the section heading to expand it, or change the mode in the Advanced Kit.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: Selecting a result does nothing
text: Why: The result is the page you are already on. The kit closes without reloading it. What to do: Choose another result, or use the Reload page quick action.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: The kit opens on every page
text: Why: Its Focus mode is on. What to do: Select Focus mode so it is no longer gold, then close the kit.

title: Menu Kit troubleshooting
heading: The status chip says Beta
text: Why: The chip shows the release status of the whole site, which is currently Beta . It is not a problem. What to do: For the status of the page you are on, open the [Status Kit](../../status-kit/README.md).

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: How is the Menu Kit different from the site header menu?
text: The Menu Kit opens on any page, including tool pages where the header is scrolled away, and holds the whole site in one searchable panel with tabs, recommended pages and your most-used pages.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: How is it different from the site-wide search?
text: The Menu Kit searches its own list of pages by name, section and description, and also offers quick actions. The site-wide search ( Ctrl + K , or https://auricartisan.com/search/) searches the content of pages and can search the web. See [Search](../../../search/README.md).

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Does the Menu Kit list every page on the site?
text: No. It lists the main tools and pages. Individual articles, library entries and some tool sub-pages are not in it; use the site-wide search for those.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Why do I see fewer tools than a friend?
text: The Menu Kit follows the tool visibility mode chosen in the [Advanced Kit](../../advanced-kit/README.md), which is stored in each browser. New visitors start in Basic mode.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Can I reorder or pin tiles?
text: No. The order is fixed, apart from Most Used , which follows how often you open pages from the Menu Kit.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Can I reset Most Used?
text: There is no reset button. Clearing this site's data in your browser resets it, along with your other kit preferences.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Does search understand typos?
text: Partly. It matches letters in order with gaps, so clrlib finds Color Library . It does not correct swapped or wrong letters.

title: Menu Kit FAQ
heading: Is anything I type sent anywhere?
text: No. Searching and quick actions run in your browser. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Menu Kit glossary
text: Start menu — The Menu Kit's role: one panel that lists the site's pages, like the start menu of a desktop computer. Tab — One of the seven top-level groups: Tools, Design, Analyze, Account, Library, Company, Trust. Section — A collapsible group of tiles inside a tab, such as Start Here or Utility Labs . Tile — One page in the menu, shown as an illustration and a name. Recommended — Eight entry points picked for first-time visitors, at the top of the Tools tab. Most Used — Up to eight Tools-tab pages you open most often from the Menu Kit. Results list — The ranked list that replaces the tiles while you search. It works like a command palette. Fuzzy matching — Search that matches the letters you type in order, allowing other letters in between. Quick action — A command in the results list that does something on the current page, such as Copy current URL . Status chip — The label next to the kit's title showing the site's release status, such as Beta . Tool visibility mode — The site-wide choice of Basic, Advanced, Everything or Custom tools, set in the Advanced Kit. The Menu Kit shows only tools the mode allows.

title: Menu Kit limits
heading: What the menu covers
text: - The Menu Kit lists 83 pages in 14 sections across seven tabs, plus the Recommended and Most Used sections built from the Tools tab. - It does not list individual Learn articles, blog posts, documentation articles, changelog entries or library items. Use the site-wide search for those. - The Projects tile links to an external site.

title: Menu Kit limits
heading: Search
text: - The results list shows at most 16 results. - Matching is by letters in order, then by section and name together, then by an exact phrase in the description. - It does not correct wrong or swapped letters, and it does not search the text of pages. - Results respect the tool visibility mode, so hidden tools cannot be found through the Menu Kit. - Ranking gives a modest boost to pages you open often, capped so a single much-used page does not always come first.

title: Menu Kit limits
heading: Most Used
text: - Counts only visits started from the Menu Kit, in this browser. - Covers pages in the Tools tab only. - Is not shared between browsers or devices and cannot be reset from the kit.

title: Menu Kit limits
heading: Status chip
text: The chip shows one status for the whole site, not the status of the page you are on. For per-page status, use the [Status Kit](../../status-kit/README.md).

title: Menu Kit privacy
heading: Kept in your browser
text: What Why --- --- The last tab you used To open on it next time Which sections you collapsed To keep them collapsed How many times you opened each page from the Menu Kit To fill Most Used and rank search results Position, expanded size, Focus mode and theme Shared kit preferences None of this is sent anywhere. It is removed when you clear this site's data in your browser.

title: Menu Kit privacy
heading: Downloaded
text: The first time you open the Menu Kit on a page, it downloads the list of pages and the site status from auricartisan.com. Your searches are not sent: matching happens in your browser. The Copy current URL quick action writes the page address to your clipboard, which your browser may ask permission for.

title: Status Kit
text: The Status Kit answers two questions: how finished is this part of Auric Artisan, and how is my device coping? Its This page card shows the status of the page you are on, such as Beta , Stable or Experimental . Its scanner lists every page under a path, such as /tool/ or /library/ , with each page's status, a summary and filters. Above the scanner, a collapsible System status panel shows live readings from your browser across five tabs: Network , Hardware , Memory , Display and Runtime , including your connection type, battery level, storage use, screen resolution, colour gamut and a live frame-rate graph. All readings are taken in your browser and shown only to you. Scans read pages of auricartisan.com.

title: Status Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - Visitors who want to know whether a tool is stable or still experimental before relying on it. - Anyone reporting a problem who needs to describe their device, browser and connection. - Designers checking what their display supports, such as the P3 wide gamut.

title: Status Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: On any page of https://auricartisan.com, select Page utilities in the bottom-left corner, then Status . The Status Kit has no keyboard shortcut.

title: Status Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Select Page utilities Status . The Status Kit opens with the cursor in the path box. 2. Read the This page card: the page title and its status badge. 3. Select the Hardware tab in System status to see your battery, device memory and CPU threads. 4. Type /library/ in the path box and press Enter . 5. Read the summary cards ( Pages , Tools , Stable , Beta , Issues ) and the grouped list of pages. 6. Select a filter chip such as Stable to narrow the list. 7. Select a page in the list to open it in a new tab.

title: Status Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - See the current page's status at a glance. - Scan any section of the site and count its pages by status. - Filter scan results by status and search them by title. - Re-run any of your last eight scans with one click. - Check your connection, battery, memory, storage, caches, display, frame rate, page load time, service worker, app mode, language, time zone and cookie setting.

text: Select Page utilities (bottom-left corner) Status . The launcher's tooltip reads "View the current page status and scan page status entries." There is no keyboard shortcut to open it. The kit opens with the cursor in the path box, ready for a scan.

title: Getting started with the Status Kit

title: Check a page's status
text: Every page on Auric Artisan has a status that says how finished it is. The Status Kit's This page card shows it for the page you are on.

title: Check a page's status
heading: Read the This page card
text: 1. Open the Status Kit ( Page utilities Status ). 2. Look at the This page card at the top. The card shows: - the label This page ; - a coloured status badge, for example Beta . Its tooltip reads "Current page status: Beta."; - the page's title as a link. Selecting it opens the same page in a new tab. Until the status has been worked out, the badge reads Unknown for a moment.

title: Check a page's status
heading: What each status means
text: The kit can show the labels below. The site does not publish formal definitions for them; they carry their usual software meanings. Status Meaning --- --- Stable Finished and expected to keep working as it does now Beta Complete and usable, still being refined. Most of the site is Beta, matching the site's overall status Alpha Early; expect gaps and changes Experimental A trial feature that may change a lot or be withdrawn In development Being built Under testing Being tested before a wider release Maintenance Temporarily limited while it is being worked on Research A research tool; results are exploratory Archived Kept for reference, no longer developed Deprecated Being retired; use its replacement Unknown No status could be found The scanner counts Alpha , Deprecated and Archived pages as Issues .

title: Check a page's status
heading: How a page gets its status
text: The site keeps one central list of statuses. A page takes the status of the closest entry that covers it: an entry for that exact page wins, then an entry for the folder it sits in. Pages with no closer entry take the status of the whole site, which is Beta . At the time of writing: - the Vision Simulation lab is Experimental ; - the changelog, the timeline, blog and documentation articles, the About, Accessibility and FAQ pages, the legal pages and the Collections page are Stable ; - everything else, including the home page and the tools, is Beta . These assignments change as the site develops; the kit always shows the current one.

title: Check a page's status
heading: The site status versus a page status
text: The Menu Kit shows a status chip for the whole site. The Status Kit shows the status of individual pages. They often agree, because most pages share the site's Beta status.

title: Scan a section of the site
text: The scanner lists every page of auricartisan.com whose address starts with a path you give, and shows each page's status.

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Run a scan
text: 1. Open the Status Kit. The cursor is in the path box. 2. Type a path such as /tool/ , /library/ or /company/ . You can also paste a full address such as https://auricartisan.com/library/blog/ ; only its path is used. 3. Press Enter or select Scan . While the scan runs, the results area shows Scanning pages with a running count such as 12 / 48 . The kit reads the site map to find the pages, then fetches each page to read its title, so a large section takes a little while.

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Read the results
text: When the scan finishes you see, from top to bottom: 1. Summary cards. Card Counts --- --- Pages Every page found Tools Pages in the tool categories (Tools, Color Lab and Vision) Stable Pages with the Stable status Beta Pages with the Beta status Issues Pages that are Alpha, Deprecated or Archived 2. Filter chips. All , one chip per status found, and Issues if any, each with a count. They appear only when the results contain more than one status or any issues. 3. Result count , for example 48 pages , or Showing 12 of 48 pages when a filter or search is active. 4. Target page. If a page's address matches your path exactly (for example /library/ itself), it appears first as an expanded summary with its URL , Category , Collection and Status . 5. Category groups. The other pages, grouped under collapsible headings with a count: Tools , Color Lab , Vision , Library , Company , Trust and Other . Each row shows a thumbnail, the page title and a status badge. Hover over a title to see its path. Select a page row to open that page in a new tab.

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Filter and search the results
text: - Select a filter chip to show only pages with that status, or Issues for the problem statuses. Select All to clear it. - Type in Search pages... (it appears after a scan) to show only pages whose title contains your text. The two combine. If nothing matches, you see Nothing matches with either "No pages match" and your search, or "No pages have that status. Try a different filter."

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Collapse groups
text: Select a category heading to collapse or expand it. The kit remembers which categories you collapsed.

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Recent scans
text: After your first scan, a Recent scans section lists your last eight scans, newest first. Each shows the path you typed, "Scanned" with how long ago (for example Scanned 5 minutes ago ), the number of pages, and the status of the target page. Select one to run it again.

title: Scan a section of the site
heading: Which pages are included
text: - Pages come from the site map. If the site map cannot be read, the kit falls back to the pages listed in the Menu Kit. - The home page ( / ) is never listed, even when you scan / . - Individual colour pages, whose addresses start with /color/ , are left out. - Paths are matched from the start: /tool/ finds /tool/analyzer/ but /analyzer/ finds nothing.

title: System status
text: The System status panel shows live information about your device, connection and the page, read from your browser. It refreshes every two seconds while the Status Kit is open, and at once when your connection goes on or off line.

title: System status
heading: Open, collapse and switch pages
text: - The panel is expanded when the kit opens. Select its heading ( System status ) or the chevron to collapse or expand it. With the keyboard, focus the heading and press Enter or Space . - The pill next to the heading shows Online or Offline . - Select a tab to switch between Network , Hardware , Memory , Display and Runtime . A reading shows — when your browser does not provide it. Some readings exist only in certain browsers, noted below.

title: System status
heading: Network
text: Reading What it shows --- --- Connection Your connection's effective speed class, such as 4G or 3G , or Online or Offline if the browser does not report a class Speed Estimated download speed in Mbps, with a bar (full at 20 Mbps) and the connection type, such as wifi, when known Latency Estimated round-trip time in milliseconds Data Saver On if your browser's data-saving mode is on, otherwise Off Speed, latency and data saver come from the browser's network information, which Chromium-based browsers provide and others often do not. They are the browser's rough estimates, not a speed test.

title: System status
heading: Hardware
text: Reading What it shows --- --- Battery Charge level with a bar, and Charging or On battery . The bar turns to a warning colour at 20% or below when not charging Device memory Approximate memory in GB, as the browser reports it (browsers round this and cap it) CPU threads Number of logical processor threads available to the browser Battery information is available only in some browsers.

title: System status
heading: Memory
text: Reading What it shows --- --- JS heap Memory the page's scripts are using, and the limit, with a bar that turns to a warning colour above 85%. Chromium-based browsers only Storage Space the site uses in your browser's storage, out of the space allowed, with a percentage. The bar turns to a warning colour above 90% Caches Number of caches the site has stored, for example for offline use

title: System status
heading: Display
text: Reading What it shows --- --- Resolution Your screen's size in CSS pixels, such as 1920×1080 Viewport The browser window's inner size in CSS pixels Pixel ratio Device pixels per CSS pixel, such as 2× on a high-density screen Color Colour depth in bits, such as 24-bit , and the gamut: P3 gamut for a wide-gamut display, otherwise sRGB gamut

title: System status
heading: Runtime
text: Reading What it shows --- --- Frame rate Frames drawn in the last second, with a sparkline of the last 48 seconds Page load Seconds the page took to finish loading Service worker Active if the site's offline helper is controlling the page, Registered if your browser supports one but it is not controlling this page, Unsupported otherwise App mode Installed app if you opened the site as an installed app, otherwise Browser tab Language Your browser's preferred language, such as en-GB Time zone Your device's time zone, such as Europe/London Cookies Enabled or Blocked The frame rate is measured only while the Status Kit is open, and measuring stops when you close it. The figure usually matches your display's refresh rate, for example about 60 on a 60 Hz screen, and drops when the page is busy.

title: System status
heading: Using the readings for a bug report
text: When you report a problem, the Runtime and Display tabs give most of what support needs: browser language, time zone, app mode, screen and window size, pixel ratio and gamut. Copy them by hand; the kit does not send them anywhere. See [Help](../../../../help/README.md) for how to contact support.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
text: For problems shared by every kit, see [Troubleshooting kits](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: Many readings show a dash (—)
text: Why: Your browser does not provide that information. Network speed, latency and data saver, battery, JS heap and device memory are available only in some browsers, mostly Chromium-based ones. What to do: Nothing is wrong. Try another browser if you need those readings.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: The Status Kit closes when I open another kit
text: Why: The Status Kit always closes when another kit opens, even with Focus mode on. What to do: Reopen it after using the other kit. Focus mode still reopens it on each new page.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: A scan takes a long time
text: Why: The kit fetches every page in the section to read its title. A broad path such as /tool/ or /library/ means many pages. What to do: Scan a narrower path, such as /library/blog/ . The running count shows how far the scan has got.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: "No pages found"
text: Why: No page's address starts with what you typed. Paths are matched from the start, and must be paths on auricartisan.com. What to do: Start with a slash and a top-level folder, such as /tool/ , /library/ , /company/ or /legal/ .

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: "Couldn’t complete the scan"
text: Why: The site map could not be read, usually because the connection dropped. What to do: Check your connection and select Scan again.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: A page shows Beta although it looks finished
text: Why: Pages take the site's overall Beta status unless the site has given them their own. What to do: Nothing; the status is the site's own assessment. See [Check a page's status](check-page-status.md).

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + K opens a different search
text: Why: Ctrl + K opens the site-wide search, even while the Status Kit is open. What to do: Press / to put the cursor in the path box or in Search pages... .

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: The frame rate looks low
text: Why: The page is doing heavy work, your device is busy, or power saving is limiting it. What to do: Close other heavy tabs or plug in your device, and watch the sparkline for changes.

title: Status Kit troubleshooting
heading: Storage is nearly full
text: Why: The Storage bar turns to a warning colour above 90% of the space your browser allows the site. Saved library items, notes and cached files all use it. What to do: Export and delete library items you no longer need in the [Library Kit](../../library-kit/README.md), or clear cached site data in your browser.

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Can I scan another website?
text: No. The scanner lists pages of auricartisan.com only. If you paste another site's address, only its path is used, and it is looked up on auricartisan.com. To check other websites, use the [URL Analyzer](../../../tools/accessibility-and-vision/analyzer/README.md).

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Does the Status Kit send my device details anywhere?
text: No. The readings are taken in your browser and shown only to you. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Is the Speed reading a speed test?
text: No. It is your browser's rough estimate of your connection, not a measurement.

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Why is there no keyboard shortcut?
text: The Status Kit has none. Open it from Page utilities Status .

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Does P3 gamut mean my screen is colour-accurate?
text: No. It means your browser reports that the display can show roughly the P3 range of colours. It says nothing about calibration.

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: Can I export a scan?
text: No. Scan results stay in the panel. Your last eight scan paths are remembered under Recent scans .

title: Status Kit FAQ
heading: What counts as an issue?
text: Pages whose status is Alpha , Deprecated or Archived .
