title: Status Kit glossary
text: Page status — A label that says how finished a page is, such as Beta or Stable . Site status — The status of the site as a whole, shown in the Menu Kit. Pages without their own status share it. Scan — A listing of every page whose address starts with a given path, with each page's status. Path — The part of an address after the domain, such as /library/blog/ . Site map — The site's published list of its pages, which the scanner reads. Issues — Pages with the Alpha, Deprecated or Archived status. Target page — In a scan, the page whose address matches your path exactly. Effective connection type — The browser's classification of your connection speed, such as 4G. Round-trip time (latency) — How long a message takes to reach a server and come back, in milliseconds. JS heap — Memory used by the page's scripts. Device pixel ratio — How many physical screen pixels make up one CSS pixel. 2× is typical of high-density screens. CSS pixel — The unit web pages are laid out in. It may be several physical pixels. Colour gamut — The range of colours a display can show. sRGB is the standard range; P3 is wider. Colour depth — The number of bits used per pixel to store colour, such as 24-bit. Frame rate — How many times per second the page is redrawn. Service worker — A background script that lets the site work offline and load faster. Installed app — The site opened as an app installed from the browser, rather than in a tab.

title: Status Kit limits
heading: Page statuses
text: - Statuses are the site's own labels, set centrally. They are not measured from the page. - A page without its own entry takes the status of its folder, or of the whole site ( Beta ). - The kit does not explain why a page has a given status.

title: Status Kit limits
heading: Scans
text: - Scans cover pages of auricartisan.com only, taken from the site map. - The home page and individual colour pages under /color/ are never listed. - Titles come from fetching each page, so a scan of a large section makes many requests and takes longer. - Categories come from the Menu Kit where a page is listed there, and are otherwise guessed from words in the address, so a page can land in Other or in a category that does not quite fit. - Results are not saved; only your last eight scan paths are remembered.

title: Status Kit limits
heading: System readings
text: - Readings are what your browser chooses to report. Browsers round, cap or withhold some values to protect privacy, so the same device can show different figures in different browsers. - Speed and Latency are browser estimates, not a speed test. - Device memory is approximate and capped by the browser. - Storage shows the space the site uses against the space your browser allows it, which is not your disk's free space. - Color reports whether the display can show roughly the P3 range. It is not a calibration or a measurement of colour accuracy. - Resolution and Viewport are in CSS pixels; multiply by Pixel ratio for physical pixels. - Frame rate counts redraws in the last second while the kit is open. It is an indicator, not a benchmark. - Page load is the time the page took to finish loading on this visit.

title: Status Kit privacy
heading: Read from your browser, shown only to you
text: The System status panel reads your connection estimate, battery, device memory, processor threads, memory use, storage use, cache count, screen and window size, pixel ratio, colour depth and gamut, frame rate, page load time, service worker state, app mode, language, time zone and cookie setting. These readings are displayed in the panel and not stored or sent anywhere. They stop updating when you close the kit.

title: Status Kit privacy
heading: Kept in your browser
text: What Why --- --- Your last 8 scans: the path, target page title and status, page count and time For Recent scans Which result categories you collapsed To keep them collapsed Position, expanded size, Focus mode and theme Shared kit preferences

title: Update Kit
text: The Update Kit keeps the copy of Auric Artisan in your browser up to date. Browsers and the site's offline support keep copies of the site's files so pages load quickly and work offline. After a new release, those copies can be out of date. The Update Kit notices when a newer release is out and lets you refresh everything in one step. It has no panel. You meet it in two places: an Update available notice that appears at the top of the page when a new release is detected, and the Update website command in the site's right-click menu, also available as Ctrl + Shift + U . Updating clears the site's cached files, re-downloads the files the current page uses, and reloads the page. Your saved library items, notes, settings and account are not touched.

title: Update Kit
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone who sees the Update available notice. - Anyone whose page looks broken or out of date after a release. - People who use the site offline or as an installed app, whose cached copy is used most.

title: Update Kit
heading: Where to find it
text: - The notice appears by itself at the top of any page of https://auricartisan.com when an update is available. - Right-click anywhere on a page (outside text boxes) and choose Update website . - Press Ctrl + Shift + U on any page.

title: Update Kit
heading: Quick start
text: 1. When Update available appears at the top of the page, read the version it names, such as Update available v0.9.11 . 2. Save any work in progress in the page you are on. 3. Select Update now . 4. The page reloads on the new release. Or, at any time: 1. Press Ctrl + Shift + U . 2. A message reads Checking for updates… , then the site refreshes its files and reloads the page.

title: Update Kit
heading: What you can do
text: - See when a new release of the site is available, and which version. - Update to it with one button, or put the notice away with x and update later. - Force a refresh of the site's cached files at any time, from the right-click menu or the keyboard.

title: Getting started with the Update Kit
Getting started with the Update Kit
heading: When the site checks
text: Each time a page loads, the site waits until the page is ready and then checks which release is the newest. This takes a moment and does not slow the page. - On your first visit, the site simply notes the current release. You see nothing. - On later visits, if a newer release has come out since you last updated, the Update available notice appears. - If the check cannot reach the release information, for example offline, nothing is shown.

title: Getting started with the Update Kit
heading: The notice
text: The notice appears centred at the top of the page (across the top on a phone). It shows: - Update available and the version, for example Update available v0.9.11 ; - a line such as New update found: 0.9.11 ; - an Update now button; - a small x button labelled Hide update notice . Select Update now to update. Select x to put the notice away; it comes back on your next page load until you update.

title: Getting started with the Update Kit
heading: The command
text: You can update at any time, even when no notice is showing: - Right-click anywhere on the page (not in a text box) and choose Update website . The menu shows the shortcut next to it, Ctrl+⇧+U . - Or press Ctrl + Shift + U . When an update is available, the right-click menu shows the same entry as Update available with the version and Ready , also at the top of the menu under Website update . The right-click menu itself is described in [Site features](../../../site-features/README.md).

title: Getting started with the Update Kit
heading: Your first update
text: 1. Save anything you are working on in the current page. 2. Press Ctrl + Shift + U . 3. Messages read Checking for updates… and Updating website... , then Update ready. Reloading... . 4. The page reloads. You are now on the newest release, and the notice will not appear again until the next one.

title: Getting started with the Update Kit
heading: Next steps
text: - [Update the website](update-the-website.md) — what each step does - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

title: Update the website
heading: Start an update
text: Use any of: - Update now on the Update available notice; - Update website (or Update available ) in the right-click menu; - Ctrl + Shift + U . The command always refreshes, even if you are already on the newest release. In that case the notice may show briefly with the line Refreshing website cache... .

title: Update the website
heading: What happens
text: 1. Check. The site reads its newest release number. When run from the right-click menu or the keyboard, the message Checking for updates… appears. 2. Clear cached files. The site deletes the copies of its files that your browser keeps for this site (the caches used for speed and offline use). The message Updating website... appears. 3. Refresh the offline helper. The site asks its service worker, the background part that makes offline use possible, to check for a new version of itself. 4. Re-download current files. The files the current page uses (its scripts, styles, images and data, up to 180 files) are downloaded again, bypassing the browser's cache. 5. Record the version. The site notes that you are now on the newest release. 6. Reload. The message Update ready. Reloading... appears and the page reloads. For a moment the address carries ?auric-update= and the version; it is removed once the page has loaded. If something goes wrong, the message reads Update failed. Try again. and the right-click entry changes to Retry update .

title: Update the website
heading: What is not affected
text: - Your library items, notes, calculator history and kit preferences. - Your site settings and theme. - Whether you are signed in. These are kept in your browser's storage, which the update does not clear.

title: Update the website
heading: What to expect afterwards
text: - The page you were on reloads with the new release. Unsaved work in that page's tools is lost, so save first. - Other pages refresh their files as you visit them. - Offline copies of pages are rebuilt as you browse, so if you rely on offline use, visit the pages you need again while online. - The Update available notice stays away until the next release.

title: Update the website
heading: Put the notice away without updating
text: Select x ( Hide update notice ). You can keep working on the old release. The notice returns on the next page load, and the right-click menu keeps showing Update available until you update.

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: The notice keeps coming back
text: Why: x only hides the notice for the current page. It returns on every page load until you update. What to do: Select Update now .

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: "Update failed. Try again."
text: Why: The update could not finish, usually because the connection dropped while files were re-downloading, or the browser refused access to its storage. What to do: Check your connection and run Update website again. If it keeps failing, allow site storage for auricartisan.com in your browser settings.

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: The page still looks old after updating
text: Why: Some pages you have not visited since the update still use older cached files until you open them, and some browsers keep their own short-term copies. What to do: Open the page and run Update website there, or reload it with your browser's hard-reload shortcut.

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: No notice appears, but I know there is a new release
text: Why: The notice appears only when the release number has changed since you last updated in this browser. On your first visit the site records the current release silently. If the release information cannot be reached, nothing is shown. What to do: Run Update website from the right-click menu or with Ctrl + Shift + U ; it refreshes regardless.

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: Ctrl + Shift + U does nothing, or types a character
text: Why: Some systems use Ctrl + Shift + U to enter special characters, and take the key press first. What to do: Use the right-click menu's Update website instead.

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: The right-click menu does not show Update website
text: Why: You may have switched the site's right-click menu off in favour of the browser's, or you are on a shared public portfolio page, where the entry is not offered. What to do: Hold Shift while right-clicking to get the site's menu when the browser's menu is set as default, or use Ctrl + Shift + U . See [Site features](../../../site-features/README.md).

title: Update Kit troubleshooting
heading: I lost work when the page reloaded
text: Why: Updating reloads the page, which discards unsaved work in the page's tools. What to do: Save to the library, or export, before updating. Items already saved are not affected by the update.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Why does a website need updating?
text: Your browser, and the site's offline support, keep copies of the site's files so pages load fast and work offline. After a release, those copies can be older than the site. Updating replaces them.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Will updating delete my saved work?
text: No. Library items, notes, calculator history, settings and your sign-in are kept. Only unsaved work in the page you are on is lost when it reloads.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Is the Update Kit a panel I can open?
text: No. It is the notice and the Update website command. There is no launcher for it in the page utilities bar.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: How do I know which release I am on?
text: The notice names the new version. The site's release history is at https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Does updating need a connection?
text: Yes. Files are re-downloaded from auricartisan.com.

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Should I update the installed app the same way?
text: Yes. The installed app is the same site, so the notice and the command work there too. See [Download and offline use](../../../download-and-offline/README.md).

title: Update Kit FAQ
heading: Does the Update Kit update my browser extension or VS Code extensions?
text: No. It only refreshes the website in your browser. Extensions update through their own stores.

title: Update Kit glossary
text: Release — A published version of the website, such as v0.9.11, listed in the changelog. Update notice — The Update available message at the top of the page. Cache — Copies of the site's files kept by your browser so pages load faster and work offline. Service worker — A background script from the site that manages its offline copies. Hard reload — A browser reload that ignores cached copies of the page's files. Installed app — The site installed from your browser and opened in its own window. Site storage — Data the site keeps in your browser, such as library items and settings. An update does not clear it.

title: Update Kit limits
heading: When the notice appears
text: - The site compares the newest release it can find with the release recorded the last time you updated in this browser. The notice appears only when they differ. - On a first visit the current release is recorded silently, so you will not see a notice until the following release. - If the release information cannot be reached, for example offline, no notice is shown. - The check runs once per page load.

title: Update Kit limits
heading: What an update refreshes
text: - All of the site's caches in your browser are deleted. - The service worker is asked to update itself; it is not removed. - Up to 180 files used by the current page are downloaded again. Files used only by other pages refresh when you visit those pages. - The page reloads.

title: Update Kit limits
heading: What it does not do
text: - It does not clear site storage: library items, notes, calculator history, settings and your sign-in are kept. - It does not update browser extensions, VS Code extensions or the browser itself. - It does not change anything on the server; it only refreshes your browser's copy of the site. - It cannot bypass a network or company proxy that serves old copies.

title: Update Kit privacy
heading: Stored in your browser
text: The release number you last updated to, so the site can tell when a newer one is out. Nothing else.

title: Update Kit privacy
heading: Fetched from auricartisan.com
text: - On each page load: the site's release information, to find the newest release number. - When you update: the files the current page uses, downloaded again. These are ordinary requests to auricartisan.com. No information about you or your device is sent by the Update Kit.

title: Update Kit privacy
heading: What an update deletes
text: The site's cached files in your browser. Your saved library, notes, settings and sign-in are not deleted.

title: Kits glossary
text: Kit — A floating panel that opens over any page of the site and does one job, such as calculating or finding a page. Page utilities bar — The launcher bar in the bottom-left corner of every page. Closed, it is a single round button labelled Page utilities ; open, it shows one labelled launcher per kit. Launcher — The labelled button in the page utilities bar that opens and closes one kit, for example Feature or Library . Hub — The round button that opens and closes the page utilities bar. While the bar is open it reads Close . Panel — The floating window a kit opens in. Title bar — The strip across the top of a kit panel, holding the kit's name and its controls. You drag it to move the panel. Modeless — Describes a panel that does not block the page behind it. You can keep using the page while a modeless kit is open. Focus mode — A title-bar setting that keeps a kit open when you open another kit and opens it again on the next page you load. In the Library Kit it is called Keep open . Expanded — The larger size a kit takes after you select Resize . Minimised — A kit shrunk to its title bar (or, for the Feature Kit, to a small round icon). Kit theme — A light or dark setting that belongs to one kit and can differ from the site theme. Accent colour — The highlight colour chosen in the site settings panel. It colours the gold details in the kits. Tool visibility mode — The site-wide setting chosen in the Advanced Kit: Basic , Advanced , Everything or Custom . It decides which tools the site shows. Page status — A label such as Beta , Stable or Experimental that says how finished a page is. The Status Kit shows it. Universal Library — Everything you have saved from the site's tools, kept in your browser and shown in the Library Kit. Saved item — One entry in the Universal Library, such as a palette, a gradient, a report or an image. Update notice — The Update available message the Update Kit shows at the top of the page when a newer release of the site is out.

title: Library
text: The Auric Artisan library is the reading and reference side of the site. It brings together six searchable colour libraries, the catalogue of every tool, a course of articles on colour science and accessibility, a user guide for each tool, the blog and the changelog. The colour libraries are large, browsable collections of generated colour data: 8,192 measured colours, five million palettes, 8,192 gradients, 8,192 colour harmonies, 8,192 shade scales and five million foreground and background pairs scored for contrast. Each one lets you search, filter, inspect and copy or export values for use in your own work. The rest of the library is for learning and finding your way: Collections lists every tool, Learn teaches the ideas behind them with interactive labs, Documentation explains each tool step by step, and the blog and changelog record what has been built and when.

heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers and front-end developers who need ready-made, measured colour values. - Accessibility specialists who need contrast-checked colour pairs. - Students and colour enthusiasts learning colour science. - Anyone who wants to find the right Auric Artisan tool, or learn how to use it.

title: All posts
heading: What Shipped Since April
text: - Date: 27 July 2026 - Category: Product - Link: https://auricartisan.com/library/blog/articles/2026-07-27-what-shipped-since-april An honest account of what came out of the April roadmap by late July 2026, with the reasoning, and a list of what was not yet done: - One browser extension instead of four. The colour, accessibility, developer-tools and suite extensions were merged into one product, which gained a side panel, pickers that work on any page, a custom right-click menu and a searchable settings view. Its accessibility checks grew from 20 to 97. - The Analyzer's accessibility checks were rebuilt on a 112-rule engine covering ARIA 1.2, accessible names and APCA contrast, reporting an accessibility tree, a screen-reader transcript, colour-vision simulation and a VPAT export. The rules load only when you open the tab. - Payments went live for one-time purchases, with prices and what you receive both decided by the site rather than the browser. First-party, consent-based analytics arrived at the same time. - The VS Code extension reached 0.13.2 , joining the plugins for Figma, Sketch, Penpot, Raycast and Alfred — all free. - Not yet done (as of the post): token top-ups were not on sale; accounts were single-user; cloud sync covered account settings but not saved palettes and projects; there was no single sign-on, white-label embedding or uptime guarantee.

title: All posts
heading: Auric Artisan Roadmap — Next Few Months
text: - Date: 21 April 2026 - Category: Roadmap - Link: https://auricartisan.com/library/blog/articles/2026-04-21-auric-artisan-roadmap A phased plan for the following months, summarised as Organize → Explain → Simplify → Optimize → Expand : a clearer start menu with essentials first and advanced tools hidden; a Status Kit showing each tool's stability; a casual versus advanced mode with plain-language tooltips; faster, non-freezing heavy tools; and more customisation, better split-screen work and documentation. It closes with a month-by-month plan for May, June and July 2026. The post now opens with an update noting that much of the roadmap has shipped, with a link to the changelog.

title: Changelog
text: The changelog is the versioned record of Auric Artisan's releases: "Every release, what was in it, and what it touched." It lists eleven entries, from v0.9.0 on 31 December 2025 to v0.9.11 on 12 August 2026, as a timeline, newest first. Each entry opens in place to show what changed and which parts of the platform it touched, with a link to the full release note. Its search reads the changes themselves, not just the headings, so you can ask it questions such as "when did overage arrive?" and it will find the release and highlight the words where they appear.

title: Changelog
heading: Who it is for
text: - Users who want to know what is new, or when something changed. - Teams who need to check when a feature, plan change or fix arrived.

title: Changelog
heading: Where to find it
text: - The changelog: https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/ - From the site header: Learn menu › Changelog ("Releases & improvements"). - RSS feed: https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/rss.xml - A single release: add its version after , for example https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/ 0.9.10

title: Changelog
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/. The newest release is already open. 2. Type a word into the search box, for example recorder . Matching releases stay, with the matches marked. 3. Select Releases or Patches to show only that kind of entry. 4. Select a release's header to open or close it. 5. Under Touched , select a tag to see every release that touched the same part. 6. Select Read the full release note for the complete write-up.

title: Changelog
heading: What you can do
text: - Read every release, newest first, with its version, type and date. - Search every change and see matches highlighted. - Filter by type and by the part of the platform touched. - Open and close releases one by one, or all at once. - Link straight to a release by its version. - Follow new releases by RSS.

title: Getting started
heading: The page
text: Open https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/. - Changelog , with the line "Every release, what was in it, and what it touched. The search reads the changes themselves, not just the headings — so 'when did overage arrive?' is a question this page can answer." - A facts line: 11 releases · v0.9.0 → v0.9.11 · 12 August 2026 — the latest . - A search box, Search every change — overage, recorder, dark mode… , with a clear button. - Type buttons: All , Releases , Patches . - A count, for example 11 of 11 releases , and Expand all . - The timeline: one entry per release, newest first. The newest is open when the page loads.

title: Getting started
heading: A release entry
text: The header shows the version (for example v0.9.10 ), a type badge ( release , patch , or another label such as Changelog ) and the date. Under it, a summary sentence — shortened while the entry is closed, in full when it is open. Select the header to open or close the entry. Open, it shows: Part What it contains --- --- What changed The list of changes. Notes Extra notes, where the release has them. Touched Tags for the parts of the platform the release touched, such as analyzer or pricing . Read the full release note A link to the release's own page.

title: Getting started
heading: Search
text: 1. Type a word or phrase. The timeline keeps only releases whose title, summary, changes or notes contain it. 2. Matches are marked where they appear. 3. Select the × in the box to clear the search.

title: Getting started
heading: Filter by type
text: - Releases — feature releases. - Patches — fix and clean-up releases. - All — everything.

title: Getting started
heading: Filter by what was touched
text: In an open release, select a tag under Touched . The timeline shows only releases that touched the same part, and a button appears beside the count, touching and the tag's name. Select that button, or the tag again, to stop filtering. Clear filters appears whenever a search, type or tag is active; it resets all three. If nothing matches, the page says No release matches that. with its own Clear filters button.

title: Getting started
heading: Open everything
text: Expand all opens every release currently shown; it then reads Collapse all .

title: Getting started
heading: Link to a release
text: Add and the version to the page's address, for example https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/ 0.9.11 (a leading v also works). The page opens that release and scrolls to it.

title: Getting started
heading: Follow releases
text: Add https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/rss.xml to your news reader. If the page cannot load the timeline, it says The changelog could not be loaded. with a link, Read it as a feed instead , and a plain list of All releases still links to every release note.

title: Release summaries
text: A plain-language summary of each release listed in the changelog, newest first. Each heading gives the version and date as published. For the full notes, open the release on https://auricartisan.com/library/changelog/.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.11 — 12 August 2026 (release)
text: The REST API became a metered product, and the site gained a recorder. - API credits. API calls are now measured in credits: one credit is one standard request, and heavier endpoints cost more. Specialist includes 1,000,000 credits a month and Industrial Pro 10,000,000, refreshing each billing month. Subscriptions to Industrial Pro started before 12 August 2026 keep their previous allowance. - Overage, only if you want it. Extra usage is opt-in and prepaid at $1.00 (₹85) per 100,000 credits, so you are never invoiced after the fact. You can set a monthly spend cap, and a hard ceiling of ten times your included allowance always applies. - Top-ups. You can buy credit packs from Dashboard → API keys → Add credits . Purchased credits do not expire at the end of the period. - API console on the dashboard's API Keys tab: burn-down, projection, usage chart, spend by endpoint, credit balance, spend cap, overage switch and a live call feed. - New API areas: colour science (63 colour spaces, colour difference, colour temperature), design tokens (ten export targets), a catalogue, and live usage. - API access is now for Specialist and above; other plans get a clear upgrade message. - Recorder. A site-wide screen, tab, region and canvas recorder, exporting video, animated GIF, PNG frames and posters, with trimming. - Tokens and credits are separate: tokens pay for server-side tool work, credits pay for API calls, and neither pays for the other.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.10 — 27 July 2026 (release)
text: - One browser extension. The browser extensions were combined into one redesigned product, Auric Studio, with a responsive sidebar, a Side Panel, pickers that upgrade colour inputs on any page, a custom right-click menu and a settings search. - Analyzer accessibility. The Analyzer's A11y+ tab was rebuilt on a 112-rule accessibility engine, with an accessibility tree, a screen-reader transcript, colour vision simulation and a VPAT export. The rules load only when you open the tab. - Analytics that are first-party, consent-based and free of third-party trackers. - Payments. One-time checkout went live. - VS Code extension 0.13.2 , with colour and accessibility updates.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.9 — 5 June 2026 (release)
text: - New libraries: Font, Palette, Accessibility, Shade, Harmony, Color, Gradient and Icon libraries. - Design System Generator added. - Documentation, Learn and Blog content added. - Beta replaced the "In Development" label across the site. - Installable app (PWA) , user settings , guide content , the UX Kit , security improvements and better control of basic and advanced tools. - Faster, more consistent interface: colour picker and rendering improvements, keyboard shortcut improvements, and fixes to navigation, lag and library behaviour.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.8 — 2 May 2026 (patch)
text: - Clearer home page summary and a new logo. - Vision Simulation and the Color Science Model moved into the unified panel-based simulation system. - News, Libraries and Announcement pages removed to simplify the site. - Fixes to the welcome screen, search, and interface consistency; improved Analyzer. - Legal pages restructured. - The Advanced Kit was improved and control of tool complexity added.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.75 — 19 April 2026 (changelog entry)
text: - Split-screen fixes: address, refresh, resizing, embedded pages and closing windows. - Interface fixes across colour lists, colour overview, conversion tools, contrast panels and the CIE graph. - More consistent search results. - Ishihara plate generator and the Material Lighting lab added. - Accessibility fixes: ARIA, keyboard focus and screen-reader announcements. - Fixes to the Menu Kit and Status Kit, illuminant handling in light and dark modes, the Color Formulation Lab, the converter and the Palette Visualizer lab.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.7 — 15 April 2026 (release)
text: "Deployment — Site marked 'In Development'". The website went live marked as in development, with reliability fixes to delivery, the server and the Analyzer (which now handles malformed pages more gracefully). The ASCII Art Generator and the Ishihara Plate Generator were promoted to beta.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.6 — 13 April 2026 (release)
text: "Vision Simulation & Color Model Lab Advancement". More accurate protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulations; a comparison view for RGB, LAB, OKLab and experimental colour models; side-by-side analysis and sample export in the lab; simulations up to 35% faster on large scenes.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.6 — 8 April 2026 (release)
text: "System Integration & Validation". The engine, tools, perception systems and lab were connected into one validated workflow, for fewer failures between parts of the platform.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.5 — 24 March 2026 (release)
text: "Spectral & Experimental Layer". Spectral approximation for higher-fidelity colour, experimental interfaces for trying new colour models, and documentation with examples for spectral experiments. Spectral features were marked experimental.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.4 — 20 February 2026 (patch)
text: "Tool Accuracy Refinement". Smoother gradients using LAB and OKLab interpolation, palette generation that clashes less and is more accessible, and fixes to rounding and edge cases in colour conversion.

title: Release summaries
heading: v0.9.0 — 31 December 2025 (release)
text: "Auric Artisan Pre-Release Stabilization". The platform reached a near-complete state with its engine, tools, rendering and research modules unified, and was tuned for performance and memory ahead of public release.

title: Changelog FAQ
heading: Why are there two v0.9.6 entries?
text: Two entries share version 0.9.6: "System Integration & Validation" (8 April 2026) and "Vision Simulation & Color Model Lab Advancement" (13 April 2026). A link to 0.9.6 opens the newer one.

title: Changelog FAQ
heading: What is the difference between a release and a patch?
text: Releases add features; patches fix and tidy. One entry, v0.9.75, is labelled Changelog rather than either.

title: Changelog FAQ
heading: Where do I report a problem with a release?
text: Release notes ask for steps to reproduce, your browser and operating system, the page or tool affected, and screenshots — and, for API problems, the x-request-id header from the response. See [Help](../../../../help/README.md) for how to get in touch.

title: Changelog FAQ
heading: Is every change listed?
text: The changelog lists the notable changes in each release. Smaller changes between releases, and improvements to individual tools, may appear only on the tool's own pages and guides.

title: Collections
text: Collections is the catalogue of Auric Artisan's tools. It lists every tool, engine and generator on the site — from the URL Analyzer and Vision Simulation to the Font Library, LUT Lab and the Portfolio Builder — as a grid of cards you can search, filter, sort and pin. Each card says what the tool does in one sentence and opens the tool with one click. The page learns a little from how you use it. Tools you pin stay easy to reach, tools you open often can rise to the top of the Most used order, and the Recommended order leans on both. All of this is remembered only in the browser you are using; nothing about your pins or opens is sent to an account. Every tool in the collection is free to use on every plan. The lower part of the page shows the plans, which add conveniences such as cloud sync and watermark-free exports rather than unlocking tools.

title: Collections
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone new to Auric Artisan who wants to see everything the site offers. - Regular users who want a fast way back to the tools they use most. - Designers, developers, accessibility specialists and colour-science students who want to browse by category (Accessibility, Colorimetry, Gamut & Rendering, Perception, Spectral and more) or by topic.

title: Collections
heading: Where to find it
text: - Address: https://auricartisan.com/collections/ - From any page: open the Tools menu in the site header and choose All Tools . - It works in any modern browser. You do not need an account.

title: Collections
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/collections/. 2. Look at Start here for a short list of three featured tools, or scroll to All tools . 3. Type a word such as gradient or contrast into the Search tools... box above the grid. 4. Tick a box under Category or Topics in the Filter and sort panel to narrow the list. 5. Select the pin button on a card to pin that tool; it now appears under the Pinned category. 6. Right-click a card to open the card menu: switch View , Density , Columns or Sort , or copy the tool's link. 7. Select a card to open the tool. Note: By default the site shows its Basic tool set, so Collections starts with the beginner-friendly tools. To see all 30 tools, choose Everything in the Advanced Kit. See [Show basic or advanced tools](docs/show-basic-or-advanced-tools.md).

title: Collections
heading: What you can do
text: - Browse all 30 tools as cards, in a grid or a list. - Search by name, description, category, address or topic. - Filter by one or more categories and topics at once. - Sort by title, category, recommendation, how often you use a tool, pinned first, or most detailed description. - Pin tools so they stay together under Pinned and lead the Start here shortlist. - Right-click a card for quick actions and layout settings (view, density, columns, sort, theme, reading mode). - Choose whether the catalogue shows basic tools, advanced tools, everything, or your own custom set. - Compare the plans and switch prices between monthly and annual billing, and between US dollars and Indian rupees.

title: Getting started with Collections
text: Collections is the page that lists every Auric Artisan tool. This guide walks through the page from top to bottom and ends with you opening a tool you found by search.

title: Getting started with Collections
heading: Open the page
text: Go to https://auricartisan.com/collections/, or open the Tools menu in the site header and choose All Tools . You do not need to sign in.

title: Getting started with Collections
heading: The screen, top to bottom
text: The page opens with the heading "All Auric Artisan tools, engines & generators in one place." Under it, three counters show: - Tools — how many tools the catalogue is currently showing. - Categories — how many different categories those tools belong to. - Topics — how many different topic tags those tools carry. The counters follow your tool-visibility setting (see [Show basic or advanced tools](show-basic-or-advanced-tools.md)), so they can be lower than the full catalogue of 30 tools. Beside the heading, three quick links lead to Tools (this page), Learn (the Learn library) and Pricing (the plans page). Start here is a shortlist of three featured tools shown as large cards in a slider. Each card shows the tool's name, a one-line description and its category. - The slider moves on by itself, one card at a time. A thin bar along the bottom fills up to show when the next card is due. - It pauses while your pointer is over it or while it has keyboard focus. - Use the previous and next arrow buttons, the dots under the slider, or the Left and Right arrow keys (with the slider focused) to move between cards. A counter such as 01 / 03 shows where you are. - If your system asks for reduced motion, the slider does not move by itself. Tools you pin come first in this shortlist. All tools is the full catalogue. On a wide screen it has two columns: - On the left, the Filter and sort panel with three sections you can open and close: Sort by , Category and Topics . On wide screens this panel stays in view as you scroll. - On the right, the results: a Search tools... box, a Grid / List switch, and the cards. On a narrower screen (about 900 pixels wide or less), the filter panel sits above the results instead of beside them. A line above the grid reports the count, for example 14 tools , or 3 of 14 tools when a search or filter is active. Each card shows: - the tool's artwork; - its category above the name, for example Colorimetry ; - the tool's name and a one-sentence description; - the line Free to use at the foot, because every tool is free on every plan; - a pin button in the corner. Hover over a card to see a tooltip with more detail: the category, the Mode (Basic, Advanced or Both), the tool's address on the site, and its topic tags. Further down the page: - Featured Highlights — two short notes on key capabilities (Accessibility & Analysis, Creative Generation). - The plans section, headed "Every tool here is free. Upgrade for superpowers." It shows the four plans with a Monthly / Annual switch and a USD $ / INR ₹ currency switch. See [Account and billing](../../../account-and-billing/README.md) for what each plan includes. - A closing banner, Explore All Collections , with links back to this page and to the full pricing page.

title: Getting started with Collections
heading: Your first search
text: 1. Scroll to All tools . 2. Select the Search tools... box and type palette . 3. Watch the grid update as you type. The count above the grid changes to show how many tools match. 4. Under Category in the Filter and sort panel, tick Generators . 5. The grid now shows only generator tools whose details mention "palette". 6. Select a card, for example Basic Tools , to open it. You now have the tool open. Use your browser's back button to return to Collections. Your pins and your grid or list choice are remembered in this browser for next time.

title: Getting started with Collections
heading: Next steps
text: - Learn every way to narrow the list in [Browse, search and filter](browse-search-and-filter.md). - Keep favourite tools at hand with [Pin tools and use recommendations](pin-and-recommendations.md). - Try the right-click menu in [Use the card menu](card-menu.md).

title: Browse, search and filter
text: The All tools section of https://auricartisan.com/collections/ gives you four ways to narrow the catalogue: a search box, category filters, topic filters and a sort order. They work together, and the grid updates as soon as you change any of them.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Search
text: The search box sits above the grid and reads Search tools... . 1. Select the box and start typing. 2. The grid updates on every keystroke; you do not need to press Enter . 3. To clear the search, delete the text. How matching works: - Matching ignores upper and lower case. - Each word you type must appear somewhere in the tool's details. colour vision finds tools that mention both "colour" and "vision", in any order. - A word can match part of a longer word. grad finds "gradient" and "gradients". - The details searched are the tool's name, its one-line description, its category, its address on the site, and its topic tags. Tip: The catalogue uses both spellings in places — some descriptions say "colour" and some tags say "color". If a search finds less than you expect, try the other spelling. Search does not treat them as the same word.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Filter by category
text: Open Category in the Filter and sort panel. Each category is a tick box with the number of tools in it. The categories are: Accessibility , Color Science , Colorimetry , Design Systems , Gamut & Rendering , Generators , Iconography , Perception , Publish , Spectral , Typography and Utilities . A Pinned box appears at the top of the list as soon as you pin at least one tool (see [Pin tools and use recommendations](pin-and-recommendations.md)). Rules: - With no boxes ticked, every category is shown. - Tick one box to show only that category. - Tick several boxes to show tools in any of them. Ticking Generators and Utilities shows both groups together. - Untick a box to remove it again. Categories list only the tools your tool-visibility setting allows. If a category you expect is missing, see [Show basic or advanced tools](show-basic-or-advanced-tools.md).

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Filter by topic
text: Open Topics (it starts closed). Topics are the short tags each tool carries, such as palette , accessibility or hdr . The list shows up to 14 topics — the most common ones among the tools currently in view — each with a count. - With no topics ticked, all topics are allowed. - Tick one or more topics to show tools that carry any of them.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: How the filters combine
text: A tool is shown only when it passes all three checks at once: 1. its category is one of the ticked categories (or none are ticked), and 2. it carries one of the ticked topics (or none are ticked), and 3. every word in the search box appears in its details. The line above the grid shows the result, for example 4 of 14 tools . When nothing matches, the grid is replaced by No matching tools with the advice to try a shorter search, clear the topic chip, or switch the category back to all tools.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Sort the grid
text: Open Sort by and choose an order from the Sort list: Option Order --- --- Title A to Z Alphabetical by tool name. Category A to Z Alphabetical by category. Newest first Newest first by date. Tools carry no dates, so this keeps the catalogue's own order. Oldest first Oldest first by date. Tools carry no dates, so this also keeps the catalogue's own order. Recommended Tools most likely to be useful to you first (see [Pin tools and use recommendations](pin-and-recommendations.md)). Most used Tools you open most often, and most recently, first. Pinned first Your pinned tools first, then the rest. Most metadata Tools with the fullest descriptions and most tags first. You can also change the order from the right-click card menu (see [Use the card menu](card-menu.md)).

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Grid or list
text: The Grid and List buttons beside the search box switch the layout: - Grid shows cards side by side with large artwork. - List shows one tool per row with a smaller picture beside the text, which is easier to scan. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Loading more tools
text: The grid shows 12 tools at first. As you scroll to the bottom of the grid, the next 12 load automatically. A line under the grid says where you are, for example Showing 12 of 14 tools , and then All 14 tools shown . A thin bar fills up as more of the list comes into view. If automatic loading is not available in your browser, a Load 2 more tools button (the number changes) appears instead; select it to show the next batch.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Search and sort while scrolled down
text: Once you scroll past the search box and filters, a round search button appears on the right-hand side of the screen, towards the bottom. Select it (its label is "Search and sort tools") to open a small panel with: - a Search tools... box; - a Sort list; - Category and Topics sections with the same tick boxes as the main panel. Everything in this panel stays in step with the main controls. Press Escape , or select anywhere outside the panel, to close it. The button hides again when you scroll back up to the main controls.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Result
text: You see only the tools that match your search, ticked categories and ticked topics, in the order you chose, laid out as a grid or a list.

title: Use the card menu
text: Every card in the All tools grid has its own menu. It gathers the actions for that one tool together with the settings for the whole grid, so you can change the layout without scrolling back to the controls.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Open the menu
text: 1. Scroll to All tools on https://auricartisan.com/collections/. 2. Right-click any card. On a keyboard, move focus to a card and press the context-menu key or Shift + F10 . 3. The menu opens at the pointer. If there is not enough room, it moves so it stays on screen. The menu replaces the site's usual right-click menu while you are over a card. Right-click anywhere else on the page to get the site's usual menu (see [Site features](../../../site-features/README.md)). The top line of the menu shows the card's title. A small pin mark appears before the title when that tool is pinned.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Close the menu
text: Any of these closes it: - select anywhere outside the menu; - press Escape ; - scroll the page; - resize the window; - choose Open , New tab or Copy link . The layout settings ( View , Density , Columns , Sort ) keep the menu open so you can try several in a row.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Card
text: Four buttons act on the card you right-clicked: Button What it does --- --- Pin / Unpin Pins or unpins the tool, exactly like the pin button on the card. The button is highlighted while the tool is pinned. Open Opens the tool in the current tab. New tab Opens the tool in a new browser tab. Copy link Copies the tool's full web address to your clipboard.

title: Use the card menu
heading: View
text: - Grid — cards side by side with large artwork. - List — one tool per row, easier to scan. This is the same setting as the Grid and List buttons above the results, and it is remembered in this browser.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Density
text: - Cozy — the normal spacing between cards. - Compact — tighter spacing, so more cards fit on screen. Remembered in this browser for the Collections page.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Columns
text: - Auto — the grid decides how many columns fit your screen width. - 2 , 3 or 4 — forces that many columns at every screen width. Columns apply to the grid view; the list view always shows one tool per row. Your choice is remembered in this browser for the Collections page. Tip: On a phone, Auto is usually the right choice. Forcing 4 columns on a narrow screen makes each card very small.

title: Use the card menu
heading: Sort
text: A row of buttons repeats the page's sort orders. Each shows the first word of the order's name, with a second word added where two would look the same. Hover a button to see its full name. title: Use the card menu
heading: Result
text: From one right-click you can act on a single tool and reshape the whole grid, and the grid keeps your view, density and column choices the next time you visit in this browser.

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
text: Collections can put the tools that matter to you first. It uses two signals, both kept only in the browser you are using: - Pins — tools you have marked yourself. - Opens — how often, and how recently, you have opened each tool from the Collections page. From these the page builds three groupings: Pinned , Most used and Recommended .

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
heading: Pin a tool
text: 1. Find the tool's card in All tools . 2. Select the pin button in the card's corner. Its label reads "Pin" followed by the tool's name. 3. The button fills in to show the tool is pinned, and the card is marked as pinned. You can also right-click the card and choose Pin in the card menu (see [Use the card menu](card-menu.md)). To unpin, select the same button again (its label now reads "Unpin" and the tool's name), or choose Unpin in the card menu. - The Pinned category. A Pinned tick box appears at the top of Category in the Filter and sort panel, with a count. Tick it to see only your pinned tools. When you unpin your last tool, the box disappears and the filter switches itself off. - Pinned first. Choose Pinned first in the sort list to bring pinned tools to the top while keeping everything else below them. - Start here. The three-card Start here shortlist shows pinned tools before any others. Pin three tools and the shortlist becomes your own. - Recommended. Pinned tools get a strong boost in the Recommended order.

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
heading: Most used
text: Each time you open a tool by selecting its card on the Collections page — in All tools or in Start here — the page counts that open. Selecting the pin button does not count as an open. Choose Most used in the sort list to order tools by how much you use them. The order weighs both how many times you opened a tool and how recently: Last opened Weight given to each open --- --- Within the last day Highest Within 3 days High Within a week Medium Within 30 days Low Longer ago Lowest So a tool you opened five times this week can rank above one you opened ten times last year. Tools you have never opened from this page follow, in an order based on your pins, core subjects and description depth. Note: Only opens from the Collections page count. Visiting a tool from the header menu, a bookmark or a search result does not change Most used here.

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
heading: Recommended
text: Choose Recommended in the sort list for the order the page thinks is most useful to you. It adds up several things: - Your pins. A pinned tool gets a large boost. - Your opens. Tools you open often and recently rise, up to a limit, so one busy afternoon does not bury everything else. - Core subjects. Tools whose details mention central subjects on the site — among them accessibility, WCAG, APCA, contrast, gamut, HDR, ICC, tokens, performance and workflow — rise a little for each one. - Description depth. Tools with fuller descriptions and more tags rise slightly. With no pins and no history, Recommended relies on the last two signals only, so a first-time visitor sees a stable order. Your search words and ticked filters decide which tools are shown, not their order.

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
heading: Reset your pins and usage
text: There is no single reset button for pins and usage on the page. You can clear them in these ways: - Clear pins one by one. Tick Pinned under Category to list your pinned tools, then select each pin button to unpin it. - Clear everything the site remembers. Clear this site's data (sometimes called "cookies and site data") in your browser's settings. This removes your pins, your usage history and your layout choices on this page, along with other preferences the site keeps in your browser. The Reset button in the card menu does not remove pins or usage. It only returns the layout to its defaults: grid view, cozy density, automatic columns and the first sort order ( Title A to Z ). Important: The site's own settings panel also has a Reset all button, but that resets site preferences such as theme and text size. It does not clear your Collections pins or usage.

title: Pin tools and use recommendations
heading: Result
text: Your pinned tools are grouped under Pinned , lead the Start here shortlist and top the Pinned first order, and the Most used and Recommended orders reflect how you actually use the site in this browser.

title: Show basic or advanced tools
text: Auric Artisan has 30 tools. Some are everyday tools, such as the Image Picker and the Font Library; others are scientific tools, such as Illuminants, Tone Mapping and the Psychophysics Engine. The site lets you choose which of these you see, and Collections follows that choice.

title: Show basic or advanced tools
heading: Why you might see fewer than 30 tools
text: Every tool in the catalogue is labelled with a mode: - Basic — beginner-friendly, everyday tools. - Advanced — scientific, diagnostic and power-user tools. - Both — tools that belong to every set. The URL Analyzer and the Portfolio Builder are the two tools marked this way. The site-wide tool visibility setting decides which modes are shown. Until you choose otherwise, the site uses Basic , so a first visit to Collections shows the basic tools and the two tools marked Both . The hero counters, the category counts and the result count all reflect the tools in view, not the full catalogue. You can see any card's mode in its tooltip: hover over the card and read the Mode line.

title: Show basic or advanced tools
heading: Change the setting
text: The setting lives in the Advanced Kit , one of the site's floating kits. Its button carries the tooltip "Choose Basic, Advanced, or Everything tool visibility." 1. Open the Advanced Kit . 2. Under the tool-visibility choices, select Basic , Advanced , Everything or Custom . 3. For Custom , use Choose your tools to tick the tools you want. You can type in Filter tools… to find a tool, or use Enable all , Disable all and Reset . 4. Close the kit. Collections updates straight away: the grid, the counters, the category list and the Start here shortlist all redraw with the tools the new setting allows. You do not need to reload the page. The setting applies across the site, not only on Collections, and is remembered in this browser. For everything else the Advanced Kit can do, see the [Advanced Kit docs](../../../kits/advanced-kit/README.md).

title: Show basic or advanced tools
heading: Result
text: Collections shows exactly the set of tools you asked for: the basic set, the advanced set, all 30 tools, or your own custom selection.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
text: Each entry gives the symptom, the reason, and what to do.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: A tool I know exists is not in the grid
text: Why: The site's tool-visibility setting hides tools that do not match it. The default setting, Basic , shows 14 of the 30 tools; advanced tools such as Illuminants or LUT Lab are hidden. A Custom setting hides every tool you switched off. What to do: Open the Advanced Kit and choose Everything , or switch the tool back on in Custom . The grid updates at once. See [Show basic or advanced tools](show-basic-or-advanced-tools.md).

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: The grid is empty and says "No matching tools"
text: Why: Your search words, ticked categories and ticked topics together match nothing. Every search word must appear in a tool's details, and a tool must pass the category and topic filters as well. What to do: 1. Shorten the search, or try the other spelling ( color or colour ). 2. Untick all Topics . 3. Untick all Category boxes, including Pinned .

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: The grid is not in alphabetical order, although Sort shows "Title A to Z"
text: Why: When the page first opens, the grid is in the catalogue's own order. The Sort list shows its first option, Title A to Z , but that order has not been applied yet. What to do: Choose a different order and then Title A to Z again, or right-click a card and select Title under Sort . The card menu's Reset button also applies Title A to Z .

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: "Newest first" and "Oldest first" do not change anything
text: Why: Tools have no publication dates, so both orders keep the catalogue's own order. What to do: Use Title A to Z , Category A to Z , Recommended , Most used , Pinned first or Most metadata instead.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: My pins or usage history have gone
text: Why: Pins and opens are stored only in this browser. They are not saved to your account and do not follow you to another browser or device. They are lost if you clear this site's data, use a private window, or your browser clears storage automatically. What to do: Pin the tools again. To keep pins, avoid clearing site data for auricartisan.com and do not rely on private windows.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: "Most used" does not show a tool I use every day
text: Why: Only opens made by selecting a card on the Collections page count. Opening a tool from the header menu, a bookmark, a search result or a link does not. What to do: Open the tool from its Collections card, or pin it so it always appears under Pinned and at the top of Pinned first .

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: Right-clicking a card shows the site's normal menu, not the card menu
text: Why: The card menu loads a moment after the page. It also only answers right-clicks on cards inside All tools , not on the Start here slider or the rest of the page. Some privacy or performance settings can stop the page's extra features from loading. What to do: Wait for the page to finish loading and right-click a card in the All tools grid. If it still does not appear, reload the page.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: The Columns setting makes cards tiny, or seems to do nothing
text: Why: 2 , 3 and 4 force that many columns at every screen width, so on a phone the cards become narrow. Columns have no effect in list view, which always shows one tool per row. What to do: Choose Auto under Columns , or switch View to Grid to see the column change.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: The featured slider keeps moving while I read it
text: Why: Start here plays automatically. What to do: Move your pointer over the slider or give it keyboard focus to pause it. If you prefer no movement at all, turn on your system's reduced-motion setting; the slider then stays still.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: The page says "Unable to load tools."
text: Why: The page could not fetch the tool catalogue, usually because the network connection dropped or the page was loaded from an old offline copy. What to do: Check your connection and reload the page. Meanwhile, you can reach the tools from the site header's Tools menu.

title: Troubleshooting Collections
heading: Prices show in the wrong currency
text: Why: On your first visit the page chooses a currency for your region. What to do: Select USD $ or INR ₹ above the plans. Your choice is remembered.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: How many tools are there?
text: Thirty. With the default Basic tool-visibility setting, Collections shows 14 of them; choose Everything in the Advanced Kit to see all 30. See [Show basic or advanced tools](show-basic-or-advanced-tools.md).

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Are the tools free?
text: Yes. Every card says Free to use , and the plans section states "Every tool free on every plan". Paid plans add conveniences such as cloud sync, version history, batch power, API access and watermark-free exports.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Do I need an account to pin tools?
text: No. Pins work without signing in. They are stored in the browser you are using.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Will my pins appear on my phone too?
text: No. Pins and usage history stay in the browser where you made them. Signing in does not copy them to other devices.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: What is the difference between Pinned, Most used and Recommended?
text: - Pinned is the tools you chose yourself. - Most used is the tools you open most often and most recently from this page. - Recommended combines your pins and opens with how central a tool is to the site's main subjects and how fully it is described. See [Pin tools and use recommendations](pin-and-recommendations.md).

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Does Auric Artisan see which tools I pin or open here?
text: The Collections page keeps pins and opens in your browser and does not send them to Auric Artisan. The site's own analytics, which run only with your consent, are covered by the privacy policy. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Collections FAQ
heading: How do I reset the page to how it was?
text: Right-click a card and select Reset to restore the layout (grid view, cozy density, automatic columns, Title A to Z ). To clear pins, unpin each tool. To clear usage history as well, clear this site's data in your browser.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Can I share a link to a tool?
text: Yes. Right-click its card and choose Copy link , then paste the address wherever you like.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Why does the right-click menu look different on cards?
text: Cards have their own menu with card actions and grid settings. Everywhere else on the page, right-clicking opens the site's usual menu.

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Why are some categories spelled "Color"?
text: Official names keep their published spelling, such as "Color Science" and "Colorimetry". Descriptions on the site use British spelling ("colour").

title: Collections FAQ
heading: Where do I find guides for each tool?
text: Each tool has a user guide in the Documentation library. See [Documentation](../../documentation/README.md).

text: Term Meaning --- --- Card One tool's tile in the grid: artwork, category, name, description and a pin button. Catalogue order The fixed order in which tools are listed in the catalogue. The Reference lists all 30 tools in this order. Category The broad group a tool belongs to, such as Colorimetry or Utilities. Each tool has exactly one. Pin A mark you put on a tool so it is grouped under Pinned and comes first in Start here and Pinned first . Reading mode A site setting that makes pages calmer and easier to read. The card menu's Reading switch turns it on and off. Start here The slider of three featured tools near the top of the page. Tool visibility The site-wide setting, chosen in the Advanced Kit, that decides which tools appear: Basic, Advanced, Everything or Custom. Topic A short tag on a tool, such as palette or hdr . A tool can have several. The Topics filter lists up to 14 of the most common.

title: Limits and accuracy
text: Collections is a catalogue, not a measurement tool. Its numbers and orders are simple, local and predictable. This page says what they mean.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Counts
text: - The hero counters and category counts cover only the tools your tool-visibility setting shows. With the default Basic setting, Tools reads 14, not 30. - Topics counts different tags among the tools in view. The Topics filter lists only the 14 most common of them, so a rarer tag cannot be chosen as a filter; type it into the search box instead.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Search
text: - Search is a plain text match. It does not correct typing mistakes and does not know that "color" and "colour" mean the same thing. - Every word you type must match. Adding a word can only narrow the results.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Sort orders
text: - Newest first and Oldest first have no effect, because tools carry no dates. - Most used counts only opens from the Collections page itself, in this browser. It knows nothing about how you use the tools elsewhere, or on other devices. - Recommended is a fixed recipe, not a learning system. It adds points for your pins and opens, for mentions of core subjects (such as accessibility, WCAG, contrast, gamut, HDR and ICC) and for how fully a tool is described. It is a starting point, not advice about which tool is right for a job. - The boost from your opens is capped, so heavy use of one tool cannot push every other tool to the bottom of Recommended .

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: What Collections is not
text: - It is not a record of your work. Pins and usage are conveniences that can be lost when browser data is cleared. - It does not sync. Nothing you do on this page follows your account to another browser. - It does not rate tools. The order of the catalogue and of Start here is not a ranking of quality.

title: Privacy
heading: What stays in your browser
text: The Collections page remembers a few things in your browser's local storage. None of it is sent to Auric Artisan or saved to your account. What Why How to remove it --- --- --- Pinned tools To show Pinned , Pinned first and your Start here picks. Unpin each tool, or clear this site's data. title: Colour libraries
text: Auric Artisan has six colour libraries. Each is a large, searchable collection of generated colour data that you can browse, filter, inspect and copy or export. They share one idea: every item carries its measurements with it, so you can choose colours by what they do — how they contrast, how they step, how they read to people with colour vision deficiencies — and not only by how they look in a thumbnail. The libraries are free to use and need no account. They open in any modern browser.

title: Colour libraries
heading: The six libraries
text: Library What it holds Address --- --- --- [Color Library](color-library/README.md) 8,192 measured colours, each in seven colour spaces with contrast and colour-blindness data. https://auricartisan.com/library/color/ [Palette Library](palette-library/README.md) 5,000,000 generated palettes, filterable by hue, lightness, chroma, harmony method and WCAG. https://auricartisan.com/library/palette/ [Gradient Library](gradient-library/README.md) 8,192 gradients with OKLCH metadata, 2 to 46 stops, and a measured verdict on banding. https://auricartisan.com/library/gradient/ [Harmony Library](harmony-library/README.md) 8,192 colour harmonies across 23 colour-theory schemes, plus a tool that names the scheme your own colours form. https://auricartisan.com/library/harmony/ [Shade Library](shade-library/README.md) 8,192 OKLCH shade scales with tint and shade tokens and contrast checks. https://auricartisan.com/library/shades/ [Accessibility Library](accessibility-library/README.md) 5,000,000 foreground and background pairs scored against WCAG, APCA and colour vision deficiency. https://auricartisan.com/library/accessibility/

title: Colour libraries
heading: Which library do I need?
text: - One colour, with its numbers: the Color Library. - A set of colours that work together: the Palette Library, or the Harmony Library if you want a named colour-theory scheme. - A smooth blend between colours: the Gradient Library. - One colour taken from light to dark for a design system: the Shade Library. - Text and background colours that pass contrast rules: the Accessibility Library.

title: Accessibility Library
text: The Accessibility Library — the Accessibility Color Pair Library — answers one question: "What may I write on this? " You choose a background colour (the page calls it the ground ) and a contrast target, and the page draws a map of every foreground colour, with a line showing exactly where text starts to pass. Contrast depends on both colours continuously, so the answer is a territory, not a list, and the boundary moves with hue: at the same lightness, yellow gives far more contrast than blue, so "just make it darker" means different things for different hues. Around the map, the page gives you a concrete answer — up to twelve foreground colours, one per 30° of hue, that clear your target on your ground, ready to copy as CSS — and an audit for colours you already have: paste your palette and each colour is placed on the map, with how much lighter or darker it would need to be to pass. Behind all of this is an index of 5,000,000 scored foreground and background pairs. Like the other libraries, it is defined by a seed rather than stored, so any record — for example acc 91 — can be cited in an audit and recomputed by whoever reads it. Every figure is computed in your browser.

title: Accessibility Library
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers choosing text, icon and UI colours for a given background. - Accessibility specialists auditing a palette against a ground, or citing a reproducible pair. - Developers who want a set of passing foregrounds as CSS custom properties. - Anyone learning how contrast, lightness and hue interact.

title: Accessibility Library
heading: Where to find it
text: Open https://auricartisan.com/library/accessibility/ in a current browser. It is also listed as Accessibility Library ("Tested accessible color pairs") under Libraries in the site header's Learn menu. No account is needed.

title: Accessibility Library
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/library/accessibility/. The ground starts as 1D2A3E (a dark navy) and the target as 4.5:1 . 2. Choose a ground: one of the four preset swatches, or the colour picker for any colour. 3. Choose a target: 3:1 , 4.5:1 or 7:1 . 4. Drag on the map. The panel beside it shows your foreground on the ground, its contrast ratio and whether it passes. 5. Read Territory to see how much of the colour space passes on this ground. 6. Scroll to the picks and select Copy as CSS to take up to twelve passing colours. 7. Paste your own palette into Or bring your own to see which colours fail and by how much.

title: Accessibility Library
heading: What you can do
text: - See, for any background, every foreground colour that reaches 3:1, 4.5:1 or 7:1. - Read a colour's WCAG contrast ratio, APCA lightness contrast (Lc), and how well it stays distinct under ten simulated vision conditions. - Get up to twelve passing foregrounds across the hue circle, and copy them as CSS custom properties. - Audit up to 24 of your own colours against the ground, with the lightness change each failure needs. - Swap foreground and ground to ask the question the other way round. - Look up any of five million scored pairs by id, and browse pairs that pass. - Automate the same answers through the site's REST API.
