title: Analyse the collection
text: The Harmony , Accessibility and Stats tabs describe many palettes at once. A browser cannot count five million palettes, so each tab measures a sample and says how big it was.

title: Analyse the collection
heading: The sample
text: Every tab opens with a line such as: Measured on 2,000 palettes from the start of the collection. Five million cannot be counted in a browser, so these are a sample — the API samples the same way. - No filter or search: the sample is the first 2,000 palettes of the collection. - A filter or search is on: the page looks through up to 40,000 palettes from the start of the collection and keeps up to 2,000 that match. The line then says, for example, Measured on 812 palettes matching this filter, out of 40,000 derived . - An id is in the search box: the sample is that one palette. The sample is rebuilt every time you change a filter or search, so the tabs always describe the filter the grid is showing. If nothing in the looked-at stretch matches, the tabs show No palettes and suggest widening the filter.

title: Analyse the collection
heading: Harmony tab
text: Four cards, each a bar chart with counts: Card What it counts --- --- Generation method How many sampled palettes carry each method label. Dominant hue bucket How many have each dominant hue: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple or pink. Harmony classification How many are classified Neutral , Triadic , Analogous or Monochrome from their measured hues (see [Inspect a palette](inspect-a-palette.md)). Lightness & chroma profile How many are Dark (L < 0.4) , Mid (0.4-0.7) or Light ( 0.7) , and Muted (< 0.07) , Balanced or Vivid ( 0.15) .

title: Analyse the collection
heading: Accessibility tab
text: Row Meaning --- --- Has any AA pair (4.5+) Palettes with at least one pair of colours at 4.5:1 or more, as a count and percentage. Has any AAA pair (7+) Palettes with at least one pair at 7:1 or more. Largest mutually-legible set The most colours from one palette that all reach 4.5:1 against each other, for example 2 of 5 (sRGB allows 3) . Every palette has ten pairs, so the sample has ten times as many pairs as palettes. The card counts AAA pairs ( = 7:1) , AA pairs ( = 4.5:1) and Below AA . This card answers a practical question: how many of a palette's five colours can all be used as text on each other? The page explains why the answer can never be five. Contrast depends only on how light each colour is, and between black and white there is room for at most three lightness levels that are each 4.5:1 apart — and only two at 7:1. So no five-colour palette can have all ten pairs at AA , here or anywhere. The card shows how many sampled palettes allow 1, 2 or 3 mutually legible colours, marking 3 as (the ceiling) . Up to 24 palettes that contain at least one legible pair, ordered by their strongest pair. The page notes that two is what this collection realistically offers: a legible trio needs a near-black, a mid-tone and a near-white to turn up together in one palette, which the page reports did not happen in any of the 60,000 palettes it measured. The cards work like cards in the grid: select one to inspect it, select a swatch to copy it.

title: Analyse the collection
heading: Stats tab
text: A line first states how many sampled palettes contain a pair at 4.5:1 or better, "so they can carry body text on themselves". Then four histograms: Card Range Bands --- --- --- Avg lightness (OKLCH L) 0 to 1 10 Avg chroma (OKLCH C) 0 to 0.30 10 Hue spread 0 to 360 degrees 12 Best pair contrast 1:1 to 15:1 14 Values beyond a histogram's range are counted in its last band. The best pair is charted rather than the worst because, as the page explains, with five colours some pair is nearly always close to identical, so the worst pair says little about whether a palette can carry text.

title: Analyse the collection
heading: Keeping the tabs current
text: Each tab is drawn when you open it and redrawn after any change of filter or search. If a tab looks out of date, select it again.

title: Analyse the collection
heading: Result
text: You can see, for any filter, what share of palettes can carry text, which methods and hues dominate, and how light and colourful the palettes tend to be — with the size of the sample stated every time.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: How the collection works
text: Each palette has a number from 0 to 4,999,999, and an id made from that number: pal followed by the number written in base 36 (digits 0–9 then letters a–z). Palette 0 is pal 0 , palette 10 is pal a , palette 13,368 is pal abc . The five colours of a palette are worked out from its number every time you need them, so they never change. Because every palette can be reached by its number, the unfiltered grid can show any part of the collection instantly. A filtered grid cannot: the only way to find the hundredth blue palette is to look through every palette before it. So the page scans forward in chunks as you scroll, and the counter under the grid tells you how far it has looked.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Scroll the whole collection
text: With no search or filter: - The grid starts at pal 0 and scrolls continuously. - The counter reads, for example, 1–48 of 5,000,000 palettes . - A browser cannot make a page tall enough to scroll through five million palettes, so the scrollbar stops before the end. When it does, the counter adds scroll reaches N; search an id for the rest . Every palette beyond that point can still be opened by searching for its id. - Back to top returns to pal 0 .

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Jump to a palette by id
text: 1. Type an id into Search by id or hex… , for example pal abc , or type the palette's number, for example 13368 . 2. The grid shows only that palette, and the counter reads 1 palette, by id . 3. If the id is outside the collection, the counter reads No palette with that id . An id or number anywhere in either search box takes priority over everything else: filters are ignored while an id is shown.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Search by hex or method
text: Type anything that is not an id, for example 3a or analogous . A palette matches when every word you type is found in: - its id; or - its generation method; or - the hex code of any of its five colours (with or without ). The Filter inside results box works the same way; words in both boxes are combined. Clear empties only the second box. Searching counts as a filter, so it starts a scan (see below).

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Filters
text: Filter Options What it tests --- --- --- Dominant hue All hues , Red , Orange , Yellow , Green , Cyan , Blue , Purple , Pink The palette's overall hue: the average of its five OKLCH hues, weighted so that more colourful colours count more. Chroma Any chroma , Muted (< 0.07) , Balanced , Vivid ( 0.15) The average OKLCH chroma of the five colours. Balanced is 0.07 to 0.15. Lightness Any lightness , Dark , Mid , Light The average OKLCH lightness: Dark below 0.40, Mid 0.40 to 0.70, Light above 0.70. Method All methods , complementary , triadic , analogous , tetradic , golden ratio , random , monochromatic The generation method the palette is labelled with. All filters and searches combine: a palette must pass every one.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Read the counter while filtering
text: With any filter or search active, the counter reads, for example: - 96 matches from 1,500 derived — the page has worked out 1,500 palettes so far and 96 of them match. - 4,210 matches from 5,000,000 derived · all five million looked at — the scan has reached the end of the collection. Scroll down to make the scan continue; each step works out another stretch of palettes. A rare filter combination may need to look through many palettes before the first match. Until then the grid shows Nothing matched yet with the advice Scroll to keep looking, or widen the filter — a rare one can go a long way into five million before the first hit.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Sort
text: Sort by has these options: Option Order --- --- Sort: original By palette number (default). Lightness ↑ Darkest palettes first (average OKLCH lightness). Lightness ↓ Lightest first. Chroma ↑ Least colourful first (average chroma). Chroma ↓ Most colourful first. Hue (rainbow) By dominant hue, from 0°. Random Shuffled. Five million palettes cannot be put in order in a browser. Any sort other than Sort: original therefore works on a bounded first stretch of the collection — the first 1,500 palettes the page works out, or the matches among them when a filter is on — and orders those. With a filter on, the counter says so, for example 96 matches, ordered within the first 1,500 derived . The sorted grid does not grow as you scroll. Tip: To see, say, the most colourful palettes of one method, choose the method first and then Chroma ↓ . You are ordering the matches the page has found, not the whole collection.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Shuffle, random, reset
text: - Shuffle sets Sort by to Random . Like any sort, it shuffles the first stretch of the collection. - Open a random palette picks a palette from anywhere in the five million and opens it on Inspect . - Reset empties both search boxes, sets every filter back to "All" or "Any", and sets the sort back to Sort: original . - Export visible opens the Export tab.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Cards
text: Each card shows: - five swatches, each labelled with its hex code — select a swatch to copy that hex code (the page confirms, for example, 3A5F8C copied ); - the palette id and its method; - Inspect — opens the palette on the Inspect tab (selecting the card anywhere outside the buttons and swatches does the same); - Copy — copies all five hex codes, separated by commas ( Palette hexes copied ); - Save or Saved — saves or unsaves the palette. With the keyboard, Tab moves between swatches; Enter or Space on a swatch opens its palette on Inspect .

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: Result
text: You can reach any of the five million palettes directly by id, or scan for palettes with the hue, chroma, lightness or method you need, and the counter always tells you how much of the collection the answer is based on.

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Quick copies from the grid
text: - Select one swatch to copy that colour's hex code. - Select Copy on a card to copy all five hex codes separated by commas, for example 28ACE4, 715ED2, F84461, 6F30E7, BBC8BA .

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Export one palette
text: Open the palette on the Inspect tab (see [Inspect a palette](inspect-a-palette.md)). You can then use either the Quick export row on Inspect , or the Selection card on the Export tab. They produce the same results. If no palette is open, the Export tab says No palette selected. Click Inspect on any card in the Library tab to enable selection exports. The examples use palette pal 0 . Variable names are built from the palette id and the colour's position, 1 to 5. Quick export Export tab What is copied --- --- --- Copy HEX HEX list The five hex codes, one per line. Copy CSS vars CSS variables A :root block with one custom property per colour. Copy SCSS SCSS variables Five Sass variables. Copy Tailwind Tailwind config A colour object you can paste into theme.extend.colors . css :root { --pal 0-1: 28ACE4; --pal 0-2: 715ED2; --pal 0-3: F84461; --pal 0-4: 6F30E7; --pal 0-5: BBC8BA; } text $pal 0-1: 28ACE4; $pal 0-2: 715ED2; $pal 0-3: F84461; $pal 0-4: 6F30E7; $pal 0-5: BBC8BA; json { "pal 0": { "c1": " 28ACE4", "c2": " 715ED2", "c3": " F84461", "c4": " 6F30E7", "c5": " BBC8BA" } } These are the real colours of pal 0 , which is labelled complementary . Quick export Export tab File Contents --- --- --- --- Download JSON JSON pal 0.json The id, each colour's hex, RGB, OKLCH and Lab, and the metadata: method, colour count, average ΔE, entropy and the full 5 × 5 contrast table. Download ASE Adobe ASE pal 0.ase An Adobe Swatch Exchange file with five RGB swatches named pal 0 1 to pal 0 5 . Opens in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and other apps that read ASE. Download SVG SVG strip pal 0.svg A 600 × 220 strip of the five colours, each labelled with its hex code. Download PNG PNG strip pal 0.png An 800 × 320 image of the same strip. The page confirms each download with Downloaded and the file name. Open in Coolors (on Inspect , and under External on the Export tab) opens the palette on coolors.co in a new tab, with the five colours already loaded. Coolors is a separate website; what you do there is governed by its own terms.

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Export design tokens
text: Design tokens are named colour values in a format a design system or app platform understands. 1. On Inspect , select Design tokens… . A dialog opens, titled with the palette id. 2. In Token prefix , type the name your tokens should start with. The default is brand . 3. Select a format tab. The preview shows the file, with a line above it giving the number of tokens, the file name and the file's length, for example 5 tokens · tokens.css and a character count. 4. Select Copy to copy the preview, Download to save that format, or Download all to save every format in one ZIP file. Format tab File name --- --- W3C Design Tokens tokens.json CSS Variables tokens.css SCSS tokens.scss Tailwind Config tailwind.config.js Style Dictionary style-dictionary.tokens.json Material UI Theme theme.ts iOS (SwiftUI) Colors.swift Android colors.xml colors.xml Download all names the ZIP after the palette, for example palette-pal-0.zip . Close the dialog with ✕ or by selecting outside it.

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Share a link
text: 1. On Inspect , select Copy share link . The Share link dialog opens, titled with the palette id. 2. The dialog explains: "Anyone with this link can open a copy. State is encoded in the URL — no account needed." 3. Select Copy (it changes to Copied! ), Share via… (on devices that offer a system share sheet), or Open in new tab . 4. Select Close when you are done. Anyone who opens the link lands on the Palette Library with the palette open on Inspect . The link carries the palette's id and colours; nothing is stored on a server. If the palette cannot be found, the page says Shared palette not found in current dataset .

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Export many palettes
text: The Export tab's second card is headed Visible page and carries a badge with a number of palettes. It exports the same sample the analysis tabs measure (see [Analyse the collection](analyse-the-collection.md)): with no filter, the first 2,000 palettes of the collection; with a filter, up to 2,000 matching palettes from the first 40,000 looked at. Group Button Contents --- --- --- Bulk download Download JSON (visible page) Every palette in full, with export time, source and count. Download CSV (visible page) One row per palette: palette id,method,c1,c2,c3,c4,c5 . Download CSS variables One :root block with five variables per palette. Download SCSS variables Five Sass variables per palette. Download compact JSON The count and each palette's id and five hex codes. Sample formats Download .txt hex list Every hex code, one per line. Download tailwind.config.js fragment A Tailwind configuration with one colour group per palette. Files are named palette-page- plus the number of palettes and the date, for example palette-page-2000-2026-09-24.csv . If the sample is empty, the page says Nothing to export . Note: "Visible page" means the measured sample, not only the cards on your screen. To export exactly one palette, use the Selection card instead.

title: Copy, export and share
heading: Result
text: The palette is on your clipboard, in a file your design tool or code can read, in a design-token format for your platform, or in a link someone else can open.

title: Inspect a palette
text: The Inspect tab turns one palette into a full report.

title: Inspect a palette
heading: Open a palette
text: - Select Inspect on a card, or select the card outside its swatches and buttons. - Focus a swatch and press Enter or Space . - Select Open a random palette . - Open a share link someone sent you (see [Copy, export and share](copy-export-and-share.md)). Before any palette is open, the tab shows No palette selected and explains what you will see.

title: Inspect a palette
heading: The colour strip
text: Five tall columns, one per colour. Each shows: - a descriptive name made of three words — a tone, a colourfulness and a hue — for example soft muted blue ; - the hex code. Select a column to copy its hex code. Word Meaning (from OKLCH) --- --- Tone: deep , rich , soft , pale Lightness below 0.35, below 0.55, below 0.75, and 0.75 or more. Colourfulness: neutral , muted , saturated , vivid Chroma below 0.04, below 0.10, below 0.18, and 0.18 or more. Hue: red , orange , yellow , green , teal , blue , purple , pink The colour's OKLCH hue angle.

title: Inspect a palette
heading: Palette summary
text: The Palette summary card carries a badge that classifies the palette from its real colours: Badge When --- --- Neutral Average chroma below 0.05. Triadic The widest gap between any two hues is more than 90°. Analogous The widest gap is more than 30°. Monochrome The widest gap is 30° or less. The card's rows: Row Meaning --- --- Palette ID The id, such as pal abc . Global index The palette's number in the collection. Method The generation method the palette is labelled with. Colors 5. Avg L\ (OKLCH) The average OKLCH lightness of the five colours, 0 to 1. Avg chroma The average OKLCH chroma. Hue span The widest angle between any two of the five hues, in degrees (0 to 180). DeltaE avg The average colour difference between each pair of colours (CIE76, in Lab). Larger means more varied. Entropy How many different hue families the palette covers, as a fraction: the number of 36° hue bands its colours fall in, divided by 5. Min pair contrast The lowest WCAG contrast ratio between any two of its colours. Max pair contrast The highest. If it is 4.5:1 or more, at least one pair can carry body text. Note: The Method row and the badge can disagree. The method is the label the palette carries in the collection; the badge is measured from the colours themselves. When you need a particular relationship between hues, trust the badge and the Hue span .

title: Inspect a palette
heading: Pair-by-pair WCAG contrast
text: All ten pairs of the five colours, each with its contrast ratio, for example 1B2A4A / F0E6D2 11.48 : 1 . Ratios of 4.5:1 or more are shown as good, 3:1 to 4.5:1 as a warning, and below 3:1 as failing. Use this list to choose foreground and background pairs from the palette: - 4.5:1 or more — normal body text (WCAG AA). - 7:1 or more — normal text at AAA. - 3:1 or more — large text (at least 18 point, or 14 point bold) and graphical objects such as icons.

title: Inspect a palette
heading: Quick export
text: A row of actions for this palette: Copy HEX , Copy CSS vars , Copy SCSS , Copy Tailwind , Download JSON , Download ASE , Download SVG , Download PNG , Open in Coolors , Save to library (or Unsave ), Copy share link and Design tokens… . Each is described in [Copy, export and share](copy-export-and-share.md).

title: Inspect a palette
heading: One card per colour
text: Five cards, headed Color 1 to Color 5 with the hex code. The badge on each heading shows its contrast on white and on black, for example 6.6:1 / 3.2:1 . Each card lists: Row Format --- --- HEX 3A5F8C RGB rgb(58, 95, 140) OKLCH Lightness as a percentage, chroma and hue, for example 47.87% 0.085 254.14 CIE L\ a\ b\ L, a and b, for example 39.54, 1.04, -28.90 WCAG vs white The contrast ratio against FFFFFF . WCAG vs black The contrast ratio against 000000 . Two small buttons under the rows copy the hex code and the rgb() value. Select any card's heading to fold it away, and again to unfold it.

title: Inspect a palette
heading: Result
text: You know what each colour is called and measures, how varied the palette is, and exactly which of its colours can be used as text on which.

title: Save palettes
heading: Save a palette
text: Either: - select Save on the palette's card in the grid (it changes to Saved ); or - open the palette on Inspect and select Save to library under Quick export (the page confirms Saved ). The Saved tab's badge goes up by one.

title: Save palettes
heading: See your saved palettes
text: Select the Saved tab. Your palettes appear as cards, the most recently saved first. The cards work like cards in the grid: select a swatch to copy it, Copy to copy all five, Inspect to open the palette, or Saved to unsave it. A note above the cards says your palettes are Also saved to your Library workspace with image previews , with a link. With nothing saved, the tab shows No saved palettes yet and explains how to save one.

title: Save palettes
heading: Remove a palette
text: Select Saved on its card, or Unsave under Quick export on Inspect (the page confirms Removed ). The palette leaves the Saved tab and your Library.

title: Save palettes
heading: In your Library
text: Each saved palette is also added to your Library as a palette named, for example, Palette pal abc , described by its method and colour count, with a picture of its five colours. Open your Library from any page with Ctrl + Shift + L . See the [Library Kit docs](../../../../kits/library-kit/README.md).

title: Save palettes
heading: Limits
text: - The Saved tab keeps up to 500 palettes. Saving more drops the oldest from the list. - Saved palettes are kept in this browser, not in your account. They do not follow you to another browser or device, and clearing this site's data removes them. Because every palette is fixed by its id, writing down an id such as pal abc is a permanent way to keep a palette: search for the id at any time to get the same five colours.

title: Save palettes
heading: Result
text: Your chosen palettes are one tab away on the Palette Library and also in your Library next to everything else you have saved.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Could not load palette database"
text: Why: The page could not download the short description of the collection it needs to work out palettes, usually because of a dropped connection or a content blocker. What to do: Check your connection, allow auricartisan.com in any content blocker, and reload.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A filter shows "Nothing matched yet"
text: Why: A filter starts a scan from the beginning of the collection. A rare combination, such as Dark lightness with Vivid chroma and one method, may need to look through many palettes before the first match. What to do: Scroll down to let the scan continue, or widen the filter. Watch the counter: N matches from M derived shows how far it has looked.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Filtering feels slow
text: Why: Every palette the scan looks at is worked out on the spot. The page does this in small steps so it stays responsive, but a rare filter can mean a lot of work. What to do: Remove a filter you do not need, or use the search box to jump straight to a known id.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The scrollbar stops before the end of the collection
text: Why: No browser can make a page tall enough for five million palettes. The counter says scroll reaches N; search an id for the rest . What to do: Type the id or number of the palette you want into Search by id or hex… . Every palette can be reached this way.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A sort does not seem to cover the whole collection
text: Why: Sorting needs the whole set in hand, and five million palettes cannot be ordered in a browser. Any sort other than Sort: original orders only a first stretch of the collection, and the sorted grid does not grow as you scroll. What to do: Combine the sort with filters so the stretch it orders is the one you care about. For a full, streaming browse, use Sort: original .

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Filters seem to be ignored
text: Why: The search box contains an id or a plain number. An id always wins, and the grid shows only that palette ( 1 palette, by id ). What to do: Remove the id or number from both search boxes.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The palette's method does not match its colours
text: Why: The Method is a label each palette carries in the collection. The badge on Palette summary ( Neutral , Triadic , Analogous , Monochrome ) is measured from the actual colours, and the two can disagree. What to do: When the relationship between hues matters, judge by the badge and the Hue span , not the method label. See [Limits and accuracy](../others/limits-and-accuracy.md).

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Export visible" exported more palettes than I can see
text: Why: The Visible page export uses the same sample as the analysis tabs: up to 2,000 palettes, not only the cards on screen. What to do: To export one palette, open it on Inspect and use the Selection card or Quick export .

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A share link opens the page but not the palette
text: Why: The link may have been cut short when it was pasted, or edited. What to do: Ask for the link again, or ask for the palette id and search for it. If the page says Shared palette not found in current dataset , the id in the link is not valid.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The ASE file will not open
text: Why: ASE files are read by Adobe apps and some other design tools; not every app supports them. What to do: Import it through your app's swatches or palette panel rather than opening it as a document. If your app does not read ASE, use the JSON, CSS or design-token exports instead.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Saved palettes have gone
text: Why: Saved palettes live in this browser only; clearing site data, a private window, or another browser or device will not show them. The Saved tab also keeps only the latest 500. What to do: Save them again, or keep their ids — an id always gives the same palette.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Are there really five million palettes?
text: Yes. Each of the 5,000,000 palettes is defined by its number and worked out when you view it. The same id always gives the same five colours.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Why not store them?
text: Written out in full, the collection was 3.9 GB. Working palettes out as you scroll keeps the page fast and the download tiny.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: How do I get back to a palette I found?
text: Note its id (for example pal abc ) and type it into the search box, save it, or copy a share link.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Why does a filter say "derived"?
text: Because the page has to work out palettes to test them. 96 matches from 1,500 derived means it has looked at 1,500 palettes and 96 passed.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Can every colour in a palette be used as text on every other?
text: No — not in this library or any other. There is only room for three lightness levels that are all 4.5:1 apart, so at most three colours can all be legible on each other, and in practice palettes here offer two. Use Pair-by-pair WCAG contrast on Inspect to find the pairs that work. See [Analyse the collection](analyse-the-collection.md).

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: What do the method names mean?
text: They are the palette's generation-method labels: complementary , triadic , analogous , tetradic , golden ratio , random and monochromatic . The badge on Inspect measures the hue relationship the colours actually have.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Which export should I use?
text: - Pasting into CSS: Copy CSS vars . - A Tailwind project: Copy Tailwind , or Design tokens… › Tailwind Config . - Adobe apps: Download ASE . - A design system or native app: Design tokens… . - A presentation or mood board: Download PNG or Download SVG .

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Do I need an account?
text: No. Saving keeps palettes in this browser and in your Library without signing in.

title: Palette Library FAQ
heading: Is there an API?
text: Yes. The heading links to the Palette Library API guide, and the Automate this note names the call ( GET /v1/palette/library , 3 API credits per call). See [Public API](../../../../../services/public-api/README.md).

title: Palette Library glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- ASE Adobe Swatch Exchange, a swatch file format read by Adobe apps and other design tools. Base 36 Writing numbers with the digits 0–9 and the letters a–z. Palette ids use it: pal a is palette 10. Chroma How colourful a colour is compared with a grey of the same lightness. The page uses OKLCH chroma. Contrast ratio The WCAG 2 measure of the lightness difference between two colours, from 1:1 to 21:1. 4.5:1 is the AA level for body text; 7:1 is AAA. Derived Worked out on the spot from the palette's number rather than read from storage. Design tokens Named colour values in a format a design system or platform reads, such as CSS variables, a Tailwind config or an Android colors.xml . Dominant hue A palette's overall hue: the average of its five hues, weighted towards the more colourful colours. Entropy On Inspect : how many 36° hue bands the five colours fall in, divided by 5. 1.00 means five different hue families. Hue span The widest angle between any two of a palette's five hues, from 0° to 180°. Method The generation-method label a palette carries, such as triadic . Mutually legible A set of colours that all reach a contrast threshold against each other, so any one can be text on any other. OKLCH A modern perceptual colour space: lightness (0 to 1), chroma and hue angle. Palette id pal followed by the palette's number in base 36, for example pal abc . Sample The set of palettes the analysis tabs and the bulk export use: up to 2,000 palettes. Scan Looking through the collection from the start, in chunks, to find palettes that match a filter. Seed The fixed starting number from which every palette is worked out. It is why palettes never change. WCAG Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international standard for accessible web content.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Scans and samples
text: - A filtered browse is a scan from the start of the collection. It shows the matches found so far, not all matches in five million. The counter always states how many palettes were looked at. - Sorting orders a first stretch of 1,500 palettes (or the matches among them), not the whole collection. - The Harmony , Accessibility and Stats tabs, and the Visible page export, use a sample of up to 2,000 palettes: the first 2,000, or the first matches found in up to 40,000. Percentages describe that sample. Because the sample always starts at the beginning of the collection, it is consistent from visit to visit but is not a random draw from all five million.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Method labels and measured harmony
text: Each palette carries a method label (such as triadic ). The colours are worked out from the palette's number, and the label does not guarantee a particular hue relationship. The Palette summary badge and Hue span on Inspect are measured from the actual colours; rely on those when the relationship matters.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Contrast
text: - Contrast ratios use the WCAG 2 formula. They are exact for the colours as sRGB values. - WCAG 2 contrast is one requirement for readable text. Font size, weight, and the surrounding design also matter. Newer measures such as APCA can rate some pairs differently. - The ceiling of three mutually legible colours at 4.5:1 is a property of the contrast formula, not of this collection.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Colour values
text: - OKLCH and CIE Lab values are standard conversions from sRGB with a D65 white point, rounded for display. - DeltaE avg uses CIE76, which over-states differences between very saturated colours compared with newer formulas. - The three-word colour names on Inspect come from fixed lightness, chroma and hue bands. They are handy descriptions, not standard colour names.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Your screen
text: Swatches look different on different displays. The numbers are the same everywhere.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: What it is not
text: - It is not a palette generator that responds to your input. For that, see the palette tools in [Related](related.md). - It is not an accessibility audit of a design.

heading: What uses the network
text: - When the page opens, it downloads a short description of the collection from auricartisan.com. Palettes themselves are worked out in your browser. - Open in Coolors opens coolors.co in a new tab and passes it the palette's five hex codes in the address. Coolors is a separate service with its own privacy policy. - Download all in the design tokens dialog may download a small helper from auricartisan.com to build the ZIP file. - Share links contain the palette's id and colours in the link itself; nothing is uploaded when you create one. Advertising and analytics on the site follow your consent choices. See [Company and legal](../../../../company-and-legal/README.md).

title: Shade Library
text: The Shade Library is a collection of 8,192 shade scales (also called shade systems or colour ramps). A shade scale is one colour taken from very light to very dark in named steps — the familiar 50 , 100 , 200 … 900 , 950 of design systems such as Tailwind CSS or Material Design. The page puts the difference from a palette clearly: "A shade scale is not a palette. It is one colour taken through lightness so that some steps are surfaces and others are text on them." The headline, "Eight thousand ramps, and 8% of them even ", sums up what the page measures. All 8,192 scales run in one direction and all can carry text, but only 8.2% have genuinely even steps. The scales come from ten generation methods — from Material-like and Tailwind-like ramps to accessible-UI, neutral, ink-and-paper, duotone and temperature-shift systems — with 5 to 21 tokens each. For each scale you can read every token's value in HEX, RGB, OKLCH and CIE Lab, see which tokens can carry body text with black or white text on them, and export the whole scale as CSS custom properties, SCSS, a Tailwind colour group, JSON, SVG, PNG or design tokens for eight platforms.

title: Shade Library
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers and developers building a design system who need a full tint-and-shade scale for a brand colour. - Front-end developers who want token-named CSS variables or a Tailwind colour group ready to paste. - Accessibility specialists checking which steps of a scale can carry text.

title: Shade Library
heading: Where to find it
text: Open https://auricartisan.com/library/shades/ in a current browser. It is also listed as Shade Library ("OKLCH shade systems") under Libraries in the site header's Learn menu. No account is needed.

title: Shade Library
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/library/shades/. 2. Set Base hue to the hue of your brand colour, for example Blue . 3. Set Method to Tailwind Like . 4. Select Inspect on a scale. 5. Read the Token contrast ladder to see which steps carry text. 6. Under Quick export , select Copy CSS vars . 7. Paste the variables into your stylesheet.

title: Shade Library
heading: What you can do
text: - Browse, search and filter 8,192 scales by base hue, chroma, lightness and method. - Sort by lightness, chroma, hue, score or number of tokens. - Inspect a scale: token names, descriptive colour names, summary metrics, a contrast ladder and every token's values. - Read distributions of methods, hues, profiles and accessibility across your filtered set. - Copy a scale as hex, CSS, SCSS or Tailwind; download JSON, SVG or PNG; export design tokens; share a link. - Save scales in your browser and your Library, and export whole filtered sets.

While the collection loads, the grid shows Loading shade library... . 3. The grid fills and the counter reads, for example, 1–24 of 8,192 scales . If loading fails you see Could not load shade library . See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

title: Getting started
heading: Your first task: a blue scale for a design system
text: 1. Set Base hue to Blue . 2. Set Method to Tailwind Like to get the familiar 50–950 token names. 3. Select Inspect on a scale you like. 4. Read the Shade summary : Tokens , Auto AA tokens and Min adjacent contrast . 5. Read the Token contrast ladder : each step's contrast with the better of black or white text. 6. Under Quick export , select Copy CSS vars . The page confirms CSS variables copied . 7. Paste the block into your stylesheet and use the variables for surfaces, borders and text. Result: a full blue scale as CSS custom properties, with the steps that can carry text identified.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: The grid
text: The counter reads, for example, 1–24 of 1,148 scales , or Nothing to show ; the grid then says No shade systems match — Try clearing a filter, or searching a broader method, hex or token. Cards: select a swatch to copy its hex; Copy copies all hex codes, comma-separated ( Shade hexes copied ); Save saves or unsaves ( Shade saved / Shade removed ); Inspect , or anywhere else on the card, opens it. With the keyboard, Enter or Space on a focused swatch opens the scale.

title: Browse, search and filter
heading: A note on evenness
text: The page's introduction points to evenness — whether a scale's steps are equally spaced — as the property that matters most, and reports that 8.2% of scales are genuinely even. The current filter row does not include an evenness filter. To judge evenness for one scale, open it on Inspect and read Min adjacent contrast and the Token contrast ladder : large jumps between neighbouring steps show up there.

title: Copy, export and share
heading: One scale
text: Open the scale on Inspect . Use Quick export , or the Selection card on the Export tab (headed Selection - and the id). With nothing open, the Export tab says No shade system selected. Click Inspect on any card in the Library tab to enable selection exports. Names in the output come from the scale's name with the hex codes removed, in lower case with dashes: Material Like FF724C 00001 becomes material-like-00001 . Each variable ends in the token name. Quick export Export tab What is copied Message --- --- --- --- Copy HEX HEX list All hex codes, comma-separated. HEX list copied Copy CSS vars CSS variables A CSS class holding one custom property per token. CSS variables copied Copy SCSS SCSS variables One Sass variable per token. SCSS copied Copy Tailwind Tailwind config A colour group keyed by token. Tailwind copied For the first scale in the collection: css .aa-shade-material-like-00001 { --material-like-00001-50: fff0ec; --material-like-00001-100: ffdfd7; --material-like-00001-300: ff886b; --material-like-00001-500: ff724c; --material-like-00001-700: cd5531; --material-like-00001-900: 4b1200; --material-like-00001-950: 1e0400; } text $material-like-00001-50: fff0ec; $material-like-00001-100: ffdfd7; ... $material-like-00001-950: 1e0400; text "material-like-00001": { "50": " fff0ec", "100": " ffdfd7", ... "950": " 1e0400" } Tip: The CSS variables are declared on a class, not on :root . Either add that class to an element, or change the selector to :root after pasting. Rename the prefix to something meaningful in your project, such as --brand-500 . heading: Design tokens
text: Select Design tokens… . The dialog is titled with the scale's name. Token prefix starts as color , and every token keeps its step name: color-50 , color-100 … color-950 . title: Inspect a scale
text: Open a scale with Inspect , by selecting the card, with Enter or Space on a focused swatch, with Open a random scale , or from a share link. Until then the tab shows No shade system selected .

title: Inspect a scale
heading: The token strip
text: One column per token, labelled with the token name and a descriptive colour name — for example 500 - soft vivid orange — and the hex code. Select a column to copy its hex.

title: Inspect a scale
heading: Shade summary
text: The badge gives the scale's profile: Badge When --- --- Neutral Average chroma below 0.035. Hue Shift Its hues span more than 35°. Light Average lightness above 0.72. Deep Average lightness below 0.38. Balanced Anything else. The badges are checked in that order, so a scale is Neutral before it can be Hue Shift , and so on. Row Meaning --- --- Shade ID For example shade 000000 . Global index The scale's number. Method For example Material Like . Base The base colour the scale is built around. Tokens Number of steps. Avg L (OKLCH) Average lightness, 0 to 1. Avg chroma Average OKLCH chroma. Hue span Widest hue difference between two tokens. Score The quality score recorded for the scale. Auto AA tokens How many tokens reach 4.5:1 with automatic text (near-black on light tokens, white on dark ones), for example 4 / 7 . All tokens is good; 70% or more is a warning; less is poor. Min adjacent contrast The lowest contrast between two neighbouring tokens — how close the two most similar steps are.

title: Inspect a scale
heading: Token contrast ladder
text: Each token with its hex and its contrast with automatic text, for example 500 FF724C 2.71 : 1 auto text . Automatic text is near-black ( 111111 ) on tokens whose luminance is above 0.5, and white otherwise. Use the ladder to decide which steps can hold body text (4.5:1 or more), large text (3:1 or more), or should be used only as fills.

title: Inspect a scale
heading: Quick export
text: Copy HEX , Copy CSS vars , Copy SCSS , Copy Tailwind , Download JSON , Download SVG , Download PNG , Save to library / Unsave , Copy share link and Design tokens… . See [Copy, export and share](copy-export-and-share.md).

title: Inspect a scale
heading: One card per token
text: Headed Token and the name and hex, for example Token 500 - FF724C , with a badge of its contrast on white and on black. Rows: HEX , RGB , OKLCH , CIE L\ a\ b\ , WCAG vs white , WCAG vs black , and buttons to copy the hex and rgb() value.

title: Inspect a scale
heading: Example
text: The first scale, Material Like FF724C 00001 , has seven tokens: 50 , 100 , 300 , 500 , 700 , 900 and 950 . Its ladder shows 50 , 100 , 900 and 950 well above 4.5:1 with automatic text, while 300 , 500 and 700 fall below it — those middle steps are for fills, borders and large accents, not body text.

title: Save scales
heading: Save
text: Select Save on a card, or Save to library under Quick export on Inspect . The page confirms Shade saved , and the Saved tab's badge goes up.

title: Save scales
heading: Find saved scales
text: Open the Saved tab. Scales appear as cards, most recently saved first, with a note that they are Also saved to your Library workspace with image previews . With nothing saved: No saved shade systems yet .

title: Save scales
heading: Unsave
text: Select Saved on the card, or Unsave on Inspect . The page confirms Shade removed , and the scale leaves your Library too.

title: Save scales
heading: In your Library
text: Each saved scale is added to your Library under its name (for example Material Like FF724C 00001 ), described by method, base colour and token count. Open your Library with Ctrl + Shift + L . See the [Library Kit docs](../../../../kits/library-kit/README.md).

title: Save scales
heading: Limits
text: Up to 500 scales are kept; saving more drops the oldest. Saves are kept in this browser only.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Could not load shade library"
text: Why: The collection (about 2 MB) could not be downloaded. What to do: Check your connection and any content blocker, and reload.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: I cannot find an evenness filter
text: Why: The page's introduction recommends filtering by evenness, but the current filter row has only Base hue , Chroma , Lightness and Method . What to do: Narrow the list with the other filters, then compare Min adjacent contrast and the Token contrast ladder on Inspect : uneven scales show one or two big jumps between neighbouring steps.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "No shade systems match"
text: Why: The filters together exclude everything, for example Light lightness with Ink Paper . What to do: Select Reset and add filters back one at a time.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Pasted CSS variables do nothing
text: Why: Copy CSS vars declares the variables on a class such as .aa-shade-material-like-00001 , not on :root . What to do: Change the selector to :root , or add the class to the element where you use the variables.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The middle steps fail contrast
text: Why: In almost every scale, the middle steps (around 300 – 700 ) are too close in lightness to both black and white to carry body text. That is expected: they are fills, borders and accents. What to do: Use light steps for surfaces with dark text, dark steps for text or dark surfaces with light text, and check the Token contrast ladder .

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Bulk export buttons do nothing
text: Why: No scales match the current filters. What to do: Widen the filters, then export again.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A share link does not open the scale
text: Why: The link was cut short or edited; the page may say Shared shade not in current library . What to do: Ask for the scale's id (for example shade 000000 ) and search for it.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Saved scales have gone
text: Why: Saves live in this browser only (up to 500). What to do: Save them again, or export them.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: What is a shade scale?
text: One colour taken through lightness in named steps, from a near-white tint to a near-black shade. Light steps become surfaces, dark steps become text, and middle steps become fills and accents.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: What are tokens?
text: The named steps of a scale, such as 50 , 100 … 900 , 950 . The collection uses several naming patterns and has between 5 and 21 tokens per scale.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: What do the methods mean?
text: They are the ten generation styles: Material Like , Tailwind Like , Brand System , Accessible Ui , Oklch Ramp , Neutral System , Ink Paper , Vivid Product , Duotone Shift and Temperature Shift . Tailwind Like and Material Like follow the step naming of those design systems.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: What does "8% even" mean?
text: The page reports that only 8.2% of the scales have genuinely even steps — no step much larger than the average. Even steps make a scale predictable to use.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: Can every step carry text?
text: In 403 of the 8,192 scales, every token reaches 4.5:1 with automatic black or white text. In most scales the middle steps do not. See [Analyse the collection](analyse-the-collection.md).

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: Can I use a scale in Tailwind?
text: Yes: Copy Tailwind gives a colour group keyed by token, and Design tokens… › Tailwind Config gives a full configuration file.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: Do I need an account?
text: No.

title: Shade Library FAQ
heading: Is there an API?
text: Yes. The heading links to the Shade Library API guide, and the Automate this note names GET /v1/shade/library . See [Public API](../../../../../services/public-api/README.md).

title: Shade Library glossary
text: Term Meaning --- --- Auto text The better of near-black ( 111111 ) or white text for a token: near-black on tokens with luminance above 0.5, white otherwise. Base The colour a scale is built around, usually near its middle. Contrast ratio The WCAG 2 lightness-difference measure, 1:1 to 21:1. 4.5:1 is AA for body text; 3:1 for large text. Even steps A scale in which no step between neighbouring tokens is much larger than the average step. Min adjacent contrast The contrast between the two most similar neighbouring tokens. OKLCH A perceptual colour space: lightness (0 to 1), chroma (colourfulness) and hue angle. Profile The Shade summary badge: Neutral, Hue Shift, Light, Deep or Balanced. Scale (shade system, ramp) One colour taken through lightness in named steps. Shade A darker version of a colour, towards black. Tint A lighter version of a colour, towards white. Token A named step in a scale, such as 500 .

title: Limits and accuracy
text: - Contrast uses the WCAG 2 formula. "Auto AA" tests each token against near-black or white, whichever the page picks from the token's luminance (the split is at 0.5). The other text colour can sometimes do slightly better; check WCAG vs white and WCAG vs black on the token cards. - Averages (lightness and chroma) are across all tokens, so a scale with a very light start and a very dark end can average Mid . - Base hue is the hue of the base colour only. Scales from the Temperature Shift and Duotone Shift methods deliberately change hue along the ramp; their Hue span shows how much. - Score is recorded with each scale when it was generated. It is a ranking aid, not a judgement of fitness for your project. - Evenness : the 8.2% figure is reported by the page; there is no per-scale evenness figure or filter in the current page. - The three-word colour names on Inspect come from fixed OKLCH bands and are descriptions, not standard names. - Swatches look different on different screens; the values do not. - The library is not an accessibility audit of your design. Where a token sits (text, border, background) and at what size still decides whether it passes.

title: Documentation
text: The documentation library is where Auric Artisan publishes the written guide for each tool. Its heading, "Every tool, twice", describes the idea: most subjects have two documents — a user guide , which explains how to use the tool, and a developer reference , which explains how it works and what it computes. You pick the subject, then pick which of the two you want. The index lists 54 subjects and 89 documents. 35 subjects have both a guide and a reference; the others have one. Subjects cover the site's tools (such as the URL Analyzer, Vision Simulation and the Font Library), the colour libraries, the browser extension and design-tool plugins, the generators behind the libraries, and the public REST API, including guides to using the Palette, Gradient, Harmony, Shade and accessibility collections from your own code.

title: Documentation
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone who wants step-by-step help with a tool: read its user guide. - Developers and technical users who want to know exactly what a tool measures and how: read its developer reference. - Developers automating the site's tools: read the API guides and the endpoint reference.

title: Getting started

text: 1. Type part of the tool's name or a word from its description into the search box, for example gamut . 2. If nothing matches, the page says No subject matches that. Try a tool name.

title: Getting started
heading: Show only guides or only references
text: Select Guides to hide every Reference button, or References to hide every Guide button. Subjects that have only the other kind disappear, and the count changes to match. Select Both to show everything again. You can link straight to a filtered view: add ?audience=guide or ?audience=reference to the address, for example https://auricartisan.com/library/documentation/?audience=reference.

title: Getting started
heading: Which should I read?
text: - User guide — how to use a tool: what each control does, workflows, exports and good practice. - Developer reference — how the tool works: the formulas, data and methods behind it. Useful when you need to know exactly what a number means. - API guides (the subjects whose names end in "API") — how to get the same results from your own code.

title: Read a guide
text: Documentation articles share a three-column layout on wide screens: every subject on the left, the article in the middle, and its contents on the right. On narrow screens the columns stack.

title: Read a guide
heading: The parts of the page
text: Part What it does --- --- Subject list (left) Headed Documentation . Every subject, alphabetically; the current one is highlighted and scrolled into view. Select a subject to open its first document. Breadcrumb Documentation › the subject's name. Select Documentation to return to the index. Pair switch User guide and Developer reference . The current document is highlighted; select the other to switch. If a subject has only one document, the missing half is shown greyed out, with the tooltip "No user guide for this subject yet" or "No developer reference for this subject yet". Title and introduction The subject's name and a short introduction. Author and dates Who wrote the document and when it was published or updated, where the article states them. On this page (right) The article's numbered sections. Select one to jump to it. On narrow screens it is a collapsible list. Sections The article itself. Code blocks Each has a Copy button. After copying it reads Copied ; if your browser blocks the clipboard it reads Press Ctrl C so you can copy by hand. Tables Wide tables scroll sideways rather than stretching the page. Pager (end) The pair — a link to the other document for this subject — and Next subject , the next subject alphabetically.

title: Read a guide
heading: Tips
text: - Read the user guide first, then the developer reference when you need to know exactly what a figure means. - Guides were written for the tool as it was on their stated date. If a guide and the tool disagree, trust the tool, and check this documentation set for the current behaviour. - The API guides include ready-made requests; the full endpoint list is at https://auricartisan.com/library/documentation/api/.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A subject disappeared when I chose Guides or References
text: Why: The subject has only the other kind of document. Hiding it avoids showing a row with nothing to open. What to do: Select Both .

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "No subject matches that. Try a tool name."
text: Why: No subject name or description contains your text. What to do: Use a shorter word, or the tool's name as it appears in the site's menus. Descriptions use US spelling ("color").

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The guide does not match what I see in the tool
text: Why: Guides are dated. Some tools have been redesigned since their guide was written — for example the Accessibility Library and the Palette Library. What to do: Trust the tool. Check the date on the guide, and see this documentation set for current behaviour.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The side list or the pair switch is missing
text: Why: The article could not load the list of subjects, for example because the connection dropped. The article itself is still complete. What to do: Reload the page. Use the breadcrumb or your browser's back button to reach the index.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Press Ctrl C" appears instead of "Copied"
text: Why: Your browser blocked clipboard access. What to do: The code is selected for you; press Ctrl + C (on a Mac, the equivalent copy command).

title: Documentation FAQ
heading: What is the difference between a user guide and a developer reference?
text: A user guide shows how to use a tool. A developer reference explains how it works — the methods, formulas and data behind the results.

title: Documentation FAQ
heading: Why do some subjects have only one document?
text: Some tools have only a guide so far, and some subjects (such as a measurement method behind a tool) have only a reference. The pair switch on each article shows which half exists.

title: Documentation FAQ
heading: Where is the API documentation?
text: The API guides are listed as subjects ending in "API", and the full endpoint reference is at https://auricartisan.com/library/documentation/api/. See also [Public API](../../../../services/public-api/README.md).

title: Documentation FAQ
heading: Can I follow new documents?
text: Yes, with the RSS feed at https://auricartisan.com/library/documentation/rss.xml.

title: Documentation FAQ
heading: Does the documentation library work without JavaScript?
text: Yes. The index is a plain list of links; search, the audience filter and the article side list are added on top.

title: Privacy
text: The documentation index and articles do not ask for any information and do not keep a history of what you read. Search and the audience filter run in your browser. The audience you choose can be part of the page address ( ?audience=… ), so it appears in your browser history like any other address. Articles download a list of subjects from auricartisan.com to build the side list and the pair switch. Analytics on the site follow your consent choices. See [Company and legal](../../../company-and-legal/README.md).

title: Learn
text: Learn is Auric Artisan's library of long-form articles about colour: 113 articles that run, in the page's words, "from what light is to how a press holds a colour". The Learn page presents them as a course, in the order they were written to be read, numbered 1 to 113, with about 64 hours of reading in total. You can start at article 1 and work through, or filter by one of seven categories — Foundations, Physics, Vision, Colorimetry, Digital, Design and Print — and take the part you need. Most articles are interactive. They include live demos (the site calls them labs) that you can open in a panel, adjust and explore — spectra you can reshape, contrast you can test, gamuts you can rotate — and end with a short quiz and a "Continue your journey" section that suggests what to read next based on the article, the course order and what you have already read. The Learn page remembers how far you have got, in your browser. It shows a tick next to articles you have read, a progress bar, and a link to pick up where you left off.

title: Learn
heading: Who it is for
text: - Students and self-learners who want a structured course in colour science. - Designers and developers who want the reasoning behind contrast, colour spaces, gradients and colour management. - Accessibility specialists who need the background to colour vision deficiency and contrast standards. - Anyone curious about why the sky is blue or why hot things glow.

title: Learn
heading: Where to find it
text: - The Learn page: https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/ - From any page: the site header's Learn menu, Learning Hub ("Practical color science lessons"). - Articles live at https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/articles/ followed by the article's name. - An RSS feed is available at https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/rss.xml. No account is needed.

title: Learn
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/. 2. Read the line under the heading: how many articles there are and how long the course takes. 3. Select a category chip, such as Vision , or type a topic into Search titles and topics . 4. Select an article title to open it. 5. Use the table of contents to move around, and open a Live demo to try the idea for yourself. 6. Answer the quiz at the end, then choose a suggestion under Continue your journey . 7. Come back to the Learn page later: it shows Pick up where you left off or Next in the course .

title: Learn
heading: What you can do
text: - Read 113 articles in course order or by category, with reading times. - Search titles, summaries and categories. - Track your progress in this browser, with ticks, a progress bar and a resume link. - Open interactive demos in a panel that can be docked or made full screen. - Test yourself with a quiz at the end of each article. - Get personalised "Continue your journey" suggestions, pin articles to the top of them, and rotate for more. - Print an article, or download it as Markdown or plain text.

title: Getting started
heading: Open the Learn page
text: Go to https://auricartisan.com/library/learn/, or choose Learning Hub from the Learn menu in the site header.

title: Getting started
heading: The page, top to bottom
text: Learn , with a line such as: "Every article on this site about colour, in the order it was written to be read — 113 of them, about 64 hours end to end, from what light is to how a press holds a colour. Start at one, or take the part you need." Once you have opened at least one article, a panel appears under the heading: - Pick up where you left off — the article you opened most recently and did not finish; or - Next in the course — the first article, in course order, that you have not read. It shows the article's number, title, category and reading time, and a progress bar with a line such as 12 of 113 read · about 58 hours to go . - Search titles and topics — type one or more words. An article is shown when every word appears in its number, title, summary or category. The list updates as you type. - Category chips — All and the seven categories, in the order the course introduces them: Foundations , Physics , Vision , Colorimetry , Digital , Design , Print . Each chip shows how many articles it holds. Select a chip to show only that category; select it again (or All ) to show everything. When you have narrowed the list, a line shows how much is left, for example 17 of 113 · about 11 hours . One row per article, in course order: - the article's number; - its title (select it to open the article); - its category and reading time, for example Vision and 55 min ; - a tick if you have read it; - a one-sentence summary. The article marked as next for you is highlighted. If nothing matches your search, the page says Nothing in the course matches that. with a Show all articles button that clears the search and the category. A note points to the [blog](../../blog/README.md) for shorter notes on what is being built, and the [changelog](../../changelog/README.md) for release detail.

title: Getting started
heading: How "read" is decided
text: An article counts as read once you have scrolled at least 55% of the way through it. The page remembers the furthest point you reached in each article, in this browser. See [Privacy](../others/privacy.md).

title: Getting started
heading: Your first task: start the course
text: 1. Open the Learn page. 2. Select article 1 , What Color Is and How Humans See It . 3. Read it, trying the live demos as you go. 4. Scroll to the end and answer the quiz. 5. Return to the Learn page. Article 1 now shows a tick, and Next in the course points to article 2. Result: you have started the course, and the Learn page will keep your place in this browser. The four families of printing and how each physically lays ink — explored with interactive plate cross-sections, ink-film models, and a process chooser.

title: Learn article catalogue
heading: Notes
text: - The Learn page folds three smaller categories into their neighbours: articles tagged Computational are listed under Colorimetry, and articles tagged Measurement or Workflows under Digital. This catalogue follows the Learn page. - For how to find, read and track articles, see [Getting started](getting-started.md) and [Read an article](read-an-article.md).

title: Continue your journey
text: Every Learn article ends with Continue your journey . Instead of a fixed list, the page suggests seven articles chosen for the one you are reading and for what you have already read in this browser.

title: Continue your journey
heading: What you see
text: - A line above the cards: Tailored to the article's category, followed by You've read N of 113 in the library . - A More like this button, when there are more suggestions to show. - One featured card, full width — usually the natural next article. - Six more cards. Each card has an illustration coloured by category, a small badge giving the reason it was chosen, the title, the category, a tick if you have read it, and a pin button. Badge Meaning --- --- Pinned You pinned this article. Up next in a category The next unread article in the same category, in course order. Shares a topic It shares one or more topic tags with the current article. More in a category It is in the same category. Related idea Its title or summary shares key words with the current article. Recommended A good general match.

title: Continue your journey
heading: How suggestions are chosen
text: The page scores every other article against the one you are reading: - same category: a strong boost; - each shared topic tag: a boost; - shared key words in title and summary: a small boost; - close to it in course order within the same category: a small boost; - not yet read: a boost; already read: a penalty (read articles can still appear); - the next unread article in the same category: an extra boost, so it usually takes the featured slot; - pinned by you: always first. To keep the list varied, no more than three suggestions from one category come first; the rest follow.

title: Continue your journey
heading: Pin an article
text: 1. Select the pin button on a card. Its label reads "Pin" and the title; its tooltip says Pin to top . 2. The suggestions are re-ranked, and the pinned article moves to the front with the Pinned badge. 3. To unpin, select the pin again (tooltip Pinned — click to unpin ). Pins are kept in this browser and apply on every article, so a pinned article stays at the front of the suggestions until you unpin it. These pins are separate from pins elsewhere on the site.

title: Continue your journey
heading: See more
text: Select More like this to show the next seven suggestions. Select it again to keep rotating; it wraps back to the start.

title: Continue your journey
heading: If the suggestions do not change
text: If the page cannot load the Learn catalogue (for example when offline), or the article is not in it, the author's original suggestions stay in place. They are still good links; they just are not personalised.

title: Continue your journey
heading: Result
text: You always have a sensible next step: the next article in the course, the closest related ideas, and the articles you chose to keep.

title: Read an article
text: Every Learn article follows the same layout. This page walks through it from top to bottom.

title: Read an article
heading: The header
text: - A small line reading Auric Artisan · Learn above the title. - The title and an introductory paragraph. - A row of facts, each with a bold label: the article's category and its number in the course (for example "Physics · 112"), how many live demos it has, the reading time (for example "~30 min"), and its subject. - Three actions: Action What it does --- --- Download Opens a small menu: Markdown (".md — Formatted, portable text") or Plain text (".txt — Just the words"). The file is made in your browser from the article's text; interactive demos, figures and the quiz are left out. Print Opens your browser's print dialog. ← All Articles Returns to the Learn page. Downloaded files are named after the article, without the date, for example the-color-of-heat.md . Each starts with the title, the introduction and a "Source:" line with the article's address. Press Escape to close the Download menu.

title: Read an article
heading: The table of contents
text: A Table of Contents lists the article's numbered sections. Select an entry to jump to it. A reading-progress bar at the top of the window fills as you scroll.

title: Read an article
heading: Sections
text: Articles are divided into numbered sections, typically: an introduction, several teaching sections each with a live demo, The terms, defined (a glossary), What it means for color (practical takeaways), Test your understanding , and Continue your journey . Sections fade in as you reach them.

title: Read an article
heading: Live demos
text: Each interactive lab appears in the article as a wide button labelled Live demo , with the demo's name and Expand . 1. Select the button. The demo opens in a panel over the page, marked Live , Article and Dockable . 2. Use the demo's own controls — sliders, buttons, colour pickers — and read the explanation beside it. 3. Use the panel buttons: Button What it does --- --- Dock panel Docks the panel to the side so you can read the article beside the demo. Select again to undock. Full screen Enlarges the panel to fill the window. Select again to restore. Close Closes the panel. Escape does the same. Docked and full screen are exclusive: turning one on turns the other off. Demos run entirely in your browser and do not need an account.

title: Read an article
heading: Test your understanding
text: Near the end, Quick check asks multiple-choice questions one at a time — six in recent articles. Choose an answer to see feedback, then select Next → . A counter shows your place, for example Question 1 of 6 .

title: Read an article
heading: Continue your journey
text: The last section suggests what to read next. On articles in the catalogue, the page replaces the author's fixed suggestions with personalised ones, and a line above them says, for example, Tailored to Physics · You've read 12 of 113 in the library . See [Continue your journey](continue-your-journey.md).

title: Read an article
heading: The foot of the article
text: A line gives the article's place in the course, for example Article 112 of 113 .

title: Read an article
heading: Keeping your place
text: As you scroll, the article records how far you got, in this browser. Once you pass 55% of the page, the article counts as read on the Learn page and in Continue your journey . Reaching the bottom is not required.

title: Read an article

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The Learn page shows a plain list, with no search or categories
text: Why: The page could not load the Learn catalogue, so it shows the built-in list of all articles instead. What to do: Check your connection and reload. Every link in the plain list still works.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: My progress and ticks have gone
text: Why: Progress is kept in this browser only. It does not follow you to another browser or device, and clearing this site's data, or using a private window, removes it. What to do: Nothing can restore it. Reading past 55% of an article marks it as read again.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: An article I finished is not ticked
text: Why: An article counts as read when you have scrolled at least 55% of the way through it. Jumping straight to the end with the table of contents still counts; reading only the top half does not. What to do: Scroll through the article.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Continue your journey" is the same on every visit
text: Why: If the Learn catalogue cannot load, or the article is not in it, the author's original suggestions stay. What to do: Reload with a working connection. Also note that pinned articles always come first.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A live demo will not open, or looks empty
text: Why: Demos need JavaScript and a modern browser. Some content blockers or very old browsers stop them. What to do: Allow scripts for auricartisan.com and use a current browser. Try Full screen if the demo is cramped.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The downloaded file has no demos or pictures
text: Why: Download saves the article's text only. Demos, figures and the quiz are left out by design. What to do: Use Print (or print to PDF) to keep the page as it looks.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Search finds nothing
text: Why: Every word you type must appear in an article's number, title, summary or category. Articles use US spelling in titles ("color"). What to do: Use fewer words, or try the other spelling. Select Show all articles to reset.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The articles
text: The articles are educational explanations of colour science, perception and practice. They are not standards documents; where an article describes a standard (such as WCAG or a CIE formula), the standard itself is the authority. Articles on vision and light — for example colour vision deficiency or light and the body clock — are written to educate, not to diagnose or advise on health. Consult a professional for medical questions.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The demos
text: Demos are teaching models computed in your browser. They follow the published formulas their articles describe, but: - colours on screen depend on your display, its settings and the light around you; - simulations of colour vision deficiency show typical cases, not any particular person's sight; - numbers are rounded for display. Use the site's tools for measurement work (see [Related](related.md)).

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Reading times and categories
text: Reading times are the authors' estimates. Three small categories (Computational, Measurement, Workflows) are folded into Colorimetry and Digital on the Learn page.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Progress tracking
text: "Read" means scrolled past 55% of the page in this browser. It does not know whether you actually read the text, and it is lost if the browser's site data is cleared.

title: Portfolio Builder and Portfolio Index
text: The Portfolio Builder at https://auricartisan.com/portfolio/ turns the work you make on Auric Artisan into a public page. You stack sections — headings, Markdown text, images, galleries, a timeline, stats, testimonials, your saved palettes and more, 25 kinds in all — and type straight into a live preview of the page as it builds beside you. You choose a typeface, a paper and a rhythm, and an accent colour taken from your own saved palettes and graded for contrast. A Check pane audits the rendered page for accessibility problems before anyone else sees it. When it is ready, you publish it at your own address, auricartisan.com/p/your-name , or share it privately as a self-contained link. You can also download it as an HTML file or PDF, or export the document as JSON to keep or move. Publishing again updates the same address, and you can take it down at any time. The Portfolio Index at https://auricartisan.com/portfolios/ lists portfolios in one place — those made with the builder and those people keep on their own sites — searchable by name, craft, place and colour. A builder portfolio joins it when you publish (unless you switch that off); a portfolio on your own site can be added through the Search Console.

title: Portfolio Builder and Portfolio Index
heading: Who it is for
text: - Designers, illustrators, photographers and developers who want a portfolio without building a website. - Anyone who wants to show palettes, gradients and scales they made on Auric Artisan as live, copyable values. - People who want a CV-style page, a studio one-pager or a simple link page. - Visitors looking for designers by craft, place or colour.

text: - The builder: https://auricartisan.com/portfolio/ (also in the Tools menu and on the Collections page as Portfolio Builder ). - Published portfolios: https://auricartisan.com/p/ followed by the owner's address. - The directory: https://auricartisan.com/portfolios/ - You need an Auric Artisan account, signed in, to build and publish. Viewing portfolios and the directory needs no account.

title: Portfolio Builder and Portfolio Index
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Sign in and open https://auricartisan.com/portfolio/. 2. Select Templates , pick one (for example Designer ) and select Use this template . 3. Fill in the Header : your name, headline and the details you want to show. 4. Click any text in the live preview and type over the examples. 5. Open Style and choose a typeface, paper, rhythm and accent. 6. Open Check and fix anything marked blocking. 7. Select Publish , choose Public at an address , type your address and select Publish . 8. Copy the address and share it.

title: Portfolio Builder and Portfolio Index
heading: What you can do
text: - Build a page from 25 section types, and type directly into the preview. - Start from eight templates: Designer, Developer, Photographer, Freelancer, Founder, Writer, Resume and Minimal. - Write in Markdown, or paste your own HTML and CSS into a sanitised Raw HTML section. - Show your saved palettes as live swatches visitors can copy as CSS or JSON. - Style the page with four typefaces, five papers, three rhythms and a graded accent. - Preview at fit, desktop, tablet and mobile widths, and full screen. - Audit contrast, links, alt text, headings and target sizes before publishing. - Undo and redo; your draft saves itself in the browser and, when signed in, to your account. - Export HTML, PDF or JSON; import JSON; copy a snapshot link. - Publish at your own address with a QR code, a share card, a view count and control over search, the index and PDF downloads. - Find portfolios in the Portfolio Index, and list yours — including one you host elsewhere.

title: Getting started
heading: Your first portfolio
text: 1. Select Templates . The Start from a template dialog opens. 2. Choose Designer and select Use this template . The page fills with example sections. 3. In Header , type your Name and a Headline / tagline . Leave fields blank to use your profile details. 4. In the preview, click the Selected Work heading and any example text, and type your own. 5. Open Style , choose a Typeface and Paper , and pick an accent from your palettes. 6. Open Check . If it lists anything as Blocking , fix it; the Publish button stays disabled until you do. 7. Select Publish . Choose Public at an address , type an address in Your address and wait for it to be confirmed as available. 8. Select Publish . The dialog shows your live address with Copy , Open and QR code . title: Edit in the preview
text: The live preview is not only a picture of your page: you can write in it. Click a heading and type; the change is saved and appears everywhere the portfolio goes.

title: Edit in the preview
heading: Type into the page
text: 1. Hover over text in the preview. Editable text shows a faint outline. 2. Click it. A coloured outline shows you are editing. 3. Type. Empty fields show grey example text until you fill them. 4. Finish: - Enter finishes a one-line field (a heading, a name, a button label). - In longer fields (quotes, descriptions, code, Markdown), Enter starts a new line; click elsewhere to finish. - Escape finishes too. Pasting into a plain field pastes text only, without formatting. Section Editable in the page --- --- Heading The heading text Text / Markdown The whole text (kept as Markdown) Two columns Each column (kept as Markdown) Quote The quote and the attribution Testimonial The quote, name and role Callout The text (kept as Markdown) Button The label Call to action The heading, text and button label Image The caption Code The code Skills / Tags The title Timeline The title, and each entry's date, title, subtitle and description Stats The title, and each metric's value and label Feature list The title, and each feature's title and description Steps The title, and each step's title and description FAQ / Accordion The title, and each question and answer Everything else — image addresses, embeds, tables, links, alignment, tone, columns, which palettes to show — is a choice rather than words, so it lives on the section's card. Clicking such a section in the preview selects it and opens its card in the Content column, ready to edit. Buttons and links in the preview do not navigate while you are building; clicking one means "edit this".
