title: Export and import
heading: The credit line
text: At the foot of the menu, the switch "Made with Auric Artisan" credit — "On every exported HTML and PDF. Paid plans can drop it." — adds a small "Made with Auric Artisan" line at the end of exported files. - On a paid plan that includes watermark-free exports, you can switch it off. - On a free plan, switching it off explains that watermark-free exports are a paid perk; the portfolio, the editor and every export stay free. See [Account and billing](../../account-and-billing/README.md). The switch affects downloads only, not your published page.

title: Export and import
heading: Printing and PDF
text: The PDF comes from your browser's print function. The page is set to print its colours and background exactly; if your browser still drops backgrounds, turn on its "Background graphics" option. If nothing opens, the builder says Allow pop-ups to print.

title: Export and import
heading: Snapshot links
text: A snapshot link carries the entire portfolio inside the address itself (after ). Opening it shows the page at https://auricartisan.com/portfolio/public/ without any account. - It is a copy taken at that moment: later edits do not change it. - It works without a published address, and keeps working offline once opened. - Portfolios with several embedded images make very long links, which some apps and sites will not accept. A large avatar is left out of snapshot links. - Nothing is stored on the site. See [The published page](the-published-page.md) for what a visitor sees.

title: Export and import
heading: Result
text: You have your portfolio as a file you can host or print, a JSON backup you can restore, or a link that works anywhere.

title: Header and avatar
text: The Header panel at the top of the Content column controls the top of your portfolio: "The top of your portfolio. Leave a field blank to follow your profile."

title: Header and avatar
heading: The fields
text: Field Limit Show switch Notes --- --- --- --- Name 80 characters Always shown Blank follows your profile's display name. Headline / tagline 120 characters Always shown Also used on your share card. Email 120 characters Show — off by default The address you publish can differ from the one you sign in with. Location 80 characters Show — on by default Placeholder "City, Country". Website 200 characters Show — on by default — Avatar (image address) 500 characters Show — on by default Or pick a picture (below). Accent A colour picker — The page's accent colour, also set from Style . A blank field is not "no value" — it means "use my profile". The profile's value appears as grey placeholder text in the empty field, so you can see what the page will say. Type into the field to use a different value just for your portfolio; clear it to go back to following your profile. Changes to your profile then reach the portfolio automatically. A Show switch that is off keeps that detail off the page, off exports and out of anything you publish or share, even if the field has a value. The Use the built-in header switch turns the whole header block (name, avatar, headline and details) on or off. Turn it off when your page has its own opening — for example a Raw HTML hero — so it is not preceded by a second one. While it is off, the Avatar, Location and Email switches are greyed out.

title: Header and avatar
heading: Choose an avatar
text: 1. Double-click the avatar circle in the Header panel, or double-click your picture in the preview ("Double-click to choose a picture"). 2. Pick an image file. 3. The builder resizes it to a small square, stores it inside your portfolio and confirms Avatar updated. Because the picture is stored in the portfolio, it travels with every export, snapshot link and publish. Resizing also removes hidden photo information (such as camera and location data) from the file. Messages you may see: - Turn the built-in header on first. — the header is switched off. - That picture is too large even shrunk. Try a smaller one. - That file could not be read as a picture. You can also paste an image address into Avatar instead. With no avatar, the page shows your initial. Note: A snapshot link has little room, so a large avatar is left out of snapshot links (the initial is shown instead). Published pages keep it.

title: Header and avatar
heading: Result
text: The top of your portfolio says exactly who you are, with only the details you chose to show.

title: List your portfolio
text: There are two ways into the [Portfolio Index](portfolio-index.md): publish with the Portfolio Builder, or add a portfolio you keep on your own site through the Search Console.

title: List your portfolio
heading: A portfolio made with the builder
text: 1. Publish your portfolio at an address (see [Publish and share](publish-and-share.md)). 2. In the publish dialog's settings, keep Let search engines list it and List it in the Portfolio Index switched on (both are on by default). 3. Wait a little: builder portfolios are copied into the index within fifteen minutes of publishing. It joins as Made here , with its palette, crafts and headline. Changes you publish later are copied in the same way. To leave the index, switch off List it in the Portfolio Index (or Let search engines list it ) and select Publish these changes . Unpublishing also removes it.

title: List your portfolio
heading: A portfolio on your own site
text: You add these in the Search Console's Portfolios tab at https://auricartisan.com/search/console/ portfolios (the Add one you host button on the index goes there). You need to be signed in. 1. Open the Portfolios tab. It lists Made with the Portfolio Builder and Kept on your own sites . 2. Under Add a portfolio you keep elsewhere , fill in: Field Required Notes --- --- --- Address Yes For example https://yourname.com/work/ . Name Yes Yours, or the studio's. Up to 120 characters. Where you work No City, country. Up to 80 characters. One line about the work No Up to 200 characters. Craft No Comma between, up to 8. Colours you work in No Hex codes, up to 8. Swatches preview them. What people will find it by No A few sentences, up to 600 characters. 3. Select Add it . What happens next depends on the address: - On a site you have verified in the Search Console's Your sites tab: "Verified: … is proved to be yours, so it goes into the index straight away." It appears with a Verified mark. - On any other site : "Not a site you have verified here, so a person reviews it before it appears." It shows as Waiting for review until a reviewer approves it, and then appears as Reviewed . To get the Verified mark, verify your site first. See the [Search documentation](../../search/README.md) for how to prove you own a site. There is a limit to how many portfolios one account can add: "That is as many as one account can add. Take one out to add another."

title: List your portfolio
heading: Check your entries
text: The Portfolios tab shows each entry with its status: Status Meaning --- --- In the index Listed and searchable. Verified On a site you have proved is yours. Waiting for review Someone will check it before it appears. Featured Chosen to be shown first. Hidden by a moderator Removed from view by a reviewer; a "Reviewer's reason" may be shown. Not in the index / Not listed Not currently listed. Joining on the next copy A builder portfolio that will appear at the next copy. For your builder portfolio, the tab also explains why it might not be listed — for example that you switched off List it in the Portfolio Index , or that it asks search engines not to list it — with Change it in the builder .

title: List your portfolio
heading: Change or remove an external entry
text: - Select Change on the entry, edit the fields, and select Save changes (or Cancel ). Edits to an entry that is not on a verified site go back for review. - Select Take it out to remove it: "It leaves the index now." You can keep it instead with Keep it .

title: List your portfolio
heading: Result
text: Your portfolio is in the index, marked Verified if you proved the site is yours, and you can see its status and change or remove it at any time.

title: Manage sections
text: A portfolio is a stack of sections , shown top to bottom in the order you set. Each section has a card in the Content column.

title: Manage sections
heading: Add a section
text: Any of these adds one: - Add a section at the foot of the Content column: type in Search sections… to narrow the 25 types, then select a tile. Each tile shows the type's name and a short hint; hover for the hint. If nothing matches, it says No sections match that search. The builder confirms, for example, Added a Timeline section. - In the preview, the add control at the end of the page, or Add a section below on a section's rail (see [Edit in the preview](edit-in-the-preview.md)). - The command field: type "add" and choose, for example, Add a Gallery section . New sections start empty; grey example text (placeholders) shows what goes where, and disappears as you type. With no sections yet, the column says No sections yet — add one below to start building.

title: Manage sections
heading: The section card
text: Control What it does --- --- Drag handle (⠿) Drag to reorder ("Drag to reorder"). Chevron (▾) Expand or collapse the card's fields. Type icon and name Which kind of section it is. Hidden badge Shown when the section is hidden from the portfolio. Eye button Hide from portfolio / Show in portfolio . Hidden sections stay in your draft but are left out of the page, exports and publishing. ↑ / ↓ Move up / Move down . More actions (⋯) Move to top , Move to bottom , Duplicate , Delete . Messages confirm actions, such as Section duplicated. and Section removed — Ctrl+Z to undo.

title: Manage sections
heading: Bulk actions
text: Above the cards, a bar shows the section count, Collapse all (or Expand all ) and Bulk actions ▾ : Action Effect Message --- --- --- Expand all Opens every card. All sections expanded. Collapse all Closes every card. All sections collapsed. Show all sections Un-hides every section. All sections shown in the portfolio. Hide all sections Hides every section. All sections hidden from the portfolio. Reverse order Flips the order. Section order reversed. Clear all sections Deletes every section. All sections cleared — Ctrl+Z to undo. Every bulk action can be undone.

title: Manage sections
heading: Tips
text: - Hide a section instead of deleting it when you might want it back later. - A page where every section is hidden cannot be meaningfully published; the publish dialog warns Every section is hidden — the page would be empty . - The section count in the top bar and in the preview bar counts all sections, hidden or not.

title: Manage sections
heading: Result
text: Your sections are in the order you want, with the ones you are not ready to show hidden.

title: Markdown and Raw HTML
heading: Markdown
text: Markdown is a simple way to format text with ordinary characters: bold , Heading , - item . The Text / Markdown , Two columns , Callout and FAQ answer fields accept it. You type You get --- --- Heading to Heading Headings, levels 1 to 6 bold , italic Bold, italic [label](https://example.com) A link [label](https://example.com "Title") A link with a title <https://example.com or a bare https://example.com A link ![alt text](https://example.com/pic.png) An image code Inline code A line of three or more - , or A horizontal rule quoted A block quote (quotes can contain other Markdown) - item or 1. item , indented for sub-items Lists, including nested lists - [ ] task , - [x] done Task lists, shown as ticked or unticked boxes that visitors cannot change A pipe table with a --- row, and :---: for alignment A table; wide tables scroll sideways Three backticks, optionally followed by a language A code block Tips: - Links and images need full https:// addresses. An address with spaces can be wrapped in angle brackets: <https://example.com/my file.png . - Images from other websites load on your published page as long as they are served over https:// . - A line break inside a paragraph is kept as a line break.

title: Markdown and Raw HTML
heading: Raw HTML
text: The Raw HTML section lets you paste your own markup and styles. Because your published page is opened by strangers, the builder cleans the HTML first. - Page structure: div , span , section , article , header , footer , main , nav , aside , figure , details and summary , headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, hr . - Text markup: strong , em , code , pre , blockquote , mark , small , sub , sup , abbr , time , kbd and similar. - Media: img , picture , source , video , audio , track ; also progress and meter . - Inline SVG for icons and diagrams: shapes, paths, text, gradients, masks and clip paths. - Attributes: class , id , style , role , aria- , data- , title , lang and each element's usual attributes (such as href , src , alt ). -

title: The Portfolio Index
text: The Portfolio Index at https://auricartisan.com/portfolios/ is "Every portfolio, in one place": portfolios made with the Portfolio Builder and portfolios people keep on their own sites, "searched together by name, craft, place and colour". Anyone can browse it; no account is needed.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: The page
text: - The heading, with Publish yours (opens the Portfolio Builder) and Add one you host (opens the Search Console's Portfolios tab). - Four counts: In the index , Made here , From elsewhere , Verified . - The search box. - Source buttons, Filters , the results, and How a portfolio gets in .

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: Search
text: Type into Search by name, craft, place or a colour like d3af37 , or press / anywhere on the page to jump to it. Results update as you type; Escape clears the box. Words are matched against names, headlines, crafts, places and descriptions, with allowance for typing mistakes and word beginnings. You can also use: You type It means --- --- "exact words" Those words together, in that order. -word Leave out results with that word. A hex colour such as d3af37 Portfolios whose colours are nearest to it come first (colours are compared perceptually, in OKLab). tag:branding or tag:"brand identity" A craft. in:lisbon A place. made:here / made:elsewhere Builder portfolios / portfolios on other sites. is:verified or verified Verified portfolios only. Under the box, Try offers example tokens — such as made:here , is:verified and a colour — built from what is in the index; select one to put it in the box.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: Filter
text: Control Options --- --- Source buttons All , Made here , Elsewhere , each with a count. Filters Opens the filter row; a number shows how many are on. Verified only Only portfolios whose owner proved the site is theirs. Colour Colour family : Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Teal, Blue, Violet, Pink, Neutral. Craft The crafts in the index ( · none yet when there are none). Location The places in the index. Every count reflects your other filters, so you can see what each choice would leave. Active filters are shown as removable chips.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: Sort and view
text: Sort Order --- --- Best match By relevance to your search. Recently updated Featured portfolios first, then most recently updated. Newest Newest first. Name, A to Z Alphabetical. Most viewed Most viewed first. Grid and List switch the layout. In the grid, a featured portfolio at the top gets a larger spotlight card.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: The cards
text: Each card shows the portfolio's colours as a cover, its source ( Made here or Elsewhere ), a Verified mark ("The owner proved it is theirs") or Reviewed for a checked external entry, an avatar or initials, the name and place, the headline, up to four crafts, where it lives, when it was updated, and Open portfolio . External portfolios open in a new tab. The list view shows the same facts in a row. Results come 24 at a time; Show N more of M loads the next batch.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: Messages
text: Message Meaning --- --- Loading the index… The index is loading. "N portfolios" (and "for" your search) The number of results. Nothing matches your search / No portfolios match these filters Loosen the search or filters. The index is empty so far. No portfolios have been listed yet. The index is new. The first few get the front row. Only a few portfolios are listed. The portfolio index could not be reached The page could not load the index; try again later.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: Share a search
text: The address of the page updates with your search, filters, sort and view, so you can copy it to share exactly what you are looking at, and the browser's Back button steps back through your changes.

title: The Portfolio Index
heading: How a portfolio gets in
text: The page explains three steps: 1. Publish, or add an address — "Builder portfolios are copied in within fifteen minutes of publishing. Portfolios on other sites are added in the Search Console." 2. Proof lists it at once — an address on a site you have verified goes in straight away, marked Verified; anything else waits for someone on the Auric Artisan team to review it. 3. Found by what it holds — name, craft, place and colour. "Leave whenever you like: switch off “List it in the Portfolio Index” the next time you publish." See [List your portfolio](list-your-portfolio.md). The index is searched in your browser and needs JavaScript. Without it, every builder portfolio is still at its own address.

title: Preview and check
heading: Preview widths
text: The Live preview bar has four width buttons: Button Width Use --- --- --- Fit (default) The width of the preview column, at full size Writing and editing. Desktop 1160 px Checking the desktop layout. Tablet 800 px Checking a tablet layout. Mobile 390 px Checking a phone layout. The bar shows the current width (for example Desktop · 1160px ) and the number of sections. Desktop, Tablet and Mobile may be scaled down to fit the column; Fit is the width to write at. The builder remembers your choice in this browser. Fullscreen preview (the button at the right of the bar) enlarges the preview to fill the screen; select it again, or press Escape , to leave.

title: Preview and check
heading: Full preview in a new tab
text: Select Preview in the top bar (or the command Open a full preview ). The finished page opens in a new tab, exactly as an exported HTML file would look. If nothing opens, the builder says Allow pop-ups to preview. — allow pop-ups for auricartisan.com.

title: Preview and check
heading: The Check pane
text: Open Check . It audits the page as it is actually rendered — the colours, sizes and text a visitor will get — against WCAG 2.2 AA. Finding Severity What it means The fix it suggests --- --- --- --- Text below AA Blocking when well below; otherwise a warning Normal text is under 4.5:1 against its background. "Take a darker step from the same palette in Style, or change the paper." Large text below AA Blocking when well below; otherwise a warning Large text (24 px, or about 19 px bold) is under 3:1. "Deepen this colour, or set the text larger so the 3:1 threshold applies." A link with no text Blocking A link with nothing readable inside it. "Give it text, or an aria-label if it is deliberately an icon." A link that does not say where it goes Blocking Link text such as "click here", "here", "read more", "more", "link", "this", "learn more" or "see more". "Name the destination in the link itself." An image with no alt text Blocking An image with no description for screen readers. "Describe what the image shows, or set alt="" if it is decoration." Heading jumps from hN to hM Warning A heading level is skipped, for example h2 to h4. "Make this an h3, or add the level it skipped." A target smaller than 24px Warning A link or button smaller than 24 × 24 pixels. "Give it padding, or set a minimum height." A colour this check could not read Warning Text in a colour format the check does not measure (for example from Raw HTML). "Pick this colour from the Style pane, which works in sRGB and is graded." Each finding explains why it matters and names the section it is in. Contrast findings show the colour pair and ratio, for example " 9A8F7B on FBFAF7 is 3.05:1". 1. Read the summary: how many faults, in how many places, and how many would stop the page going online — or "None of them blocks publishing." 2. When there are several kinds, use the filter chips All , Blocking and Contrast . 3. Select a finding. The preview scrolls to it and outlines the element. 4. Fix it in the section card, the preview, or Style . The pane updates. When everything passes, it says the pairs checked "against WCAG 2.2 AA. Nothing to fix." If the preview has not rendered yet, it says The preview has not rendered yet. While any Blocking finding remains, the Publish button is disabled and its tooltip says, for example, "2 things to fix in Check before this can go online". Warnings do not block publishing. Saving and exporting are never blocked. While you work in Content , a dot on the Check tab tells you there is something to look at.

title: Preview and check
heading: Result
text: You have seen the page at every width, and it goes online without contrast, link, alt-text or heading problems.

title: Publish and share
text: Select Publish in the top bar. The dialog, headed Portfolio and Put this online , shows Not published until your page is live. If Publish is greyed out, the Check pane has blocking findings to fix first; see [Preview and check](preview-and-check.md).

title: Publish and share
heading: Choose who can see it
text: Choice What it means --- --- Public at an address "Anyone with the link can open it, and it stays current — publish again and the same address shows the new version." Only people I send the link to "No address on the site, and search engines never see it." The builder gives you a snapshot link instead: "The link is the portfolio" — it needs no account, works offline, never updates, and can be too long to paste in some places if the page has several images.

title: Publish and share
heading: Publish at an address
text: 1. Choose Public at an address . 2. In Your address , after auricartisan.com/p/ , type the name you want. - Lower case letters, numbers and hyphens, 2 to 31 characters. - While you type, the field says Checking… , then whether the address is available; a tick shows when it is yours to take. - Under the field, Or take offers suggestions based on your name. 3. Look at the side panel: - What a shared link shows — the card people see when your address is shared in a chat or social app: your name, headline and avatar, "Drawn from your header, and refreshed every time you publish." - Ready to go — a checklist: Address is yours to take , how many sections will be published, Name is set , Headline is set . A missing item says what to do, for example A headline is what the share card shows . 4. Select Publish (it reads Publishing… ). The line under it says "It goes live at once, and you can take it down whenever." 5. The builder confirms Published at and your address.

title: Publish and share
heading: When it is live
text: The dialog title becomes Live since and the date, and shows: Part What it does --- --- Your address For example auricartisan.com/p/your-name . Copy Copies the address ( Copied ). Open Opens the live page. QR code / Hide code Shows a QR code "For a slide or a card" that "Points at the same address, so it keeps working after you republish." Since you published "This is exactly what visitors are seeing." — or "You have edits here that are not published yet." / "You have changed a setting that is not published yet." Publish these changes Appears when there is something new to publish. Updates the live page at the same address. Reach The number of views and "views since" the date you published — "Counted as a number and nothing else — no visitor records, no addresses." The top bar also shows your address and whether it is live.

title: Publish and share
heading: Settings
text: Select Search, the Portfolio Index, PDF and views to open the switches. A summary beside it reads, for example, "In search · In the index · …". Switch Default What it does --- --- --- Let search engines list it On Off keeps it out of Google while the link still works for anyone you send it to. List it in the Portfolio Index On Lists it at https://auricartisan.com/portfolios/, "searchable by craft, place and colour". Needs Let search engines list it on. Allow a PDF download On Visitors get a PDF button for a print-clean copy of the page. Show the view count On Shows views at the foot of the page. You always see the count in the dialog. Change a switch, then select Publish these changes for it to take effect.

title: Publish and share
heading: Take it down
text: Under Take it down : "The address stops working at once. It also becomes free for someone else to take — so if you might come back, leave it up and switch off the search listing instead." 1. Select Unpublish . It changes to Yes, take it down for a few seconds. 2. Select Yes, take it down to confirm. 3. The builder confirms Unpublished. The address no longer shows anything. Your draft stays in the builder; you can publish again later, at the same address if it is still free.

title: Publish and share
heading: Share a private link
text: 1. Choose Only people I send the link to . 2. Select Copy the link . "Nothing is stored on the site." 3. Paste the link to the people you choose.

title: Publish and share
heading: Close
text: Select Close (or press Escape ).

title: Publish and share
heading: Result
text: Your portfolio is live at your own address, or shared privately, and you control whether search engines, the Portfolio Index and PDF downloads can reach it.

title: Save, undo and sync
heading: Autosave
text: There is no Save button. Every change is saved automatically. The top bar shows the state: Label Meaning --- --- Saved Kept in this browser. Tooltip: "Kept in this browser. Sign in and it follows you." Saved to your account Kept in this browser and on your account. Tooltip: "Kept in this browser and on your account". Saving your draft never changes what visitors see. Only Publish does that.

title: Save, undo and sync
heading: Draft sync
text: When you are signed in, your draft is also kept on your account, so it follows you to another browser or device. - Open the builder on another device and it loads the newer copy: Loaded your portfolio from your account. (when this browser had nothing) or Loaded the newer draft from your account. - A brand-new, untouched starter page never overwrites real work on your account. - The builder does not replace a draft you are in the middle of editing. - If the account copy cannot be reached, the builder keeps working in this browser and tries again later.

title: Save, undo and sync
heading: Undo and redo
text: - Select Undo or Redo in the top bar ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)", "Redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z)"), or use the commands Undo and Redo in the command field. - Undo covers adding, editing, moving, hiding, duplicating and deleting sections, bulk actions, templates and imports. - The buttons are greyed out when there is nothing to undo or redo. Many messages remind you, for example Section removed — Ctrl+Z to undo.

title: Save, undo and sync
heading: Keep a copy yourself
text: To keep a backup or move a portfolio between accounts, use Export › Export JSON , and Import JSON… to bring it back. See [Export and import](export-and-import.md).

title: Save, undo and sync
heading: Result
text: Your work is never lost to a closed tab, follows you when you are signed in, and any change can be taken back.

title: Section types

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The builder shows "Sign in to build your portfolio"
text: Why: Building needs an account. What to do: Select Sign In , then return to https://auricartisan.com/portfolio/.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Publish is greyed out
text: Why: The Check pane has one or more blocking findings. The button's tooltip says how many. What to do: Open Check , select each Blocking finding and fix it. See [Preview and check](preview-and-check.md).

title: Troubleshooting
heading: In the publish dialog, Publish stays disabled
text: Why: The address is not valid or not available yet. What to do: Use 2 to 31 lower-case letters, numbers and hyphens, wait for the availability check, or pick one of the Or take suggestions. If it says Could not check that just now. , try again in a moment.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "That portfolio is larger than half a megabyte."
text: Why: Uploaded images (in Image and Gallery sections, or a large avatar) are stored inside the portfolio and make it too big to publish. What to do: Host the images elsewhere and paste their https:// addresses instead of uploading them.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Images do not show on the page
text: Why: The address is not https:// , points to a page rather than an image, or the image host does not allow other sites to show it. What to do: Use a direct https:// link to the image file, or upload it (keeping the size limit in mind). Add alt text so the Check pane does not flag it.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: My Raw HTML looks different, or parts are missing
text: Why: The builder removes scripts, iframes, forms, event attributes, javascript: addresses and fixed or sticky positioning, and limits each <style block to its own section. What to do: See [Markdown and Raw HTML](markdown-and-raw-html.md). Use the Embed section for videos and prototypes.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: An embed says "Paste a YouTube, Vimeo, CodePen, Figma or Spotify link."
text: Why: Only trusted hosts are allowed: YouTube, Vimeo, CodePen, Spotify, SoundCloud, Figma, Google and CodeSandbox, over https:// . What to do: Use a share link from one of those services.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The Work / Projects section is empty
text: Why: It shows palettes and other items saved in your Library, in this browser. With nothing saved, it says Your published work will appear here once you save assets in the Library. What to do: Save palettes from the colour tools or libraries, then reload the builder.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Undo with Ctrl+Z does nothing
text: Why: Keyboard undo does not respond while you are typing in a field, and may not respond on the builder page at all. What to do: Use the Undo and Redo buttons in the top bar, or the Undo and Redo commands.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "Allow pop-ups to preview." or "Allow pop-ups to print."
text: Why: Preview and Download PDF open a new tab, which your browser blocked. What to do: Allow pop-ups for auricartisan.com.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The exported PDF has no background colours
text: Why: Browsers can drop backgrounds when printing. What to do: Turn on the print dialog's background graphics option.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: I cannot switch off the credit line
text: Why: Watermark-free exports are part of paid plans. What to do: Keep the credit, or see [Account and billing](../../account-and-billing/README.md). It never appears on your published page.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A snapshot link does not open
text: Why: The link was cut short when pasted, or the browser is very old. What to do: Copy a fresh link, or publish at an address instead, which has a short link.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: My portfolio is not in the Portfolio Index
text: Why: It was published less than fifteen minutes ago, List it in the Portfolio Index or Let search engines list it is off, or (for an external portfolio) it is waiting for review. What to do: Check the switches in the publish dialog, or its status in the Search Console's Portfolios tab. See [List your portfolio](list-your-portfolio.md).

title: Troubleshooting
heading: "The portfolio index could not be reached"
text: Why: The directory could not load. What to do: Try again later. Builder portfolios are still available at their own addresses.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: My draft is different on another device
text: Why: Drafts sync to your account only when you are signed in. The newer copy wins, but a draft you are actively editing is not replaced. What to do: Sign in on both devices, and reload the builder on the second one.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Is the Portfolio Builder free?
text: Yes. Building, publishing and exporting are free on every plan. Paid plans can remove the "Made with Auric Artisan" credit from exported files.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Do I need an account?
text: To build and publish, yes. To view portfolios and the Portfolio Index, no.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Can I change my address later?
text: Unpublish and publish again at a new address. Taking a page down frees its address for others, so your old link stops working.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Does publishing again change the address?
text: No. Publish these changes updates the same address.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Can I keep my portfolio private?
text: Choose Only people I send the link to to share a snapshot link that is not stored on the site and never seen by search engines. Or publish with Let search engines list it and List it in the Portfolio Index switched off.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Who can see my email address?
text: Only if you switch on Show next to Email . It is off by default.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Is the view count tracking visitors?
text: No. It is "Counted as a number and nothing else — no visitor records, no addresses."

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Can I host the portfolio myself?
text: Yes. Download HTML gives you a single file to put on any web host. You can then add that address to the Portfolio Index through the Search Console.

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: What does "Verified" mean in the Portfolio Index?
text: The owner proved, in the Search Console, that the site hosting the portfolio is theirs. Other external portfolios are reviewed by a person before they appear, and are marked Reviewed .

title: Portfolio FAQ
heading: Can I import a portfolio from another tool?
text: Only files exported from this builder with Export JSON .

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Size
text: - A published portfolio can be up to half a megabyte. Uploaded images and pictures are stored inside it and use that space quickly; linking to images hosted elsewhere does not. - Snapshot links carry the whole portfolio in the address. With several embedded images they become very long, and some apps and sites will not accept them. Large avatars are left out of snapshot links.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The Check pane
text: - It checks the rendered page for text contrast (WCAG 2.2 AA), link text, image alt text, heading order and target size. It is a strong pre-flight, not a full accessibility audit: it cannot judge whether your alt text is accurate, whether your content is clear, or how the page behaves with every assistive technology. - Text in colour formats it cannot measure is reported as unknown rather than passed. - Contrast is measured against the page's own paper. Text over images is not measured.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Style
text: - Accents offered in Style come from palettes saved in your Library in this browser. - The No background paper takes its text colour from the visitor's light or dark theme, so the page can look different for different visitors.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Drafts and sync
text: - Drafts sync to your account when you are signed in. If both devices change the draft, the newer copy wins; the builder will not overwrite a draft you are in the middle of editing. - Images in the Work / Projects section come from your Library in the browser you publish from.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: The Portfolio Index
text: - Builder portfolios are copied into the index within fifteen minutes of publishing. - External portfolios that are not on a verified site wait for a person to review them. - The index honours your search-engine setting: with Let search engines list it off, the portfolio is not listed. - Colour search compares colours perceptually (OKLab); results are ordered by closeness, not by exact match.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Published pages
text: - The view count is a single number. It does not identify visitors. - Embeds are limited to trusted hosts; Raw HTML is cleaned, so some markup is removed by design.

title: Privacy
heading: While you build
text: What Where Notes --- --- --- Your draft This browser, and your account when signed in Syncing to your account lets it follow you between devices. Your preview width This browser A convenience setting. Your draft is not public. Nothing a visitor sees changes until you publish.

title: Privacy
heading: When you publish
text: What becomes public at your address: - everything in your visible sections (hidden sections are left out); - the header details you chose to show — your name and headline always; email, location, website and avatar only if their Show switches are on; - a copy of the Library items in your Work / Projects section, taken at the moment you publish. Your sign-in email is not published unless you type it into the header and switch on Show . Settings under your control: - Let search engines list it — off keeps the page out of search engines. - List it in the Portfolio Index — off keeps it out of the directory. - Allow a PDF download and Show the view count . The view count is "Counted as a number and nothing else — no visitor records, no addresses." Uploaded avatars are re-encoded, which removes hidden photo information such as camera and location details.

title: Privacy
heading: Snapshot links
text: A snapshot link contains the portfolio itself. Nothing is stored on the site, but anyone who has the link can open it, and it cannot be withdrawn: it keeps working even if you later change or delete your portfolio. Share it only with people you trust.

title: Privacy
heading: The Portfolio Index
text: A listed portfolio shows its name, headline, place, crafts, colours, avatar, address and when it was updated. External entries show what you entered in the Search Console.

title: Privacy
heading: Remove it
text: - Unpublish takes the page down at once; the address stops working. - Switch off List it in the Portfolio Index and publish the change to leave the directory. - Take it out removes an external entry. For the site's privacy policy, see [Company and legal](../../company-and-legal/README.md).

title: Search and the Search Console
text: The search page at https://auricartisan.com/search/ finds tools, Learn articles, documentation, blog posts, changelog entries, portfolios and every other page on Auric Artisan. The search runs in your browser: the page downloads a small index of the site once, and everything you type is matched on your device. Results appear as you type, sorted by relevance, and you can narrow them to one section, sort them, and use a few simple operators such as "a phrase" , -word and type:learn . Because this is a colour site, the search also answers colour questions directly. Type a hex code such as d3af37 and an answer card shows the colour with its contrast against black and white. Type two hex codes and it judges them as a text and background pair against WCAG 2.1. Type the name of a common tool, such as contrast , and a card takes you straight to it. The globe button switches to a second index: Auric Artisan's own crawl of the web, an independent index much smaller than the big search engines. Site owners can put their own site into that index, and see how it is found, with the free Search Console at https://auricartisan.com/search/console/.

title: Search and the Search Console
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone looking for a tool, article or guide on Auric Artisan. - Designers and developers who want a quick colour or contrast answer without opening a tool. - People searching the wider web for colour and design resources. - Site owners who want their site in Auric Artisan's web index and want to know why a page is or is not included.

title: Search and the Search Console
heading: Where to find it
text: - The search page: https://auricartisan.com/search/ (also in the site menu under Search ). - From anywhere on the site: open Spotlight with Ctrl + K , type, and choose View all results for your query. - Select text on any page, right-click and choose Search this site . - The Search Console: https://auricartisan.com/search/console/ (in the site menu under Search , and linked from the bottom of the search page as Put your site in it ). - Searching needs no account. The Search Console needs an Auric Artisan account.

title: Search and the Search Console
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/search/. 2. Type at least two characters, for example oklch gradient . Results appear as you type. 3. Select a section tab, such as Learn , to see only that kind of page. 4. Hover a result, or press the down arrow, to see why it ranked where it did. 5. Press Enter or select a result to open it. 6. Type a hex code such as 1d2a3e to see the colour and its contrast. 7. To search the web instead, select the globe button beside the field and press Enter .

title: Search and the Search Console
heading: What you can do
text: - Search every page on the site, on your device, with typo correction and related-word matching. - Narrow results by section: All , Tools , Learn , Docs , Blog , Portfolios or Pages . - Sort by Relevance , Newest or A–Z . - Use phrases, exclusions and field filters such as tag: and title: . - Get instant colour, contrast-pair and tool answers. - See the score and matched fields behind every result. - Search Auric Artisan's own web index, with suggestions, spelling correction and paging. - In the Search Console, prove you own a site, request crawls, and see coverage, searches, clicks and positions for it.

title: Getting started with search
heading: Before you start
text: You need nothing but a browser. Searching the site needs no account and no sign-in. The first time you open the page it prepares its index; the status line then reads Index ready with the number of items indexed.

title: Getting started with search
heading: A tour of the page
text: Before you type, the page shows a start screen: - The search field at the top, with the placeholder Search Auric Artisan . A clear button appears once you type, and the globe button beside it switches to web search. - A privacy line : Indexed on this device — nothing you type leaves the browser . Your recent searches sit on the same line, with Clear . - Three example cards that run real queries when you select them: - Paste a hex — a colour with its contrast against black and white. - Give it two — a pair of colours judged for contrast. - Narrow by section — the query type:learn contrast , with how many pages it matches. - A ribbon of sections with how many pages each holds (for example Learn, Documentation, Tools), and the total number of pages in the index . Each section links to its own page. - More ways to ask — buttons for the operators type:learn , "a phrase" , -word and tag:oklch . Select one to put it in the field. - A line about the globe : it searches a second index, Auric Artisan's own crawl of the web, with a link to Put your site in it .

title: Getting started with search
heading: Your first search
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/search/. 2. Type contrast . After the second character, results start to appear. 3. Because contrast is also the name of a tool, a Tool card leads the page with Open the tool . The results list follows. 4. Add a word: contrast charts . The tool card goes away, because a tool card appears only when the whole query names the tool. 5. Look at the line under the field. It shows how your query was read: each word as a chip, and related words, shown dashed, that were matched at reduced weight. 6. Select the Learn tab to see only Learn articles. The number on each tab is how many results it holds. 7. Press the down arrow to highlight the first result. A panel shows why it ranks there. 8. Press Enter to open it.

title: Getting started with search
heading: Try a colour
text: 1. Clear the field with the clear button or Escape . 2. Type 777777 ffffff . 3. A Contrast pair card shows the ratio 4.48:1 and a table of AA and AAA results. Grey 777777 on white just misses AA for body text, although it passes for large text. 4. Select Swap them to put the background first, or Open the checker to continue in the Contrast Checker.
