title: Overview section
text: The Overview is the first section of the dashboard (https://auricartisan.com/auth/dashboard/ overview). It answers "is my account in order?" first, then shows your work, then suggests what to do next. Everything it shows is read from your account and from this browser; a part with nothing true to say is left out rather than filled with zeros. On a wide screen the Overview has a main column and a side column. On a screen narrower than about 1,024 pixels, the side column moves to the top because it holds the things you most need to act on.

title: Overview section
heading: The statement
text: The statement opens the main column. - Statement — the heading is the current month and year. - A one-line summary appears when there is something to say, for example "One key is doing the work." or "3 keys are in use." Below it is a ledger. A row appears only when it has a real value: Row Shows --- --- Plan Your plan name Credits used API credits used this billing period, with the period as a note (plans with API access, once usage has loaded) Credits left Included API credits left, with "N days left in the period" Your work The number of items you have saved, with a note such as "12 palettes · 3 collections · 40 KB"; or Nothing yet Two-factor authentication On , or Not set up with a Set it up button that opens Security & Privacy If rows are left out, a line says so, for example "3 more rows appear here once there is something to put in them — credits, storage, a published page." Whether your portfolio is published is shown in the Profile section, on the Public portfolio card. When API usage has loaded, a small table, Where the credits went , lists the endpoints that used the most credits. At the foot, Plan & usage in full opens the Plan & Usage section.

title: Overview section
heading: Your work
text: - The heading counts what you have saved, for example "12 things you made.", or reads "Nothing here yet." - The line under it reads "Palettes, scales and gradients from your Universal Library, newest first." or, when empty, "Anything you save from a tool lands here. Open a tool and make something." - Open the library (or Open the tools when empty) takes you there. - Up to twelve tiles show your newest saved items. Each tile shows the colours as swatches, the name, up to two hex values and how long ago it changed. Select a tile to open the library. The count comes from the library saved in this browser. Work saved in another browser is not included.

title: Overview section
heading: Next
text: Up to three suggestion cards, each with a button and a × to dismiss it. Suggestions only appear when they apply: Card Shown when Button --- --- --- Turn on two-factor Two-step verification is off (highlighted as the most urgent) Set it up Group your work You have more than two saved items and no collections Open the library Make an API key You have no API keys Create a key Dismissing a card hides it in this browser. Clearing the browser's site data brings dismissed cards back. Note: API keys work only on plans that include API access (Specialist and above). On other plans, Make an API key leads to a section that explains the API is not part of your plan.

title: Overview section
heading: Start something
text: A row of quick links: Colour tools , Palettes , Gradients , Shades , Contrast , Analyse a page and All tools .

title: Overview section
heading: The side column
text: A checklist of four items, with a progress ring and a count such as "2 of 4 done": 1. Add your name 2. Choose a username 3. Verify your email 4. Add a profile photo Each unfinished item has a button ( Add , Pick or Verify ) that opens the Profile section. The card disappears once all four are done. Your token balance for server-backed tool work. - The large figure is your balance. - Beside it: "of 250 a month" (for example) on a plan with a monthly allowance, or "tokens" on the free plan's one-time grant. - The bar shows how much of this period's included allowance is left. It is hidden for a one-time grant, which never expires. - The note explains the balance, for example "250 of these lapse at the end of the period.", "100 do not expire.", or "This period's allowance is waiting to be claimed." The card is hidden if you have no balance and no allowance. See [Tokens](tokens.md). Shows the browser and operating system you are using now, for example "Chrome on Windows", with Active now .

title: Overview section
heading: Related
text: - [Getting started with the dashboard](getting-started.md) - [Profile section](profile.md) - [Plan & Usage section](plan-and-usage.md) - [Security & Privacy section](security-and-privacy.md)

title: Delete your account
text: The Danger zone , at the bottom of Security & Privacy , holds the two actions that cannot be undone: - Erase this browser's workspace — clears the library, collections, drafts and preferences stored in this browser. Anything saved to the account stays. - Delete this account — permanently deletes your profile, portfolio, keys, sessions and billing history. There is no undo and no recovery. The zone is locked until you prove it is you, and each action asks for its own confirmation word on top of that.

title: Delete your account
heading: Before you delete
text: - Export anything you want to keep. See [Export your data](export-your-data.md). Download invoices you need from Plan & Usage . - Revoke or note your API keys. They stop working when the account is deleted. - Consider a refund first if you bought a plan in the last 7 days. See [Refunds](refunds.md). - Accounts created with Google or GitHub need a password to unlock the danger zone. If you never set one, the zone says "Set an account password before using these actions." Set one with Forgot password? first — see [Passwords](passwords.md add-a-password-to-a-google-or-github-account).

title: Delete your account
heading: Unlock the danger zone
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Security & Privacy . Scroll to Danger zone . Its state reads Locked . 2. The list Behind this door names the two actions it contains. 3. Under First, type this sentence , type the sentence shown exactly: "I understand these actions cannot be undone". A hint says "That matches." when it does, or "Not yet — it has to match word for word." 4. Under Then your account password , type your password. 5. Select Unlock for 5 minutes . Result: the state reads Unlocked and a timer shows "Unlocked — relocks in 5:00". The actions appear. When the timer reaches zero the zone locks itself again; select Lock now to lock it sooner. Reloading the page does not lock it early. Tip: If you read the site in Hindi, type the sentence as it is displayed, in Hindi.

title: Delete your account
heading: Erase this browser's workspace
text: 1. Unlock the danger zone. 2. Next to Erase this browser's workspace , select Erase . 3. Type ERASE in Type ERASE to confirm . 4. Select Erase again (it becomes available once the word matches). Select Cancel to stop. Result: "Cleared N stored items from this browser. Reload to see it." — or "There was nothing stored in this browser." Only this browser's library, portfolio draft, dashboard preferences and collection preferences are cleared. Your cookie choice and theme are kept, and your account, plan, keys and anything published are untouched.

title: Delete your account
heading: Delete this account
text: 1. Unlock the danger zone. 2. Next to Delete this account , select Delete account… . 3. Read the warning: "This immediately and permanently erases your profile, portfolio, API keys, sessions, and billing history. There is no undo and no recovery." 4. Type DELETE in Type DELETE to confirm . 5. Type your password in Confirm your password . 6. Select Permanently delete account (available once both are filled in). Select Cancel to stop. Result: "Permanently deleting your account…", then "Account deleted. Redirecting…", and the home page opens. You are signed out on every device. If it fails: "Could not delete your account — check your password and try again."

title: Delete your account
heading: What deletion does
text: - The account is closed immediately. You are signed out everywhere and cannot sign in to it again. - Your personal details are removed from the account: the name, email address, password and two-step secret no longer belong to it. - API keys stop working, because they only work for an active account. - The dashboard describes the result as erasing "your profile, portfolio, API keys, sessions, and billing history". The next section explains how payment records are handled.

title: Delete your account
heading: What is kept, and why
text: The Security page (https://auricartisan.com/security/) explains that "Account erasure anonymises personal data in place rather than destroying financial records. Tax law requires invoices to be retained, and an invoice naming nobody is not a valid record — so the transaction remains and your identity does not." The Data Retention and Deletion Policy adds that backup copies and security logs may persist until their normal rotation completes, and that records required by law, disputes or security may be kept longer. The FAQ says personal data is scheduled for deletion within about 90 days unless the law requires it to be kept.

title: Delete your account
heading: What deletion does not touch
text: - Your browser. Work saved in this browser (the library, drafts, preferences) is not on the account and is not removed by deleting it. Use Erase this browser's workspace first, or clear your browser's site data. - Copies you made. Exports, downloaded files and anything you published elsewhere. - The browser and VS Code extensions. They keep their own local data; uninstall them to remove it.

title: Delete your account
heading: Ask for deletion instead
text: If you cannot sign in, you can ask for deletion through the contact page with the topic Privacy or data , from the email address on the account. See [Contact and support](../../../help/contact-and-support.md).

title: Delete your account
heading: Messages
text: Message Meaning --- --- "That password is not right." The password was wrong; the password field is cleared. "The sentence does not match. It has to be word for word." Retype the sentence. "Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes." Wait and try again. "Set an account password before using these actions." A provider account with no password. "Confirm your email address first." Verify your email address. "This page could not prove it is still your session. Reload the page and try again — your password is fine." Reload the page. "The danger zone is not available on this server yet. Nothing is wrong with what you typed." The zone shows Unavailable ; contact support to delete the account.

text: - [Security & Privacy section](security-and-privacy.md) - [Data Retention and Deletion Policy summary](../../company-and-legal/docs/data-retention-and-deletion.md)

title: Device sign-in
text: The Auric command-line tool ( auric , listed as @auric-artisan/cli on the API documentation page) signs in without asking for your password in the terminal. Instead it shows a short code, and you approve that code in a browser where you are already signed in. This is called a device sign-in. The approval page is https://auricartisan.com/auth/device/. Its heading is Authorize Auric CLI .

title: Device sign-in
heading: Before you start
text: - You need an Auric Artisan account, signed in in your browser. - Your email address must be verified. Device approval is one of the features locked until you verify (see [Verify your email](verify-email.md)). - Install the command-line tool as described on the API documentation page: [Public API](../../../services/public-api/README.md).

title: Device sign-in
heading: Approve a device
text: 1. In your terminal, run: bash auric login 2. The tool prints a short code and an approval address. 3. Open the address in your browser. If you are not signed in, the page sends you to sign in and brings you back. 4. The page shows Signed in as and your email or name, so you can check it is the right account. 5. If the address included the code, it is already in Device code . Otherwise type it; it has the form ABCD-EFGH (letters and numbers; the dash is added for you). 6. Select Authorize CLI . Result: "CLI authorized. You can return to your terminal." The form disappears and the command-line tool continues, signed in as you. Its requests then use your account's plan and quota. Other commands the tool documents for this: bash auric whoami auric logout

title: Device sign-in
heading: Messages
text: Message What to do --- --- "Enter the device code shown in your terminal." The Device code field is empty. An error about an invalid or expired code Run auric login again to get a new code, and approve it promptly. A message about email verification Verify your email first, then try again.

title: Device sign-in
heading: Only approve codes you started
text: Approving a code lets whoever is running that terminal act as your account. Only approve a code you just generated yourself, on a computer you trust. If you approve one by mistake, sign out of the tool with auric logout on that computer and review Security & Privacy in the dashboard.

title: Device sign-in
heading: Related
text: - [API keys](api-keys.md), the other way to authenticate your own code - [Public API](../../../services/public-api/README.md)

title: Emails and messages
text: Your Auric Artisan account has no message inbox of its own. Everything the site needs to tell you arrives by email, at the address on your account, and replies to anything you send through the contact form arrive by email too.

title: Emails and messages
heading: Emails the account sends
text: Email When it arrives What to do with it --- --- --- Verification link After you sign up with email and password, or when you ask for a fresh link Open it within 24 hours and select Confirm email ownership . See [Verify your email](verify-email.md). Welcome Once your account is usable — straight away for Google or GitHub sign-ups, after verification for email sign-ups Nothing; it lists places to start: the tools, the Learn library and your dashboard. Replying reaches a person. Password reset link When you use Forgot password? Open it within one hour. See [Passwords](passwords.md). Receipt After a purchase Keep it; it carries your order reference, which starts with order . Contact form confirmation When you send a message through the contact page Nothing; it confirms the message arrived. Reply to your message When Auric Artisan answers Reply in the same thread. Email is delivered through Resend, named on the Security page as a third-party provider.

title: Emails and messages
heading: Where replies come from
text: The contact page routes each topic to one of three addresses, and replies come from the same one: Address Topics --- --- hello@auricartisan.com Using a tool , Billing , Something else developer@auricartisan.com A bug , API or integration security@auricartisan.com Security , Privacy or data Invoices name support@auricartisan.com for questions about an invoice. See [Contact and support](../../../help/contact-and-support.md) for reply times and how to write a useful message.

title: Emails and messages
heading: Beware of look-alikes
text: Auric Artisan asks you to pay only through the Razorpay checkout on auricartisan.com. If an email asks you to pay somewhere else, or asks for your password or backup codes, do not act on it; report it through the contact page.

title: Emails and messages
heading: Change the email address on the account
text: The email address cannot be changed from the dashboard yet. Its field in Profile is read-only and says "Email changes are not supported yet — contact support." Write through the contact page from your current address.

title: Emails and messages
heading: Related
text: - [Sign up](sign-up.md) - [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md the-verification-email-did-not-arrive)

title: Export your data
text: The dashboard can put your account details and the work saved in this browser into one JSON file (a plain-text data format that most tools can read). Nothing secret is included.

title: Export your data
heading: Download the export
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Security & Privacy . 2. Find the row Export everything . 3. Select Export . Result: "Export downloaded." and a file named like auric-artisan-export-2026-09-25.json (the date of the export) is saved by your browser.

title: Export your data
heading: What the file contains
text: Section Contents --- --- exported at When you made the export profile Your account details as the site holds them: display name, username, email address, bio, website, location, photo and related account fields preferences Your dashboard preferences portfolio Your Portfolio Builder draft as saved in this browser portfolio stats The view, download and share counters kept in this browser library Everything in My Library in this browser — palettes, gradients, collections and other saved items

title: Export your data
heading: What it does not contain
text: - Secrets. Passwords, two-step verification material and API keys are never included. - Work saved in other browsers. The library and portfolio sections come from the browser you are using. Export from each browser you use. - Receipts. The on-screen description mentions receipts, but your invoices are not written into this file. View, print or save them as PDF from Plan & Usage › Invoices & Payment History — see [Invoices and receipts](invoices-and-receipts.md).

title: Export your data
heading: A complete copy of what Auric Artisan holds
text: The Privacy Policy lists a right to portability — "a portable copy of applicable data where technically feasible" — and a right of access. For a copy of data held on Auric Artisan's servers beyond this export (for example order and payment records, or contact messages), write through the contact page with the topic Privacy or data (reply time: within 30 days). See [Contact and support](../../../help/contact-and-support.md).

title: Export your data
heading: Keep the file safe
text: The export holds your email address and profile details. Store it somewhere private.

title: Export your data
heading: Related
text: - [Security & Privacy section](security-and-privacy.md) - [Delete your account](delete-your-account.md) — export first if you plan to delete - [Privacy](../others/privacy.md)

title: Invoices and receipts
text: Every payment, refund and chargeback on your account is listed in the dashboard, and each one has its own printable invoice page.

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Find your payment history
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Plan & Usage (or choose Billing & plan in the header account menu). 2. Scroll to Invoices & Payment History . The table lists Date , Description (Payment, Refund or Chargeback, with the plan and term), Amount , Status (Paid, Failed or Refunded) and a View link. It shows 25 rows at a time; use <- Newer and Older - to page through more. With no purchases yet it reads "No payments yet. Receipts appear here after your first purchase."

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Open an invoice
text: 1. Select View on a row. 2. The invoice page opens at https://auricartisan.com/auth/billing/invoice/ with that invoice's reference in the address. The invoice shows: Part Contents --- --- Header Auric Artisan — "Color science platform & creative tools", the website and the support email address Invoice , Date , Status The invoice reference, the date and Paid, Failed or Refunded From Auric Artisan, "Internet · Worldwide", support@auricartisan.com Billed to Your name and email address Line items What was bought (the plan and its term) and the amount, then the Total Payment note "Payment processed via" the provider (Razorpay), and the payment reference Footer "Auric Artisan is operated under Indian law. Questions? Email support@auricartisan.com and quote the invoice number above."

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Print or save as PDF
text: 1. Open the invoice. 2. Select Print / Save as PDF . 3. In your browser's print dialog, choose a printer, or choose Save as PDF (the wording depends on your browser).

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Share or keep the link
text: Select Copy invoice URL to copy the invoice's address; the button briefly reads Copied . Only you can open it: the page needs you to be signed in to the account that made the payment. Select ← Back to billing to return to the dashboard.

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Receipts and GST
text: The Subscription and Billing Policy explains that Auric Artisan is not currently registered for GST. That means: - no GST or other tax is added at checkout — the price you see is the total you pay; - the receipts issued are payment receipts, not GST tax invoices: they carry no GSTIN and no tax component; - they cannot be used to claim input tax credit. If you need a GST invoice for a business purchase, the policy asks you to wait until registration is in place rather than buying on the assumption that one will follow. Note: The invoice page has a section for GST details ("This is a tax invoice. GST is inclusive in the total.") that appears only when an invoice actually carries tax. Under the current policy you should not expect to see it.

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Your receipt email and order reference
text: The contact page's Billing topic says your order or invoice ID "is in your receipt email. It starts with order ." Quote it whenever you contact Auric Artisan about a payment. The confirmation page after checkout shows the same Order reference with a copy button.

title: Invoices and receipts
heading: Messages on the invoice page

title: Passwords
text: This page covers three tasks: resetting a password you have forgotten, changing a password you know, and adding a password to an account that was created with Google or GitHub.

title: Passwords
heading: Password rules
text: Every Auric Artisan password must have: - 12 to 128 characters, - both upper-case and lower-case letters, - at least one number, - at least one symbol, - no single character repeated four or more times in a row, - not be a common password such as "password123". Passwords are stored only as a one-way hash (the Security page names PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations), so nobody at Auric Artisan can read or recover your password. A reset replaces it rather than revealing it.

title: Passwords
heading: Reset a forgotten password
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/auth/ and select Forgot password? under the password field. 2. The Recover access. panel opens. If you had typed an email address in the sign-in form, it is copied into Email . 3. Type the email address on the account (not your username) and select Send Reset Link . 4. The page always answers "If that address belongs to an account, a one-hour reset link is on its way." It says the same whether or not the address has an account, so nobody can use the form to find out who is registered. 5. Open the email and select the reset link within one hour. 6. The page Set a new password opens. Type a new password in New Password and again in Confirm Password . Select the eye button to show what you typed. 7. Select Reset password . Result: "Password updated. Redirecting to sign in…" and, a moment later, the sign-in page. Sign in with the new password. Resetting a password ends every existing sign-in on every device. Select ← Back to Sign In on either panel to return without resetting. Message Meaning --- --- "This reset link is missing a token." The address is incomplete. Open the full link from the email. "Password must be at least 12 characters." Checked before sending. The full rule list above also applies. "Passwords do not match." The two fields differ. An expired or used link message Each link works once and for one hour. Request a new one.

title: Passwords
heading: Change your password
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Security & Privacy . 2. The Password cell in the readout strip says when the password was last set, for example "Set when you signed up", "Unchanged since you signed up", "Changed today", "Changed yesterday" or "Changed 42 days ago". 3. Select Change in that cell. A small form opens below the strip. 4. Type your Current password , a New password (12+ chars, mixed) , and Repeat new password . 5. Select Update password . Select Cancel to close the form without changing anything. Result: "Password changed." Changing the password signs you out everywhere, including this browser, so the dashboard returns you to the sign-in page. Sign in with the new password. Message What to do --- --- "New passwords do not match." Retype the new password in both fields. "Current password is incorrect." Check the current password, or reset it instead. "Password changed in another session. Sign in again." The password was changed somewhere else a moment ago. Sign in with the newest password.

title: Passwords
heading: Add a password to a Google or GitHub account
text: An account created with Google or GitHub has no Auric Artisan password. You need one to unlock the dashboard's danger zone (for example, to delete the account); without one the danger zone says "Set an account password before using these actions." 1. Sign out, or use a private window. 2. Follow [Reset a forgotten password]( reset-a-forgotten-password) with the email address of your Google or GitHub account. 3. Set a password from the emailed link. Result: you can sign in with either the provider or the email address and password.

title: Plan & Usage section
text: The Plan & Usage section (https://auricartisan.com/auth/dashboard/ plan) shows what you pay for and what you use: your plan, your usage meters, your invoices, and — on plans that include the REST API — your API keys, credits and spend controls. The header menu items Billing & plan and API keys both open this section, as do the older addresses billing and api-keys . What you see depends on your plan: - On Apprentice and Artisan , the section shows your plan and receipts, and one card explaining that the API is not part of your plan. - On Specialist and Industrial Pro , it also shows the full API console. - If your account holds API keys from an earlier plan, the API console stays visible whatever you pay now, so you can still see and revoke those keys.

title: Plan & Usage section
heading: Current Plan
text: The Current Plan panel names your plan and its state in one line: Line When --- --- "You're on the free Apprentice plan." Free plan "Artisan — active until 12 Oct 2026. Does not renew automatically." (plan and date vary) A paid pass, which ends on that date "Your Artisan subscription has ended." A plan that has ended "Payment for your Artisan plan failed — please update your payment method." A failed payment "Artisan — no active subscription on this account." The plan is named but has no active purchase behind it Buttons: Button What it does --- --- Change Plan Opens the pricing page Request a refund Shown on a paid pass. Its tooltip explains: "This pass does not renew, so there is nothing to cancel — you will not be charged again. Use this to ask for a refund instead." It opens the contact page. See [Refunds](refunds.md). Note: A Cancel Subscription button exists for a genuine recurring subscription, which would say when it renews. Auric Artisan does not sell recurring subscriptions today, so you will normally see Request a refund instead. See [Plan terms, renewal and cancelling](plan-terms-and-cancelling.md). Under the plan line is a list of meters. Each shows how much you have used against your plan's figure ( ∞ means unlimited), with a bar that changes colour when you pass two-thirds of the figure and again when you reach it. Meter Counts Apprentice figure --- --- --- Vision sims today Vision simulations run today 25 URL analyses this month Page analyses in the Analyzer this month 20 SVG recolors this month SVG downloads from SVG Recolor this month 15 Experiment runs Psychophysics Engine runs 25 Projects Saved items in your library 20 Team seats Seats on the account (every account is single-user today) 1 Paid plans show their own, higher or unlimited, figures. A meter with nothing to count on your plan is hidden. If nothing has been used yet, the list says "No usage to report yet — your meters will appear as you use the tools." Things to know about the meters: - Daily meters reset each day and monthly meters each calendar month, both in UTC. - Counts include use recorded in this browser, so a meter can differ between browsers until the account's own figure catches up. - Projects is counted from the library saved in this browser. - Every tool stays usable. The pricing page describes vision simulations as unmetered, because they run in your browser.

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
text: Every paid plan sold on Auric Artisan is a one-time purchase of a fixed period — one month or twelve. This page explains what that means in practice.

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: Nothing renews
text: - No recurring subscription is created when you buy a plan. - No payment mandate, standing instruction or saved card is kept for a future charge. - No second charge is ever scheduled. So there is no renewal to be surprised by, and nothing to cancel. The dashboard's plan line says so: for example "Artisan — active until 12 Oct 2026. Does not renew automatically." Note: Some policy pages use the word "subscription". The Terms of Service explain that, on Auric Artisan, it means the plan record and its billing period — not a recurring charge.

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: When a pass ends
text: The pass ends on its own at the end of the term you bought. You do not need to do anything. - The account returns to the free Apprentice plan. - Every tool keeps working. - Your saved work is not touched. It lives in your browser, so it stays exactly where it is whatever your plan does. - The paid conveniences stop: ad-free browsing, watermark-free exports, the monthly token allowance and any higher limits. - The plan's included API credit allowance ends with it. Purchased API credits stay on the account (see below).

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: Buying another term
text: To continue, buy another pass from the pricing page when the current one ends, the same way you bought the first. See [Buy a plan](buy-a-plan.md). An upgrade starts as soon as the payment clears.

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: Stopping early
text: Because there is no future charge, stopping early means asking for a refund rather than cancelling: - Within 7 days of purchase, a refund is unconditional. - After 7 days, refunds are considered case by case. On a paid pass, Plan & Usage shows a Request a refund button where a cancel button would otherwise be. It opens the contact page. See [Refunds](refunds.md).

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: Tokens and API credits when a plan ends
text: Balance What happens --- --- Included monthly tokens Expire at the end of the billing period, as they would anyway Purchased tokens Stay on the account (token packs are not on sale today) Included API credits End with the paid period Purchased API credits Stay on the account and do not expire. They become spendable again if the account returns to a plan with API access. Overage is prepaid, so a plan ending never leaves an outstanding bill for API usage.

title: Plan terms, renewal and cancelling
heading: If recurring billing is ever introduced
text: The Subscription and Billing Policy and the Refund Policy both promise that, if a genuine recurring subscription is offered later, checkout will present it as one, with the renewal date and amount shown before you authorise payment and a working cancel control in your account — and that the policies will be updated before the first such charge. The dashboard already has a Cancel Subscription button for that case; it appears only on a plan that actually renews.

title: Plans and pricing
text: This page restates the pricing page at https://auricartisan.com/company/pricing/ as of the date above. The pricing page is authoritative: if a figure here and there ever differ, the pricing page and the checkout are what you are charged by.

title: Plans and pricing
heading: The model in one paragraph
text: Every tool is free on every plan. Paid plans add conveniences and scale — ad-free browsing, watermark-free exports, a monthly token allowance for server-backed work, higher limits and, from Specialist, the REST API. A paid plan is a one-time pass for one month or twelve months: it does not auto-renew, and there is nothing to cancel. Plan purchases carry a 7-day money-back window, and an account is required before any payment.

title: Plans and pricing
heading: Tokens and API credits
text: Two separate meters, explained in full on their own pages: - Tokens pay for server-backed work you start in a website tool: 100 once on Apprentice, then 250, 1,000 or 2,500 a month. One token is sized at a reference rate of about $0.10. See [Tokens](tokens.md). - API credits pay for REST API calls: 1,000,000 a month on Specialist, 10,000,000 on Industrial Pro, none on Apprentice or Artisan. One credit is one standard request; heavier endpoints cost more. See [API credits and spend controls](api-credits-and-spend.md). Neither pays for the other and nothing converts between them.

title: Plans and pricing
heading: Token estimator
text: The Tokens — what each plan includes section has a small estimator. Type how many tokens you expect to use a month (or use − and + , or select a plan tile). It names the smallest plan whose allowance covers that number, for example "Specialist includes 1,000 tokens every billing month — 300 fits inside that allowance." Above the largest allowance it suggests Talk to us . Top-ups are not on sale: "Tokens come with a plan today — we don't sell them separately."

title: Plans and pricing
heading: Trials, discounts and custom deals
text: - Free trial — there is no trial of paid plans. The free Apprentice plan is the trial, and the 7-day money-back window covers a paid plan that is not right for you. - Nonprofit and student discounts — arranged by hand, not with a code (there is no discount field at checkout). Write to Auric Artisan through the contact page with proof of eligibility before you buy. The pricing page says the price is then agreed, and either you pay the normal price and the difference is refunded through Razorpay, or the plan is activated without a charge. - Volume, custom rate limits or a contract — use Talk to us on the pricing page. - Switching plans — an upgrade starts when the payment clears. There is no downgrade to arrange: a pass runs for its term and stops. Automatic proration is not available; contact Auric Artisan if a change leaves a real difference in your favour.

title: Profile section
text: The Profile section (https://auricartisan.com/auth/dashboard/ identity) holds who you are on the site: the name that signs anything you publish, and the username your public page lives at. The panel is headed Who you are .

title: Profile section
heading: The fields
text: Field What it is Rules --- --- --- Profile photo Your photo, shown in the header, the dashboard and your portfolio PNG, JPG or GIF, up to 2 MB. It is cropped to a square. Display name The name shown on your profile and anything you publish Up to 64 characters Username Your handle, typed after the @ . Your public page lives at this address, and you can sign in with it. 3–30 characters: letters, numbers and underscores. It can be changed once every 30 days. Bio "A line or two about what you make." title: Profile section
heading: Edit your profile
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Profile . 2. Change any of the fields. 3. Watch the How you appear card on the right: it previews the header of your public page as you type — photo, name, @handle , bio, website and location. 4. Select Save changes . Result: "Profile saved." appears under the button. The note beside the button explains that the details are "Saved to your account, and used anywhere you publish." If something is wrong, the message names it, for example "Bio must be 500 characters or fewer." or "Website must be a valid http(s) URL."

title: Profile section
heading: Change your username
text: 1. Type the new handle in Username . 2. After a short pause the line under the field reports availability: "Checking…", then "@name is available." or a reason, such as "That username is taken.", with up to three suggestions ("Try: …"). 3. Select Save changes . Result: "@name is yours." The username is saved before the other fields, so if the handle is refused, your other edits are not lost and the message says why. Rules and limits: - You can change your username once every 30 days. Before that, the message says "You can change your username again in N days." - A username someone has just given up is held for 30 days before anyone else can take it ("That username was recently released and is not yet available."). - Reserved words are refused, and so are names too close to an existing one ("That username is too similar to one in use."). - Changing the username changes the address of your public portfolio.

title: Profile section
heading: Change your photo
text: 1. Double-click the Profile photo strip (or focus it and press Enter or Space ). 2. Choose an image file. 3. The strip shows the file name with "will upload on Save", and the preview updates. 4. Select Save changes . "That image is over 2 MB" or "Please choose an image file" appears if the file cannot be used. The photo is resized to a small square before it is uploaded. Double-click your photo in the dashboard masthead to open the photo viewer. It shows the photo large, with your name and email, and three buttons. Changes here save straight away — there is no Save changes step. Button What it does --- --- Change photo Choose an image file; it is uploaded at once ("Photo updated.") Gallery Opens the Auric avatar gallery (below) Remove Removes the photo ("Photo removed."); your initial is shown instead Close the viewer with the × button, by clicking outside it, or with Esc .

title: Profile section
heading: The Auric avatar gallery
text: Instead of a photo you can pick a drawn character avatar. Open the photo viewer and select Gallery . - The header reads Auric avatars — "540 designs · 9 categories · 3 formats". - Two tabs: Free (120 designs) and Paid (420 designs). - Filters: All , Companions , Wildlife , Farm , Ocean , Fantasy , Future , Botanical , Cosmic , Signature , 3D and Animated . A filter is greyed out when the open tab has nothing in it. - The Paid tab opens with a featured signature character, Auric Muse , marked 3D and Animated . - Select a design to use it. It is applied immediately ("Avatar updated."). On the free plan, paid designs are shown locked; selecting one opens an upgrade dialog explaining that "The premium avatar studio — 420 sculpted 3D and animated designs — is included with any paid plan." On a paid plan every design is available and the header chip reads "All 540 included". A chosen avatar is saved as an ordinary image, so it stays yours if your plan changes.

title: Refunds
text: This page summarises the Refund Policy at https://auricartisan.com/legal/refund/. The policy page is authoritative; this page explains how to use it.

title: Refunds
heading: What you can get back
text: Purchase Refund terms --- --- Plan pass (one month or twelve) Within 7 days of purchase, refunded for any reason. After 7 days, considered case by case. Prepaid API credits Within 7 days of that purchase, to the extent they are unused. Credits already spent on API requests are not refundable; a partly used balance may be refunded pro rata at Auric Artisan's discretion. Token packs Within 7 days if unused; partly used packs may be refunded pro rata at Auric Artisan's discretion. Token packs are not on sale today. Included allowances Not refundable separately. The tokens and API credits that come with a plan are part of the plan price, and refunding the plan refunds them with it. Advertising bookings In full at any time before the campaign starts; after that, case by case. After the 7-day window, the policy says refunds are considered against the purchase terms shown at checkout, payment-provider records, account status, usage and applicable law.

title: Refunds
heading: Ask for a refund
text: 1. Open the dashboard and select Plan & Usage . 2. In Current Plan , select Request a refund . (This button appears on a paid pass.) 3. The contact page opens. Choose the Billing topic. 4. Fill in your name and the email address on the account. 5. In the reference field ( Order or invoice ID ), paste your order reference. It is in your receipt email and on the confirmation page, and starts with order . 6. In the message, give the purchase date and what you bought, and say you want a refund. 7. Select Send . Go to https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/ and follow steps 3–7. The policy says both routes "reach the same place; the button simply saves you finding the page". Use the email address associated with the purchase. Result: you get a confirmation email, and a reply from Auric Artisan in the same thread. The Billing topic lists a reply time of 1–2 days.

title: Refunds
heading: How long it takes
text: Approved refunds are issued through Razorpay to the original payment method within 5–7 business days of approval. Your bank or card issuer may take longer to show it on your statement.

title: Refunds
heading: What a refund removes
text: - A refunded plan ends at once: plan benefits are removed and the account returns to the free Apprentice plan. - Refunded tokens or API credits are deducted from the balance they were granted to. - Your work stays yours. Content and projects you created are not removed. The confirmation page for a refunded order says "The payment for this order has been refunded in full" and that anything the order activated has been removed. The payment appears as Refunded in Invoices & Payment History .

title: Refunds
heading: Charges you do not recognise
text: If you see a charge that appears to be from Auric Artisan and you did not make it, or you were asked to pay outside the official checkout, contact Auric Artisan through the contact page with the date, amount, payment provider and any transaction reference. Do not send full card numbers, passwords or other secrets.

title: Security & Privacy section
text: The Security & Privacy section (https://auricartisan.com/auth/dashboard/ security) answers two questions: who can get into the account, and what leaves it. Its heading counts what is signed in right now, for example "2 devices are holding this account open." The line beneath reads: "End anything you do not recognise — a device you revoke here is signed out immediately." The older addresses settings and sessions open this section too.

title: Security & Privacy section
heading: The readout strip
text: Four cells state the account's condition. The cell that needs attention is highlighted. Cell What it says Control --- --- --- Password When the password was last set: "Set when you signed up", "Unchanged since you signed up", "Changed today", "Changed yesterday" or "Changed N days ago" Change — see [Passwords](passwords.md change-your-password) Two-factor "Off — nothing but your password" (highlighted), or "On — N backup codes left" Enable 2FA or Disable 2FA — see [Two-step verification](two-step-verification.md) Usage data "On — anonymous usage only" or "Off — nothing is collected" A switch that records your choice on your account Cookies Your cookie choice: "Not answered yet", "Necessary only", or "Necessary +" the optional categories you accepted Change opens the Cookie Policy page, where you change it Select the switch to turn it on or off. The choice is saved to your account at once. If it cannot be saved, the cell says "Changed here, but not saved to your account"; try again later. This switch is separate from your cookie choice. On the website, analytics events are only sent when you have accepted the Analytics cookie category, and never when your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control (see [Privacy overview](../../../help/privacy.md)).

title: Security & Privacy section
heading: Signed-in devices
text: A sheet lists every browser or device where the account is signed in, with Sign out everywhere at the top. Column Shows --- --- Device An icon (phone or computer), the browser and system — for example "Safari on iPhone" — and "Signed in 3 d ago" or This device Where The network address the sign-in came from Last active How long ago it was last used, for example "12 min ago" (action) Revoke , or the This device label on your own row Your own device is always the first row and has no Revoke button, so you cannot sign yourself out by accident here. If the list cannot tell which row is yours, it says "This list does not say which device you are reading on, so every row can be revoked — including this one." 1. Find the row you do not recognise. 2. Select Revoke . Result: that device is signed out immediately and the row disappears. 1. Select Sign out everywhere . The button changes to Sign out every other device? 2. Select it again within about six seconds to confirm. If you wait, it resets. Result: "Signing out…", then every other device is signed out. The device you are using stays signed in. To sign out this device too, use Sign out in the header account menu. Under the sheet, a line summarises the last 30 days, for example "14 sign-ins in the last 30 days, none failed" or "…, and 2 failed attempts". Failed attempts are highlighted because they are worth a second look. If nothing is recorded: "No sign-ins recorded in the last 30 days". Select See all sign-ins to open a list of recent successful sign-ins (up to six), each with the browser, system, network address and time. Select Hide sign-ins to close it. If you see failed attempts you did not make, change your password and turn on two-step verification.

title: Security & Privacy section
heading: Export everything
text: A single row: Export everything — "Your profile, portfolio, collections and receipts as one JSON file. Nothing secret is included — passwords, two-factor material and API keys stay out." Select Export . What the file contains is described in [Export your data](export-your-data.md).

title: Security & Privacy section
heading: Danger zone
text: The last panel is the Danger zone , which holds the two actions that cannot be undone: Erase this browser's workspace and Delete this account . It starts Locked . To open it you type a confirmation sentence and your password, and it then stays open for five minutes. A list headed Behind this door names what it contains before you unlock it. Everything reversible lives elsewhere: devices on the sheet above, keys under Plan & Usage, your public page in the Portfolio Builder. Full walkthrough: [Delete your account](delete-your-account.md).

text: - [Sign in and sign out](sign-in.md) - [Two-step verification](two-step-verification.md) - [Export your data](export-your-data.md) - [Reference](reference.md security-and-privacy-section)

title: Sign in and sign out
text: The sign-in page is https://auricartisan.com/auth/. Select Sign in in the site header to open it; it returns you to the page you were on once you are in.

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: Sign in with your email or username
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/auth/. The Sign In tab is selected and the panel reads Welcome back. 2. In Email or username , type either the email address on the account or your username (without the @ ). 3. Type your Password . Select the eye button to show it. 4. Optional: tick Remember me to stay signed in on this browser (see [How long a sign-in lasts]( how-long-a-sign-in-lasts)). 5. Select Sign In . 6. The first time you submit, the Auric human check appears: repeat the three-mark sequence and select Verify sequence , then select Sign In again. How the check works is described in [Sign up](sign-up.md the-auric-human-check). 7. If the account has two-step verification, the Second factor. panel appears; see [Sign in with a second factor]( sign-in-with-a-second-factor). Result: the message "Identity confirmed. Opening your workspace…" appears and the site opens: - the page you were trying to reach, if you came from a link that needed sign-in; otherwise - the dashboard, if your account has no username yet; otherwise - the home page. Message What to do --- --- "Enter your email or username." The first field is empty. "Enter a valid email address." You typed an @ , so the field is checked as an email address, and it is not a valid one. "Usernames are at least 3 characters." or "Use letters, numbers and underscores only." Without an @ , the field is checked as a username. "Password is required." The password field is empty. "Complete the Auric human check before continuing." A check is on screen but not completed. Wrong credentials, a locked account or a server problem show a message at the top of the panel. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md i-cannot-sign-in).

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: Sign in with Google or GitHub
text: 1. On the Sign In tab, under or continue with , select Google or GitHub . 2. Complete the provider's sign-in if asked. Result: you return to Auric Artisan signed in. Use the same provider you signed up with; an email address that already has a password account cannot be signed in with a different provider (the message is "This email already has an account. Sign in with the method already connected to it.").

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: Sign in with a second factor
text: If two-step verification is on, a second panel appears after your password: 1. The panel Second factor. says "Enter the current six-digit code. This sign-in expires in 10:00", with a countdown. 2. Open your authenticator app and type the current 6-digit code in Verification Code . 3. Select Verify . Result: "Second factor confirmed. Opening your workspace…" If you do not have your authenticator: 1. Select Use a backup code . 2. Type one of your backup codes in Backup Code (format XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX ). 3. Select Verify . Each backup code works once and is used up only when it is accepted. Select ← Back to code entry to return to the 6-digit code, or Cancel sign-in to start again. If the 10-minute countdown runs out, the page returns to the sign-in form with "That sign-in request expired. Start again." Details: [Two-step verification](two-step-verification.md).

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: How long a sign-in lasts
text: Choice How long you stay signed in --- --- Remember me ticked Up to 30 days on this browser. The Cookie Policy lists the session cookie as lasting "up to 30 days, or until sign-out or expiry". A sign-in that goes unused for seven days ends sooner. Remember me not ticked Until you close the browser, and no longer than 24 hours. Google or GitHub Treated as a normal sign-in without Remember me. Signing in on one device does not sign you out anywhere else. Each browser is a separate signed-in device, listed under Security & Privacy › Signed-in devices . Some actions end your sign-ins on purpose: - Changing your password signs you out everywhere, including the browser you changed it in. Sign in again with the new password. - Resetting a forgotten password also ends all existing sign-ins. - Revoking a device, or Sign out everywhere , ends those sessions immediately. - Deleting the account signs you out everywhere.

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: If you are already signed in
text: Opening the sign-in page while signed in sends you straight on to the page you asked for, or the home page. If your email address is not verified yet, the page shows Confirm your inbox. instead — see [Verify your email](verify-email.md).

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: The account menu
text: When you are signed in, the header shows your photo, first name and plan instead of Sign in . Select it to open the account menu: Item Goes to --- --- Signed in as Shows your name and email address Dashboard "Overview and recent activity" — the dashboard Profile "Identity and profile photo" — the Profile section Billing & plan "Subscription and invoices" — the Plan & Usage section API keys "Manage developer access" — the Plan & Usage section Sign out "End this session securely"

title: Sign in and sign out
heading: Sign out
text: 1. Select your account chip in the header. 2. Select Sign out . Result: this browser's session ends. Other devices stay signed in; to end them too, use Sign out everywhere in [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md).

title: Sign up
text: You can create an account in two ways: with an email address and a password, or with an existing Google or GitHub account. Both are free and neither asks for a card. The sign-up form is at https://auricartisan.com/auth/ register. You can also open https://auricartisan.com/auth/ and select the Create Account tab, or select Create account in the site header.

title: Sign up
heading: Sign up with email and password
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/auth/ and select Create Account . The panel is headed Create your identity. 2. Fill in the fields: Field What to enter Rules --- --- --- Display Name The name shown on anything you publish Required, 2–64 characters Username Your public handle, typed after the @ Required, 3–30 characters: letters, numbers and underscores only. You can sign in with it instead of your email. Email Your email address Required, a valid address Password Your password 12–128 characters, upper and lower case letters, at least one number and one symbol, no character repeated four or more times in a row, not a common password Confirm Password The same password again Must match 3. As you type the username, a tick means it is available and a cross means it is not. Hover over the mark, or read the message under the field, for the reason. 4. As you type the password, a checklist shows which of the six rules are met, and a label reads Password strength: Weak , Fair , Good or Strong . Select the eye button to show or hide what you typed. 5. Tick I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy . Both names are links to the full documents. 6. Select Create Account . 7. The Auric human check appears the first time you submit, with the message "One quick check that you are human, then we will sign you in." Complete it (see below), then select Create Account again. Result: the panel changes to Confirm your inbox. It shows your email address partly masked, a 24-hour Verification window countdown, a Resend button (available after 60 seconds) and Continue to limited workspace . Continue with [Verify your email](verify-email.md). Note: If the email address already has an account, the same confirmation screen appears but offers Return to sign in instead of Continue to limited workspace . No second account is created. Sign in with the existing account, or use Forgot password? if you do not remember its password.

title: Sign up
heading: The Auric human check
text: The human check replaces a traditional CAPTCHA. It proves a person is at the keyboard for this one attempt. 1. A sequence of three marks is shown, with a countdown. 2. Below it, select the same marks in the same order from the choices. Each choice you select fills the next answer slot. 3. To undo a choice, select its slot and it is removed. 4. When all three slots are filled, select Verify sequence . 5. If it matches, the status reads "Human signal verified. This proof is single use." Message What it means --- --- "Enter your email or username before verifying the sequence." The check is tied to the address or username in the form. Fill that in first. "Take a moment, then verify the sequence again." You answered faster than a person usually can. Wait a second and select Verify sequence again. "That did not match. Repeat the displayed sequence." The order was wrong. The slots are cleared; try again. "This check expired. Request a new sequence." The countdown ran out. Select New sequence . "A fresh human check is required for another attempt." Each proof works once. After a failed or completed attempt, complete a new check. A proof belongs to the email or username you typed when you verified. If you change that field afterwards, the proof no longer applies and you need a new check.

title: Sign up
heading: Sign up with Google or GitHub
text: 1. On the Create Account tab, under or sign up with , select Google or GitHub . 2. Sign in to that provider if asked, and allow Auric Artisan to use your account. 3. You return to Auric Artisan signed in. Result: your account is created with the provider's email address, which counts as verified, so there is no verification email to wait for. A welcome email confirms that you signed in with Google or GitHub, "so there's no password to remember." - An account created this way has no Auric Artisan password. Actions that ask for your password — such as unlocking the danger zone to delete the account — ask you to set one first. To set one, use Forgot password? on the sign-in page with the account's email address. See [Passwords](passwords.md). - If an account already exists for the provider's email address, you see "This email already has an account. Sign in with the method already connected to it." Use that method instead. - If the provider account has no verified email address, you see "Your provider account has no verified email address." Verify it with the provider, or sign up with email and password. Other messages you might see after returning from a provider are listed in [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md google-or-github-sign-in-errors).

title: Sign up
heading: After you sign up
text: - You are on the free Apprentice plan. - If you have no username (possible for some older accounts), the dashboard asks for one. - Next: [Verify your email](verify-email.md), then [Getting started with the dashboard](getting-started.md).

title: Tokens
text: Tokens meter the work that runs on Auric Artisan's servers when you start it from a website tool — for example rendered page analyses, snapshots and whole-site accessibility crawls in the Analyzer. Everything that runs in your browser is free and unmetered. Tokens belong to your account, so you need to be signed in to have or spend them.

title: Tokens
heading: How many tokens each plan includes
text: Plan Included tokens Renews? --- --- --- Apprentice (free) 100, once No — a one-time starter grant Artisan 250 a month Yes, each billing month Specialist (coming soon) 1,000 a month Yes, each billing month Industrial Pro (coming soon) 2,500 a month Yes, each billing month One token is sized at a reference rate of about $0.10 of metered work. The pricing page describes the Artisan allowance as "250 pages a month however you spend them — a 24-page crawl costs 24".

title: Tokens
heading: What a run costs
text: The Analyzer shows the token cost of a run beside the button that starts it — "This run", the cost, and your balance — before you spend anything. After a site scan it shows a receipt: what was authorised, what was scanned, what was charged, and anything returned (pages that failed are free, and tokens held for pages a site did not have are given back). The Analyzer's own guide explains the costs of each kind of run: [Analyzer](../../tools/accessibility-and-vision/analyzer/README.md). If you do not have enough, the meter says how many more you need, for example "3 more than you have." For a site scan it offers the number of pages your balance can cover.

title: Tokens
heading: Claim your tokens
text: 1. Sign in. 2. Open the Analyzer at https://auricartisan.com/tool/analyzer/. 3. In its token meter, select Claim 100 free tokens (signed out, the button reads Sign in · 100 free tokens and takes you to sign in first). Result: the meter shows your balance. The starter grant is given once per account; clearing your browser's data does not give you a second one, and the balance you had comes back when you sign in again. On a paid plan, the dashboard's Tool tokens card tells you when "This period's allowance is waiting to be claimed."

title: Tokens
heading: Check your balance
text: Your balance is in two places: - Dashboard › Overview › Tool tokens — the balance, "of 250 a month" (or "tokens" for the one-time grant), a bar for this period's included tokens, and a note such as "250 of these lapse at the end of the period." See [Overview section](dashboard-overview.md tool-tokens). - The Analyzer's token meter — your balance next to the cost of the run you are about to start.

title: Tokens
heading: Expiry
text: - Included monthly tokens expire at the end of the billing period in which they were granted. They do not roll over. When a new period starts, a new allowance is granted. - The Apprentice starter grant does not expire, and it does not refresh when it is spent. - Purchased tokens do not expire at the period boundary, according to the Subscription and Billing Policy. Token packs are not on sale today, so today every token comes with a plan. - When you spend tokens, the included (expiring) ones are used first.

title: Tokens
heading: When you run out
text: Server-backed runs stop; everything that runs in your browser keeps working. The Analyzer says "You're out of tokens." Your options are to wait for your next monthly allowance, or to move to a plan with a larger allowance. Top-ups are not on sale; if you expect to pass your allowance, the pricing page asks you to tell Auric Artisan what you need through the contact page.

title: Tokens
heading: Tokens are not API credits
text: Tokens API credits --- --- --- Pays for Server-backed work you start in a tool on the website Requests your own code makes to the REST API One unit One unit of metered tool work, about $0.10 One standard API request; heavier endpoints cost 2–25 Included 100 once on Apprentice; 250, 1,000 or 2,500 a month None on Apprentice or Artisan; 1,000,000 or 10,000,000 a month When it runs out Server-backed runs stop Calls are refused, unless you turned on prepaid overage Neither pays for the other. Running out of tokens never stops your API calls, and running out of API credits never stops a crawl.

title: Tokens
heading: Refunds and tokens
text: Refunding a plan payment also removes the tokens that purchase granted. See [Refunds](refunds.md).

title: Two-step verification
text: Two-step verification (the dashboard calls it Two-factor or 2FA ) adds a second check after your password: a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone or computer. The codes use the standard TOTP method (time-based one-time passwords, which change every 30 seconds), so any common authenticator app works. Two-step verification is free on every plan.

title: Two-step verification
heading: Turn it on
text: 1. Install an authenticator app if you do not have one. 2. Open the dashboard and select Security & Privacy . 3. The Two-factor cell in the readout strip reads "Off — nothing but your password" and is highlighted while it is off. Select Enable 2FA . 4. The form below the strip says "Setting up… fetching your secret." and then "Scan this with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows." 5. Scan the QR code with the app. If you cannot scan, use the text under "Can't scan? Enter this secret manually:", or select Open in authenticator on a device that has the app. 6. Type the 6-digit code the app shows into the box (placeholder 123456 ). 7. Select Verify & enable . Result: "Two-factor authentication is ON. Store these one-time backup codes somewhere safe:" followed by ten backup codes. 8. Select Download backup codes to save them as a text file named auric-artisan-backup-codes.txt , or copy them somewhere safe and offline. The Two-factor cell now reads "On — 10 backup codes left", and the button changes to Disable 2FA . Important: The backup codes are shown once. There is no screen to view them again. Keep them where you can reach them if you lose your phone.

title: Two-step verification
heading: Sign in with two-step verification
text: 1. Sign in with your email or username and password as usual. 2. The Second factor. panel appears with a 10-minute countdown. 3. Type the current code from your authenticator app in Verification Code and select Verify . If you do not have the app with you, select Use a backup code , type one backup code (format XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX ) and select Verify . Each backup code works once; it is used up only after it is accepted. The Two-factor cell shows how many are left. Full sign-in details: [Sign in and sign out](sign-in.md sign-in-with-a-second-factor).

title: Two-step verification
heading: Turn it off
text: 1. Open Security & Privacy and select Disable 2FA . 2. The form says "Confirm your password and a current authenticator code to turn 2FA off." 3. Type your Account password and a current code from your authenticator app. 4. Select Disable 2FA . Result: "Two-factor authentication disabled." The cell returns to "Off — nothing but your password".

title: Two-step verification
heading: Get new backup codes
text: The dashboard has no separate control for new backup codes. If you are running low, turn two-step verification off and on again: completing setup replaces any old backup codes with a new set of ten, and you scan a new QR code into your app.

title: Two-step verification
heading: Setup messages
text: Message What to do --- --- "Code is invalid. Try again." Type the code currently shown in the app. Check that your device's clock is set automatically. "2FA setup expired — start again." The setup took too long. Select Enable 2FA again and scan the new code. "Code is invalid." (when turning off) Use a current code from the app. "Password is incorrect." (when turning off) Retype your account password.

title: Two-step verification
heading: How it is protected
text: The Security page (https://auricartisan.com/security/) states that two-factor secrets are encrypted before they are stored, under a key held separately, so a copy of the database alone cannot generate anyone's codes. The QR code is drawn by Auric Artisan itself, so the secret is never sent to an outside image service.

title: Two-step verification
heading: Reminders on the dashboard
text: While two-step verification is off, the Overview shows it as Not set up with a Set it up button, and its Next list leads with Turn on two-factor . You can dismiss that suggestion with its × button.

title: Two-step verification
heading: If you lose your authenticator
text: - Use a backup code to sign in, then turn two-step verification off and on again with your new device. - If you have neither the app nor a backup code, contact support through https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/ (topic Security ) from the email address on the account. See [Contact and support](../../../help/contact-and-support.md).

title: Verify your email
text: When you sign up with an email address and password, Auric Artisan sends a one-time link to prove the address is yours. Accounts created with Google or GitHub are already verified and skip this page.

title: Verify your email
heading: What stays locked until you verify
text: You can sign in and use the dashboard straight away — the sign-up screen calls this the "limited workspace". The sign-in page lists what stays locked until the address is verified: - billing (buying a plan), - promotions, - API keys, - device approval (signing in the command-line tool).

title: Verify your email
heading: Verify from the email
text: 1. Open the verification email from Auric Artisan and select its link. 2. The page https://auricartisan.com/auth/verify-email/ opens with the heading One click confirms it is really you. It removes the link's code from your address bar straight away. 3. Check that you asked for this account. The panel reads Ready to verify. "Confirm this address only if you requested the account." 4. Select Confirm email ownership . Result: the heading changes to Email verified. with "Ownership is confirmed and protected account features are now unlocked." and the message "Verification complete. This link cannot be used again." Select Open workspace to go to the dashboard. A welcome email follows. Note: The page asks you to press a button on purpose. Email security scanners and link previews open links automatically; the extra step means a preview can never verify an account on your behalf.

title: Verify your email
heading: Time limits
text: - A verification link works for 24 hours. The page shows the time left as Maximum link window , and says "Server time is authoritative". - On the sign-up screen, Verification window counts down the same 24 hours. If it reaches zero you see "The verification window expired. Request a new email." - Each new link replaces the previous one. Always use the newest email.

title: Verify your email
heading: Get a new link
text: There are three places to ask for a new link. Each has a short wait between requests (60 seconds by default). Where Control Confirmation --- --- --- The Confirm your inbox. screen after sign-up, or the sign-in page while unverified Resend verification email (shows Resend in 60s while waiting) "A fresh verification link has been sent." The verification page, after a failed link Send a fresh link (shows Send again in a number of seconds while waiting) "A fresh one-time link was sent. Open the newest email to continue." The dashboard's Your account is nearly there panel Send it again "Sent — check your inbox" You must be signed in to request a new link. If you are not, the verification page says "Sign in to request a fresh verification link."

title: Verify your email
heading: Messages on the verification page
text: Heading Meaning What to do --- --- --- Verification link missing. The address you opened has no verification code Open the complete link from the email, or request a fresh one Verification link unavailable. "The link has expired, was already used, or has been replaced." Request a fresh link and use the newest email Verification could not be completed. The link may have expired, been used or been replaced Request a fresh link Verification link expired. The one-time window closed Request a fresh verification email Verification status unavailable. The page could not check the link Try again from the latest email If the service cannot be reached, the page says your link is still available and you can try again.

title: Reference
text: This page lists every control in the account area, screen by screen. Labels are as they appear on screen. For step-by-step instructions, follow the links to the task guides.

title: Reference

Each new link replaces the old one; use the newest. 4. From the dashboard, use Send it again in the Your account is nearly there panel. 5. If nothing arrives, check that you typed the email address on the account (not your username) and look in spam. - Reset requests are rate-limited; wait a few minutes before asking again. - Links last one hour and work once. Request a new one if yours has expired. - Accounts created with Google or GitHub receive a reset link too; that is how you add a password.

The field is read-only: "Email changes are not supported yet — contact support." Once every 30 days. A username that someone gives up is held for 30 days before anyone else can claim it. Changing a password signs out every device, including the one you are using, so that anyone holding an old session loses it. Sign in with the new password. The FAQ page says multiple accounts are technically permitted, but using them to get around usage limits may lead to all of them being suspended. No. Everything arrives by email. Nothing renews, no card is stored, and there is nothing to cancel. There is nothing to cancel. The pass ends by itself and the account returns to the free plan. To stop early, ask for a refund: [Refunds](refunds.md). No. The free Apprentice plan is the trial, and paid plans have a 7-day money-back window. Everything Razorpay offers at checkout: cards, UPI, netbanking and wallets. Auric Artisan never sees your card, UPI or bank details. Yes, in US dollars. Auric Artisan is not currently registered for GST, so no GST is added and receipts are payment receipts, not GST invoices. Yes, arranged by hand before you buy. Write through the contact page with proof of eligibility. There is no discount code field. An upgrade starts as soon as the payment clears. There is no downgrade to arrange: a pass runs its term and stops. Proration is not automatic; contact Auric Artisan if a change leaves a real difference in your favour. Nothing. Your saved work lives in your browser and stays where it is. Every tool keeps working.

title: FAQ
heading: Tokens and credits
text: Tokens pay for server-backed work you start in a website tool, such as whole-site crawls. API credits pay for calls your own code makes to the REST API. They are separate and never convert. See [Tokens](tokens.md). Included monthly tokens expire at the end of the billing period. The free plan's 100 starter tokens do not expire but do not renew. Not today. Token packs are defined but not on sale; tokens come with a plan. No. Overage is off by default and prepaid: it can only spend credits you already bought, and nothing is ever invoiced afterwards. You can also set a monthly spend cap. See [API credits and spend controls](api-credits-and-spend.md).

title: FAQ
heading: Security and data
text: Yes. It is free and takes a minute. See [Two-step verification](two-step-verification.md). Security & Privacy › Signed-in devices . You can revoke any device, or sign out everywhere else. Your account details, dashboard preferences, and the portfolio draft and library saved in the browser you export from. No passwords, two-step material or API keys. See [Export your data](export-your-data.md). It closes at once and you are signed out everywhere. Personal details are removed; payment records are kept in anonymised form because tax law requires invoices to be retained. Work in your browser is not affected. See [Delete your account](delete-your-account.md).

title: Glossary
text: Account chip — The photo, first name and plan shown in the site header when you are signed in. Selecting it opens the account menu. Allowance (included) — The tokens or API credits that come with a plan for each billing month. Included allowances do not roll over. Annual term — A plan pass bought for twelve months, costing ten times the monthly price. API credit — The unit that meters REST API calls. One credit is one standard request; heavier endpoints cost more. Separate from tokens. API key — A secret string that lets your code call the REST API as your account. Shown once when created; begins with aa live . Apprentice — The free plan. Every tool, 100 one-time starter tokens, no API access. Artisan — The paid plan on sale today: ad-free browsing, watermark-free Pro exports, 250 tokens a month and higher limits. Auric human check — A short test on the sign-in page (repeat a sequence of three marks) that proves a person is signing in. Each proof works once. Backup code — One of ten single-use codes, in the form XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX , that replaces an authenticator code at sign-in. Billing period — The month (or the twelve months) a plan pass covers. Monthly allowances refresh at the start of each billing month. Chargeback — A payment reversed by your bank rather than refunded by Auric Artisan. Shown as a row type in payment history. Danger zone — The locked panel at the bottom of Security & Privacy holding the two irreversible actions: erasing this browser's workspace and deleting the account. Device code — The short code ( ABCD-EFGH ) the command-line tool shows so you can approve it in a browser. Device sign-in — Signing in the command-line tool by approving its code in a browser where you are already signed in. Hard ceiling — A limit of ten times the included API allowance per month, applied to every account whatever its settings. Industrial Pro — The highest plan: 10,000,000 API credits and 2,500 tokens a month. Marked coming soon. Invoice — The printable record of one payment, refund or chargeback, opened from Invoices & Payment History . Currently a payment receipt, not a GST tax invoice. Limited workspace — The account before its email address is verified: usable, but with billing, promotions, API keys and device approval locked. Order reference — The identifier of a purchase, starting with order . Quote it in any payment question. Overage (paid overage) — Letting API calls continue past the included allowance by spending prepaid credits. Off by default. Plan pass — A one-time purchase of a paid plan for a fixed term. It does not renew. Prepaid credits — API credits you have bought. They do not expire at the end of a period. Proration — Adjusting a price for part of a period. Not automatic on Auric Artisan. Rate limit — The most API requests allowed per minute: 300 on Specialist, 3,000 on Industrial Pro. Razorpay — The payment company that processes every payment on Auric Artisan. Session — One signed-in browser or device. Listed under Signed-in devices . Specialist — The plan that adds the REST API with 1,000,000 credits a month and 1,000 tokens a month. Marked coming soon. Spend cap — A monthly limit, in US dollars, on how much paid overage can spend. Starter grant — The 100 tokens the free plan includes once. They do not expire and do not renew. Token — The unit that meters server-backed work you start in a website tool. Sized at about $0.10 of work. Separate from API credits. TOTP — Time-based one-time password: the six-digit codes an authenticator app shows, changing every 30 seconds. Two-step verification (2FA) — Asking for an authenticator code as well as your password when you sign in. Username (handle) — Your public name on the site, shown as @name . It is the address of your public portfolio and can be used to sign in. Verification link — The one-time link emailed to prove your address is yours. Valid for 24 hours.
