title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy/ — version 2.2, effective 27 April 2026, last updated 23 May 2026. The official policy is authoritative.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Use Auric Artisan for colour science, learning, theme generation and creative exploration. - Use web analysis only on sites you own or are authorised to test. - Do not use security analysis for intrusion, scanning abuse, bypassing controls or harm. - Vision simulations and Ishihara-style plates are informational, not medical diagnostics. - Respect intellectual property, privacy, security and the law.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: What you may do (section 2)
text: - Explore colour science and compare models. - Read and reference the articles for learning and creative work. - Build palettes, themes and design material. - Create and export themes for legitimate sites, apps and brands. - Review sites for performance, responsiveness, accessibility signals, palettes, security posture and interface quality. - Run analysis on sites you own, manage or have permission to evaluate. - Use the simulations for non-certified personal, academic, creative or technical research.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: What is prohibited (section 3)
text: - Anything unlawful. - Using analysis or reports to attack, exploit, disrupt or access systems without authorisation. - Bypassing security controls, rate limits or access restrictions. - Reverse engineering, decompiling, scraping, copying or bulk-extracting the platform. - Submitting sites, files or content you have no right to analyse. - Uploading malware, spam, deceptive content, harmful scripts or illegal material. - Harassment, threats, hate speech, discrimination, impersonation or abuse of communication features. - Presenting outputs as certified, medical-grade, legal, governmental or safety-critical results. - Abusing free access, automated requests or public endpoints in ways that degrade the platform.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Web analysis and security testing (section 4)
text: Authorisation is required; no intrusive activity (exploitation, credential testing, denial of service, unauthorised scanning); no claims of a certified audit unless independently verified; respect third parties; treat findings as guidance.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Vision simulations and Ishihara-style tools (section 5)
text: Simulations are model-based approximations. Ishihara-style plates are not medical-grade. Do not use them to diagnose, screen, certify or make medical decisions; consult qualified professionals.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Communication, collaboration and content (sections 6–7)
text: Where sharing or feedback features exist: no abusive or misleading content, no impersonating Auric Artisan, staff, partners, institutions or other users, no spam, phishing or harassment. You are responsible for what you submit, for having the rights to it, and for how you use outputs.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Enforcement (section 8)
text: Pricing pages alone are not an invitation to probe billing systems. Auric Artisan may limit, throttle, block or disable access; remove content; suspend accounts; and report illegal activity — without prior notice where needed for security, availability, legal compliance or safety.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
heading: Reporting (section 9)
text: Report behaviour, content or activity that may break the policy through the contact page.

title: Accessibility statement
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/company/accessibility/ (last updated 23 May 2026). The official page is authoritative; this is a summary. For practical help using the site with assistive technology or comfort settings, see [Accessibility of the site](../../../help/accessibility.md).

title: Accessibility statement
heading: The commitment
text: The goal, in the statement's words: "Everyone should be able to use Auric Artisan effectively, regardless of ability, device, or interaction method." Accessibility is treated as part of design and development. Because the platform has complex visual, analytical and experimental tools, the statement says full accessibility across every feature "may not always be achievable", and improvements are made where technically feasible.

title: Accessibility statement
heading: What it aims to support
text: Where possible, the platform aims to support: - Semantic HTML — proper heading hierarchy and landmarks; - Keyboard navigation — all core functionality from the keyboard; - Readable text — contrast-aware design, scalable layouts and legible type; - Assistive technology — compatibility with modern browsers and screen readers; - ARIA attributes — added meaning for dynamic content and widgets; - Focus management — visible focus indicators and a logical tab order. It encourages you to adjust your device, browser or assistive tools as well.

title: Accessibility statement
heading: Stated limits
text: - Some tools and simulation interfaces may have limitations because of their technical nature, real-time rendering, colour-dependent output or experimental design. - Auric Artisan does not guarantee that all content will meet every accessibility standard at all times. - Spectral visualisations, the Ishihara-style generator and real-time rendering experiments may not be fully accessible to all users; alternative text and data views are provided where possible. - The Ishihara-style generator and vision simulations are exploratory and do not replace medical-grade testing.

title: Accessibility statement
heading: Standard it reviews against
text: The statement says Auric Artisan aims to review important user-facing areas against WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidance where practical, and to prioritise the fixes with the greatest impact.

title: Accessibility statement
heading: Reporting a barrier
text: The statement asks you to report accessibility barriers through the official support channels: email developer@auricartisan.com or use the contact form at https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/. It says reasonable efforts may be made to address concerns within the platform's technical scope. How to write a useful report: [Contact and support](../../../help/contact-and-support.md).

title: Author page
heading: Who writes Auric Artisan
text: Chirag Bansal is the founder and engineer of Auric Artisan and, in the page's words, "the author of everything published here". He builds and maintains the platform end to end — the colour engine, the tools, the site and the writing — works in India, and publishes the browser extension and the VS Code extensions.

title: Author page
heading: What the work covers
text: - Colour science — the engine for CIE XYZ, L\ a\ b\ , LCH, Oklab, sRGB and Display P3, colour-difference formulas (CIE76, CIE94, CIEDE2000, CMC), chromatic adaptation, gamut mapping with selectable rendering intents, and metamerism. - Colour vision — simulation models following Viénot, Brettel and Mollon (1999), Brettel, Viénot and Mollon (1997), and Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009). The Ishihara-style generator is a teaching tool, not a medical device. - Accessibility — the rule engine behind the Analyzer: WCAG 2.2 and APCA contrast, ARIA 1.2 validation, accessible-name computation, screen-reader transcript modelling, colour-vision-deficiency checks and VPAT-style reporting. - Tooling — the cross-browser extension and the VS Code extensions.

title: Author page
heading: How the articles are written
text: - The articles and documentation are written by hand, not commissioned or syndicated. - Where an article states a formula or threshold, it is the one the code uses. - Articles name the published models they rest on. Most carry no formal bibliography; the page says a references section is "something the library is still missing". - Interactive figures in the Learn library compute their results live with the same engine the tools use, so you can check a result yourself. - Corrections are welcome and made in place, with the revision date updated.

title: FAQ page
heading: Quick answers (from the top of the page)
text: - Auric Artisan is a colour-science platform: tools, simulations, web analysis and learning resources. - More than 70 vision simulation models based on the Viénot, Brettel and Machado algorithms, for education and design, not clinical use. - Web analysis covers WCAG contrast, security headers, performance signals and palette extraction. - Theme generation exports CSS custom properties, design tokens, Tailwind configuration, SCSS and Figma-compatible output. - Many tools work without an account. - You own the content and exports you create. - Only data needed to operate is collected; personal information is never sold. - Simulation outputs are software models, not certified for clinical, regulatory or safety-critical use. - Every tool is free on every tier; paid plans are one-time purchases through Razorpay.

title: FAQ page
heading: The ten sections
text: Section What it answers --- --- 1. Platform and company What Auric Artisan is, who it is for, that it is free, that it is not a government platform, and who builds it 2. Colour science and tools Supported colour spaces, colour-difference formulas (with rough ΔE00 thresholds: under 1 imperceptible, 1–2 perceptible on close inspection, over 2 clearly different), chromatic adaptation, metamerism, Oklab, and limits for colour-critical professional work 3. Vision simulations The algorithms, their accuracy, using them to test designs, the Ishihara-style generator's limits, and the conditions simulated 4. Web analysis and accessibility What the analysis checks, whether URLs are stored, WCAG AA versus AAA, and how palettes are extracted 5. Theme generation and exports Export formats, perceptually even scales, commercial use of generated themes, and the built-in accessibility audit 6. Accounts and access Whether you need an account, multiple accounts, and age requirements 7. Content and ownership Who owns your outputs, the platform's own intellectual property, and quoting its articles 8. Billing and subscriptions The pricing model, whether payments are accepted, and refunds 9. Privacy and security What is collected, local versus server processing, account deletion, encryption and cookies 10. Support and contact How to contact support, report an inaccuracy, or report a vulnerability

title: FAQ page
heading: Answers worth knowing
text: - Is it free? Yes, every tool on every tier. Paid plans add conveniences. - Do you store the URLs I analyse? The FAQ says no URL history or page content is retained after the analysis session. - Can I use generated themes commercially? Yes. Auric Artisan claims no rights over tool outputs. - Can I quote the articles? Brief quotation with attribution and a link is acceptable; full reproduction needs written permission (hello@auricartisan.com). - Multiple accounts? Technically permitted, but using them to get round usage limits may lead to suspension of all of them. - Minimum age? No specific age group; parents and guardians should review the Terms before letting minors create accounts. - Refunds? A 7-day money-back window on plan purchases; approved refunds return in 5–7 business days. - Is traffic encrypted? Yes, HTTPS with HSTS; passwords are hashed.

title: FAQ page
heading: Where other pages give newer or more specific detail
text: The FAQ was last updated before some later changes. These notes point you to the page that is more specific. Note: Account creation. The FAQ says accounts "may be available where the auth system is enabled". Accounts are live: the Terms of Service (updated 12 August 2026) list registration, sign-in and the dashboard as live. Note: Managing sessions. The FAQ's tip mentions a "Sessions page in your account settings". Signed-in devices are now under Security & Privacy in the dashboard. See [Security & Privacy section](../../account-and-billing/docs/security-and-privacy.md). Note: Deleting an account. The FAQ says access is disabled immediately and personal data is scheduled for deletion within about 90 days unless the law requires it to be kept. The dashboard describes deletion as immediate and permanent, and the Security page explains that payment records are kept in anonymised form for tax law. See [Delete your account](../../account-and-billing/docs/delete-your-account.md). Note: Reporting a vulnerability. The FAQ says to email hello@auricartisan.com with "Security" in the subject. The Security page and the contact form route security reports to security@auricartisan.com, with acknowledgement within 24 hours. Use security@auricartisan.com. See [Security page](security-page.md). Note: Currency. The FAQ describes payments in INR. The pricing page charges US dollars outside India and rupees within it.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Only data needed to operate, secure and improve the platform is kept. - Account, session, billing and API data are kept only as needed. - Tool inputs are processed only as needed; temporary processing data is deleted or anonymised when no longer required. - Security logs and abuse-prevention records may be kept for a limited period. - You can request deletion of applicable personal data through the contact channels.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Retention principles — Minimal retention: purpose limitation, storage limitation, accountability, and practices that follow what is actually deployed. 2. Types of data kept Data How long --- --- Contact and support messages As needed to respond and keep records Tool inputs (URLs, colours, images, palettes, settings) Only where necessary Generated outputs (reports, palettes, themes, exports, previews) May be temporarily stored, cached or delivered Usage analytics (aggregated or anonymised) May be kept to improve the platform Security logs (IP addresses, request metadata, abuse signals, errors) For security, debugging and abuse prevention Billing records As required by tax, accounting, payment-provider and financial rules 3. Tool processing data — What processing can involve. Avoid entering sensitive personal data, credentials, medical records, payment information or private tokens into exploratory tools unless a feature asks for it and explains why. 4. Deletion requests — Request account deletion through the account controls or support. A valid request is reviewed; eligible data in active systems is removed, minimised or anonymised within a reasonable period; backups and security logs may persist until their normal rotation. Save anything you need first — deleted data may not be recoverable. 5. Automatic deletion — Temporary processing data, cached reports and extracted assets may be removed after use; session tokens, cookies and local preferences expire according to browser settings or platform configuration; security logs are kept for a limited period. 6. Legal and compliance retention — Data may be kept longer when law, valid legal requests, disputes, investigations, abuse prevention, security or financial record-keeping require it, and then deleted, minimised or anonymised. 7. Your rights — Access, correction, export, restriction, objection, withdrawing consent, appeal and deletion, depending on applicable law (GDPR, India's DPDP Act, CCPA/CPRA and others). Use the account controls, the contact page or official support channels. Requests are answered within the time the law requires. 8. Data security — Access controls, secure transport, logging, monitoring and encryption where appropriate. See [Security Policy](security-policy.md). 9. Changes — May be updated; continued use means acceptance.

title: Privacy Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/ — version 2.3, effective 27 April 2026, last updated 27 July 2026. The official policy is authoritative. This summary is for understanding only.

title: Privacy Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Only the minimum data needed to operate and improve the platform is collected. - Sign-in, sessions and security features process authentication data where enabled. - Payments go through Razorpay; raw card, UPI or bank details are not stored. - Web analysis inputs can include URLs, page metadata, screenshots, extracted colours and scan results. - Theme, eye-rest and interface preferences may be stored locally in your browser. - Personal data is not sold or used for behavioural advertising.

title: Privacy Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Scope — Covers all Auric Artisan tools, pages and features. Using the platform means agreeing to these practices. 2. Current platform status — Accounts, the dashboard, API keys and one-time purchases are live; recurring subscriptions are not offered. Payment credentials go to Razorpay and never touch Auric Artisan's servers. 3. Data collected - Usage data — first-party analytics, only with consent: the event name, the page path (never query strings), the referrer's origin, and a few coarse properties such as device class. No cookies, no cross-site tracking; Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured. No consent means no events. - Device data — browser, operating system, screen size, language and technical environment. - Tool input data — what you enter into tools. - Communication data — what you send through contact forms, email or feedback. - Account data — email, display name, authentication details, sessions, security events and saved preferences. - Not intentionally collected: raw card details, government IDs, precise location, biometric identifiers or medical diagnostic data. 4. Web analysis data — URLs, titles, metadata, screenshots, page structure, text snippets, palettes, performance metrics, layout information and security headers. Submit only sites you own or are authorised to test; do not submit private dashboards, credentials or restricted systems. 5. Local storage and preferences — Browser storage and cookies keep the site usable and remember preferences (theme, language, layout, eye rest, recent tool state, consent). Many stay on your device. 6. How data is used — Running the tools; understanding anonymous usage and fixing problems; security; answering messages; supporting account features. No behavioural profiling or automated decisions with legal or similar effects. 7. No sale of personal data — Not sold, rented or traded; no data brokers or cross-site behavioural tracking. 8. Advertising and payments — Only order records are kept (item, amount, payment reference). Personal data is not used for targeted advertising; the policy says it will be updated before or alongside any new advertising features. 9. Security and protection — HTTPS/TLS in transit and safeguards appropriate to the platform's stage. Vision simulations and the Ishihara-style generator are not medical tools. 10. Third-party services — Cloudflare (hosting, DNS, CDN, compute and storage for account, preference and order data), Razorpay (payments) and Google Fonts (font files on some pages; Google receives the technical request, such as your IP address). Analytics is first-party. 11. Data retention — Kept only as long as needed. Temporary tool data briefly; web analysis data cached temporarily; local preferences until you clear them; contact messages as needed for support; anonymous analytics longer in aggregate. Details: [Data Retention and Deletion Policy](data-retention-and-deletion.md). 12. Your rights — Depending on where you live: access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection, withdrawing consent, grievance and appeal, and opting out of sale or targeted advertising (Auric Artisan does not sell data). Use the platform's controls, clear browser storage, adjust cookie settings, or contact Auric Artisan. 13. Legal compliance — Aims to follow India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and similar laws where they apply. 14. Changes — May be updated; material changes communicated through the platform or other reasonable channels; continued use means acceptance.

title: Refund Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/refund/ — version 4.0, effective and last updated 16 August 2026. The official policy is authoritative. The step-by-step guide is [Refunds](../../account-and-billing/docs/refunds.md).

title: Refund Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Sold through Razorpay checkout: one-time plan passes and prepaid API credit packs. Token packs are defined but not on sale; advertising bookings are arranged by hand. - Nothing renews automatically; a plan pass covers its term and stops. There is no subscription to cancel. - Every tool is free on every tier. - One-time plan purchases have a 7-day money-back window from the purchase date. - Approved refunds go back to the original payment method within 5–7 business days. - A refund ends the plan benefits, or removes the tokens or API credits the purchase granted. - Tokens and API credits are separate, and each is refunded on its own terms. - Unused prepaid API credits are refundable within the same 7-day window; spent credits are not. - Advertising bookings are refundable in full before the campaign starts.

title: Refund Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. What is sold today — Plan passes (one month or twelve months) and prepaid API credit packs. Advertising bookings are paid through a link sent after an enquiry. All payments go through Razorpay on auricartisan.com (cards, UPI, netbanking); Auric Artisan never sees your credentials. An account is required before any payment. 2. Pricing model — Every tool is free; paid plans add conveniences. Prices, durations and inclusions are shown at checkout. 3. 7-day refund window - Plans — refunded for any reason within 7 days of purchase. - Token packs — within 7 days if unused; partly used packs may be refunded pro rata at Auric Artisan's discretion. - Prepaid API credits — within 7 days to the extent unused; spent credits are not refundable; partly used balances may be refunded pro rata. The credit ledger on your account records every grant and debit. - Included allowances — part of the plan price; refunded with the plan, not separately. - After 7 days — case by case, against the checkout terms, provider records, account status, usage and law. 4. How to request — Use Request a refund in the Billing tab of your dashboard (the Plan & Usage section), or write through the contact page from the email address used for the purchase. Include the purchase date, what you bought and the order or payment reference. 5. Processing and effect — Refunds go through Razorpay to the original method within 5–7 business days of approval; your bank may take longer. The entitlement ends: plan benefits are removed and the account returns to the free tier; refunded tokens or credits are deducted. Your content and projects stay yours. 6. Advertising bookings — Full refund before the start date; after that, the undelivered portion case by case. 7. Accidental or unauthorised charges — Contact Auric Artisan with the date, amount, reference and any receipts. Do not send full card numbers, passwords or private keys. 8. Ending a plan, renewals and cancellation — Nothing renews, so there is nothing to cancel. A plan ends by itself and the account returns to Apprentice; every tool stays free and your work stays yours. Stopping sooner means asking for a refund. If recurring billing is ever introduced, it will be presented as such at checkout with the renewal date and amount, with a working cancel control, and the policy will be rewritten before the first such charge. Purchased tokens and API credits are not confiscated when a plan ends. Overage is prepaid, so no usage bill can follow. 9. Contact — Through the contact page.

title: Security page
heading: The overview
text: The page describes a layered ("defence in depth") design and headlines four figures: 256-bit AES encryption, a 9-step security pipeline, more than 20 security modules and a 3-tier defence model.

title: Security page
heading: Defence-in-depth architecture
text: Three tiers and a token layer work together: server-side checks that run before any request is handled; abuse detection that escalates from throttling to a challenge to a block; a behavioural check that scores signals such as pointer movement, typing cadence and timing without interactive challenges; and signed tokens verified on the server.

title: Security page
heading: Request security pipeline
text: Every request passes nine steps in order, and is rejected at the first one that fails: rate limiting, CSRF protection, request validation, session integrity, token verification, bot scoring, abuse analysis, escalating countermeasures (soft throttle, visual challenge, temporary block, permanent ban) and security logging.

title: Security page
heading: Encryption and data protection
text: - TLS 1.3 in transit, with HSTS. - Stored data encrypted at rest by Cloudflare; Auric Artisan does not run its own storage. - API keys, signing secrets and database credentials kept in an encrypted secret store that cannot be read back. - Two-factor secrets encrypted before storage under a separately held key.

title: Security page
heading: Authentication and access control
text: - Passwords hashed with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations; they cannot be recovered, only replaced. - API keys kept only as a SHA-256 hash plus a short prefix; shown once. - TOTP two-factor authentication with backup codes. - OAuth sign-in protected with PKCE and state checks. - Device and session management: sessions rotate, expire on inactivity, have a maximum lifetime and can be revoked remotely.

title: Security page
heading: Infrastructure security
text: Deployed on Cloudflare's edge network, with DDoS protection, a web application firewall and bot management; strict security headers on every response; HSTS with a one-year max-age, submitted for browser preload lists; each worker isolated in its own sandbox.

title: Security page
heading: Payments
text: - Cards never reach Auric Artisan: payments go through Razorpay, a PCI-DSS compliant gateway. - Orders are priced from Auric Artisan's own catalogue, so a modified browser cannot change what a purchase costs. - Payment notifications are verified before they affect an account, and delivering one twice grants an entitlement once. - Account erasure anonymises personal data rather than destroying financial records, because tax law requires invoices to be kept: "the transaction remains and your identity does not."

title: Security page
heading: What we do not claim
text: The page lists its own limits: - No formal certification — not SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA certified. - No external penetration test — the measures are implemented and tested by Auric Artisan, not independently audited. - Operated by one person — fixes ship quickly, but there is no 24/7 on-call rotation and no separation of duties; response times are best effort. - Third-party dependencies — email through Resend, payments through Razorpay, hosting and storage through Cloudflare; their security practices are their own.

title: Security page
heading: Responsible disclosure
text: - Send a detailed report to security@auricartisan.com: the vulnerability, steps to reproduce and any proof of concept. - Or use the contact form, which opens with the Security queue selected: https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/?topic=security. - Do not disclose publicly until the issue has been investigated and patched. - Stated aims: acknowledge within 24 hours, an initial assessment within 72 hours, and a fix for confirmed vulnerabilities within 30 days. - "Researchers acting in good faith will never face legal action." The contact form's Security topic asks you not to paste a working exploit into the form; send the location and impact, and a way to send the rest will follow.

title: Security Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/security/ — Security Policy & Safe Use , version 2.2, effective 27 April 2026, last updated 23 May 2026. The official policy is authoritative. For the technical description of how the platform is protected, see the separate [Security page](security-page.md).

title: Security Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Account, session, billing, API and tool traffic are protected where those features are enabled. - Web analysis must only be used on sites you own or are authorised to test. - Security checks in web analysis are informational — not a certified audit or penetration test. - Collection and retention of submitted URLs, reports and metadata is kept to a minimum. - No system can guarantee perfect security.

title: Security Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Principles — Minimisation, least privilege, responsible tooling, and improving controls as infrastructure matures. 2. Current infrastructure status — Payments are valid only through official live checkout flows. 3. Data and transmission security — Encrypted transport; limited access to submitted inputs and reports; secure, HttpOnly session cookies and CSRF checks for signed-in requests; origin checks, request-size limits, security headers and rate limits on sign-in routes; local storage for preferences where practical. 4. Web analysis scope — Only for sites, pages and assets you own, control or have permission to test. Do not probe, stress or exploit others' systems; do not present results as certification; do not submit private URLs, credentials or admin pages unless authorised; do not misrepresent another organisation's security. 5. Access control and internal practices — Restricted administrative access, separate development and production, no secrets in public code, reviewed dependencies. 6. Your responsibilities — Submit only what you may analyse; keep credentials and confidential URLs out of tool inputs; check outputs before relying on them; use vision tools only for exploration and learning; report issues responsibly rather than attempting unauthorised access. 7. Limitations and non-certification — No guarantee of absolute security; outputs are not certified industrial, medical, regulatory or safety-critical results. 8. Vulnerability reporting — Report through the contact page with enough detail to reproduce. Do not access, change, delete, download or disclose data that is not yours; act in good faith. 9. Security incidents — Investigate, contain, fix, and notify affected users or authorities where the law requires. 10. Changes — May be updated.

title: Security Policy
heading: Reporting a vulnerability in practice
text: The Security page gives the specific route: email security@auricartisan.com, or use the contact form's Security topic (https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/?topic=security). It aims to acknowledge within 24 hours. See [Security page](security-page.md responsible-disclosure).

title: Subscription and Billing Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/subscription-billing/ — version 2.4, effective and last updated 16 August 2026. The official policy is authoritative. The practical guides are in [Account and billing](../../account-and-billing/README.md).

title: Subscription and Billing Policy
heading: Key points
text: - One-time plan passes are sold through Razorpay checkout (cards, UPI, netbanking). Token packs are defined but not on sale — tokens arrive with a plan. - Recurring subscriptions are not offered: a purchase grants a fixed period, never auto-renews, and leaves nothing to cancel; to stop early, ask for a refund. - An account is required before any payment. - No one is charged unless an official checkout clearly shows the final terms. - Every tool is free on every tier; paid plans add conveniences and higher quotas. - API usage is metered in credits against a published allowance — 1,000,000 on Specialist, 10,000,000 on Industrial Pro. - API credits and tokens are separate balances. - API overage is opt-in, off by default and strictly prepaid: no API usage is ever invoiced after the fact. - Industrial Pro subscriptions started before 12 August 2026 keep their unlimited API allowance.

title: Subscription and Billing Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Current billing status — Account registration and checkout for one-time plan passes and prepaid API credit packs. Recurring billing is not enabled. Changes to what or when you are charged are announced in the policy before they take effect. 2. Pricing pages and preview information — Prices and plan tables on the site are not purchase offers unless a live checkout presents final terms. Preview prices, names and features may change. 3. Payments, renewals and cancellation — What is live: one-time passes and prepaid API credit packs through Razorpay on auricartisan.com. No automatic renewal, no mandate, no stored card. An account is required. No cancellation flow exists because no recurring charge exists; ending early is a refund. Stripe is not enabled; every live payment goes through Razorpay. 4. Paid services — A single charge for one month or twelve. Plan scope, price, term and refund rules are shown before payment. The price you see is the total you pay : no GST or other tax is added or collected, because Auric Artisan is not currently registered for GST; receipts are payment receipts, not GST invoices, and cannot be used for input tax credit. If you need a GST invoice, wait until registration is in place. When a term ends the account returns to Apprentice. To stop earlier, a refund is unconditional within 7 days and case by case after; the dashboard carries a Request a refund button. If recurring billing is introduced later, the renewal date and amount will be shown before payment, with a working cancel control, and the policy updated first. 5. API usage credits, overage and spend caps - 5.1 Measurement — One credit per standard request, weighted up for heavier endpoints (weightings in the API documentation). Counted per account, not per key. Allowances: 1,000,000 on Specialist, 10,000,000 on Industrial Pro, refreshing each billing month; none on plans without API access. - 5.2 Overage — When the allowance is used up, requests are refused and nothing is charged. Optional overage (off by default) spends prepaid credits at $1.00 (about ₹85) per 100,000; if the balance does not cover a request, it is refused. No usage is invoiced afterwards and no debt is created. - 5.3 Spend caps — A monthly cap in money, up to $10,000, limiting overage only. - 5.4 Hard ceilings — Ten times the included allowance per month, whatever the settings; support can raise it. - 5.5 Expiry — Included credits and tokens expire at the end of their period. Purchased credits and tokens do not expire at period boundaries while the account is open. The Apprentice starter grant is one-time and non-renewing. - 5.6 Plans ending and downgrades — The included API allowance ends with the plan. Purchased credits are kept and become spendable again on a plan with API access. Check your plan can spend credits before buying: a balance bought on Apprentice or Artisan is recorded and does not expire, but cannot be spent there. - 5.7 Previously sold unlimited access — Industrial Pro purchases before 12 August 2026 are metered at 1,000,000,000 credits a billing month. - 5.8 Changes — Weightings, allowances and the overage rate may change; credits already bought keep their number. 6. Advertisements — Paid plans include an ad-free option. Ads shown to free users are limited and consent-gated; private data is not used for advertising profiles. 7. Mistaken or unauthorised charges — Contact Auric Artisan with the date, amount, provider and any reference; it is checked against checkout and provider records. 8. Service availability and development — Features may change. Web analysis is for sites you own or may analyse. Simulations and Ishihara-style generators are exploratory. 9. Changes — The policy may be updated as the checkout, pricing or service model changes. Note: The policy calls the refund button part of the dashboard's "Billing tab". In the current dashboard it is in the Plan & Usage section; the old Billing address still leads there.

title: Terms of Service
heading: Key points
text: - Auric Artisan provides colour tools, colour-science resources, web analysis, theme generation and visual simulations, including more than 70 vision simulation models. - Web analysis is for sites and assets you own or are authorised to test. - Accounts are live. One-time purchases go through Razorpay; recurring subscriptions are not offered. - API access is metered in API credits against a published monthly allowance; overage is opt-in, prepaid and never invoiced afterwards. - API credits and tokens are separate balances, and neither pays for the other. - Outputs are exploratory and informational — not certified professional, medical, legal, security or accessibility advice. - The Ishihara-style generator does not replace medical-grade Ishihara plates.

title: Terms of Service
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Introduction and agreement — Using the platform means agreeing to the Terms and the policies they reference. The plain-language note: use the tools responsibly, respect ownership and safety limits, and understand the platform is still evolving. 2. What Auric Artisan provides — Colour tools and models, articles, simulations, web analysis (security-oriented checks, Lighthouse-like performance review, responsive review, palette extraction, structure and visual analysis) and theme generation. 3. Current platform status — Registration, sign-in and the dashboard are live. Plan passes and advertising bookings are sold as one-time purchases through Razorpay; token packs are not on sale. Nothing renews and no mandate is stored; "subscription" in the Terms means the plan record and its period, not a recurring charge. Every tool is free on every tier. API access is included from Specialist and metered against a finite allowance for purchases on or after 12 August 2026. Features may change. Pay only through the Razorpay checkout on auricartisan.com. 4. Eligibility and access — You are responsible for complying with the laws, permissions and consent rules where you are. Some parts need registration; access can vary by tool, region and capacity. 5. Accounts and security — You are responsible for keeping your credentials secure, keeping recovery details current, and for all activity through your account. 6. Acceptable use — No unlawful activity, harassment, abuse, spam, unauthorised access or disruption. No scraping, reverse engineering, overloading, copying, reselling or redistributing the platform without written permission. Full rules: [Acceptable Use Policy](acceptable-use-policy.md). 7. Web analysis and authorised testing — Analyse only what you own, manage or are explicitly authorised to test. Do not use findings to attack or gain access to anything. Security observations are informational and are not a certified audit; other observations are guidance. You are responsible for having permission before submitting a site. 8. User content and ownership — You keep ownership of what you create, upload or submit, subject to third-party rights. Auric Artisan receives only the limited permission needed to process it and run the platform. You are responsible for not infringing others' rights. See [Content and IP Policy](content-and-ip-policy.md). 9. Simulations and disclaimers — Outputs are informational and "as is", and must not replace certified medical, legal, governmental, accessibility, security, industrial, regulatory or safety-critical review. The Ishihara-style generator is not a clinical tool and does not diagnose. 10. Pricing, payments and billing — Auric Artisan sells one-time plan passes, token packs and advertising bookings through Razorpay; price, duration and inclusions are shown at checkout. Tokens and API credits are separate. API usage is metered against a finite allowance; exhausted allowances are refused, not billed. Overage is optional, off by default and prepaid, limited by your spend cap and a ceiling of ten times the allowance, and never invoiced afterwards. Industrial Pro purchases before 12 August 2026 keep their unlimited API allowance. Billing, cancellation, tax and refunds follow the Subscription and Billing Policy and Refund Policy in force at purchase, including the 7-day money-back window. Report any other payment request as fraudulent. 11. Third-party services and availability — The platform relies on third parties for hosting, analytics, infrastructure and security, and is not responsible for their outages or behaviour. Tools and services may be changed, paused or removed. 12. Liability, governing law and changes — To the extent the law allows, no liability for indirect, incidental, consequential, special, exemplary or punitive damages from use, reliance on outputs, interruption, data loss or third-party issues. The Terms are governed by the laws of India, and aim to align data practices with laws including India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The Terms may be updated; continued use means acceptance. Together with the referenced policies, they form the agreement between you and Auric Artisan. Note: Section 10 mentions payments "in INR" and lists token packs among things sold, while section 3 says token packs are not on sale. The pricing page charges US dollars outside India and rupees within it, and marks token top-ups "not on sale". Follow the pricing page and checkout for what is actually offered.

title: Transparency and Ethics Policy
text: Official page: https://auricartisan.com/legal/transparency/ — Transparency & Ethics Policy , version 2.2, effective 27 April 2026, last updated 23 May 2026. The official policy is authoritative.

title: Transparency and Ethics Policy
heading: Key points
text: - Auric Artisan explains what its tools can and cannot do. - Web analysis outputs are guidance, not certified security, accessibility or performance audits. - Vision simulations and the Ishihara-style generator are exploratory, not medical diagnostics. - Pricing, account, checkout and paid features apply only where clearly enabled. - The platform stays independent and documents limitations, changes and data practices.

title: Transparency and Ethics Policy
heading: Section by section
text: 1. Philosophy — "Tools should respect intelligence": help people understand what they are doing instead of hiding it behind vague output; avoid inflated claims; make limits visible. 2. Operational transparency — A commitment to document what data is collected and why; what the tools can and cannot do; when outputs are estimates, heuristics or models; how submitted material is processed; what is still in development; and changes to terms, pricing, access, payments or availability. 3. Accuracy and limitations — Results can depend on browser behaviour, rendering, source quality, network conditions and implementation. Web analysis results are not certified audits, official Lighthouse reports, legal compliance reviews or guaranteed findings. Vision models may not match every viewer, display or lighting condition. The Ishihara-style generator is not a medical device. 4. Automation and AI — Where automated systems, machine learning or AI-assisted tools are used, the aim is to say so in the interface or documentation; outputs should be reviewed; none are presented as professional certification or advice. 5. Advertising and commercial status — No behavioural profiling for advertising, no use of private data for ad targeting, no hidden sponsorship mixed into tool outputs; sponsored content will be clearly distinguishable. 6. Pricing status and fairness — No hidden fees or surprise charges; costs shown before purchase; a clear line between free, preview and paid; advance notice where practical for material changes. 7. Neutrality and independence — Not a government entity, medical provider, certification body, standards authority or testing laboratory. No partnerships that compromise privacy, data integrity, honest labelling or editorial independence. 8. User responsibility — Verify outputs and use your own judgement: analyse only what you may; do not treat analysis as a professional audit or simulations as diagnosis; review generated material before production; respect others' rights. 9. Ongoing evaluation — Tool labels, model limits, explanations and privacy notices are reviewed as features are added. Feedback about unclear pricing, data handling or limits is welcome through the contact page. 10. Changes — May be updated; continued use means acceptance.

title: Glossary
text: These definitions explain terms as the policies use them. They are not legal definitions and do not change the policies. Acceptable use — The rules on what you may and may not do with the platform; set out in the Acceptable Use Policy. Anonymise — To remove the link between data and a person, so the data remains but no longer identifies anyone. Auric Artisan anonymises payment records on account erasure. APCA — The Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm, a newer way to measure text contrast, used alongside WCAG ratios in the Analyzer. Authorised testing — Analysing a site, page or asset you own, manage or have explicit permission to test. The only kind of web analysis the policies allow. CCPA / CPRA — California's consumer privacy laws, named in the Privacy Policy among the laws it aims to follow where they apply. Chargeback — A payment reversed by your bank or card issuer. Consent (cookie consent) — Your choice, recorded in your browser, about which optional cookie categories may run. CSRF — Cross-site request forgery: a trick that makes your browser send a request you did not intend. The site uses a CSRF cookie and checks to prevent it. Data minimisation — Collecting and keeping only the data that is needed. Do Not Track (DNT) / Global Privacy Control (GPC) — Browser signals asking sites not to track you. Auric Artisan's analytics honours both. DPDP Act — India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, named in the Terms and Privacy Policy. Effective date — The date a policy took effect. Last updated is the date of its latest change. Entitlement — What a purchase gives your account, such as a plan's benefits or a credit balance. A refund ends the entitlement. Erasure (right to) — The right to ask for personal data to be deleted, where applicable. First-party — Set or run by auricartisan.com itself, rather than by another company. GDPR / UK GDPR — The European Union's and the United Kingdom's data-protection laws. GST — India's Goods and Services Tax. Auric Artisan is not currently registered for GST, so no GST is charged and receipts are not GST invoices. HSTS — HTTP Strict Transport Security: a rule telling browsers to use only secure HTTPS connections to the site. Input tax credit — A business's ability to offset GST paid on purchases; not available on Auric Artisan's receipts. Licence (noun) — Permission to use something under conditions. The License Agreement gives you a limited licence to use the platform. Mandate — A standing permission for a merchant to charge you again. Auric Artisan stores none. Overage — API use beyond the included monthly allowance, paid from prepaid credits only if you turn it on. PCI-DSS — The card industry's security standard. Razorpay, which handles card details, is PCI-DSS compliant. Penetration test — An authorised simulated attack to find weaknesses. The Security page states that no external one has been done. Plan pass — A one-time purchase of a paid plan for a fixed term; it does not renew. Portability (right to) — The right to receive a copy of your data in a usable format. Pro rata — In proportion; for example, refunding the unused part of a partly used balance. Processing licence — The limited permission you give Auric Artisan to process what you submit, only as needed to run the tool. Responsible disclosure — Reporting a security weakness privately and giving time to fix it before telling anyone else. Retention — How long data is kept. SLA — Service-level agreement: a contractual promise of uptime. Auric Artisan has none yet. SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA — Security and privacy certifications or regimes. The Security page states Auric Artisan holds none of them. Telemetry — Usage data a program sends back to its maker. The browser extension and VS Code extensions send none. Third party — A company other than Auric Artisan, such as Cloudflare, Razorpay, Google Fonts or Resend. TLS — Transport Layer Security, the encryption behind HTTPS. WCAG — The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines published by the W3C. Level AA and AAA are its common targets.

title: VS Code extensions
text: Auric Artisan publishes seventeen free extensions for Visual Studio Code under the publisher auric-artisan . They bring the same design system as the website into your editor: colour and accessibility linting, a theme with a live Theme Studio, icon and emoji libraries, file icon themes, a live server, a file workspace, a font hub and a formatter. None of them sends telemetry. Two of them are packs that install a set in one step: the Icon Pack installs Modern, Drawn, Playful and Emoji, and the Studio Full Pack installs Color, Accessibility and Code Health. Every member stays its own extension that you can disable on its own. New to installing extensions? Start with [Install and set up](install-and-setup/README.md).

title: Install and set up the Auric Artisan VS Code extensions
text: Auric Artisan publishes seventeen extensions for Visual Studio Code under the publisher name auric-artisan . They cover colour themes, file icons, icon and emoji libraries, colour and accessibility tooling, code health, a live development server, a file workspace, a font hub and a code formatter. Every extension is free and installs on its own. Two of them are extension packs : a pack contains no features of its own and simply installs a group of other extensions in one step. This folder covers everything that is the same for all seventeen: finding and installing an extension, installing from the command line or from a VSIX file, using the packs, installing in editors built on VS Code (Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium), updating, disabling and removing, where settings live, how Settings Sync treats them, switching the interface to Hindi where an extension supports it, and where to report a problem. The guides for what each extension does live in that extension's own folder. This folder only gets you to the point where the extension is installed and configured the way you want.

title: Install and set up the Auric Artisan VS Code extensions
heading: Who it is for
text: - Anyone installing an Auric Artisan extension for the first time. - Teams that want to install the same set of extensions on several machines, or share settings through a repository. - People using Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium or another editor based on VS Code. - Anyone who needs to update, roll back, disable or remove an extension, or report a problem.

title: Install and set up the Auric Artisan VS Code extensions
heading: Where to find the extensions
text: - The Visual Studio Marketplace, publisher auric-artisan . Each extension has a page at https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=<extension ID . - The Auric Artisan VS Code page: https://auricartisan.com/vscode/ - Inside VS Code: the Extensions view ( Ctrl + Shift + X ). The full list of extension IDs, with the minimum VS Code version each one needs, is in [the reference](docs/reference.md). To install from a terminal, pass the extension ID to the VS Code command-line launcher: text code --install-extension auric-artisan.auric-artisan-live

title: Install and set up the Auric Artisan VS Code extensions
heading: Quick start
text: 1. Open VS Code and check its version under Help › About (on macOS, Code › About Visual Studio Code ). Compare it with the minimum in [the reference](docs/reference.md). 2. Open the Extensions view with Ctrl + Shift + X . 3. Type the exact ID with the @id: prefix, for example @id:auric-artisan.auric-artisan-formatter , and clear any other filter such as @installed . 4. Check that the publisher shown under the name is Auric Artisan ( auric-artisan ), then select Install . 5. Open the Command Palette ( Ctrl + Shift + P ) and type the extension's command prefix, for example Auric Formatter , to see its commands. 6. Open File › Preferences › Settings and search for the extension's setting prefix (for example auricFormatter ) to review its options. 7. If VS Code asks whether you trust the folder you opened, read [Settings, sync and workspace trust](docs/settings-and-sync.md) before you answer: several extensions limit what they do in an untrusted folder.

title: Install and set up the Auric Artisan VS Code extensions
heading: What you can do
text: - Install any extension from the Extensions view, the command line or a VSIX file. - Install a whole group in one step with the Icon Pack or the Studio Full Pack. - Install in Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium and other editors based on VS Code. - Update, roll back to an earlier version, disable or uninstall an extension. - Choose between user settings and workspace settings, and share a configuration with a team. - Keep extensions and settings in step across machines with VS Code Settings Sync. - Use the extensions in Hindi where they support it: Auric Artisan Live, Auric Artisan Theme and Auric Artisan Emoji. - Get support, with the information support needs.

title: Install an extension from the Extensions view
text: The Extensions view is the panel inside VS Code where you search the Visual Studio Marketplace and install, update and manage extensions. This is the simplest way to install any Auric Artisan extension, and it needs a network connection to the Marketplace.

title: Install an extension from the Extensions view
heading: Before you start
text: - Check your VS Code version. Open Help › About (on macOS, Code › About Visual Studio Code ). Each extension states the lowest version it runs on. The lowest version across the family is 1.74; Auric Artisan Live and Auric Artisan File System need 1.95. The [reference](reference.md) lists every extension. - Open a folder if the extension works on a project. Auric Artisan Live, File System and Formatter act on the folder you have open. The icon, theme and library extensions work without one.

title: Install an extension from the Extensions view
heading: Install
text: 1. Open the Extensions view: select the Extensions icon in the Activity Bar, or press Ctrl + Shift + X . 2. In the search box, type the extension ID with the @id: prefix. For example: text @id:auric-artisan.auric-artisan-live The @id: prefix returns exactly one extension. You can also type a name such as Auric Artisan and browse the results. 3. Remove any other filter from the search box, such as @installed or @disabled . A leftover filter hides extensions you have not installed yet. 4. Select the result. Check that the publisher shown under the name is Auric Artisan and that the identifier on the page matches the ID you searched for. 5. Select Install . 6. If VS Code shows a trust prompt for the publisher, read it and confirm. When installation finishes, the Install button changes to Disable and Uninstall (or a settings gear), and the extension is active. Most Auric Artisan extensions do not need a restart.

title: Install an extension from the Extensions view
heading: Check it worked
text: - Command Palette. Press Ctrl + Shift + P and type the extension's command prefix. Each extension groups its commands under a prefix, shown in the table below. - Activity Bar or Explorer. Some extensions add their own icon to the Activity Bar (for example Auric Live and Auric Font Hub ) or a section to the Explorer (for example Auric Files and Auric Formatter ). - Features tab. On the extension's page in the Extensions view, the Features tab lists every command, setting and keyboard shortcut the extension contributes. Auric Artisan Font Hub Auric Artisan Font Hub (and Auric Font Hub for Show Logs ) auricFontLib. Auric Artisan Formatter Auric Formatter auricFormatter. Auric Artisan Theme Auric Theme auricTheme. Auric Artisan File Icons Auric Artisan File Icons auricFileIcons. Auric Icons: Modern Auric Icons: Modern auricIcons. Auric Icons: Drawn Auric Icons: Drawn auricIconsDrawn. Auric Icons: Playful Auric Icons: Playful auricIconsPlayful. Auric Artisan Emoji Auric Artisan Emoji auricEmoji. Auric Artisan Icon Studio Auric Icon Studio auricIconStudio. title: Install an extension from the Extensions view
heading: Install several at once
text: - Install a pack to get a set in one step. See [The two extension packs](extension-packs.md). - Run several code --install-extension lines in a terminal. See [Install from the command line](install-from-command-line.md). - Add the IDs to your repository's .vscode/extensions.json so VS Code recommends them to everyone who opens the project.
