title: Design tokens and personalisation
heading: Design tokens
text: Turn one seed colour into a complete, contrast-checked token system. 2–4 credits. Ramps are stepped in OKLCH so every hue is perceptually even, chroma follows a gamut-aware envelope so the light and dark ends stay distinct, and foreground roles are measured: --color-on-primary is whichever of white or ink actually clears 4.5:1. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- seed colour Yes The seed colour name string No System name used in file headers harmony string No analogous (default), complementary , triadic or mono include string array No Any of color , space , radius , type . Default all. dark boolean No Include dark-mode roles. Default true . Returns meta , contrast , out of gamut and tokens . bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/tokens/generate" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"seed":" c9a227","name":"Auric","harmony":"analogous"}' Render a token deck for a platform. There are ten targets, from CSS custom properties to Jetpack Compose. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- tokens array Yes Objects of { name, value, group? } : the tokens array from generate, or your own format string Yes See /v1/tokens/formats name string No System name for the file header raw boolean No true returns the file itself, as a download, instead of a JSON envelope bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/tokens/export" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"format":"css","tokens":[{"name":"--color-primary","value":" c9a227"}]}' The ten token export targets.

title: Design tokens and personalisation
heading: Personalisation
text: These endpoints drive the palette search behind the website's personalisation generator. A brief combines seed colours, style keys, an intent and weights. Everything a brief may name, with the ranges the engine really applies: the 18 style profiles with their chroma, lightness and saturation windows, the five intents, the 19 hue relationships and their offsets, the 17 type systems, and the gradient and poster catalogues. Read it before writing a brief. Returns styles , intents , relationships , type systems and limits . The 17 briefs the tool ships, in request shape; each can be posted straight to the endpoints below. Returns count and presets . Grow a working set of colours from seeds and a brief. The search works within this pool. The response also returns the brief resolved to numbers. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- colors string array No Seed colours, up to 64. Defaults to the tool's own eight. styles string array No Style keys from the vocabulary intent string No ui (default), brand , poster , editorial or dashboard target integer No Pool size, 1–240. Default 64. warmth number No 0–100. Default 52. seed integer No Omit for a random one; it is always returned Returns brief , pool and profile . bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/personalize/pool" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"colors":[" 0F172A"," D3AF37"],"styles":["luxe","editorial"],"target":24}' Rank a palette you already have on the search's six scores: preference, harmony, diversity, contrast, style fit and accessibility. Omit relationship and every hue geometry is tried, with the best fit reported. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- palette string array Yes 2–12 colours relationship string No A relationship id to measure against styles string array No The brief it is judged for intent string No One of the five intents accessibility number No 0–100, how hard accessibility is weighted. Default 72. Returns score , measured as , best pair and alternatives . Search: N candidates in, the best K out, each with its breakdown. The response reports what the sweep did: how many candidates were sampled, how many survived de-duplication and where the cut fell. Contrast and colour vision are weights in the score, not filters, so a candidate that reads badly is ranked down rather than removed. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- colors , styles , intent — No The brief note string No Free text, matched against curated colour memories depth integer No Candidates to sample, 8–1200. Default 320. keep integer No How many to return, 1–120. Default 24. palette size integer No Colours per palette, 5–12. Default 6. diversity number No 0–100. Default 68. accessibility number No 0–100. Default 72. cvd safe boolean No Weight colour-vision separation. Default true . unique boolean No Drop repeated signatures. Default true . seed integer No The same seed and brief always give the same result Returns brief , sweep and palettes . bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/personalize/palettes" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"colors":[" 0F172A"," D3AF37"],"styles":["luxe","editorial"],"intent":"brand","depth":400,"keep":12}' One brief in, a design system out: the sweep, then from its leading palette, gradients, type pairings, UI colour pairs with WCAG and APCA measured, poster compositions, and a token deck with tonal ramps, light, dark and high-contrast themes and a contrast matrix. include trims both the response and the work. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- colors , styles , intent — No The brief include string array No Any of palettes , gradients , typography , ui pairs , posters , tokens . Default all. derived integer No Palettes each derived section covers, 1–24. Default 8. depth integer No Candidates to sample, 8–1200. Default 320. keep integer No Palettes to keep, 1–120. Default 24. seed integer No Omit for a random one; it is always returned Returns leader , palettes , gradients , typography , ui pairs , posters and tokens . bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/personalize/system" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"colors":[" 0F172A"," D3AF37"],"styles":["tech","minimal"],"intent":"ui","include":["tokens","ui pairs"]}'

title: Usage, jobs, webhooks and GraphQL
heading: Usage
text: Per-day, per-endpoint usage history. Parameter In Description --- --- --- since query Earliest day to include, YYYY-MM-DD . Defaults to seven days back. bash curl "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/usage" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" Your tier, limits and month-to-date consumption. bash curl "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/usage/me" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" json {"tier":"pro","plan":"specialist","auth type":"api key", "limits":{"rate per minute":300,"monthly quota":1000000}, "this month":{"slot":"2026-08","used":412}} used counts credits, not calls. The last 100 individual calls, with rolling latency and error statistics. It answers "what is happening right now", where /v1/usage answers "how much have I used". Pass the returned cursor back as since to poll for new calls only. Parameter In Description --- --- --- limit query 1–100. Default 50. since query Sequence number from a previous cursor Returns cursor , stats and events . The same live feed, pushed over Server-Sent Events (SSE). It emits hello on connect with current stats, usage for each request, and heartbeat every 15 seconds. Connections are capped at 10 minutes; a browser EventSource reconnects on its own. 5 credits, charged once when the stream opens; events are free. bash curl "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/usage/stream" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY"

title: Usage, jobs, webhooks and GraphQL
heading: Async jobs
text: Long-running work runs as a job: you queue it, get an id back at once, then poll or follow it. The job types available, and what each accepts. Queue a job. 25 credits. The body is the parameter set for the chosen job type, so its shape varies; GET /v1/jobs documents each type. bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/jobs/palette-batch" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"count":500}' Poll one job. 1 credit per poll. bash curl "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/jobs/id/<id " \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" Follow a job to completion over SSE instead of polling.

title: Usage, jobs, webhooks and GraphQL
heading: Webhooks
text: The event types you can subscribe to. Public, so you can check whether the API fits before you buy. Events mentioned in the documentation include job.succeeded and quota.threshold , which fires when you cross 80% of your included credits. bash curl "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/webhooks/events" Subscribe a URL to one or more events. Deliveries are signed: verify the signature header before trusting a payload. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- url string Yes HTTPS endpoint to deliver to events string array Yes From /v1/webhooks/events bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/webhooks" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"url":"https://example.com/hook","events":["job.succeeded"]}' List your subscriptions, fetch one, or revoke one. bash curl -X DELETE "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/webhooks/<id " \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY"

title: Usage, jobs, webhooks and GraphQL
heading: GraphQL
text: The GraphQL playground. Public. Run a GraphQL query against the same resolvers as the REST endpoints. 2–4 credits. Useful when one round trip should answer several questions, such as converting a colour, checking its contrast and simulating it at once. Field Type Required Description --- --- --- --- query string Yes The GraphQL document variables object No Variable values bash curl -X POST "https://api.auricartisan.com/v1/graphql" \ -H "x-api-key: $AURIC API KEY" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"query":"{ contrast(foreground: \" 000\", background: \" fff\") { ratio wcag aa } }"}'

title: Vision and Ishihara
text: The vision endpoints distinguish two kinds of identifier: - Models are simulation engines, such as brettel-deutan . List them with GET /v1/vision/models . - Conditions are documented vision conditions, such as deuteranopia or glaucoma . List them with GET /v1/vision/conditions . /v1/vision/simulate takes a model. The palette and audit endpoints take conditions.

title: Glossary
heading: API terms
text: API key. A secret string, starting aa , that identifies your account on each request. Created in the dashboard and shown once. Async job. Work that takes too long for one request. You queue it, receive an id, then poll it or follow it over SSE. Credit. The unit your monthly quota is counted in. A standard call costs 1; heavier calls cost more. Cursor. A position in a scanned collection. Pass next cursor back as cursor to continue. Discovery endpoint. A public, unmetered endpoint that describes the API, such as /v1/catalog . GraphQL. A query language that lets one request ask several questions at once, through /v1/graphql . Hard ceiling. The absolute monthly limit, ten times the included allowance, that stops runaway usage. OpenAPI. A standard, machine-readable description of an HTTP API, served at /v1/openapi.yaml . Overage. Usage beyond the included credits, paid from a prepaid credit balance, and only if you turn it on. Quota. Your included credits for the month. Rate limit. How many requests you may make per minute. Scope and stage. In the analyzer, a stage is one group of checks; scope is the list of stages you ask for. Server-Sent Events (SSE). A way for a server to push a stream of events over one HTTP connection, used by the usage and job streams. Spend cap. A monthly limit, in money, you set on overage. Truncated. A scanned-collection response whose scan budget ran out before the page filled; it does not mean nothing matches. Webhook. A URL you register to receive signed event notifications, such as job.succeeded .

title: Glossary
heading: Colour science
text: CCT and Duv. Correlated colour temperature, in kelvin, describes a near-white light by the temperature of the closest black-body colour. Duv is how far the colour sits from that black-body curve (the Planckian locus); beyond about ±0.05 a temperature no longer describes it. CIEDE2000, CIE94, CIE76, CMC. Formulae for Delta E, the perceptual difference between two colours. CIEDE2000 is the most accurate and the API's headline figure. Colour space. A system for describing colours with numbers. The API's registry has 63. Illuminant. A standard reference light, such as D65 (average daylight), used to define white. OKLab and OKLCH. Perceptual colour spaces in which equal numeric steps look like equal visual steps. OKLCH writes OKLab as lightness, chroma and hue. Planckian locus. The curve of colours a black body glows at different temperatures. White point. The colour a space treats as white, such as D65.

title: Glossary
heading: Accessibility
text: APCA. The Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm from the WCAG 3 drafts, which scores contrast as Lc with polarity. Auric SD. Auric Artisan's own contrast grading, with Flexible and Strict variants and grades from A+ to F. Banding. Visible steps in a gradient that should look smooth. Colour-vision deficiency (CVD). Reduced ability to tell some colours apart, such as protanopia or deuteranopia. Contrast ratio. WCAG's measure of the difference in luminance between two colours, from 1:1 to 21:1. Body text needs 4.5:1 at level AA. Polarity. Whether text is dark on light (BoW) or light on dark (WoB). WCAG. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Colour science
text: - Delta E: CIEDE2000 is the headline figure and is verified against the Sharma reference set, the standard test data for that formula. - Colour temperature is only meaningful near the Planckian locus. The response reports Duv and a meaningful flag; beyond about ±0.05 Duv, a temperature does not describe the colour. - Nearest colour in the atlas uses CIE76 distance in Lab, and the response names the metric.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Accessibility
text: - Contrast checks work on the colours you send. They cannot know what is actually behind text on a real page; for that, measure the rendered page, for example with the website's Analyzer or the browser extension. - APCA is a draft method for WCAG 3; its thresholds may change. - /v1/accessibility/map returns null lightness for hues that can never reach the target on a background. That is a real answer, not a failure. - /v1/accessibility/audit and /v1/accessibility/picks refuse to return colours that do not meet the target.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Vision simulation
text: - Simulations model how colours may appear with a deficiency; they are not a diagnosis, and individual vision varies. - /v1/vision/palette and /v1/vision/audit simulate colour conditions; spatial conditions are listed under refused .

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Collections
text: - Library and corpus records are derived from a published seed, so ids are reproducible and citable. - Statistics endpoints count or sample the collection and state the sample they used. - In the five-million-record collections, a filtered browse scans a budget of records. A truncated page is not proof that nothing matches.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Analyzer
text: - /v1/analyzer/inspect reads page source only. It refuses contrast, the accessibility engine, deep DOM analysis, performance, the rendered-versus-raw comparison and simulation rather than guess. - palette returns declared colours, not the colours that cover the most pixels; media misses anything added by JavaScript. - There is no overall score. The markup-level a11y category is not the analyzer's full accessibility engine. - PDF reports show Latin characters only.

title: Limits and accuracy
heading: Operational limits
text: - Image request bodies are limited to 4 MB. - Usage streams are capped at 10 minutes per connection. - Rate limits, quotas and ceilings are listed in [Plans, credits and quotas](../docs/plans-credits-and-quotas.md).

title: Privacy
text: This page covers what the API's documentation says about data. The site's privacy policy, https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/, covers your account as a whole.

title: Privacy
heading: Keys
text: - The full key is shown once, when you create it, and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. Nobody can recover it later. - Each successful request updates the key's "last used" time, visible in your dashboard.

title: Privacy
heading: Usage records
text: The API keeps a record of your use so it can meter and report it: - per-day, per-endpoint history, available through GET /v1/usage ; - the last 100 individual calls with latency and errors, through GET /v1/usage/live and the stream; - your month-to-date credits, through GET /v1/usage/me . Error responses carry a request id so a specific call can be traced when you ask for support.

title: Privacy
heading: What you send
text: The API processes the colours, palettes, images, reports and other values you send in order to answer the request. Do not send personal data you do not need to.

title: Privacy
heading: Analyzer requests
text: POST /v1/analyzer/inspect fetches the public URL you name and reads its source. Private and reserved addresses are refused. POST /v1/analyzer/render fetches nothing: it renders the report you send.

title: Privacy
heading: Webhooks
text: Webhook deliveries go only to the HTTPS URLs you register, and are signed so you can verify they came from the API.

text: Auric Artisan is building small plugins that bring its colour and accessibility checks into design tools and launchers: Figma, Penpot, Sketch, Raycast and Alfred. None of them is published yet. In the meantime, the same checks are available today in the [browser extension](../browser-extension/README.md), in the VS Code extensions (see the VS Code extensions section of these docs), and in the tools on https://auricartisan.com.

title: Design tool plugins
heading: Planned capabilities in brief
text: These descriptions come from the site's plugins guide and may change before release. - Design plugins (Figma, Penpot, Sketch): check the contrast of text against its effective background in the selected frame or layers (or the current page when nothing is selected), report the WCAG ratio and APCA Lc of failing pairs, select or outline failing layers, nudge failing colours toward a target ratio, generate palettes from a seed colour, and preview protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia and achromatopsia. - Launcher plugins (Raycast, Alfred): check the contrast of two colours typed as HEX, rgb() , hsl() or CSS colour names, and copy the ratio, the APCA value, normalised HEX values or a summary. - Privacy: the plugins are designed to run locally in their host application, without an Auric Artisan account or API key for contrast checks.

The official statement is https://auricartisan.com/company/accessibility/, summarised in [Accessibility statement](../website/company-and-legal/docs/accessibility-statement.md).

title: Accessibility of the site
heading: What the site aims to support
text: The Accessibility Statement names these aims: semantic HTML with headings and landmarks; keyboard access to all core functionality; readable, contrast-aware and scalable text; compatibility with modern screen readers; ARIA semantics for dynamic widgets; and visible focus with a logical tab order. It says important areas are reviewed against WCAG 2.1 Level AA where practical.

title: Accessibility of the site
heading: Screen readers
text: - Pages use headings and landmarks, so heading and region navigation work. - Dialogs such as the upgrade dialog keep focus inside while open and return it when closed. - Status messages (saved, copied, errors) are announced as they appear on the account pages and in forms. - Charts in the account dashboard have a Show as table equivalent. - The human check on the sign-in page names each mark for assistive technology ("Add" and the mark's name).

title: Accessibility of the site
heading: Known limits
text: The statement is candid that some things may not be fully accessible: spectral visualisations, the Ishihara-style generator and real-time rendering experiments depend on colour and graphics by nature. It says alternative text and data views are provided where possible, and that full accessibility across every feature may not always be achievable.

title: Contact and support
heading: Send a message
text: 1. Open https://auricartisan.com/company/contact/. 2. Under What is this about? , select a topic. (With the keyboard, the topics are one stop: use the arrow keys.) 3. Fill in Name and Email (both required). Use the email address on your account for account or billing questions. 4. Fill in the reference field — its label changes with the topic. 5. Write your Message (up to 2,000 characters; a counter shows how many you have used). The toolbar offers Bold , Italic , Inline code , Bulleted list , Code block and Link ; Ctrl + B , Ctrl + I and Ctrl + K work too. The message is sent as plain text, and pasted text loses its formatting. 6. Optional: add up to four screenshots (see below). 7. Select Send . Result: "Thanks. Your message was sent." You receive a confirmation at the address you gave. The reply comes from the topic's inbox, in the same email thread. If your message leads to a change, you get the link when it ships. If something is missing, the form says so: "Name is required.", "Enter a valid email address.", "Message cannot be empty." or "Message exceeds 2000 characters." If sending fails: "Something went wrong. Please try again or email directly."

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Clear site data and start fresh
text: Clearing Auric Artisan's site data in your browser removes everything the site keeps in that browser: - your library of saved palettes, gradients, collections and exports; - your portfolio draft; - your settings (theme, language, accent colour, text size and so on) and your cookie choice; - the offline cache; - your sign-in on that browser. It does not touch your account, your plan, your published portfolio or anything on other devices. Important: Export anything you want to keep first — see [Export your data](../website/account-and-billing/docs/export-your-data.md) — because the library exists only in your browser. - To clear only your saved work and preferences but stay signed in: dashboard Security & Privacy › danger zone › Erase this browser's workspace . - To clear only the offline cache: https://auricartisan.com/download/ › Reset cache . - To reset only settings: Settings › Reset all . The Cookie Policy lists where to find the controls: Browser Where --- --- Chrome Settings › Privacy and security › Cookies and other site data Firefox Settings › Privacy & Security › Cookies and Site Data Safari Settings › Privacy › Manage Website Data Edge Settings › Cookies and site permissions › Manage and delete cookies Find auricartisan.com and remove its data, then reload the site.

title: Glossary
text: Terms used across the website, the extensions and these docs. Tool-specific terms are defined again in each tool's own glossary. Account and billing terms are in [Account and billing glossary](../website/account-and-billing/others/glossary.md); legal terms are in [Company and legal glossary](../website/company-and-legal/others/glossary.md).

title: Glossary
heading: General and site terms
text: Accent colour — The highlight colour the site uses for buttons and marks. Auric gold by default; you can change it in Settings . API — Application programming interface: a way for your own code to use Auric Artisan's functions over the internet. The REST API is metered in API credits. Cache — Copies of pages and files your browser keeps so they load faster or work offline. Collection — A named group of saved items in your library. Design tokens — Named values (colours, sizes, spacing) exported in a format a build system reads, such as JSON, so a design system can be shared between design and code. CSS custom properties — Variables in CSS, written like --color-primary , that design tokens are often exported as. Export — Saving a result out of a tool as a file (PNG, SVG, PDF, JSON, CSS and so on) or as copied text. Kit — A floating panel that opens over any page, such as the Library Kit. My Library — Your saved palettes, gradients, reports and exports, kept in your browser. PWA — Progressive web app: a website your browser can install like an app and keep available offline. Service worker — The part of a website that runs in the background of your browser to manage the offline cache. Token (tool token) — The unit that pays for server-backed work you start in a website tool, such as a whole-site crawl. Not the same as a design token.

title: Glossary
heading: Accessibility terms
text: AA and AAA — WCAG conformance levels. For text contrast, AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; AAA requires 7:1 and 4.5:1. APCA — Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm: a newer contrast measure that reports a lightness contrast value (Lc) and accounts for text size and polarity (dark on light versus light on dark) better than the WCAG ratio. ARIA — Accessible Rich Internet Applications: attributes that tell assistive technology what an interactive element is and what state it is in. Assistive technology — Tools such as screen readers, magnifiers and switch devices that help people use computers. Contrast ratio — The WCAG measure of how different two colours are in brightness, from 1:1 (identical) to 21:1 (black on white), calculated from their relative luminance. Focus indicator — The visible outline that shows which element the keyboard is on. Large text — In WCAG, text at least 18 point, or 14 point bold. Screen reader — Software that reads the screen aloud or to a braille display. Touch target — The area you tap. WCAG 2.2 asks for at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels; its enhanced level asks for 44 by 44. WCAG — Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the W3C's standard for accessible web content. Versions 2.1 and 2.2 are referred to across the site.

title: Glossary
heading: Colour vision
text: Achromatopsia — Absence of working cone cells, leaving vision without colour. Anomalous trichromacy — All three cone types are present but one responds abnormally, weakening some colour distinctions. Protanomaly, deuteranomaly and tritanomaly affect the long-, medium- and short-wavelength cones. Colour vision deficiency (CVD) — Reduced ability to tell some colours apart; often called colour blindness. Cone cells — The light-sensitive cells in the eye that see colour. There are three kinds: L (long wavelength, reddish), M (medium, greenish) and S (short, bluish). Dichromacy — One cone type is missing. Protanopia (no L cones), deuteranopia (no M cones) and tritanopia (no S cones). Ishihara plate — A pattern of coloured dots hiding a number, used to screen for colour-vision deficiency. Auric Artisan's generator makes Ishihara-style plates for learning only. Vision simulation — A model that shows approximately how an image looks with a given colour-vision deficiency or eye condition. Auric Artisan uses the Viénot 1999, Brettel 1997 and Machado 2009 models.

title: Glossary
heading: Colour science
text: Chroma — How colourful a colour is compared with a grey of the same lightness. Chromatic adaptation — The eye's adjustment to the colour of the light, so a white page looks white under warm or cool light. Transforms such as Von Kries, Bradford, CIECAT02 and CAT16 model it. CIE — The International Commission on Illumination, which publishes the standards behind most colour science. CIE XYZ — The 1931 colour space derived from human colour-matching experiments; the reference most other spaces are defined from. CIELAB (L\ a\ b\ ) — A colour space designed so that equal distances look roughly equally different: L\ is lightness, a\ runs green to red, b\ runs blue to yellow. CIELUV — A related uniform space often used for light sources and displays. CMYK — Cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink; the colour model of print. Conversions from screen colours are approximations. Colour space — A system of numbers for describing colours, such as sRGB, Display P3 or CIELAB. Delta E (ΔE) — A number for how different two colours look. Formulas include CIE76, CIE94, CIEDE2000 (ΔE00, the current standard) and CMC l:c. As a rough guide, a ΔE00 under 1 is not noticeable. Display P3 — A wide-gamut colour space used by many modern screens; it holds more saturated colours than sRGB. Gamut — The range of colours a device or colour space can show. Gamut mapping — Bringing colours that are outside a target gamut into it while keeping them looking as close as possible. HDR — High dynamic range: images and displays with a wider range of brightness than standard. HSL, HSV (HSB), HWB — Cylindrical ways of writing sRGB colours by hue plus saturation and lightness, value (brightness), or whiteness and blackness. Easy to use, but not perceptually uniform. Hue — The attribute that makes a colour red, yellow, green, blue and so on, often given as an angle. ICC profile — A standard file that describes how a device or colour space reproduces colour, used by colour management. Illuminant — A standard description of a light source's spectrum. D65 is average daylight; D50 is used in print; A is incandescent light; F2 and F11 are fluorescent lights. LCH / OKLCH — The polar forms of CIELAB and Oklab: lightness, chroma and hue. Lightness — How light a colour looks, independent of its hue. LUT — Look-up table: a file (commonly .cube ) that maps input colours to output colours, used for colour grading. Luminance (relative) — How bright a colour is, weighted by the eye's sensitivity; the basis of the WCAG contrast ratio. Metamerism — Two colours that match under one light but not under another, because their spectra differ. Munsell system — A colour-order system describing colours by hue, value and chroma, used as a physical reference. Oklab — A modern perceptually uniform colour space (Björn Ottosson, 2020) with steadier hue as lightness changes; used for smooth palettes and scales. Perceptually uniform — A colour space in which equal numeric steps look like equal visual steps. Rendering intent — The rule used when gamut mapping, for example keeping colours exact where possible or keeping their relationships. Spectral power distribution — How much light a source or surface gives off at each wavelength. sRGB — The standard colour space of the web and most consumer screens. Standard observer — The CIE's average human colour-matching response, measured for a 2° or 10° field of view. Tonal scale (ramp) — A series of tints and shades of one colour, such as steps 50 to 950, ideally spaced evenly to the eye. Tone mapping — Compressing HDR brightness into the range a standard display can show. White point — The colour a space or device treats as white, such as D65.

title: Glossary
heading: Colour harmony
text: Analogous — Colours next to each other on the colour wheel. Complementary — Colours opposite each other on the wheel. Split-complementary — A colour plus the two neighbours of its complement. Triadic — Three colours evenly spaced around the wheel. Tetradic (square) — Four colours in two complementary pairs, or evenly spaced.

title: Glossary
heading: Perception research
text: Psychophysics — Measuring how physical stimuli (such as colour differences) relate to what people perceive, usually through controlled experiments.

title: Privacy overview
text: This page brings together what the policies and the product say about your data. The authoritative documents are the Privacy Policy (https://auricartisan.com/legal/privacy/), the Cookie Policy (https://auricartisan.com/legal/cookies/), the Data Retention and Deletion Policy and, for the browser extension, the Extension Privacy Policy. Plain-language summaries of each are in [Company and legal](../website/company-and-legal/README.md).

The FAQ page says no URL history or page content is kept after the analysis session. Server-backed tool work When you start a run that uses tokens Contact messages and attachments When you use the contact form Order records: item, amount, payment reference When you buy something Analytics events Only with consent (below) The Privacy Policy says colour calculations, palettes, vision simulations and theme generation run in your browser where possible and are not sent anywhere.

title: Privacy overview
heading: Analytics and consent
text: - Analytics is first-party: events go to Auric Artisan's own servers. There are no third-party analytics scripts and no analytics cookies. - Events are sent only if you accepted the Analytics category in the cookie bar or on the Cookie Policy page. No choice means no events. - Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control in your browser turn analytics off regardless. - An event contains the event name, the page path (never the query string), the referrer's origin, and a few coarse properties such as device class. The dashboard's Usage data switch (in Security & Privacy ) records your choice on your account; the cookie choice is what governs analytics on the website.

title: Privacy overview
heading: Third parties
text: Company Role (as the policies describe it) --- --- Cloudflare Hosting, DNS, CDN, compute and storage for account, preference and order data Razorpay Payments. Card, UPI and bank details go to Razorpay directly and never reach Auric Artisan. Google Fonts Font files on some pages; Google receives the technical request, such as your IP address Resend Email delivery (named on the Security page) Free-plan pages can show sponsored slots. The Subscription and Billing Policy says ads shown to free users are limited and consent-gated, and that private data is not used for advertising profiles.

title: Privacy overview
heading: What each product collects
text: Product Summary --- --- Website, no account Your browser keeps your work and settings; servers see page requests, tool inputs for server-backed work, and analytics only with consent Website, with account The above, plus account, security and order records Browser extension Reads a page only when you use a tool on it; stores everything in the browser's extension storage; no analytics, telemetry or network requests with your data VS Code extensions Described on https://auricartisan.com/vscode/ as needing no account and sending no telemetry REST API Your requests and usage, metered against your account

title: Privacy overview
heading: No sale, no tracking across sites
text: The Privacy Policy states that Auric Artisan does not sell, rent or trade personal data, does not take part in data-broker networks or cross-site tracking, and does not use personal data for behavioural advertising or automated decisions with legal effects.
